rows.original: "You p-probably think I'm crazy, don't you?" Probably, but you'll humor her for a bit. So, the vision, what happened? "Look, before I begin, I just want to say that when the visions involve me and I follow them, they've never led me astray. Like, never. Can't say the same for anyone else, because I don't go around spying on people all hours of the day. That's creepy." But she sees them in visions anyway. "Yeah, but that's like, different." Nina moves to take a swig from her jug, realizes it's empty, then briefly contemplates the cosmic injustice of existence before shrugging and placing the empty jug down by the other half-dozen. "I don't go around looking for them, they come to me." That's splitting hairs, but you're getting sidetracked. "Right. So I saw you heading out of here, and going northeast into the woods — you know, the part that's all cold bog. There, you found one of those old elven mines that dug up bog iron in the before days, when people still used that stuff. That's when you came across a really nasty customer in there!" A nasty customer? What does she mean exactly? "Oh, just your average construct left over from the elves who once worked that mine. But you want to know what's dangerous? Once you went further in, you took the first tunnel to the left. It led to — " she gesticulates wildly with her hands — "one of those big dug-out caves. You know, the kind where they leave pillars in to hold up the ceiling so it doesn't fall on them. Now here's where it gets really important, so listen up." You're listening. Nina makes several false starts, stumbling over her words, but finally manages to get them out. "So, there're a lot of pitfalls in that cavern — not because of the elves, mind you. Or well, because of the elves, but not on purpose. Once they realized they'd dug too many holes and weakened the floor into a cavern below them, they didn't have a choice but to abandon the place. "So, if you don't want to go plummeting to your doom in the darkness, just don't step in them. Not stepping into the pitfalls is key — now, you would rightly ask what kind of idiot would walk straight into a hole? Well, I'll tell you: it was pretty dark in the vision and there was a lot of loose footing. If you step, you die. Step and perish." That was incredibly enlightening and helpful, not stepping in holes. Certainly no one would think of that on their own.[pc.isDK | About as useful as %"if you don't want to die, don't get killed", in fact. ] Nina drains her jug. "You're welcome. Now, once you made it to the other end of the cavern, you found a pile of old rotting boxes that the elves had left behind centuries ago. I saw you getting something real super-important from them, and that's where the vision ended." What was this super-important thing, to use her own words? A contemplative tapping of fingers upon table. "Eh, no idea. Everything went fuzzy at that point, but I remember that it was important, very much so, and I'd be pretty grateful if I could get my hands on it. See, it was in the vision, and visions don't lie. At least for me." [party.has etheryn |While Nina continues drinking herself further into her stupor, you turn to Ryn and ask her if there's any possibility that there's even the slightest smidgen of truth in everything that the harpy just spouted. Ryn thinks a moment, then nods cautiously. "She's right about the old elven mines, at least. They were closed sometime during great-grandmother's and grandmother's reign, first from exhaustion of bog iron and eventually when grandmother started sluicing the melt from the mountains for tin and copper to make bronze in the wake of the Godswar. But you don't need to have any kind of clairvoyant or prophetic powers to know a bit of history." And her assessment? "Well... admittedly boer'alvar history isn't knowledge I'd expect a harpy to be acquainted with, but there's nothing in anything she said that solidly proves anything. On the other hand, she hasn't said anything that disproves her claims of visions, so there's that." ] Hm, you see. You ponder this a moment while Nina eyes you, and then she pulls herself together and raises her head to give you a small smile. "You'll take it." How does she know? Another vision? "Nope, don't need any visions for that. You asked, which meant you were curious and wanted to know more; you wouldn't have done that if you weren't interested. Hence, it's not too much of a stretch to guess that you'll play along. I don't know if you believe me or not, but that doesn't matter; belief isn't really required in this circumstance." How would you go about getting there? "We-ll...you wandered about for a bit, then there was this old lightning-struck tree, just a solid block of ash way high. From there, the entrance to the mine was just a little north of there." So, that's how it's going to be. Well, you might or might not do as her vision suggests, and it's possible, but not certain, that you'll head into this abandoned elven mine and retrieve for her... whatever it is that she thinks is so important. "Great!" Nina raises her jug in cheers. "I'll be waiting for you, then. With plenty of ale, of course. Ru-mie!"
rows.translation: 你大概觉得我疯了吧，对吧？” “大概吧，但你也只会陪她闹一会儿而已。那么，那些幻象，到底发生了什么？” “听着，在开始之前，我只想说：每当这些幻象与我有关，而我选择跟随它们的指引时，它们从来都没有让我走错路。真的，从来没有。不过对于其他人来说，我就不敢保证了，因为我可不会整天去偷窥别人……那样太变态了。 但她还是在幻象中看到了它们。 “是啊，不过那总归是不一样的吧。”尼娜伸手去喝她的水壶里的水，却发现水壶已经空了，于是她短暂地思考了一下这种存在的“宇宙级不公”，然后耸了耸肩，把空水壶放在那六七个水壶旁边。“我并不是主动去寻找它们的，它们会主动找到我。 这简直是在吹毛求疵了，但你现在已经偏离主题了。 “没错。我看见你从这里出发，然后向东北方向走进了森林——就是那片全是冷沼泽的地方。在那里，你找到了那些古老的精灵矿井，它们在很久以前人们还使用那些铁矿的时候就被挖掘出来了。就在那里，你遇到了一个非常棘手的麻烦人物！ 一个难缠的顾客？她到底是什么意思？ “哦，其实就是那些曾经在那个矿场工作的精灵们留下的普通构造物罢了。但你想知道真正危险的地方在哪里吗？当你继续往里面走，遇到第一个向左的隧道时，它就会通向——”她用手势比划着，“其中一个巨大的挖掘洞穴。你知道的，就是那种需要用柱子来支撑天花板，防止它塌下来的洞穴。现在，关键的地方来了，所以请仔细听。 你在听。 尼娜几次语塞，说话时结结巴巴，但最终还是把话讲完了。“所以，那个洞穴里有很多危险之处——不过，这并不是因为那些精灵。或者说，至少不是因为它们因为那些精灵并不是故意这么做的。当他们意识到自己挖了太多洞，导致下方的地面变得松软，甚至形成了一个洞穴时，他们别无选择，只能放弃这个地方。 “所以，如果你不想在暗影中坠入毁灭，就不要踩进那些洞里。避免掉入这些陷阱才是关键——现在，你可能会问：究竟什么样的傻瓜会直接走进坑里去呢？其实，我想告诉你：当时的视线非常模糊，而且地面也布满了松软的杂物。一旦踩上去，就会立刻丧命。踏入其中，便会丧命。” 这确实非常有启发意义，也极具帮助作用，能让人避免掉入那些陷阱。当然，没有人会自己想到这个办法的。[pc.isDK | 其实，这跟“如果你不想死，就别被杀”差不多有用。 ] 尼娜喝光了她的水壶里的水。“不客气。后来，当你穿过洞穴的另一端时，你发现了一堆精灵们几个世纪前留下的旧箱子。我看到你从那些箱子里拿出了某样非常重要的东西，然后幻象就到此结束了。” 用她自己的话来说，那件非常重要的东西到底是什么呢？ 她若有所思地用手指轻敲着桌子，说道：“呃，我也不清楚。在那个时候，所有的事情都变得模糊不清了，但我记得那东西确实非常重要。非常确实如此，如果我能得到它，我会非常感激。你看，这个东西在那个预知中出现过，而预知是不会骗人的。至少对我来说是这样。 [party.has etheryn |当尼娜继续饮酒，逐渐陷入昏迷时，你转向小琳，询问她：那个女妖刚才说的那些话，是否有一丝半点真实性？小琳思考了一会儿，然后谨慎地点了点头。 至少，她关于那些古老的精灵矿井的说法是正确的。那些矿井在曾祖母和祖母在位期间就被关闭了——起初是因为沼铁资源枯竭，后来则是因为在‘神战’之后，祖母开始从山中提取熔融物来提取锡和铜，从而用来制造青铜。不过，你并不需要具备什么预知能力或超自然的力量，才能了解一些历史知识。” 那么，她的说法呢？ “嗯……诚然，关于布尔人的历史，并不是我认为一个女妖会了解的内容，但她所说的那些话，并没有任何能够确凿证明任何事情的证据。另一方面，她并没有说过任何……的话。证明是错误的她声称自己看到了某些景象，也就是这么一回事。 ] 嗯，你瞧。你仔细思考着这个问题，而尼娜则一直注视着你，然后她振作起来，抬起头，对你微微一笑。 “你会接受的。” 她是怎么知道的？又是通过某种预知能力吗？ “不，并不需要什么预知能力。你提出了这个问题，这说明你很感兴趣，想要了解更多；如果你不感兴趣的话，就不会这么做了。因此，猜测你会配合下去也并不是太牵强。我不知道你是否相信我，但这并不重要；在这种情况下，相信与否其实并不是必需的。你打算怎么才能到达那里呢？” “我们……你会先在周围逛一会儿，然后会看到那棵被闪电击中的老树，那只是一棵高高的、由灰烬构成的树干。从那里开始，矿井的入口就在稍微往北一点的地方。所以，事情就会这样发展。嗯，你可能会按照她的建议去做，也可能会不这么做；你确实有可能进入这座被废弃的精灵矿井，去为她取回……那些她认为非常重要的东西，但这也并非必然会发生。 太好了！”妮娜举起她的酒壶欢呼道，“那我就等着你来了。当然，当然还会准备充足的麦酒。鲁米！
rows.raw: " "You p-probably think I'm crazy, don't you?" Probably, but you'll humor her for a bit. So, the vision, what happened? "Look, before I begin, I just want to say that when the visions involve me and I follow them, they've never led me astray. Like, never. Can't say the same for anyone else, because I don't go around spying on people all hours of the day. That's creepy." But she sees them in visions anyway. "Yeah, but that's like, different." Nina moves to take a swig from her jug, realizes it's empty, then briefly contemplates the cosmic injustice of existence before shrugging and placing the empty jug down by the other half-dozen. "I don't go around looking for them, they come to me." That's splitting hairs, but you're getting sidetracked. "Right. So I saw you heading out of here, and going northeast into the woods — you know, the part that's all cold bog. There, you found one of those old elven mines that dug up bog iron in the before days, when people still used that stuff. That's when you came across a really nasty customer in there!" A nasty customer? What does she mean exactly? "Oh, just your average construct left over from the elves who once worked that mine. But you want to know what's dangerous? Once you went further in, you took the first tunnel to the left. It led to — " she gesticulates wildly with her hands — "one of those big dug-out caves. You know, the kind where they leave pillars in to hold up the ceiling so it doesn't fall on them. Now here's where it gets really important, so listen up." You're listening. Nina makes several false starts, stumbling over her words, but finally manages to get them out. "So, there're a lot of pitfalls in that cavern — not because of the elves, mind you. Or well, because of the elves, but not on purpose. Once they realized they'd dug too many holes and weakened the floor into a cavern below them, they didn't have a choice but to abandon the place. "So, if you don't want to go plummeting to your doom in the darkness, just don't step in them. Not stepping into the pitfalls is key — now, you would rightly ask what kind of idiot would walk straight into a hole? Well, I'll tell you: it was pretty dark in the vision and there was a lot of loose footing. If you step, you die. Step and perish." That was incredibly enlightening and helpful, not stepping in holes. Certainly no one would think of that on their own.[pc.isDK | About as useful as %"if you don't want to die, don't get killed", in fact. ] Nina drains her jug. "You're welcome. Now, once you made it to the other end of the cavern, you found a pile of old rotting boxes that the elves had left behind centuries ago. I saw you getting something real super-important from them, and that's where the vision ended." What was this super-important thing, to use her own words? A contemplative tapping of fingers upon table. "Eh, no idea. Everything went fuzzy at that point, but I remember that it was important, very much so, and I'd be pretty grateful if I could get my hands on it. See, it was in the vision, and visions don't lie. At least for me." [party.has etheryn |While Nina continues drinking herself further into her stupor, you turn to Ryn and ask her if there's any possibility that there's even the slightest smidgen of truth in everything that the harpy just spouted. Ryn thinks a moment, then nods cautiously. "She's right about the old elven mines, at least. They were closed sometime during great-grandmother's and grandmother's reign, first from exhaustion of bog iron and eventually when grandmother started sluicing the melt from the mountains for tin and copper to make bronze in the wake of the Godswar. But you don't need to have any kind of clairvoyant or prophetic powers to know a bit of history." And her assessment? "Well... admittedly boer'alvar history isn't knowledge I'd expect a harpy to be acquainted with, but there's nothing in anything she said that solidly proves anything. On the other hand, she hasn't said anything that disproves her claims of visions, so there's that." ] Hm, you see. You ponder this a moment while Nina eyes you, and then she pulls herself together and raises her head to give you a small smile. "You'll take it." How does she know? Another vision? "Nope, don't need any visions for that. You asked, which meant you were curious and wanted to know more; you wouldn't have done that if you weren't interested. Hence, it's not too much of a stretch to guess that you'll play along. I don't know if you believe me or not, but that doesn't matter; belief isn't really required in this circumstance." How would you go about getting there? "We-ll...you wandered about for a bit, then there was this old lightning-struck tree, just a solid block of ash way high. From there, the entrance to the mine was just a little north of there." So, that's how it's going to be. Well, you might or might not do as her vision suggests, and it's possible, but not certain, that you'll head into this abandoned elven mine and retrieve for her... whatever it is that she thinks is so important. "Great!" Nina raises her jug in cheers. "I'll be waiting for you, then. With plenty of ale, of course. Ru-mie!" "

rows.original: So, what was in the vision she had when you approached her? What did you do?
rows.translation: 那么，当你接近她的时候，她脑海中浮现出了什么画面？你做了什么呢？
rows.raw: "So, what was in the vision she had when you approached her? What did you do?"

rows.original: Nina doesn't say anything, but rolls one storm-gray eye up at you. You match her stare for several moments, perhaps feeling a little silly for it — by all appearances, the glassy, glazed-over gaze is absolutely devoid of all lucidity. [pc.willpowerRange 80 |Nothing happens for a little while longer, the two of you meeting eyes over the table. Then, with a start, you realize that your thoughts have been drifting away from this silly game of chicken with a drunk harpy, your limbs feeling deadened and numb; if not for your ample willpower you wouldn't have noticed that you're losing control over your body and actions. The world around you slowly begins to blur away, until all that remains is Nina's one good storm-gray eye staring not at you, but through you and into your mind. This is not good, to put it lightly. Now that you know what's happening, you furiously fight to wrest back control of your person — and feel Nina's jolt of surprise as you're momentarily able to break her control over your mind. |After several moments, it becomes clear that nothing more is going to happen, be it from Nina being unwilling or more likely, unable to comprehend your question due to her state of permanent drunkenness. Given that this was about what you expected, you shrug and see if you can't ask her anything else. ]
rows.translation: 妮娜什么也没说，只是翻起一只暴风灰色的眼睛看着你。你与她对视了好一会儿，或许还觉得这样做有点傻——从外表来看，那呆滞、蒙着一层雾的目光里绝对没有半点清醒的意识。 [pc.willpowerRange 80 |又过了一小会儿，什么也没有发生，你们两人隔着桌子四目相对。然后，你猛地一惊，意识到自己的思绪已经偏离了这场和醉酒鹰身女妖玩的愚蠢斗鸡游戏，你的四肢也变得麻木迟钝；要不是你有充沛的意志力，你根本不会注意到自己正在失去对身体和行动的控制。周围的世界开始缓缓模糊，直到剩下的只有妮娜那只完好的暴风灰色眼睛，它不是看着你，而是看穿你，直看进你的脑海。 说得轻一点，这可不太妙。既然你知道了正在发生什么，你便拼命挣扎，想要夺回对自己身体的控制——并感到妮娜一阵惊讶的电流，因为你短暂地打破了她对你心智的控制。 |过了好一会儿，显然不会再有什么事情发生了，要么是妮娜不愿意，要么更可能是她处于永久醉酒的状态，无法理解你的问题。既然这大致在你的预料之中，你便耸耸肩，看看还能不能再问她别的什么。 ]
rows.raw: " Nina doesn't say anything, but rolls one storm-gray eye up at you. You match her stare for several moments, perhaps feeling a little silly for it — by all appearances, the glassy, glazed-over gaze is absolutely devoid of all lucidity. [pc.willpowerRange 80 |Nothing happens for a little while longer, the two of you meeting eyes over the table. Then, with a start, you realize that your thoughts have been drifting away from this silly game of chicken with a drunk harpy, your limbs feeling deadened and numb; if not for your ample willpower you wouldn't have noticed that you're losing control over your body and actions. The world around you slowly begins to blur away, until all that remains is Nina's one good storm-gray eye staring not at you, but through you and into your mind. This is not good, to put it lightly. Now that you know what's happening, you furiously fight to wrest back control of your person — and feel Nina's jolt of surprise as you're momentarily able to break her control over your mind. |After several moments, it becomes clear that nothing more is going to happen, be it from Nina being unwilling or more likely, unable to comprehend your question due to her state of permanent drunkenness. Given that this was about what you expected, you shrug and see if you can't ask her anything else. ]"

rows.original: You blink. Just what [pc.isDK |the fuck ]did she do to you? "I demonstrated my ability to defend myself from the less scrupulous patrons of this bar, with a gentle hand nonetheless. Usually a bad headache — it would cause problems for Rumie and you if I did more. Wasn't this what you wanted to know?" Sure, but did she have to demonstrate?[pc.isDK | Gods, you're still not sure she's fully gone from your head! ] "...You would've dismissed my words as the drunken ramblings of a crazy harpy. Which, to be fair, they are." Well, she's not wrong... "If it makes you feel better, I promise not to influence you in such a manner again unless it is to protect my person.[pc.isDK | So please, for both our sakes, if you would constrain your very understandable anger... ]" [pc.isDK |Pft. She'd better not fucking ever do that again. ]Fine. Perhaps you should move on from the subject, then.
rows.translation: 你眨了眨眼。她究竟[pc.isDK |他妈的 ]对你做了什么？ “我只是在证明，自己有能力抵御酒吧里那些不择手段的顾客，而且用的还是温和手段。通常只会让人头疼得厉害——若再多做一点，就会给露米和你惹上麻烦。这不正是你想知道的吗？” 当然，可她非得亲自演示吗？[pc.isDK |诸神啊，你甚至还不确定她是否已经彻底离开了你的脑袋！ ] “……不然你只会把我的话当成一只疯狂鹰身女妖的醉后胡言。公平地说，它们也的确是。” 好吧，她也不能算说错…… “如果这样能令你好受些，我保证，除非为了保护自己，否则不会再用这种方式影响你。[pc.isDK |所以，为了我们双方着想，请你克制一下这份完全可以理解的怒火…… ]” [pc.isDK |嘁。她最好他妈的永远别再来一次。 ]好吧。那么，也许你该换个话题了。
rows.raw: " You blink. Just what [pc.isDK |the fuck ]did she do to you? "I demonstrated my ability to defend myself from the less scrupulous patrons of this bar, with a gentle hand nonetheless. Usually a bad headache — it would cause problems for Rumie and you if I did more. Wasn't this what you wanted to know?" Sure, but did she have to demonstrate?[pc.isDK | Gods, you're still not sure she's fully gone from your head! ] "...You would've dismissed my words as the drunken ramblings of a crazy harpy. Which, to be fair, they are." Well, she's not wrong... "If it makes you feel better, I promise not to influence you in such a manner again unless it is to protect my person.[pc.isDK | So please, for both our sakes, if you would constrain your very understandable anger... ]" [pc.isDK |Pft. She'd better not fucking ever do that again. ]Fine. Perhaps you should move on from the subject, then."

rows.original: You attempt to reach out with your sense of self, but the element of surprise is gone. Nina's voice rings in your mind, without the slightest hint of slurring: Please, this is simply to answer your question; I mean you no harm. Rumie would be quite cross with us both if we caused trouble in her bar. And don't try this with anyone else; you aren't even a dreamwalker. Others might be less amused, even if the attempt would bear no fruit. Something tightens about your consciousness, clearly indicating it could crush you if it so desired, and then is gone, slithering away from your senses to whence it came.
rows.translation: 你试图用自己的意识去尝试联系对方，但那种突如其来的惊喜感已经消失了。尼娜的声音在你的脑海中回荡，她的发音清晰得没有任何含糊之处： 拜托，我这么做只是为了回答你的问题，并没有恶意。如果我们在露米的酒吧里惹麻烦，她肯定会生我们两人的气。另外，别对别人也这么试；你甚至都不是“梦行者”，其他人可能不会觉得这有什么好笑的，即使你的尝试最终没有任何结果。 某个东西这种意识的力量会紧紧束缚着你，清晰地显示出：如果它愿意的话，完全有可能将你压垮；然后，它又会悄然消失，从你的感官中溜走，回到它最初出现的地方。
rows.raw: " You attempt to reach out with your sense of self, but the element of surprise is gone. Nina's voice rings in your mind, without the slightest hint of slurring: Please, this is simply to answer your question; I mean you no harm. Rumie would be quite cross with us both if we caused trouble in her bar. And don't try this with anyone else; you aren't even a dreamwalker. Others might be less amused, even if the attempt would bear no fruit. Something tightens about your consciousness, clearly indicating it could crush you if it so desired, and then is gone, slithering away from your senses to whence it came."

rows.original: Try to turn the tables on her, turnabout is fair play.
rows.translation: 试着反过来对付她吧，以牙还牙才是公平的。
rows.raw: "Try to turn the tables on her, turnabout is fair play."

rows.original:
It takes a gigantic surge of effort to tear your eyes away from Nina, but the presence in your consciousness is gone the moment you do so. Now that it's no longer around, the momentary void it's left in your thoughts leaves you with little doubt that whatever this was, it could have crushed your psyche in moments.
            
            "You should be proud," Nina mumbles through the alcohol. She's clearly capable of being lucid even under the influence when she wants to, and it's no longer surprising. "Few who aren't dreamwalkers have wills as strong as yours, but you went above and beyond that, being able to catch me off-guard."
rows.translation:
要将视线从尼娜身上移开，确实需要耗费巨大的精力，但一旦你做到了，那个形象就会立刻从你的意识中消失。如今它已经不在了，它在你脑海中留下的那片空白，让你毫不怀疑：无论这是什么，它都可能在瞬间摧毁你的心理。
            
            “你应该感到骄傲，”妮娜在酒精的作用下喃喃说道。显然，当她想要保持清醒时，她是完全有能力做到这一点的，这一点已经不再令人惊讶了。“那些不是梦游者的人中，很少有人能拥有你这样坚强的意志力，而你更是做得更加出色，竟然能够让我措手不及。”
rows.raw:
"
            It takes a gigantic surge of effort to tear your eyes away from Nina, but the presence in your consciousness is gone the moment you do so. Now that it's no longer around, the momentary void it's left in your thoughts leaves you with little doubt that whatever this was, it could have crushed your psyche in moments.
            
            "You should be proud," Nina mumbles through the alcohol. She's clearly capable of being lucid even under the influence when she wants to, and it's no longer surprising. "Few who aren't dreamwalkers have wills as strong as yours, but you went above and beyond that, being able to catch me off-guard.""

rows.original: You've had enough, she's made her point. Break the stare and disengage your mind from hers.
rows.translation: 你已经受够了，她已经把意思表达清楚了。别再盯着她看，把你的注意力从她身上移开吧。
rows.raw: "You've had enough, she's made her point. Break the stare and disengage your mind from hers."

rows.original: So, Rumie said something about odd things happening to people who bother her...
rows.translation: 所以，露米说过，那些打扰她的人会遇到一些奇怪的事情……
rows.raw: "So, Rumie said something about odd things happening to people who bother her..."

rows.original: [rand |"Have you ever seen a wraith before? Or even something that's sufficiently wraith-touched?" [var0 |Actually, you have. And the Wraith in question didn't even look too bad, to be honest. Nina tilts her head to the side so much that it's just about touching her shoulder, blinks, then shrugs. "Yeah, that sounds about right. But what I'm talking about is most people, and you and I don't count amongst that bunch." So, what about them? |Actually, you have. And you never want to see another one ever again. Nina shrugs, your claim of having seen a monstrosity out of legend rolling off her like water off a duck. "Don't blame you. But was what you saw really what it was?" What does she mean? |No, you haven't. But everyone knows stories about them, and if even a quarter of said stories have but a grain of truth to them, you sincerely hope you never will. "Well, about those stories, you ever wonder why the descriptions of a Wraith is different between each one? Like in one you get a shapeless blob, another you get a huge insect, or someone says it's a large black bear that absorbs all light?" You motion for her to go on. ] "See, it's like this. Wraiths don't actually have a form — they're just immaterial shadows, all amorphous and nasty. That's one of the reasons they're so desperate to come into worlds like ours, to be tangible, to be real. But here's the rub: our minds interpret them as these dark monsters because just seeing a living shadow from the void between the spheres is simply too freaky. Our noggins chicken out, and substitute in all kinds of crazy things that become accounts in the history books of what wraiths look like. That's why no two are ever the same." Hmm... "Don't you think the mind is a strange thing? I'd know, I've got one, even if it's thoroughly pickled. Cheers!" She's either making too much sense, or she's crazy. "I know, right? Some days I ask myself whether I'm making all of this up, and I have to admit that it's a possibility." |"You know... not all of the visions that I have tell me things that I can actually act upon. Most of the stuff that comes to me, I don't even know half of what it is, let alone can I do something about that knowledge. But where the visions actually make sense, they've never steered me wrong. "Sure, it's an exercise of trust in my own crazy mind, but experience speaks: every time I've followed a vision, I've pulled through; every time I've gone against or even ignored it, everything collapsed into the unknown and unknowable, outside of what ought to be. Doesn't take long for a harpy to figure out the easiest way to do things." That sounds... counterintuitive. She's a harpy! "So?" Well... flight. Freedom. That sort of thing. The power to decide one's own fate, instead of having one's decisions and future held hostage by visions from her dreams, waking or otherwise. Does that hold any meaning for her, given that she's one of Sorra's creatures? "See, I'm a practical woman. When the goddess decides to grant me safety, a warm place to sleep, and all the booze I can drink, her ideals will be in the running for how I should live my life. Until then, I'm perfectly fine with the visions which've done more for me than the goddess ever has." |"So a while ago, I drank too much brazenberry ale — yeah, that can happen sometimes. So, I was walking home — " Home? Nina squints up at you blearily. "What? I've got a home." If she lives elsewhere other than Rumie's bar, you wouldn't know it. Every time you've seen her, she's been in this very spot drinking her brains out. Even Rumie claims she never moves from the spot. "And you trust that Rumie's behind the bar all day, yeah? Every time I come in here she's at that counter doing bartender things." Well, Rumie doesn't deny living here in the Wayfort. "Pfff. Anyway, I was walking home when the ground suddenly rose and hit me in the head! It's sneaky that way sometimes, you have to be very careful when dealing with the ground. I passed out, and when I came to I was in an odd-looking cave. By the way, I don't live in a cave. Not anymore." [pc.isDK |Maybe you stuttered, but you're pretty sure you asked her to tell you something interesting. |Go on... ] "I'm getting to the good part. Gods, was I lost! And thirsty! Good thing I had some emergency ale on me, so I drained the jug to the last drop, and when I came to I was in my bed all snug and sound. Clean forgot everything that'd happened." ...Now she's getting incoherent here. What does she mean, forgot everything that'd happened? She just told you it, so clearly she remembers. Unless this is a confession of having made everything up? Something snaps in Nina's eye, and she looks at you as if seeing you for the very first time in her life. "Oh hey. How's it going?" This... you know what, forget it. |"Want to know more about lurelings? Those legendary creatures of the deepest ocean and lightless caves?" [QUEST_WINTER_WOLF.stateRange 9 |Sure. You've only ever met the one, but it was under circumstances that didn't lend themselves well to conversation |Yes and no at the same time; everyone knows of the campfire tales, but actual knowledge is rare ]. What about them, did she see them in some vision or the other? "Oh, even better. I talk to a couple all the time." ...Really, now. "Yeah. Especially Gerry. He's not a bad guy if you get to know him, especially if you have a bit of brew on hand. Bit of a philosopher, likes to natter on about 'descent into center' or something like that. Me, I'm just there to be exotic. Anyways, you know what they're really after this time? The latest game to pass the years dreamwalking?" Yes? "They're searching for a diamond, a big shiny diamond that glows in the dark brighter than distilled spirits set on fire. It's one of a kind, so the lurelings want to put it on a stand in their little conclave in the Ways Between and stare at it knowing that they've become completely and utterly cool and awesome. Yeah. That's what they've been doing for the last century or so, makes for a bit of sport without actually hurting anyone. Or at least, anyone they count as anyone, which is everyone who is as powerful a psion as they all are. Which most of us aren't. Maybe not even me." So, the last part of her statement aside... it's just a big glowing diamond? Not really a hunk of ley-crystal, or some kind of ancient artifact that predates the Godswar? Just a diamond that shines in the dark? That's kind of lame as far as a story goes. Nina shrugs. "That's what Gerry told me after downing a casket of brazenberry ale; they just want the diamond because it looks pretty and cool. Any more, and there'd be actual stakes involved — it'd stop being just a game to pass the time. That'd be bad, not just for them, but for you and me, too." She's just had one too many ales. "Yeah well, that's, like, your opinion." |"Crystals. Just... crystals. Every time there's any kind of mystical arcane mess around, you tend to find crystals. Like, you ever wonder why crystals seem to feature so prominently everywhere weird stuff turns up? It's like the two are connected, or something." [pc.isMage |Well, there's a perfectly reasonable explanation for that. Natural formations of ley-crystals tend to aggregate power, and all that power in one place does indeed inevitably produce mystical arcane messes, as she so eloquently puts it. |Crystals are what they are — isn't that why wizards go after them a lot of the time? Especially those ley-crystal things? ] "Yeah, but it still happens even when the crystals aren't ley-crystals." Nina shakes her head and has another swig of ale to calm her nerves. "It's just weird, you know? Like, every time you go really deep underground and need some light to see by, bam! There're crystals everywhere, and they all give off a convenient glow for you to find your way around with. That kinda thing. Well, you know what I think?" Yes? "See, there's some kind of primordial being deep inside the earth — half person, half rock, half whatever horrendous being that comes from beyond the ways —" That doesn't add up, or at least, it adds up to more than one. "That doesn't matter when it comes to creatures like that. Now, am I the one telling the story, or you?" Does it matter when her source is literally %"it came to me in a dream"? "Anyways. This primordial entity, it wants to do something, anything, because boredom. At the same time, it can't leave, because it needs all that heat and pressure to simply continue existing. That's where the crystals come in — they're there to primarily serve as its eyes and ears let it observe all the fun things that're going on where it's cool enough for other creatures to exist. "Anyways. It's vitally important that you don't touch, lick, kick, punch, feed, jump over or sing to weird cave crystals, as it can be disastrous for your mind; you don't want an ancient consciousness like that even so much as touching your head, let alone trying to get into it. Most crystals are inert and simply observe, but you really, really don't want to take that chance to begin with. Trust me on this. But wizards being the fools that they are, they carve up the crystals and take little bits to the surface to do whatever with. Really, wizards — truly no sense of right and wrong." All right, let's suppose for one moment that she's absolutely right about all of this. Just about every modern spellcaster in existence uses a crystal, if not a gem focus. Do those count, too? Is it a ploy by this... thing deep under the earth to have eyes and ears everywhere on the surface, for the sole sake of not being bored? "I mean, if you were such a thing, why wouldn't you?" Nina takes a heavy swig of her ale. "I'd be bored right out of my skull after a day, let alone thousands of years." |"You know, I hate dust. I'm really glad that Rumie keeps this bar spick and span, because I wouldn't be able to bear it otherwise." [pc.isDK |Given that she sits here all day, your only surprise is that she hasn't actually begun to gather a nice coating of it of her own. Nina shudders at the thought and gulps down several large swigs of brazenberry ale to calm her nerves. "Oh no no no no. Can't abide that. I lift this fat butt of mine at three in the afternoon every day so that Rumie can clean my spot. It's important to be clean and neat." |It's good that Rumie [wayfort.hasMaids |and the maids keep |keeps ] the Wayfort clean. It's your home, after all, and you wouldn't want it being all dusty. "Good, good. I like you already. Not that I didn't before, but anyone with a neat home is to be respected." Nina gulps down several large swigs of brazenberry ale to emphasize her point. ] That's quite a visceral reaction she had there — she really dislikes dust that much? "Of course I do! It gets in your feathers. It gets in your nose. And worst of all, it gets in your drink. Hate dust." She leans in conspiratorially and stage-whispers into your ear. "Ordinary dust's bad enough. But dark dust..." Oh, this is going to be good. Sure, you'll play along — what can she tell you about this so-called %"dark dust"? "Well, you clearly know about the Ways Between, which surrounds our world." Nina sets down her jug and mimes a ball with her hands. "But beyond that is where the wraiths came from — the horrible dark between the worlds. There aren't many things there, but what is plentiful — relatively speaking — is dark dust. The Ways keeps most of it from coming in, but some gets through when portals naturally open, or it filters into the world when we disturb that space with our dreams... nasty stuff. "You don't ever want to get close to any of it in any quantity, even someone psionically dull like you. Tiny specks will give you nightmares. More will give you hallucinations. Enough to smudge a finger is really, really bad; there probably won't be enough left of your psyche to fill a mental soup bowl. But not to worry, there isn't that much in one spot to cause more than bad dreams, not unless someone is crazy enough to start intentionally collecting the stuff. And if that's the case, you have bigger problems on hand than the complete shattering and dissolution of your mind." You've certainly never seen any of this mystical dust. Maybe she just has an allergy. |"Go ahead and drink the water," Nina mumbles. "It's too late anyways, has been for a couple generations now." What about the water? Why shouldn't you drink it, even if it's as she says and there's not much point now? "It's... it's the order Astrida," Nina mumbles. "Those at the top. [pc.swornGod nareva |I know that you recently joined with them and most are okay people, it's just those at the very top. You should know what you've gotten yourself into, if nothing else |I've never dared tell anyone because I know they come in and drag people away, but you... you're different ]. "You see, the black-scales gather up all the relics they can find of the old era, anything that might prove concretely what happened then, instead of folklore and hearsay. They put them on ships and transport them to a faraway island, where they have a museum in a deep grassy valley. Only a few pieces are ever on display, but beneath the mountains of that valley in an underground lake there's a seven-headed hydra with one amethyst eye; the black-scales revere it as a divine beast of the goddess." This is crazy, and very possibly blasphemy to boot. This is the ale talking, right? Nina ignores you and keeps going, her jug of ale completely forgotten. "The hydra... it devours secrets, you see. The black-scales feed it the relics they collect, and it spews out these tiny invisible magical motes that wind up in its pool. The pool flows out to the underground rivers, and from there into the ocean... the motes get into the springs, they get into the rain. Every last drop of water in the world is just about contaminated, and nothing can remove these motes. "You can't see them, you can't detect them in any way mundane or magical. When you drink them, you gradually forget... slowly, so slowly that you never notice it happening. But there's nothing really worth forgetting these days, it's already too late. Drink up as much as you like." There's no need for all of this, she knows that, right? The loss of just about all real historical accounts before the Godswar has more to do with the turmoil that happened and still continues to happen today; that can wipe the slate pretty clean all by itself without need for any mystical hanky-panky. Enough generations have passed that there're just about no people around now who were alive during that time; there's a better answer for this lapse in history than the Narevans secretly spiking all the water in the world. You're not saying that Nina's visions are necessarily wrong... but there's a layer of interpretation between whatever she received and what she's telling you now. Maybe something got lost in there? Either way, she should probably keep mum about this — [pc.swornGod nareva |while you think it's just the ale talking, given that you've personally been all chummy with the goddess and never heard her or her closest talk about such a thing, other Astrida might be much less amused by her spreading such talk |you don't think the Narevans are going to drag her away because of what she supposedly knows, but they might do so for spouting nonsense ]. It would be a pity if Nina weren't here one day; the bar wouldn't be the same without her drunken self. [party.has agnimitra |"I... I'm not completely sure about that, [pc.name]," Agni whispers when Nina is suitably distracted with her jug of ale. "I don't think I've ever found an explanation for why exactly I keep on forgetting most of my past." But that still doesn't match up with Nina's crackpot theory. First off, there are people who still remember the Godswar. Rare, but they're around. Secondly, Agni herself hasn't just forgotten details about the Godswar, she's forgotten just about everything save her previous families. Like you said, even if Nina's visions are correct, the visions still need to be interpreted and there's a lot of room for error there. "Hmm." Agni looks a less troubled at that, but it's plain that she still has doubts. She clearly wants to believe — having an explanation handed to her neatly packaged would be convenient, but it just can't be true. ] |"You ever wonder why, despite the amazing number of peoples that exist all over the world with all kinds of body shapes and physiologies, that a whole bunch are interfertile? I mean, we don't really think of it, but when it comes to peoples there're a whole lot of different ones, and each of them can get pregnant from the other and make half-whatevers. Sure, this wouldn't be odd in itself, but when you compare how common it is amongst people compared to animals... well, when you put a horse and a donkey together, you get a mule, which often is a dead end on its own. But that's not the case with people." Not to mention how it is with harpies and true breeders, or with goblins and their ability to take bits and pieces from other peoples. But that's still not really a reason to find it odd in and of itself, right? Like, you could turn her argument the other way and say that it's animals that're odd. "N-no, you don't get it." Gripped by a sudden urgency, Nina drains her current jug in several gulps, looks disappointed at its emptiness, and then sighs. "The real reason why so many disparate peoples can fuck and still produce viable, fertile kids is that we all used to be one people, you see. Or a handful at most, take your pick. Sexy progenitors from ancient times." And what's her source for this? "I saw it in a dream." Uh-huh. "It's because of the ley-lines, you see. They carry the lifeblood of the world, and where they cross, ley-crystals form — scabs, as it were. There's just so much life-force that it does things to people who unwittingly live close to one: most of the time they just die or turn into twisted messes, but maybe one in every ten thousand lucks out and gets something that isn't detrimental or lethal, but actually livable, if not good." So what she's saying is that all the races of Savarra were descended from one or a handful of progenitor peoples, and the ley-lines turned them into what they are today over generations? "Not just the ley-lines. There's a lot of interference and direction there — for example, during the Godswar. But mostly, yes. At heart, we're all a play on the same basics, which is why our bits still work with each other." And all of this was revealed to her in a dream vision. "Yes. One after I drank a pretty bad batch of honey mead." Yeah, that's definitely the drink. "Well, that's just like, your opinion." And so is hers. |There's something that you'd like to know: how did she wind up losing the eye? "You mean this one?" she says, pointing at her eyepatch. Yes. "To begin with, 'losing' implies that I ever had it to begin with. When I was still in the egg, I made a terrible deal with entities beyond this world to be left alone in exchange for my eye. Now, it's forever separate from me, doomed to haunt the darkest of nights, scaring livestock, souring milk, causing rains of blood, that sort of thing." Really? "Gods no, I was screwing with you; I wouldn't be slumming it in a bar drinking myself into a stupor if my eye was out on a rampage of mischief. But it's true that I simply never had one to begin with; there're plenty of tales about people losing part or all of their sight in exchange for mystical powers. Maybe I'm just one of them. Maybe it's just a coincidence." Her visions have never told her? "Nope. As much stuff as comes to me... this is one of the things that's never popped up in a vision before. If there's any deeper meaning to me being born blind in one eye, I sure don't know it." ]
rows.translation: [rand |你以前见过幽灵吗？或者那种被幽灵影响得很深的生物？ [var0 |其实，你确实做到了。而且说实话，那个所谓的“幽灵”看起来也并不太糟糕。 尼娜把头歪到了一边，以至于头几乎要碰到肩膀了，她眨了眨眼，然后耸了耸肩：“嗯，听起来挺合理的。但我的意思其实是大多数那些人啊，你我显然不属于那一类人。” 那么，他们又该如何看待呢？ |其实，你确实看到了。而且你永远都不想再看到第二遍了。 尼娜耸了耸肩，对于你声称看到了传说中的那种怪物，她完全不以为然。“也不能怪你……但你看到的真的就是它吗？” 她这话是什么意思呢？ |不，你还没有听说过。但每个人都知道关于它们的故事，而如果这些故事中哪怕有四分之一的内容是真实的，那你真希望自己永远都不会遇到这种事情。 “嗯，关于这些故事，你有没有想过为什么对‘幽灵’的描述会各不相同呢？有时候它被描述成一个没有形状的团块，有时候又被说成是一只巨大的昆虫，还有人认为它是一只能够吸收所有光线的黑色巨熊。” 你示意她继续说下去。 ] 你看，其实就是这样的。怨灵其实并没有具体的形态——它们只不过是一些无形的阴影，毫无形状，也极其恶心。这就是为什么它们如此迫切地想要进入像我们这样的世界，想要变得有形，想要真实的但问题在于：我们的大脑会将这些现象解读为那些暗影的怪物，因为仅仅看到从两个球体之间的虚空中出现的那些活生生的阴影，就已经足够令人毛骨悚然了。我们的恐惧心理会让我们胡乱想象出各种离奇的东西，而这些想象最终就被记录在了关于“幽灵”外貌的历史记载中。这就是为什么没有两件事是完全相同的。” 嗯…… “你不觉得大脑是一件很奇妙的东西吗？我当然知道，因为我也有一个，虽然它已经被‘彻底腌制’过了……干杯！” 她要么是说得太有道理了，要么就是疯了。 我懂的，对吧？有时候我会怀疑自己是不是在编造这一切，不得不承认，这种可能性确实是存在的。 |你知道……我看到的那些幻象，并不是所有的都能让我采取实际行动。大多数出现在我脑海中的信息，我甚至根本不明白它们到底意味着什么，更不用说能否根据这些知识去做些什么了。但那些真正有意义的幻象，从来都没有让我走错方向。 当然，这其实是在考验我对自己那疯狂想法的信任程度，但经验告诉我们：每次我坚持自己的愿景去行动，最终都能成功；而每次我违背或忽视它，一切都会陷入未知，变得无法预测，偏离了应有的方向。对于一只女妖来说，找出做事的最简单方法并不需要太长时间。” “这听起来……似乎有悖常理。但她毕竟是一只女妖啊！” “那又怎样？” “嗯……飞行啊。自由啊。就是这种东西。能够自己决定自己的命运，而不是让梦境中的幻象——无论是清醒时出现的，还是其他时候出现的——来左右自己的决定和未来。对于她来说，既然她是索拉创造的生物之一，这种能力是否有什么意义呢？ 你看，我是个务实的女人。当女神决定赐予我安全、一个温暖的地方睡觉，以及我想喝的所有酒时，她的那些理想才真正开始影响我该如何生活。但在那之前，那些曾经为我带来实际帮助的幻象，已经足够让我满足了——它们带来的好处，甚至比女神赐予我的还要多。" |所以，不久前我喝了太多铜莓啤酒——嗯，这种事情有时候也会发生。之后，我就开始往家走……” 家？ 尼娜眯着眼睛，有些困惑地看着你：“什么？我当然有家啊。如果她不住在露米的酒吧里，你根本不会注意到这一点。每次你见到她，她总是在这个地方喝得酩酊大醉。就连露米自己也说，她从来都不会离开这个地方。 所以你相信露米一整天都待在酒吧里，对吧？每次都是这样我进来吧，她正在那个柜台后面做调酒师的工作呢。” 嗯，露米并没有否认自己现在住在荒废驿堡这里。 “哼，总之，我当时正在走回家，突然地面隆了起来，砸到了我的头上！有时候地面真是会突然做出这种动作，跟它打交道的时候可得非常小心。我晕了过去，等醒来时，发现自己在一个看起来很奇怪的洞穴里。顺便说一下，我现在并不住在洞穴里……至少不再住了。 [pc.isDK |也许你说话时有些结巴，但你很确定自己确实让她告诉你一些事情。有趣的事。 |继续吧…… ] 现在我要讲到有趣的部分了。天啊，我当时真的迷路了，而且还非常口渴！幸好我带了一些应急用的麦酒，于是我把整罐酒都喝得一干二净。等我恢复意识的时候，已经躺在床上，一切都恢复正常了。那些发生的事情，我都完全忘记了。……现在她的说话变得支支吾吾了。她是什么意思，难道把发生的一切都忘了吗？她刚才不是已经告诉你们了吗，显然她还记得。除非这是她在承认自己把一切都编造出来了…… 尼娜的眼睛里仿佛突然亮起了什么光芒，她看着你的眼神，就像是在这一刻第一次见到你一样。“哦，嗨，最近怎么样？” 这个……算了，算了，别管了。 |想了解更多关于幽灵鱼的信息吗？那些生活在最深的海域和无轻型洞穴中的传奇生物？ [QUEST_WINTER_WOLF.stateRange 9 |当然。你只见过那个人一次，而且当时的情况并不适合进行交谈。 |可以说是，也可以说不是；每个人都知道那些篝火边的故事，但真正了解其中真相的人却很少。 ]那他们呢？她是不是在某种幻象中看到了他们？” “哦，甚至更好。我经常和他们中的几个人聊天呢。” ……真的，现在就在聊天。 “是啊。尤其是杰里。如果你真正了解他，就会发现他并不是个坏人，尤其是当你喝了一点酒之后。他有点像个哲学家，总喜欢谈论“回归中心”之类的概念。而我呢，只是个用来增添气氛的角色罢了。总之，你知道这次他们真正想要什么吗？最新那款能够穿越时空、实现梦想的游戏吗？ 他们在寻找一颗钻石，一颗巨大的、闪闪发光的钻石，它在暗影中发出的光芒甚至比点燃的蒸馏酒还要明亮。这种钻石独一无二，所以那些诱骗者想要把它放在他们位于‘道路之间’的小聚会场所里，仔细端详它，从而让自己觉得自己简直酷毙了、厉害极了。是啊，过去一个世纪左右他们一直在做这件事——这其实算是一种娱乐活动，而且并不会真正伤害到任何人。至少，不会伤害到他们认为“重要”的人，也就是那些拥有与他们同样强大的灵能的人。我们大多数人其实都不是这样。也许连我也不例外。 所以，先把她陈述中的最后那部分先放在一边……其实就只是一颗会发光的钻石而已？并不是什么莱水晶，也不是什么早在神战之前就存在的古老神器？只不过是一颗在暗影中会发光的钻石？从故事情节的角度来看，这未免太单薄了些吧。 妮娜耸了耸肩：“杰里喝了一整箱铜莓啤酒后就是这么告诉我的——他们想要那颗钻石，只是因为它看起来既漂亮又酷炫而已。要是再有其他原因的话，他们就不会这么做了。赌注如果真的涉及到感情，那就不再只是为了消磨时间而玩游戏了。那样就不好了，不仅对他们来说是这样，对我们来说也是。” 她只是喝了太多啤酒而已。 “嗯，那只是你的看法罢了。 Me, I'm just there to be exotic. Anyways, you know what they're really after this time? The latest game to pass the years dreamwalking?" Yes? "They're searching for a diamond, a big shiny diamond that glows in the dark brighter than distilled spirits set on fire. It's one of a kind, so the lurelings want to put it on a stand in their little conclave in the Ways Between and stare at it knowing that they've become completely and utterly cool and awesome. Yeah. That's what they've been doing for the last century or so, makes for a bit of sport without actually hurting anyone. Or at least, anyone they count as anyone, which is everyone who is as powerful a psion as they all are. Which most of us aren't. Maybe not even me." So, the last part of her statement aside... it's just a big glowing diamond? Not really a hunk of ley-crystal, or some kind of ancient artifact that predates the Godswar? Just a diamond that shines in the dark? That's kind of lame as far as a story goes. Nina shrugs. "That's what Gerry told me after downing a casket of brazenberry ale; they just want the diamond because it looks pretty and cool. Any more, and there'd be actual stakes involved — it'd stop being just a game to pass the time. That'd be bad, not just for them, but for you and me, too." She's just had one too many ales. "Yeah well, that's, like, your opinion." |"Crystals. Just... crystals. Every time there's any kind of mystical arcane mess around, you tend to find crystals. Like, you ever wonder why crystals seem to feature so prominently everywhere weird stuff turns up? It's like the two are connected, or something." [pc.isMage |Well, there's a perfectly reasonable explanation for that. Natural formations of ley-crystals tend to aggregate power, and all that power in one place does indeed inevitably produce mystical arcane messes, as she so eloquently puts it. |Crystals are what they are — isn't that why wizards go after them a lot of the time? Especially those ley-crystal things? ] "Yeah, but it still happens even when the crystals aren't ley-crystals." Nina shakes her head and has another swig of ale to calm her nerves. "It's just weird, you know? Like, every time you go really deep underground and need some light to see by, bam! There're crystals everywhere, and they all give off a convenient glow for you to find your way around with. That kinda thing. Well, you know what I think?" Yes? "See, there's some kind of primordial being deep inside the earth — half person, half rock, half whatever horrendous being that comes from beyond the ways —" That doesn't add up, or at least, it adds up to more than one. "That doesn't matter when it comes to creatures like that. Now, am I the one telling the story, or you?" Does it matter when her source is literally %"it came to me in a dream"? "Anyways. This primordial entity, it wants to do something, anything, because boredom. At the same time, it can't leave, because it needs all that heat and pressure to simply continue existing. That's where the crystals come in — they're there to primarily serve as its eyes and ears let it observe all the fun things that're going on where it's cool enough for other creatures to exist. "Anyways. It's vitally important that you don't touch, lick, kick, punch, feed, jump over or sing to weird cave crystals, as it can be disastrous for your mind; you don't want an ancient consciousness like that even so much as touching your head, let alone trying to get into it. Most crystals are inert and simply observe, but you really, really don't want to take that chance to begin with. Trust me on this. But wizards being the fools that they are, they carve up the crystals and take little bits to the surface to do whatever with. Really, wizards — truly no sense of right and wrong." All right, let's suppose for one moment that she's absolutely right about all of this. Just about every modern spellcaster in existence uses a crystal, if not a gem focus. Do those count, too? Is it a ploy by this... thing deep under the earth to have eyes and ears everywhere on the surface, for the sole sake of not being bored? "I mean, if you were such a thing, why wouldn't you?" Nina takes a heavy swig of her ale. "I'd be bored right out of my skull after a day, let alone thousands of years." |"You know, I hate dust. I'm really glad that Rumie keeps this bar spick and span, because I wouldn't be able to bear it otherwise." [pc.isDK |Given that she sits here all day, your only surprise is that she hasn't actually begun to gather a nice coating of it of her own. Nina shudders at the thought and gulps down several large swigs of brazenberry ale to calm her nerves. "Oh no no no no. Can't abide that. I lift this fat butt of mine at three in the afternoon every day so that Rumie can clean my spot. It's important to be clean and neat." |It's good that Rumie [wayfort.hasMaids |and the maids keep |keeps ] the Wayfort clean. It's your home, after all, and you wouldn't want it being all dusty. "Good, good. I like you already. Not that I didn't before, but anyone with a neat home is to be respected." Nina gulps down several large swigs of brazenberry ale to emphasize her point. ] That's quite a visceral reaction she had there — she really dislikes dust that much? "Of course I do! It gets in your feathers. It gets in your nose. And worst of all, it gets in your drink. Hate dust." She leans in conspiratorially and stage-whispers into your ear. "Ordinary dust's bad enough. But dark dust..." Oh, this is going to be good. Sure, you'll play along — what can she tell you about this so-called %"dark dust"? "Well, you clearly know about the Ways Between, which surrounds our world." Nina sets down her jug and mimes a ball with her hands. "But beyond that is where the wraiths came from — the horrible dark between the worlds. There aren't many things there, but what is plentiful — relatively speaking — is dark dust. The Ways keeps most of it from coming in, but some gets through when portals naturally open, or it filters into the world when we disturb that space with our dreams... nasty stuff. "You don't ever want to get close to any of it in any quantity, even someone psionically dull like you. Tiny specks will give you nightmares. More will give you hallucinations. Enough to smudge a finger is really, really bad; there probably won't be enough left of your psyche to fill a mental soup bowl. But not to worry, there isn't that much in one spot to cause more than bad dreams, not unless someone is crazy enough to start intentionally collecting the stuff. And if that's the case, you have bigger problems on hand than the complete shattering and dissolution of your mind." You've certainly never seen any of this mystical dust. Maybe she just has an allergy. |"Go ahead and drink the water," Nina mumbles. "It's too late anyways, has been for a couple generations now." What about the water? Why shouldn't you drink it, even if it's as she says and there's not much point now? "It's... it's the order Astrida," Nina mumbles. "Those at the top. [pc.swornGod nareva |I know that you recently joined with them and most are okay people, it's just those at the very top. You should know what you've gotten yourself into, if nothing else |I've never dared tell anyone because I know they come in and drag people away, but you... you're different ]. "You see, the black-scales gather up all the relics they can find of the old era, anything that might prove concretely what happened then, instead of folklore and hearsay. They put them on ships and transport them to a faraway island, where they have a museum in a deep grassy valley. Only a few pieces are ever on display, but beneath the mountains of that valley in an underground lake there's a seven-headed hydra with one amethyst eye; the black-scales revere it as a divine beast of the goddess." This is crazy, and very possibly blasphemy to boot. This is the ale talking, right? Nina ignores you and keeps going, her jug of ale completely forgotten. "The hydra... it devours secrets, you see. The black-scales feed it the relics they collect, and it spews out these tiny invisible magical motes that wind up in its pool. The pool flows out to the underground rivers, and from there into the ocean... the motes get into the springs, they get into the rain. Every last drop of water in the world is just about contaminated, and nothing can remove these motes. "You can't see them, you can't detect them in any way mundane or magical. When you drink them, you gradually forget... slowly, so slowly that you never notice it happening. But there's nothing really worth forgetting these days, it's already too late. Drink up as much as you like." There's no need for all of this, she knows that, right? The loss of just about all real historical accounts before the Godswar has more to do with the turmoil that happened and still continues to happen today; that can wipe the slate pretty clean all by itself without need for any mystical hanky-panky. Enough generations have passed that there're just about no people around now who were alive during that time; there's a better answer for this lapse in history than the Narevans secretly spiking all the water in the world. You're not saying that Nina's visions are necessarily wrong... but there's a layer of interpretation between whatever she received and what she's telling you now. Maybe something got lost in there? Either way, she should probably keep mum about this — [pc.swornGod nareva |while you think it's just the ale talking, given that you've personally been all chummy with the goddess and never heard her or her closest talk about such a thing, other Astrida might be much less amused by her spreading such talk |you don't think the Narevans are going to drag her away because of what she supposedly knows, but they might do so for spouting nonsense ]. It would be a pity if Nina weren't here one day; the bar wouldn't be the same without her drunken self. [party.has agnimitra |"I... I'm not completely sure about that, [pc.name]," Agni whispers when Nina is suitably distracted with her jug of ale. "I don't think I've ever found an explanation for why exactly I keep on forgetting most of my past." But that still doesn't match up with Nina's crackpot theory. First off, there are people who still remember the Godswar. Rare, but they're around. Secondly, Agni herself hasn't just forgotten details about the Godswar, she's forgotten just about everything save her previous families. Like you said, even if Nina's visions are correct, the visions still need to be interpreted and there's a lot of room for error there. "Hmm." Agni looks a less troubled at that, but it's plain that she still has doubts. She clearly wants to believe — having an explanation handed to her neatly packaged would be convenient, but it just can't be true. ] |"You ever wonder why, despite the amazing number of peoples that exist all over the world with all kinds of body shapes and physiologies, that a whole bunch are interfertile? I mean, we don't really think of it, but when it comes to peoples there're a whole lot of different ones, and each of them can get pregnant from the other and make half-whatevers. Sure, this wouldn't be odd in itself, but when you compare how common it is amongst people compared to animals... well, when you put a horse and a donkey together, you get a mule, which often is a dead end on its own. But that's not the case with people." Not to mention how it is with harpies and true breeders, or with goblins and their ability to take bits and pieces from other peoples. But that's still not really a reason to find it odd in and of itself, right? Like, you could turn her argument the other way and say that it's animals that're odd. "N-no, you don't get it." Gripped by a sudden urgency, Nina drains her current jug in several gulps, looks disappointed at its emptiness, and then sighs. "The real reason why so many disparate peoples can fuck and still produce viable, fertile kids is that we all used to be one people, you see. Or a handful at most, take your pick. Sexy progenitors from ancient times." And what's her source for this? "I saw it in a dream." Uh-huh. "It's because of the ley-lines, you see. They carry the lifeblood of the world, and where they cross, ley-crystals form — scabs, as it were. There's just so much life-force that it does things to people who unwittingly live close to one: most of the time they just die or turn into twisted messes, but maybe one in every ten thousand lucks out and gets something that isn't detrimental or lethal, but actually livable, if not good." So what she's saying is that all the races of Savarra were descended from one or a handful of progenitor peoples, and the ley-lines turned them into what they are today over generations? "Not just the ley-lines. There's a lot of interference and direction there — for example, during the Godswar. But mostly, yes. At heart, we're all a play on the same basics, which is why our bits still work with each other." And all of this was revealed to her in a dream vision. "Yes. One after I drank a pretty bad batch of honey mead." Yeah, that's definitely the drink. "Well, that's just like, your opinion." And so is hers. |There's something that you'd like to know: how did she wind up losing the eye? "You mean this one?" she says, pointing at her eyepatch. Yes. "To begin with, 'losing' implies that I ever had it to begin with. When I was still in the egg, I made a terrible deal with entities beyond this world to be left alone in exchange for my eye. Now, it's forever separate from me, doomed to haunt the darkest of nights, scaring livestock, souring milk, causing rains of blood, that sort of thing." Really? "Gods no, I was screwing with you; I wouldn't be slumming it in a bar drinking myself into a stupor if my eye was out on a rampage of mischief. But it's true that I simply never had one to begin with; there're plenty of tales about people losing part or all of their sight in exchange for mystical powers. Maybe I'm just one of them. Maybe it's just a coincidence." Her visions have never told her? "Nope. As much stuff as comes to me... this is one of the things that's never popped up in a vision before. If there's any deeper meaning to me being born blind in one eye, I sure don't know it." ]"

rows.original: She has visions and possesses all this cosmic knowledge, right? Why doesn't she tell you something interesting?
rows.translation: 她拥有预知能力，还掌握了这些宇宙间的知识，对吧？那她为什么不告诉你一些有趣的事情呢？
rows.raw: "She has visions and possesses all this cosmic knowledge, right? Why doesn't she tell you something interesting?"

rows.original:
"It's not easy on you, that's all I can say," Nina mumbles, peering into her jug with great intent, as if it holds the answers to the great mysteries of life. "Why do you think I drink so much?"

        You don't know about that. People are perfectly capable of being hopeless drunkards without some great and terrible sorrow behind it all.
        
        The harpy is silent for a moment, then sighs. "I... don't regret it, let's make that clear from the start. That kind of rage against the heavens and their mistress isn't going to solve anything. That being said, neither has it been easy — ever wonder what kids are like growing up with such powers? I'm just glad that I wasn't born a pale elf or something, that might've just made it even worse. People like the avanai, they know how to handle chicks who can set things on fire with their minds, but...eh. I got lucky, that's all. No great and terrible mishaps when I was still little. Usually, I just wound up answering my sisters before they'd even spoken, which wasn't so bad. Didn't stop them from kicking me out on my butt first chance behind Mother's back, though.
        
        "If you're lucky, you know someone more experienced who dreams in a similar way that you do, and he or she can guide you along that path without accidentally hurting other people; psions happen often enough amongst them birds that they have a whole system for handling such kids. For most of us, that doesn't happen and we've to figure it out for ourselves."
        
        Psions? Does she mean Dreamwalkers?
        
        "Dreamwalkers, psykers, lunatics, crazies... and all dream." Nina takes another swig of brazenberry ale. "That's the common term, yes, and a lot of us do call ourselves that. Dreamwalkers. I just like to have a bit of a mouthful at times."
        
        She makes it sound like some kind of great and terrible curse, but while practitioners of the arcane might draw an extra glance or two, it's not like they're actively persecuted or anything.
        
        "Didn't say we were. Most people can't even figure out we're different from wizards and their like."
        
        [pc.isMage
            |You can see why. Everything she's described about her powers so far hasn't fallen out of the reach of your average hedge wizard — a fireball? That's conjuration. Reading someone's mind, or messing with someone's thoughts and perceptions? That's illusion for you. [var0
                |Come to think of it, you even know a couple of arcane spells that mimic psions' reputed powers.
            ]
            
            A small smile creeps over Nina's face. "You're smart to have figured it out. But yes, there's nothing fancy about being able to pick something up with your mind when everyone and their mother knows how to cast mage hand or somesuch.
            |Can she explain? Given her description of her kind, you'd have imagined that the differences would be quite obvious.
            
            Nina laughs softly and shakes her head. "No, not really. Fireballs? That's one of the first things any hedge wizard does. Reading someone's mind, creating false perceptions and memories? An illusionist could do that. There's nothing fancy about being able to pick something up with your mind when everyone and their mother knows how to cast mage hand or somesuch — most people judge us by the end results, which is why for most the matter is simply academic.
        ]
        
        "I do prefer it this way, though. Outside of certain peoples — like the avanai — and monsters, we dreamwalkers are rare enough that people usually don't think to protect themselves from us unless specifically prompted otherwise. That, and being mistaken for hedge wizards helps us live reasonably normal lives."
        
        It might be a long shot, but can she teach you psionics? [pc.isDK
            |Since she's slumming in your bar with Rumie, she can consider it a one-off payment for her rent
            |You'd like to learn to open your mind, if it's possible to begin with
        ].
        
        "Not if you don't have any potential, and forgive me for being blunt, but you don't; you're as dull as a doornail in that regard. If you were a dreamwalker, you'd have known since you were very young since you'd have been causing all kinds of trouble for everyone around you, yourself included." Nina takes another swig of brazenberry ale to wet her lips. "[pc.willpowerRange 80
            |Sure, you have a pretty strong will, so you might've been a notable dreamwalker, but the gods clearly have other plans for you
            |Nothing to be ashamed of, you're just normal unlike me
        ]. Like I said, there're plenty of arcane spells and the like out there that'd let you do similar things to us, so if you're really intent on it that's your best shot. It won't ever be the genuine article, but it doesn't have to be.
        
        "Any more questions?"
        
        You do, but this will have to do for a down-and-dirty, and [pc.bg arcanist scholar acolyte
            |in order to properly sate your academic curiosity, it'd have to be a proper interview and you don't have time for that, nor have you come up with some proper avenues of inquiry
            |to be quite honest, you're not sure that even Nina herself has the answers to some of the questions you want to ask in the same way that fish can't explain how or why they swim despite being in water all day
        ].
        
        "Cool. You want to talk about something else?"
rows.translation:
这对你来说确实不容易，我只能这么说，”妮娜喃喃道，她专注地盯着自己的水壶，仿佛里面藏着生命中所有重大谜团的答案。“你为什么觉得我会喝这么多酒呢？”

“你并不了解内情。有些人之所以会成为无可救药的酒鬼，其实并不一定是因为有什么深重的悲痛在背后驱使他们如此。
        
        那只女妖沉默了一会儿，然后叹了口气说道：“我……并不后悔，从一开始我们就把这一点说清楚吧。那种对上天及其主宰者的愤怒根本解决不了任何问题。不过，这样的生活也确实并不容易——你有没有想过，拥有这样的力量，孩子们会如何成长呢？我只是庆幸自己不是生来就是那种苍白精灵之类的生物，否则情况可能会更糟。像阿瓦奈这样的人，他们知道该如何应对那些能用意念引发火灾的女孩子，但是……唉，我只是运气好而已。在我还小的时候，并没有发生过什么重大而可怕的事情。通常情况下，我总是在我的姐妹们开口之前就回答了她们的问题，这其实也没什么不好。不过，这并没有阻止她们在母亲不在场的时候，一有机会就把我赶出去。
        
        如果你运气好的话，会遇到某个经验更丰富的人，他的思维方式与你相似，他可以引导你走上这条道路，同时避免伤害到他人；在那些拥有灵能的群体中，这种情况其实相当常见，因此他们有一套完善的体系来帮助这类人。但对我们大多数人来说，这样的机会并不存在，所以我们必须自己摸索出前进的道路。
        
        灵能者？她指的是梦行者吗？”

“梦行者、灵能者、疯子……其实他们都在做梦。”妮娜又喝了一口铜莓啤酒，“没错，这就是大家常用的称呼，我们很多人也确实这样称呼自己。梦行者……我只是有时候喜欢用这种说法来表达而已。
        
        她把这种能力描述得好像是一种既伟大又可怕的诅咒，但实际上，那些研究神秘学问的人或许会多看她几眼，但并不会因此而受到迫害或什么。

“我也没说过我们会受到迫害啊。大多数人都根本搞不明白我们和巫师们有什么不同。
        
        [pc.isMage
            |你现在应该明白为什么了。她所描述的那些能力，对于一个普通的护林巫师来说，根本都不是什么难以实现的事情——释放火球？那不过是简单的咒术而已。读取别人的思想，或者干扰别人的感知与认知？对你来说，这些也不过是幻术罢了。 [var0
                |仔细想来，你甚至掌握了几种能够模仿灵能者据说拥有的能力的神秘法术。
            ]
            
            尼娜的脸上浮现出一丝微笑：“你能想出来，真是聪明。不过，其实用意念来拾取物品这种能力并没有什么特别的之处——毕竟现在每个人都会使用‘法师之手’之类的法术啊。
            |她能解释一下吗？根据她对自己这一群体的描述，你可能会认为这些差异应该非常明显才对。

尼娜轻声笑了笑，然后摇了摇头：“不，并不是这样的。火球术？这是任何一位护林巫师都会最先学会的法术之一。读懂别人的心思，制造虚假的感知与记忆？这正是魔术师所能做到的。当几乎每个人都能使用“法师之手”之类的法术时，那种仅凭意念就能获取信息的能力其实并没有什么特别的之处——大多数人都是根据最终的结果来评价我们的，因此对于他们来说，这种能力往往只是一种理论上的存在罢了。
        ]
        
        不过，我确实更喜欢这样。除了某些人——比如阿瓦奈族——以及怪物之外，我们这些梦游者本来就非常稀少，所以人们通常不会想到要保护自己免受我们的伤害，除非有特别的提示。再加上我们经常被误认为是护林巫师，这些因素都让我们能够过上相对正常的生活。”

虽然希望渺茫，但她能教你灵能技巧吗？ [pc.isDK
            |既然她和露米一起在你的酒吧里混时间，那她可以把这笔钱当作一次性的房租支付吧。
            |如果你愿意的话，其实是可以试着学会敞开心扉的。
        ]如果你没有任何潜力，那我只能直言不讳了——你确实没有；在这方面，你简直毫无天赋。如果你是个‘梦行者’，你早就应该意识到了。因为从你很小的时候起，你就会给周围的人，包括你自己，带来各种各样的麻烦。”妮娜又喝了一口铜莓啤酒，润了润嘴唇，继续说道。[pc.willpowerRange 80
            |确实，你的意志力相当坚强，因此你本有可能成为一名杰出的梦行者，但诸神显然为你安排了其他的命运。
            |没什么好羞愧的，你只是很普通，而我不像你。
        ]正如我所说，外面有很多类似的神秘法术之类的东西，它们也能让你做出和我们一样的事情来。所以，如果你真的下定决心要这么做的话，这应该是你最好的选择。虽然这永远不会是真正原汁原味的东西，但也不一定非得如此。

“还有其他问题吗？”

如果你还有疑问的话，不过对于这个问题的简单回答来说，这就已经足够了。 [pc.bg arcanist scholar acolyte
            |要想真正满足你的学术求知欲，就必须进行一次正规的访谈，但你现在没有时间这么做，也没有想出任何合适的探究途径。
            |说实话，你甚至不确定妮娜自己是否能够回答你那些想要提出的问题——就如同鱼儿虽然整天都在水中，却无法解释自己为何会游泳、如何游泳一样。
        ]不错。你想聊点别的吗？
