rows.original: When you enter Matiha’s office [atWF |at the top of the summoned tower |within the dungeons of the Wayfort ], you find the witch you were looking for – sitting in her chair, leaning far enough backward that her chair is standing only on its rear two legs, with her feet kicked up and resting on her desk. Her oversized hat sits on her chest, covering (most of) her boobs and hiding her face. It’s... an atypical position for her to be in. It’s almost like she’s asleep in what is one of the most unsophisticated positions she could think of. You gently knock your knuckles against the wood of her door to get her attention. She moves her left hand to the brim of her hat and lifts it off her eyes; when she sees you, she lets out a sigh through her nose and lowers her hat back down. She doesn’t say anything; she doesn’t invite you in or shoo you away; aside from lifting her hat, she doesn’t acknowledge you at all. [matiha.hasKids |When you enter Matiha’s office, the woman herself is in a modestly chipper mood: she’s up and about, a wand in her right hand and an open book in her left, humming a rhythmless ditty to herself as she waggles it in front of a small wooden doll that’s sitting on her desk, surrounded by loose thread. She uses the tip of her wand to turn the page, and then, after reading the next few sentences, she mouths something to herself and taps the end of the wand against the doll’s head, and suddenly, the thread pooled around it picks up and starts to twist and spin around it, dressing it up in their colors. It winds up [matiha.numKids 1 2 3 |not really looking like anything, but she doesn’t seem too bothered by it. In fact, she seems to like it |coming out much better than her first attempt: the threads are still a bit crooked in some places, but the colors at least identifiably make up a person this time |looking about as well as she could hope to make it without learning to sew the threads on herself: the doll is visibly a person, and, going by how the colors are set up, it almost looks like herself ]. "Ah," she says in delight, setting down her wand to pick up the doll, "lovely." You knock on her door to get her attention; rather than jump from being startled, she turns with all the finesse and poise of a woman that is perfectly comfortable in her abode, knowing where everything is at all times. "[pc.name]," she says jovially, stepping into your space and throwing her arms around your shoulders, pulling you in to kiss both your cheeks before holding you there. Her breasts press and bunch up against your [pc.chest], and you can feel her nipples poking against your [pc.skinFurScales]. She’s clearly in a very good mood; you ask [matiha.numKids 1 2 |what the occasion is. "Well, sweetheart, I decided that I enjoyed having a child with you so much that I thought it’d be worth the time and effort to do it all again," she says with a laugh. "'Once more with feeling,’ as they say!" [pc.isBimbo |... Is she asking for you to knock her up again? Or is she saying that she’s been knocked up again? "The second," she says with a conniving little giggle, her mouth crooking wryly, "although the first may be in the cards down the line once more." |This is quite the departure from how she was when you two had your first child. She was acting like she’d lost all her money from gambling or something. "That’s," she starts, then stops, crinkling her nose as she thinks about what you just said. "That’s not too far from the truth, honestly. I acted that way because I wasn’t certain how I was going to support a child at all, with my current living conditions, and that it was going to upend my lifestyle and my studies. And while we’re still far from ideal, this is still the best that I could hope for – and I’ve decided that our arrangement has room for one more." ] |if it’d be right to assume that she’s... eating for two once more. "Indeed it is," she says, rubbing her nose against yours and smiling through her words. "I’ve never had a particular penchant for white magic – or necromancy, I suppose – but I’ve come to appreciate the true magic that comes with bringing new life into this world. That nursery in Hawkethorne is truly a gift! With [atWF |that yokel village so close by |the tower’s ability to be anywhere in Savarra with just a thought ], my little underlings are as close as can be; we can spend as much time with them as we like; and I still have access to all of my tools here without worrying about one of my little jewels getting into a book or a potion that they shouldn’t be." Well... as long as she’s happy. ] "Now, then," she says, disengaging from you and twisting away. With a twist of her wand, the doll falls onto its back and tumbles over itself, one side over the other, until it falls off the desk – and straight into a woven handbasket she had left at the desk’s foot, already filled with other child-friendly toys and baubles she had either made or collected in the meantime. "Once more, [pc.name], as the [pc.mf |father |mother ] to our child, you have some responsibilities of your own to manage. It’ll be in due time when your [silly |[rand |beby |bappy |bby |bab |babu |beb ] |baby ]’s mother has in need of you and your...." Matiha pauses – and, with her back still turned to you, her dress starts to ride high on her already-overexposed thighs, exposing more and more leg to you the higher it climbs. She’s pulling on the front of her dress so that it exposes more skin, right up until it crawls over the swell of her ass cheeks, with just a thin line of leftover fabric hiding the sheer cleavage of her butt. "... attention." Well, that’s certainly one way to get her message across. |It’s clear that she’s in something of a mood, but... you enter her chamber and ask her if she’s alright, or if she needs anything. Maybe she’s just got something of a stomach bug, after all. "I’m pregnant, [pc.name]," she says, her voice being muffled from underneath the fabric of her hat. [pc.isBimbo |Oh, wow, congratulations! Who’s the lucky daddy? Or mommy, as the case might be. "Its yours," she says with some exasperation that you’d ask something so obvious. |... Oh. Knowing her and her... disposition, you can’t imagine that it’s anyone other than yours. Matiha doesn’t offer you anything further; it’d probably upset her mood if you asked. ] The news stuns you for a moment, but you think to pull one of the guest chairs up from the corner of the room and bring it beside her. She remains totally still, calm as if she were dead; she doesn’t react to the sound of you moving her furniture or you taking a seat next to her. Rather than ask a question you already know the answer to, you ask her how far along the baby is. "About a month, I’d estimate," she answers, "given all the recent cramps and sicknesses." Then, unprompted, she removes her hat from her face, sliding it down her torso so that its wide rim covers everything from her neck to as far down as her knees with the hat’s enormous brim. "It’s funny, in a strange way. I’m an accomplished witch and scholar; I once solved the riddles of the Jotun and one of their abstract mana absorption spells to create an artifact of near-limitless potential – and the idea of raising a child has me like...." She looks down across her body, most of it obscured by her hat. "This." Does she want the kid? "If you had asked me ten, or perhaps even five years ago, the answer would have been ye – well, it would have been 'yes, depending on who the father was,’" she replies. "Back then, when I was so focused on that rune stone, a child was a long-term investment. It meant a protégé. It meant someone to carry on my work. If the father had the right aptitude, it meant someone with a greater grasp on magic than either of their parents." You laugh. Someone with a greater grasp on magic than herself? "As foolhardy as it sounds," she answers, turning to face you for the first time since you entered the office. A warm smile that meets her eyes spreads across her face, and her eyes meet yours for a long moment before she continues. "But, ever since the, ah, events between us, [pc.name], my priorities have... changed." She turns her head away from you, her eyes roving over the room she’s in. "Ever since you had destroyed the rune stone, the focus of my studies had been... eclectic. Unfocused. I had spent most of my life in pursuit of one thing especially, and now that it’s gone, I had the clarity to do whatever I wanted, but without the focus to do any one thing for longer than a few days. All the resources I could possibly want are within arm’s reach, and I’m caught between learning a new instrument; creating new undergarments to support a woman’s bust; and other less, ah, forward-facing pursuits, to name just a few." Her left hand goes to her stomach, patting down her enormous hat so that she can feel her abdomen through it. "And now I’m adding being a parent on top of all of that." Well, at least now she’ll have something to really capture her attention. A baby ought to be a good thing to focus on. "Well, that’s just it!" she says, jerking towards you as the words leave her mouth. "The rune stone had paused my aging, [pc.name]; I’m many, many years older than I ought to be. The idea of parenthood had never even crossed my mind. As I said, I’m an accomplished witch and scholar, but I haven’t the faintest idea on how to be a go – a... a good, proper mother." [var0 |Take it from you: it’s easier than she might think, especially with all of the resources she has on hand. This may be her first time, but it isn’t yours: you can teach her everything she needs to know about being a mom. Matiha looks at you like you had just given her hope when she thought she lost it all. "Really?" she asks. First thing’s first: stress is bad for the baby. And it’s going to be bad for the baby’s milk later, as well. |The fact that she – Matiha, a woman once so powerful that one of the very Seven sent two of her best magehunters to detain her, and they failed – is so concerned with wanting to be a good mom already gives her a strong edge on a lot of the other mothers in Savarra. It’s pretty easy to tell the good ones from the bad ones, and she’s already got the makings of a good one. Again, she smiles at you, her lips turning thin and spreading just enough that you can see the gleam of her white teeth. "Thank you," she says, reaching her hand towards you and holding on to yours. Now, that said: she said earlier that she was suffering from cramps and sickness, and lounging in her office all day like this isn’t going to be doing either of those any favors. ] You ask her what it is she likes to do to destress: she’ll learn soon that having a child inside of her isn’t going to be enough to stop her from living her life as she normally does. "Truth be told, [pc.name], the things I like to do to 'destress’ are things I’ve been doing since [atWF |you gave me the chance to stay in your fort |the rune stone had been destroyed ]," she answers. "So... I’d like to do more of that, I suppose." ... Everything? "I know to expect my hormones to get out of hand during the worst of it," she says as her hand squeezes yours – and she pulls you in closer to her, her face suddenly clouding over with her eyes drilling holes into yours. "So, yes. Everything." You’ll, ah, just have to make sure that you’re ready, then. ]
rows.translation: 当你走进玛蒂哈的办公室时[atWF |在召唤出的塔顶 |在荒废驿堡的地牢之中 ]你找到了正在寻找的那位女巫——她坐在椅子上，向后仰得如此厉害，以至于椅子只剩下后两条腿支撑着，她的双脚被抬起来，搭在桌子上。她那顶 oversized 的帽子盖在她的胸口，几乎遮住了她的整个胸部，同时也遮住了她的脸。她现在的姿势……实在有些不寻常。她几乎是以一种最简单的姿势躺着，就像在睡觉一样。 你轻轻用指关节敲了敲她的门，想引起她的注意。她将左手移到帽子的边缘，把帽子从眼前拿开；看到你的那一刻，她通过鼻子轻轻叹了口气，然后又把帽子戴了回去。她没有说任何话，既没有邀请你进去，也没有把你赶走；除了摘下帽子那一瞬间，她完全没有表现出任何对你的注意或反应。 [matiha.hasKids |当你走进玛蒂哈的办公室时，她本人显得心情相当愉快：她活蹦乱跳地走来走去，右手拿着一根魔杖，左手拿着一本打开的书，一边自顾自地哼着没有节奏的小曲子，一边把魔杖在桌子上那个被松线围着的木制小玩偶面前晃来晃去。她用魔杖的尖端翻动页面，读完接下来的几句话后，她自言自语了几句，然后将魔杖的末端轻触玩偶的头部，瞬间，缠绕在玩偶身上的线开始旋转、缠绕起来，为它披上了他们选择的颜色。 最终结果是[matiha.numKids 1 2 3 |看起来其实没什么特别的，但她似乎并不在意这一点。事实上，她似乎还挺喜欢它的。 |这次的结果比她第一次尝试要好多了：虽然有些地方的线仍然有点歪，但至少这次的颜色搭配确实能让人分辨出那是一个人。 |她的打扮已经尽她所能做到了最好，甚至没有必要自己学习缝线：这个玩偶看起来确实像一个人，而且从色彩的搭配来看，它甚至有点像她自己。 ]啊，”她高兴地说道，放下魔杖去捡起那个玩偶，“太可爱了。” 你敲她的门以引起她的注意；她并没有因为受到惊吓而慌忙反应，而是以一个对自己的住所了如指掌、始终举止得体的女人的优雅与从容转过身来。[pc.name]，哈哈，”她开心地说道，走进你的怀里，双臂环绕着你的肩膀，将你拉近自己，在亲吻你的双颊之后，还紧紧地抱着你。 她的胸部紧贴着你的身体[pc.chest]你能感觉到她的乳头轻轻触碰到你的[pc.skinFurScales]她显然正处于某种状态中。非常心情好，有什么要求都满足你。 [matiha.numKids 1 2 |嗯，亲爱的，我发现自己真的很享受和你一起生孩子这个过程。所以尽管我觉得再花时间和精力去做这些事情也是值得的，”她笑着说，“就像人们说的那样，‘再一次，但要充满感情’！ [pc.isBimbo |…她是想让你再让她怀孕一次吗？还是她在表达别的什么意思？已经又怀孕了？ “第二次，”她带着一丝狡黠的笑声说道，嘴角微微上扬，“不过第一次也有可能在未来再次发生。 |这与你们第一个孩子出生时她的表现截然不同。那时她表现得好像在赌博中输掉了所有钱一样。 “那是……”她开始说道，然后又停住了，皱着鼻子思考着你刚才说的话。说实话，这跟事实相差不远。我当时那样做，是因为考虑到以我当时的生活条件，我根本不确定该如何抚养一个孩子，而且这肯定会彻底改变我的生活方式和学业。虽然我们距离理想状态还有一定距离，但这也已经是我所能期望的最好结果了。而且我决定，我们的合作模式还有空间再容纳一个人。 ] |如果可以认为她现在又是在“为两个人进食”的话，那应该没什么不妥吧。 “确实如此，”她说道，一边用鼻子蹭着你的鼻子，一边微笑着说道，“我其实从来对白魔法或死灵法术并没有特别的兴趣，但后来我开始逐渐欣赏它们了true这种魔法，正是为这个世界带来新生命而存在的。鹰棘镇的那间婴儿房，真的是一份珍贵的礼物！ [atWF |那个离这儿这么近的乡下村庄 |只需心念一动，这座塔就能出现在萨瓦拉的任何地方。 ]我的那些小助手们就在我身边，我们可以随时与它们相处；而且我仍然可以使用这里的所有工具，完全不用担心我的那些小宝贝们会不小心把什么东西弄进不该去的书里或药水里。 嗯……只要她开心就好。 ] 那么，”她说着，从你身边拉开距离，转身走开。她轻轻一挥魔杖，那个玩偶便翻了个身，一侧翻过另一侧，最终从桌子上掉下来——正好落进了她放在桌子脚下的编织篮子里。篮子里已经装满了其他适合儿童玩耍的玩具和小装饰品，这些都是她自己制作的，或者是这段时间收集来的。“再来一次吧[pc.name]，作为我们孩子的[pc.mf |父亲 |母亲 ]，你也有一些自己的责任需要去履行。等到适当的时候，你就会明白这一点的。 [silly |[rand |宝贝 |bappy |宝贝 |bab |巴布 |beb ] |宝宝 ]她的母亲现在需要你和你的……” 玛蒂哈停顿了一下——她依然背对着你，但她的裙子逐渐向上滑落，露出她那已经相当暴露的大腿，越往上滑，露出的腿部皮肤就越多。她不断地拉扯着裙子的前部，让更多的皮肤暴露出来，直到裙子滑过她圆润的臀部，只有一层薄薄的布料遮挡着她那近乎裸露的臀部曲线。注意。嗯，这确实是传达她意思的一种方法。 rows.raw: ' When you enter Matiha’s office [atWF |at the top of the summoned tower |within the dungeons of the Wayfort ], you find the witch you were looking for – sitting in her chair, leaning far enough backward that her chair is standing only on its rear two legs, with her feet kicked up and resting on her desk. Her oversized hat sits on her chest, covering (most of) her boobs and hiding her face. It’s... an atypical position for her to be in. It’s almost like she’s asleep in what is one of the most unsophisticated positions she could think of. You gently knock your knuckles against the wood of her door to get her attention. She moves her left hand to the brim of her hat and lifts it off her eyes; when she sees you, she lets out a sigh through her nose and lowers her hat back down. She doesn’t say anything; she doesn’t invite you in or shoo you away; aside from lifting her hat, she doesn’t acknowledge you at all. [matiha.hasKids |When you enter Matiha’s office, the woman herself is in a modestly chipper mood: she’s up and about, a wand in her right hand and an open book in her left, humming a rhythmless ditty to herself as she waggles it in front of a small wooden doll that’s sitting on her desk, surrounded by loose thread. She uses the tip of her wand to turn the page, and then, after reading the next few sentences, she mouths something to herself and taps the end of the wand against the doll’s head, and suddenly, the thread pooled around it picks up and starts to twist and spin around it, dressing it up in their colors. It winds up [matiha.numKids 1 2 3 |not really looking like anything, but she doesn’t seem too bothered by it. In fact, she seems to like it |coming out much better than her first attempt: the threads are still a bit crooked in some places, but the colors at least identifiably make up a person this time |looking about as well as she could hope to make it without learning to sew the threads on herself: the doll is visibly a person, and, going by how the colors are set up, it almost looks like herself ]. "Ah," she says in delight, setting down her wand to pick up the doll, "lovely." You knock on her door to get her attention; rather than jump from being startled, she turns with all the finesse and poise of a woman that is perfectly comfortable in her abode, knowing where everything is at all times. "[pc.name]," she says jovially, stepping into your space and throwing her arms around your shoulders, pulling you in to kiss both your cheeks before holding you there. Her breasts press and bunch up against your [pc.chest], and you can feel her nipples poking against your [pc.skinFurScales]. She’s clearly in a very good mood; you ask [matiha.numKids 1 2 |what the occasion is. "Well, sweetheart, I decided that I enjoyed having a child with you so much that I thought it’d be worth the time and effort to do it all again," she says with a laugh. "'Once more with feeling,’ as they say!" [pc.isBimbo |... Is she asking for you to knock her up again? Or is she saying that she’s been knocked up again? "The second," she says with a conniving little giggle, her mouth crooking wryly, "although the first may be in the cards down the line once more." |This is quite the departure from how she was when you two had your first child. She was acting like she’d lost all her money from gambling or something. "That’s," she starts, then stops, crinkling her nose as she thinks about what you just said. "That’s not too far from the truth, honestly. I acted that way because I wasn’t certain how I was going to support a child at all, with my current living conditions, and that it was going to upend my lifestyle and my studies. And while we’re still far from ideal, this is still the best that I could hope for – and I’ve decided that our arrangement has room for one more." ] |if it’d be right to assume that she’s... eating for two once more. "Indeed it is," she says, rubbing her nose against yours and smiling through her words. "I’ve never had a particular penchant for white magic – or necromancy, I suppose – but I’ve come to appreciate the true magic that comes with bringing new life into this world. That nursery in Hawkethorne is truly a gift! With [atWF |that yokel village so close by |the tower’s ability to be anywhere in Savarra with just a thought ], my little underlings are as close as can be; we can spend as much time with them as we like; and I still have access to all of my tools here without worrying about one of my little jewels getting into a book or a potion that they shouldn’t be." Well... as long as she’s happy. ] "Now, then," she says, disengaging from you and twisting away. With a twist of her wand, the doll falls onto its back and tumbles over itself, one side over the other, until it falls off the desk – and straight into a woven handbasket she had left at the desk’s foot, already filled with other child-friendly toys and baubles she had either made or collected in the meantime. "Once more, [pc.name], as the [pc.mf |father |mother ] to our child, you have some responsibilities of your own to manage. It’ll be in due time when your [silly |[rand |beby |bappy |bby |bab |babu |beb ] |baby ]’s mother has in need of you and your...." Matiha pauses – and, with her back still turned to you, her dress starts to ride high on her already-overexposed thighs, exposing more and more leg to you the higher it climbs. She’s pulling on the front of her dress so that it exposes more skin, right up until it crawls over the swell of her ass cheeks, with just a thin line of leftover fabric hiding the sheer cleavage of her butt. "... attention." Well, that’s certainly one way to get her message across. |It’s clear that she’s in something of a mood, but... you enter her chamber and ask her if she’s alright, or if she needs anything. Maybe she’s just got something of a stomach bug, after all. "I’m pregnant, [pc.name]," she says, her voice being muffled from underneath the fabric of her hat. [pc.isBimbo |Oh, wow, congratulations! Who’s the lucky daddy? Or mommy, as the case might be. "Its yours," she says with some exasperation that you’d ask something so obvious. |... Oh. Knowing her and her... disposition, you can’t imagine that it’s anyone other than yours. Matiha doesn’t offer you anything further; it’d probably upset her mood if you asked. ] The news stuns you for a moment, but you think to pull one of the guest chairs up from the corner of the room and bring it beside her. She remains totally still, calm as if she were dead; she doesn’t react to the sound of you moving her furniture or you taking a seat next to her. Rather than ask a question you already know the answer to, you ask her how far along the baby is. "About a month, I’d estimate," she answers, "given all the recent cramps and sicknesses." Then, unprompted, she removes her hat from her face, sliding it down her torso so that its wide rim covers everything from her neck to as far down as her knees with the hat’s enormous brim. "It’s funny, in a strange way. I’m an accomplished witch and scholar; I once solved the riddles of the Jotun and one of their abstract mana absorption spells to create an artifact of near-limitless potential – and the idea of raising a child has me like...." She looks down across her body, most of it obscured by her hat. "This." Does she want the kid? "If you had asked me ten, or perhaps even five years ago, the answer would have been ye – well, it would have been 'yes, depending on who the father was,’" she replies. "Back then, when I was so focused on that rune stone, a child was a long-term investment. It meant a protégé. It meant someone to carry on my work. If the father had the right aptitude, it meant someone with a greater grasp on magic than either of their parents." You laugh. Someone with a greater grasp on magic than herself? "As foolhardy as it sounds," she answers, turning to face you for the first time since you entered the office. A warm smile that meets her eyes spreads across her face, and her eyes meet yours for a long moment before she continues. "But, ever since the, ah, events between us, [pc.name], my priorities have... changed." She turns her head away from you, her eyes roving over the room she’s in. "Ever since you had destroyed the rune stone, the focus of my studies had been... eclectic. Unfocused. I had spent most of my life in pursuit of one thing especially, and now that it’s gone, I had the clarity to do whatever I wanted, but without the focus to do any one thing for longer than a few days. All the resources I could possibly want are within arm’s reach, and I’m caught between learning a new instrument; creating new undergarments to support a woman’s bust; and other less, ah, forward-facing pursuits, to name just a few." Her left hand goes to her stomach, patting down her enormous hat so that she can feel her abdomen through it. "And now I’m adding being a parent on top of all of that." Well, at least now she’ll have something to really capture her attention. A baby ought to be a good thing to focus on. "Well, that’s just it!" she says, jerking towards you as the words leave her mouth. "The rune stone had paused my aging, [pc.name]; I’m many, many years older than I ought to be. The idea of parenthood had never even crossed my mind. As I said, I’m an accomplished witch and scholar, but I haven’t the faintest idea on how to be a go – a... a good, proper mother." [var0 |Take it from you: it’s easier than she might think, especially with all of the resources she has on hand. This may be her first time, but it isn’t yours: you can teach her everything she needs to know about being a mom. Matiha looks at you like you had just given her hope when she thought she lost it all. "Really?" she asks. First thing’s first: stress is bad for the baby. And it’s going to be bad for the baby’s milk later, as well. |The fact that she – Matiha, a woman once so powerful that one of the very Seven sent two of her best magehunters to detain her, and they failed – is so concerned with wanting to be a good mom already gives her a strong edge on a lot of the other mothers in Savarra. It’s pretty easy to tell the good ones from the bad ones, and she’s already got the makings of a good one. Again, she smiles at you, her lips turning thin and spreading just enough that you can see the gleam of her white teeth. "Thank you," she says, reaching her hand towards you and holding on to yours. Now, that said: she said earlier that she was suffering from cramps and sickness, and lounging in her office all day like this isn’t going to be doing either of those any favors. ] You ask her what it is she likes to do to destress: she’ll learn soon that having a child inside of her isn’t going to be enough to stop her from living her life as she normally does. "Truth be told, [pc.name], the things I like to do to 'destress’ are things I’ve been doing since [atWF |you gave me the chance to stay in your fort |the rune stone had been destroyed ]," she answers. "So... I’d like to do more of that, I suppose." ... Everything? "I know to expect my hormones to get out of hand during the worst of it," she says as her hand squeezes yours – and she pulls you in closer to her, her face suddenly clouding over with her eyes drilling holes into yours. "So, yes. Everything." You’ll, ah, just have to make sure that you’re ready, then. ]'

rows.original: [rand |You push open the door to Matiha’s office, and, as you expected, there she is: standing sideways in front of a body-height mirror, her hat on the desk, checking out her own form by stretching her legs and flexing her glutes, watching how her robe rides on her skin. She’s already used to exposing quite a lot of thigh, but with her pregnancy, her robe pulls along her skin, showing off more of her body than even she’s used to – and from the look on her face, you can tell that she’s not especially thrilled with it. You knock on the door’s frame, but she doesn’t turn her head to acknowledge you. "[pc.name]," she says, the eyes in her reflection turning in your direction. "Am I still attractive?" [pc.dcb |She has tits for days and her skin is as smooth as velvet. She’s not getting uglier, that’s for damn certain. |At first, the question hits you like a dart to a dartboard, but the answer comes pretty quickly: frankly, you’ve always found her attractive[pc.corruptionRange 0 50 74 |, even when she was, well, evil | (although you kinda thought she was better when she was evil) ], and a baby bump isn’t going to take away from her other features. If anything, it makes her hotter. |Yep! ] Matiha’s lips curl slightly at your word[pc.isBimbo | |s ], but it’s clear that she isn’t totally convinced. "Of course you would say that. You’re the one that did this to me." Her left hand goes up her exposed thigh, her fingers raking gently across her skin; no matter how she looks at herself, something is just off, and it’s not the obvious. "You’re not allowed to say anything different." ... It’s a bit of a risk to say, but, you always took Matiha to be the studious, bookish type that cared more about results than she did about her own personal looks. That seems sort of vain for someone like her. "I am a witch, and my focus is on my work. Those are both true. But I’m also a woman, [pc.name]," she pouts, turning her head towards you with her brow furrowed. "If it were of no concern to me, I wouldn’t spend every morning putting my makeup on, or I wouldn’t bother with my earrings. My body is as important to me as my notes." And she thinks that her pregnancy is putting that at risk? In response, Matiha sighs sadly, turning back to the mirror and lifting her arms over her head, stretching her torso to get a better look at her stomach. "It’s different," she admits. "My image was something I had curated. And I suppose a baby is, too, but it’s... it’s frustrating that I can’t have both, I suppose." Could her magic help her with that somehow? "Illusion magic, maybe. But I can’t, for example, pull the baby out and incubate it somewhere." Her arms flop down to her sides, clapping against the taut robe and her exposed legs. She snorts through her nose as she gives up. "It’s simply a matter I’ll have to life with. [matiha.hasKids |I count my blessings that I don’t seem to be accruing any stretch marks from these repeated pregnancies. |I can only hope that this doesn’t give me stretch marks... although, I suppose a touch of illusion magic wouldn’t be out-of-place for those. ]" You step up behind her and wrap your hands around her from behind, your hands coming down gently on her round stomach. You give her a quick kiss on the cheek, just behind her jaw and beneath her ear; you stare into the reflection of her eyes and tell her that you meant what you said. If she can’t believe herself that she’s still attractive, then maybe she can believe you. Matiha’s lips curl wryly, her palms going to the back of your hands and her fingers interlocking with yours. "I know you’re only saying that because it’s what I want to hear," she says. That’s not true at all! "Then I’ll just have to hold you to that later." Her fingers squeeze on your hands, and you see a little glint of light reflecting off her teeth as she smiles at you – you’ll have to put your money where your mouth is when she’s in the mood later[rand | |. Almost as if on cue, you feel Matiha’s stomach lurch underneath your hands, causing her whole body to jump in surprise. The baby just kicked! She looks at you in the mirror’s reflection, and her cheeks quickly redden with surprise before she starts giggling. "It’s not all bad," she admits as she leans against you ]. |You push open the door to Matiha’s office, and, as you expected, there she is: standing beside the desk, leaning her rump against its edge, with her nose buried deep into the spine of a book and surrounded by literal piles of others stacked as high as her thigh, just as you usually find her. Except... from the color of the book’s bindings, it seems like she’s taken to reading something a bit... below her level. You can see pictures of animals; you see larger, more exaggerated letters and fonts; you see bright, pastel colors sewn into the fabric of the book. She’s reading a children’s book, and each of the books in the thigh-high piles surrounding her are all children’s books, too, with titles ranging from What Else Is A For? to When The Clock Strikes Twelve, It’s Moo Time. You aren’t exactly up to date with modern children’s books and their trends, but even you recognize Good Morning, Sun in there, too. You jokingly ask her if she’s only in the mood for some light reading this time. "We have a baby on the way, [pc.name]," she chastises, her brow furrowing at you when she looks up from her book. Apparently, you weren’t as funny as you thought. "Their education is tantamount! Our child will have the privilege of being born in a well-enough-to-do nursery with access with a library as extensive as our own – their ignorance would be a failure on my part as their mother." Okay, you get that... but the baby isn’t even born yet, and she’s already fretting over them being 'ignorant.’ The baby hasn’t taken its first breath, much less... chosen to wear diapers over learning how to use a latrine. "I wasn’t born a witch, [pc.name]. Like any budding magician, I first learned that I had a passion, or penchant, for it, before I learned how to perform it." She looks back down to her book and turns a page, her eyes scanning the letters on it. It being a children’s book, her focus isn’t broken for very long. "My mother once told me that she read books to me every day, starting the day after I was born. I attribute the passion for knowledge that I have now to that habit of hers." And she thinks that her own kids will be just as curious and willing to learn if she does the same thing? "If I am to have a successor[matiha.numKids 1 |, or multiple successors ], then the odds of that happening are much greater if my children follow the same... regimen, I suppose, that I did." She turns another page, but she barely bothers to even look at the words before she continues. "Besides: it certainly won’t hurt their development." What if one of them doesn’t want to be a witch or wizard[pc.isMage | | or whatever ]? What if one of them wants to be a mercenary? A warrior? A bard? Matiha pauses. With laborious slowness, she takes a long sigh in and out through her nose, closes the book, sets it down on the desk, picks up a new one, and opens it to the first page. "Next question." Alright: why is she reading the children’s books? They’re not for her; they’re for the children. "For two reasons. The first is to review their contents for their subject matter and level of difficulty." She flips the page of her newest book, and when her eyes scan what is probably the only two sentences on the page, her nose curls upward in frustration. "These books focus on the inane; on the perceptive world. Look at this." She turns the book around on her wrist and shows you the page she’s on: a bright, colored picture of a pair of birds sitting in a nest in a tree, with musical notes surrounding them, with a sentence underneath them about how the birds migrate home when spring arrives. "The subject matter of these books are far too base for any child of mine," she says as you read the pages. "Of course the cow says 'moo.’ Of course some dogs say 'bark’ and some say 'woof.’ And everybody knows that Misses Sun goes to bed just as Mister Moon is getting ready for the night." She slaps the page with the back of her hand, causing the whole book to flex backwards against its spine. "But there’s nothing in here about performing even the simplest of spells, or even anything to feed a curious mind. Sometimes, on clear days, the moon is visible in the day sky. Why do Misses Sun and Mister Moon break their routines on those days? How is a child meant to conjure a gust of wind if they’re too warm on a hot day?" ... Is it possible that she’s approaching this too much as a teacher, and not enough as a mother? She’s so worried about your kid’s education that she’s been neglecting her own. Does she know how to change a diaper? [matiha.hasKids |"I’ve had some additional practice since our last child," she answers quickly and matter-of-factly, but the question seems to reach her a little deeper than either of you expected. |"A bit of manipulation magic will go quite a long way in doing all of the menial labor for me, [pc.name]. And it’s considerably more sanitary," she answers, but the question seems to reach her a little deeper than either of you expected. ] "But... as much as I don’t want to be wrong, I must admit that you’re... more correct than I am." She sets down the book and regards the tower carefully. They don’t appear to be sorted in any particular order: the tower is thin in some places and looks like it could fall over if you stomped your foot really hard. "I’ll still be reading to our child, of course. Whether they grow to be a magician or not is ancillary to the fact that I will not tolerate an ignorant child. But... their future is what they ought to make of it, not what I make of it. My record of personal achievements isn’t exactly spotless. I wouldn’t want them to make the same mistakes and fall into the same trappings that I made during my lust for knowledge." You step up beside her as she looks down at her rounded stomach, gently rolling her palms over its surface. She can’t help but laugh to herself a bit. "[matiha.hasKids |Even after all this time, i |I ]t’s just much easier to be Matiha the Witch than it is to be Matiha the Mother." Well, hey: she gives a [pc.dcb |shit |damn |heck ] about her baby’s development. She’s already gone a whole lot farther than some mothers out there. She hums and tilts her head, resting it against your shoulder for a moment. "In the meantime," she says, breaking the silence, "now is a good time for you to establish yourself as a good [pc.mf |father |other mother ] to your child’s mother, yourself." ]

rows.raw: ' [rand |You push open the door to Matiha’s office, and, as you expected, there she is: standing sideways in front of a body-height mirror, her hat on the desk, checking out her own form by stretching her legs and flexing her glutes, watching how her robe rides on her skin. She’s already used to exposing quite a lot of thigh, but with her pregnancy, her robe pulls along her skin, showing off more of her body than even she’s used to – and from the look on her face, you can tell that she’s not especially thrilled with it. You knock on the door’s frame, but she doesn’t turn her head to acknowledge you. "[pc.name]," she says, the eyes in her reflection turning in your direction. "Am I still attractive?" [pc.dcb |She has tits for days and her skin is as smooth as velvet. She’s not getting uglier, that’s for damn certain. |At first, the question hits you like a dart to a dartboard, but the answer comes pretty quickly: frankly, you’ve always found her attractive[pc.corruptionRange 0 50 74 |, even when she was, well, evil | (although you kinda thought she was better when she was evil) ], and a baby bump isn’t going to take away from her other features. If anything, it makes her hotter. |Yep! ] Matiha’s lips curl slightly at your word[pc.isBimbo | |s ], but it’s clear that she isn’t totally convinced. "Of course you would say that. You’re the one that did this to me." Her left hand goes up her exposed thigh, her fingers raking gently across her skin; no matter how she looks at herself, something is just off, and it’s not the obvious. "You’re not allowed to say anything different." ... It’s a bit of a risk to say, but, you always took Matiha to be the studious, bookish type that cared more about results than she did about her own personal looks. That seems sort of vain for someone like her. "I am a witch, and my focus is on my work. Those are both true. But I’m also a woman, [pc.name]," she pouts, turning her head towards you with her brow furrowed. "If it were of no concern to me, I wouldn’t spend every morning putting my makeup on, or I wouldn’t bother with my earrings. My body is as important to me as my notes." And she thinks that her pregnancy is putting that at risk? In response, Matiha sighs sadly, turning back to the mirror and lifting her arms over her head, stretching her torso to get a better look at her stomach. "It’s different," she admits. "My image was something I had curated. And I suppose a baby is, too, but it’s... it’s frustrating that I can’t have both, I suppose." Could her magic help her with that somehow? "Illusion magic, maybe. But I can’t, for example, pull the baby out and incubate it somewhere." Her arms flop down to her sides, clapping against the taut robe and her exposed legs. She snorts through her nose as she gives up. "It’s simply a matter I’ll have to life with. [matiha.hasKids |I count my blessings that I don’t seem to be accruing any stretch marks from these repeated pregnancies. |I can only hope that this doesn’t give me stretch marks... although, I suppose a touch of illusion magic wouldn’t be out-of-place for those. ]" You step up behind her and wrap your hands around her from behind, your hands coming down gently on her round stomach. You give her a quick kiss on the cheek, just behind her jaw and beneath her ear; you stare into the reflection of her eyes and tell her that you meant what you said. If she can’t believe herself that she’s still attractive, then maybe she can believe you. Matiha’s lips curl wryly, her palms going to the back of your hands and her fingers interlocking with yours. "I know you’re only saying that because it’s what I want to hear," she says. That’s not true at all! "Then I’ll just have to hold you to that later." Her fingers squeeze on your hands, and you see a little glint of light reflecting off her teeth as she smiles at you – you’ll have to put your money where your mouth is when she’s in the mood later[rand | |. Almost as if on cue, you feel Matiha’s stomach lurch underneath your hands, causing her whole body to jump in surprise. The baby just kicked! She looks at you in the mirror’s reflection, and her cheeks quickly redden with surprise before she starts giggling. "It’s not all bad," she admits as she leans against you ]. |You push open the door to Matiha’s office, and, as you expected, there she is: standing beside the desk, leaning her rump against its edge, with her nose buried deep into the spine of a book and surrounded by literal piles of others stacked as high as her thigh, just as you usually find her. Except... from the color of the book’s bindings, it seems like she’s taken to reading something a bit... below her level. You can see pictures of animals; you see larger, more exaggerated letters and fonts; you see bright, pastel colors sewn into the fabric of the book. She’s reading a children’s book, and each of the books in the thigh-high piles surrounding her are all children’s books, too, with titles ranging from What Else Is A For? to When The Clock Strikes Twelve, It’s Moo Time. You aren’t exactly up to date with modern children’s books and their trends, but even you recognize Good Morning, Sun in there, too. You jokingly ask her if she’s only in the mood for some light reading this time. "We have a baby on the way, [pc.name]," she chastises, her brow furrowing at you when she looks up from her book. Apparently, you weren’t as funny as you thought. "Their education is tantamount! Our child will have the privilege of being born in a well-enough-to-do nursery with access with a library as extensive as our own – their ignorance would be a failure on my part as their mother." Okay, you get that... but the baby isn’t even born yet, and she’s already fretting over them being 'ignorant.’ The baby hasn’t taken its first breath, much less... chosen to wear diapers over learning how to use a latrine. "I wasn’t born a witch, [pc.name]. Like any budding magician, I first learned that I had a passion, or penchant, for it, before I learned how to perform it." She looks back down to her book and turns a page, her eyes scanning the letters on it. It being a children’s book, her focus isn’t broken for very long. "My mother once told me that she read books to me every day, starting the day after I was born. I attribute the passion for knowledge that I have now to that habit of hers." And she thinks that her own kids will be just as curious and willing to learn if she does the same thing? "If I am to have a successor[matiha.numKids 1 |, or multiple successors ], then the odds of that happening are much greater if my children follow the same... regimen, I suppose, that I did." She turns another page, but she barely bothers to even look at the words before she continues. "Besides: it certainly won’t hurt their development." What if one of them doesn’t want to be a witch or wizard[pc.isMage | | or whatever ]? What if one of them wants to be a mercenary? A warrior? A bard? Matiha pauses. With laborious slowness, she takes a long sigh in and out through her nose, closes the book, sets it down on the desk, picks up a new one, and opens it to the first page. "Next question." Alright: why is she reading the children’s books? They’re not for her; they’re for the children. "For two reasons. The first is to review their contents for their subject matter and level of difficulty." She flips the page of her newest book, and when her eyes scan what is probably the only two sentences on the page, her nose curls upward in frustration. "These books focus on the inane; on the perceptive world. Look at this." She turns the book around on her wrist and shows you the page she’s on: a bright, colored picture of a pair of birds sitting in a nest in a tree, with musical notes surrounding them, with a sentence underneath them about how the birds migrate home when spring arrives. "The subject matter of these books are far too base for any child of mine," she says as you read the pages. "Of course the cow says 'moo.’ Of course some dogs say 'bark’ and some say 'woof.’ And everybody knows that Misses Sun goes to bed just as Mister Moon is getting ready for the night." She slaps the page with the back of her hand, causing the whole book to flex backwards against its spine. "But there’s nothing in here about performing even the simplest of spells, or even anything to feed a curious mind. Sometimes, on clear days, the moon is visible in the day sky. Why do Misses Sun and Mister Moon break their routines on those days? How is a child meant to conjure a gust of wind if they’re too warm on a hot day?" ... Is it possible that she’s approaching this too much as a teacher, and not enough as a mother? She’s so worried about your kid’s education that she’s been neglecting her own. Does she know how to change a diaper? [matiha.hasKids |"I’ve had some additional practice since our last child," she answers quickly and matter-of-factly, but the question seems to reach her a little deeper than either of you expected. |"A bit of manipulation magic will go quite a long way in doing all of the menial labor for me, [pc.name]. And it’s considerably more sanitary," she answers, but the question seems to reach her a little deeper than either of you expected. ] "But... as much as I don’t want to be wrong, I must admit that you’re... more correct than I am." She sets down the book and regards the tower carefully. They don’t appear to be sorted in any particular order: the tower is thin in some places and looks like it could fall over if you stomped your foot really hard. "I’ll still be reading to our child, of course. Whether they grow to be a magician or not is ancillary to the fact that I will not tolerate an ignorant child. But... their future is what they ought to make of it, not what I make of it. My record of personal achievements isn’t exactly spotless. I wouldn’t want them to make the same mistakes and fall into the same trappings that I made during my lust for knowledge." You step up beside her as she looks down at her rounded stomach, gently rolling her palms over its surface. She can’t help but laugh to herself a bit. "[matiha.hasKids |Even after all this time, i |I ]t’s just much easier to be Matiha the Witch than it is to be Matiha the Mother." Well, hey: she gives a [pc.dcb |shit |damn |heck ] about her baby’s development. She’s already gone a whole lot farther than some mothers out there. She hums and tilts her head, resting it against your shoulder for a moment. "In the meantime," she says, breaking the silence, "now is a good time for you to establish yourself as a good [pc.mf |father |other mother ] to your child’s mother, yourself." ]'

rows.original: Just as you approach the door leading to Matiha’s personal quarters, it, to your surprise, swings open first, pushing into you and forcing you to take a step back. On the other side is Matiha, fully dressed – although her hat sits lopsided on her head and there’s a definite splotch of dark wetness on her dress, near her crotch. "[pc.name], thank Nareva, fantastic timing!" she exclaims, and, with sudden force, she grabs you by the wrist and throws you into the room. You barely have a chance to regain your footing before Matiha puts herself on the bed, with some delicate movements, and she hikes her dress up past her waist, just underneath her breasts. "My water broke a minute ago. It’s time! The baby’s coming!"[atWF | In that case, shouldn’t you go get help? There are others in the Wayfort that have more experience with helping someone deliver a baby– "There’s no time!" she barks. "If there’s anyone else here that can help me, they’ll probably hear it from across the fort. You put this baby in me, and you’re going to help me get it out!" ] "First, go to my dresser," she starts, pointing at it with her right index finger. "Bring me the book with the red leather binding on it, quickly!" You follow the point of her finger to her dresser, and sitting atop it are a number of books, all strewn apart in a haphazard, messy pile. All their bindings are made of leather, but, thankfully, only one of them is red; it’s not very large, but four differently-colored bookmarks jut from its pages. "Grab a towel and get yourself ready, [pc.name], it’s going to happen any second now!" Matiha keeps a pile of towels sorted and rolled into balls underneath the windowsill of her room; you pick one, unfurl it across both your hands, and position yourself at her feet while she opens the book at one of the bookmarks and flips through page after page, her eyes frantically scanning them for any information she can get. "Ah," she gasps once she finds the pages she wants, and she starts reading them quickly – and her fingers start to light and glow as the magic courses through her. But, ultimately, nothing happens. Nothing that you can see, anyway. You ask her what it is she’s doing. "Mitigation spells. I’m trying to stop the pain before it happens," she replies, her words coming to you quickly enough that they almost sound like they’re blending together. "And I’m going to try a polymorph spell to make myself looser so that the baby can pass easier. [matiha.numKids 0 1 |... Wait, polymorph magic? Didn’t she once say that that’s one of the hardest schools of magic to master? And that she doesn’t specialize in it at all? "I have to try!" she answers frantically as her fingers start glowing again – but, as before, nothing happens. "Damn it!" You’re not the one about to give birth, here, but maybe this isn’t the time to be experimenting with body-sculpting magic to try and make things easier for herself. She’s all frazzled and anxious and excited; there’s a chance that, if the spell even works, it could make things worse, or permanent, or something. A baby is about to come out of her: what if her focus breaks and the spell applies to it, but not to her? |Polymorph magic, again? Didn’t it fail last time? "And I’ve learned from my mistakes!" she spits, focusing on a different spell in her book for a moment. Her fingers start to glow again – but, as before, nothing happens. "Come on, what the fuck!" You remind her to just breathe and to try and relax. This isn’t the first kid she’s had: she just need to remember what you two did to pass the last one, and it’ll be over before she realizes it. And, if that doesn’t work, she need to try and focus on the potential consequences of a failed spell. ] "What’s the point of learning magic if I can’t use it to make life easier?!" she responds indignantly as she raises her hand for another attempt – but, just as she goes back to her book, she pauses, panting like she had just come in from a jog. Her eyes reread a few sentences across the pages again and again, and then she glances to her raised hand... and then she shuts the book and tosses it aside. "Ugh, you win, [pc.name]. But if I so much as get a stretch mark from this, I’m going to kill you!" That’s a bridge you’ll cross when you get there.
rows.translation: 就在你即将走到通往玛蒂哈私人居室的门口时，门却出乎意料地先打开了，门扇猛地向你推来，迫使你后退了一步。门的另一边站着玛蒂哈，她已经穿好了衣服——不过她的帽子戴得歪歪扭扭的，而她的连衣裙在靠近大腿的位置有一块明显的湿渍。[pc.name]，多亏了娜瑞瓦，真是来得正是时候！”她激动地喊道，突然用力抓住你的手腕，将你推进房间。你还没来得及站稳，玛蒂哈就已经轻轻躺到床上，她娴熟地撩起裙子，将裙摆提到腰部以上，正好遮住胸部。“一分钟前我的羊水破了，是时候了……宝宝要出生了！[atWF | 在这种情况下，你难道不应该去寻求帮助吗？在荒废驿堡，还有其他人拥有更多的经验，能够帮助别人接生婴儿…… “没有时间了！”她厉声说道，“如果这里还有其他人能够帮助我，他们肯定已经听到我们的声音了。你把这个宝贝放进我体内吧你是这东西得靠你帮忙才能弄出来！ ] 首先，去我的梳妆台那里，”她开始说道，用右手食指指向梳妆台，“快把那本红皮封面的书拿过来！” 你顺着她的手指方向找到了梳妆台，上面堆着好几本书，全都乱七八糟地放在一起。这些书的封面都是皮革材质的，不过幸运的是，只有其中一本是红皮封面的；这本书并不大，但书页上插着四根颜色不同的书签。“拿条毛巾，准备好吧[pc.name]，随时都可能发生啊！” 玛蒂哈把一堆毛巾整理好，卷成球状放在自己房间的窗台下；你拿了一块毛巾，将其展开铺在双手上，然后站在她的脚边。这时，她打开了书，找到某个标记页，开始一页一页地翻阅，目光急切地搜寻着任何有用的信息。啊，”她找到想要的页面后，立刻开始快速阅读起来——随着魔力在她体内流动，她的手指也开始闪烁发光。 然而，最终什么也没有发生。至少，是没有任何肉眼可见的变化。你问她正在做什么。 “我在使用缓解疼痛的法术。我试图在疼痛发生之前就阻止它，”她回答道，话语的速度快得几乎让人感觉这些词语都在彼此融合。“而且我还要尝试使用变形法术，让自己变得柔软一些，这样宝宝就能更容易地出生。 [matiha.numKids 0 1 |等等，变形魔法？她不是说过这是最难掌握的魔法流派之一吗？而且她根本不是专攻这个领域的啊……” “我必须试试！”她慌忙说道，手指再次开始发光——但和之前一样，什么事情都没有发生。该死！” 虽然现在不是你要分娩的时候，但也许现在也不是尝试那些塑形魔法来让自己好受点的时候。她现在既紧张又焦虑，还充满期待；如果这些魔法真的有效，反而可能会让情况变得更糟，或者造成永久性的影响……谁知道呢。一个婴儿即将出生：如果她的注意力分散了，那么这个咒语就会作用在婴儿身上，而不会作用在她自己身上，会怎么样呢？ |又是变形魔法吗？上次不是失败了吗？ “我可是从自己的错误中吸取了教训的！”她咬牙说道，随后将注意力转移到书中的另一个法术上。她的手指再次开始发光——但和上次一样，什么效果也没有出现。拜托，搞什么鬼！” 你劝她先深呼吸，尽量放松下来。这已经不是她第一次面对这样的孩子了：她只需要回想一下你们上次是怎么顺利度过这个阶段的，事情就会在不知不觉中结束的。如果那样仍然不行，她就需要试着去考虑咒语失败可能带来的后果。 ] 如果我不能用魔法来让生活变得更轻松，那学习魔法还有什么意义呢？！”她愤愤不平地说道，同时再次举起手准备尝试——但是，就在她准备重新翻开书的时候，她突然停了下来，喘着粗气，就像刚跑完步一样。她的目光在书页上反复阅读着同样的几句话，然后又看了看自己举在手中的手部……最后，她关上了书，把它扔到了一边。“唉，算你赢了。 [pc.name]但要是我因此身上出现了妊娠纹，我绝对会杀了你！” 等到那时再想办法解决这个问题吧。

rows.original:
The next hour isn’t exactly pretty. On top of the predictable mess, Matiha is cursing, thrashing, and shouting through a natural childbirth that she thought that she was ready for. By the time it’s over, her eyeliner has been completely ruined, running as far down as her chin and staining her cheeks the whole way; her hair is a frazzled mess; and you think you heard the sound of her fingers tearing holes into her sheets from gripping it so hard. [matiha.numKids 2
            |And despite you having a bit of experience with helping Matiha deliver
            |And on top of all of that
        ], you do your best, but you’re not exactly the world’s greatest nurse.
        
        But, in the end, the baby is successfully delivered: after a harrowing hour, your [matiha.numKids 1 2
            |first child – a beautiful baby girl –
            |next child with Matiha – a healthy baby [var0
                |boy
                |girl
            ]–
        ] is brought into the world[pc.isDK
            |, naked, screaming, and blind. Sort of how you take out some of your enemies. Life is beautiful that way
        ].
        
        You wrap the baby in a towel and bring [var0
            |him
            |her
        ] to Matiha, still gasping and panting, herself looking like she’s barely conscious. But when she sees her newborn child, a warm smile spreads across her face – if she could see herself now, no doubt she’d find herself hideous, with her running makeup and unkempt hair, but that one little smile of relief was all it took for her to look like the most beautiful woman in the world.
        
        [matiha.numKids 1 2
            |"[pc.name], I’ll be honest: I’m glad our first is a girl," she says, taking the wrapped baby and holding her close to her chest. The baby coos and squirms and wriggles, but it doesn’t seem too upset or hungry just yet (and with a mom like Matiha, you hope she has a big appetite). "I’ve always wanted to have a girl... and I’ve always wanted to name her Daina."
            
            You didn’t have any plans on names for the girl on-hand anyway, so, Daina is fine with you. Although: why Daina specifically?
            
            "I just like it," Matiha laughs.
            |Matiha gasps from stiffness and exertion as she lifts her arms to take the baby from you. She holds [var0
                |him
                |her
            ] to her chest, looking just like she had when she had your firstborn, Daina. Although, unlike Daina, your next-in-line is immediately hungry and latches on to Matiha’s nipple – you had better hope that [var0
                |he
                |she
            ] has a big appetite.
        
            "We can worry about names a little later," Matiha groans as she reclines into her pillow. "I think we’ve all been through a lot, lately."
        ]
        
        With that, Matiha shuts her eyes for some well-deserved sleep, with [matiha.numKids 1 2
            |Daina nestled snuggly against her
            |her baby nursing [var0
                |him
                |her
            ]self until [var0
                |he
                |she
            ]’s had [var0
                |his
                |her
            ] fill
        ].
        
        It took both of them going to sleep for you to realize just how tired you were, and you weren’t even the one giving birth or being born. You don’t want to disturb Matiha and her baby, though, so, you just put your head down next to them for a bit. You’ll probably wake up when they do.

接下来的一个小时实在不怎么愉快。在那些预料之中的混乱之外，玛蒂哈还在经历自然分娩的过程，她原本以为自己已经做好了准备，但却一直在咒骂、挣扎、大喊大叫。等到这一切结束的时候，她的眼线已经完全毁掉了，眼线液顺着脸颊流到了下巴，把她的脸弄得通红；她的头发也乱得一团糟；而你能想象到的，就是她的手指因为抓得太紧，把床单都抓出了洞来。 [matiha.numKids 2
            |尽管你在帮助玛蒂哈完成任务方面已经积累了一些经验……
            |而且，除此之外……
        ]你已经尽了最大努力，但说实话，你也算不上世界上最出色的护士。

不过，最终宝宝还是成功出生了——在经历了那个令人紧张的小时之后，你终于完成了任务。 [matiha.numKids 1 2
            |第一个孩子——一个可爱的女婴——
            |玛蒂哈的下一位孩子——一个健康的婴儿[var0

            |赤裸着、尖叫着、双眼失明……某种程度上，这就是你消灭某些敌人的方式。这样的生活，也挺美好的。
        ]你用毛巾把婴儿包好，然后带着他/她离开。 [var0
            |他
            |她
        ]对玛蒂哈来说，她仍在喘着粗气，看起来几乎已经失去了意识。但当她看到自己刚出生的孩子时，一张温暖的笑容立刻出现在她的脸上——如果现在她能看到自己的样子，无疑会觉得自己丑陋不堪，因为妆容已经花了，头发也乱糟糟的。然而，就是那一个充满释然的微笑，让她看起来仿佛是世界上最美丽的女人。
        
        [matiha.numKids 1 2
            |"[pc.name]，说实话，我很高兴我们的第一个孩子是个女孩，”她说道，一边接过被包裹好的婴儿，将她紧紧抱在胸前。婴儿发出咿咿呀呀的声音，身体也在扭动、蠕动，但看起来她既没有太不安，也没有感到饥饿（有像玛蒂哈这样的妈妈，肯定会让宝宝有很好的食欲的）。我一直想要一个女儿……而且我一直想给她取名为达娜。”

反正你之前也没有考虑过给这个女儿取什么名字，所以达娜这个名字对你来说也挺合适的。不过，为什么偏偏要选达娜呢？
            
            我就喜欢这样，”玛蒂哈笑着说。
            |玛蒂哈因为用力过猛而喘着气，她伸出手臂从你手中接过婴儿，然后紧紧地抱住了她。 [var0

            ]她把孩子抱在胸前，样子和生下你的第一个孩子达伊娜时一模一样。不过，与达伊娜不同的是，你的这个孩子一出生就饿了，立刻开始吸吮玛蒂哈的乳头——你最好祈祷一切顺利吧。 [var0
                |他
                |她
            ]名字的事情可以稍后再考虑，”玛蒂哈一边靠在枕头上一边叹道，“我觉得我们最近都经历了很多事情。
        ]
        
        说完这些，玛蒂哈闭上了眼睛，准备好好地睡一觉。 [matiha.numKids 1 2
            |戴娜紧紧地依偎在她身边。
            |喂奶[var0
                |他
                |她
            ]直到[var0
                |他
                |她
            ]已经经历了[var0
                |他的
                |她
            ]填充
        ]直到他们俩都睡着了，你才真正意识到自己有多疲惫——尽管其实并不是你在分娩，也不是新生儿。不过你也不想打扰玛蒂哈和她的宝宝，于是就躺在他们旁边小睡了一会儿。等他们醒来时，你大概也会跟着醒来的。

rows.original:
You know, you have a bit of time on your hands. If she wanted, you two could head to the Wayportal and make your way to Hawkethorne–

    Before the words fully formed in your mouth, Matiha is standing and waving her hand towards some personal effects tucked against the far wall of the office. From them, a shoulder bag floats from the pile and makes its way straight to her hand: the bag is stuffed to the point of overflowing with books, rolled parchments... and toys. Primarily dolls with shaggy hair and cones of fabric meant to depicts dresses.
    
    "What an undue thing to suggest, [pc.name]. You had caught me so unready," she says. A thin but obvious smile creeps across her face, her eyes narrowing on yours. "But if you’re going to insist, darling, well, I suppose I can relent this once."
    
    Heh, well... you wouldn’t want to be a burden on her and her busy schedule, so, there’s no time to waste.

            |露米从大厅里走过来，看起来有些局促不安。看到你站在雕像旁，这位负责照料蜜蜂的女子犹豫了一下，整理了一下思绪，然后清了清嗓子开始说话。[pc.name]嗯，怎么了？她看起来很慌张，至少比平时更加慌张，而你几乎从来没见过她离开酒吧。是不是发生了什么事情让她受到了惊吓？”

她把手指交叉在一起。我们……我当时在桥那边的南门等着我的淡色艾尔啤酒从收获谷运过来，这时有个半裸的女孩拖着一堆杂物走了过来。整整一车的东西，只不过那些东西都是放在浮冰上的雪橇上运来的，而她非要见你。"
            
            你的胃里突然涌起一股紧张感——考虑到最近发生的事情，那个人很可能是梅拉。不过，你本以为她会从北方过来，而不是南方。不知道这是怎么回事……将注意力重新转向露米，你轻轻拍了拍她的肩膀，让她那颗紧张不安的心平静下来。这个女孩不是自称是你的宫廷法师吗？
            
            虽然没大声说出来，但她的穿着确实很适合这个角色。”露米若有所思地咬着嘴唇说道，“她应该是常青女士会的成员吧？那个女巫和她的一群人可是整个边境地区唯一的‘核能法师’——你真的聘请她来担任你的宫廷法师吗？”

这是个漫长的故事，但简短的回答就是：是的。梅拉……她现在应该还在城门外吧？
            
            如果那就是她的名字……那么没错，她就是那个人。而且她还闹出了不小的动静。有几个人在拦着她，所以我才去帮你拿东西的……”

你叹了口气。好吧，谢谢。让她回去继续工作吧，你来处理这件事。虽然你能够理解露米可能会因为梅拉这样活泼开朗的人住在荒废驿堡而感到有些不安，但你一定要确保梅拉明白基本规矩，如果她行为失检，也一定要受到相应的纠正。
        ]
    ]

"
    You've barely stepped into the little courtyard that houses the waystone statue when [wayfort.hasDaliza
        |one of Daliza's outriders comes marching up to you, trying very hard to not appear panicked. Seeing you by the statue, he stops at a respectable distance and salutes. "[pc.mf
            |Sir
            |Ma'am
        ]."
        
        What's the matter?
        
        "There's a girl by the gates demanding to see you, with a whole bunch of junk in tow. Like, a whole cart's worth, only it's got no wheels and is floating off the ground."
        
        Has she claimed to be your court mage?
        
        Relief creeps into the outrider's eyes. "Yes, [pc.mf
            |sir
            |ma'am
        ]. Quite loudly and emphatically. We thought she was some sort of merchant at first, given the sheer amount of junk she had with her and her fancy dress, but —"
        
        You cut off the poor sop with a wave of your hand. Redheaded 'nuki girl, fancy dress way out of place for the Marches, loud, demanding, bratty?
        
        "Yes, [pc.mf
            |sir
            |ma'am
        ]."
        
        He can let her in — she's expected. Neither Daliza nor the elves need to worry, you'll take her from here and give her some correction if she really gets out of hand.
        
        "Thank you, [pc.mf
            |sir
            |ma'am
        ]."
        |[wayfort.hasFarrah
            |Farrah comes sashaying up to you, a half-smile on her face. On one hand, the demoness looks inclined to be annoyed, given how strained the smile is; on the other, she's the kind who can see an opportunity in just about every situation.
            
            "Oh, I thought you'd be here. And with such perfect timing, too."
            
            Well, what's the matter? It's not like Farrah to leave her store when she could be making money; it has to be something pretty important, right?
            
            "There's a girl by the gates demanding to see you, with a whole bunch of junk in tow. Like, a whole cart's worth, only it's got no wheels and is floating off the ground. I thought it was the shipment I was waiting for to begin with, but no, it's just some girl."
            
            Has she claimed to be your court mage?
            
            Farrah taps her chin. "Actually, no. I don't think she likes me much. But with the fancy way she's dressed and all the shiny junk she had with her, she clearly has money — or at least, is used to having it. All I did was to ask if she'd be interested in buying something or maybe liquidating some of the junk from that floating sled of hers, and she gave me the stink eye. Wonder if I said something wrong?"
            
            Redheaded 'nuki girl, fancy dress way out of place for the Marches, loud, demanding, bratty? Claiming to be your court mage?
            
            "Well, she didn't say that last part, but everything else? Yeah." Farrah pauses a moment, then twitches her nose as she sniffs and crosses her arms. "Hey, you didn't tell me that you were getting a court mage, [pc.name]!"
            
            It was all rather sudden for you too, you have to admit. It's only been a few days out since the decision was made.
            
            "Ooh, this is exciting! [viviane.recruited|Not much of a market in these parts for certain things, but that looks to be changing. Sure, there's that witch in the walking house, but she procures her own stuff all the time|There hasn't really been a market here for magical knickknacks]... I should probably apologize to that girl later, butter her up a bit. What was her name again?"
            
            Later. For now, thanks for letting you know Meira's here. Neither she nor anyone else needs to worry — she'll have her turn at the brat soon enough once you've finished settling her in and dispensed with some appropriate correction.
            
            "I like the sound of that. Promise me I'll get to join in when it happens, okay?"
            |Rumie comes up to you from the great hall, looking sheepish. Seeing you by the statue, the bee-tender hesitates, gathering her thoughts before clearing her throat and beginning.
            
            "[pc.name]?"
            
            Yes, what's the matter? She looks flustered, or at least more flustered than usual, and you almost never see her away from the bar. Did something spook her?
            
            She puts her fingers together. "We-ll... I was at the southern gate just past the bridge, waiting for my shipment of pale ale to come up from Harvest Valley when there's this half-'nuki girl who comes up with a whole bunch of junk in tow. Like, a whole cart's worth, only the sled it's all on is floating, and she's demanding to see you."
            
            A tight knot forms in the pit of your stomach — given what's recently happened, it's probably Meira. That being said, you'd expected her to approach from the north, instead of the south. Wonder what was up with that. Turning your attention back to Rumie, you calm the skittish bee-tender with a pat on the shoulder. Did this girl claim to be your court mage?
            
            "Not out loud, but she was certainly dressed for the part." Rumie bites her lip pensively. "She's one of Evergreen's, isn't she? The witch and her get are the only 'nukis in all of the Marches — did you really take her on as your court mage?"
            
            It's a long story, but the short answer is yes. Meira — she's still at the gates, is she?
            
            "If that's her name... then yeah, she is. Making a pretty big fuss, too. Couple of folks are holding her off while I went to get you..."
            
            You sigh. All right, thanks. She can get back to her job while you deal with this — while you can understand that Rumie might be a bit nervous about having someone as exuberant as Meira living in the Wayfort, you'll be sure make sure Meira understands the ground rules and receives correction should she get out of hand.
        ]
    ]
    "

rows.original: Meira's voice reaches you long before you reach the southern gate — you can hear her browbeat some poor soul all the way from across the courtyard. Your rational mind knows that she's actually forming intelligible words, but the sheer force of her indignance is such that all the syllables flow together to form a steady stream of incoherent barking. You have to admit, it's rather persuasive, if only because giving her what she wants is likely to be the easiest path to getting her to shut up and go away. Happily, she turns her attention to you the moment you arrive on the scene, letting the poor sop she was browbeating scurry away to safety. "Oh hey, [pc.name]! And here I was thinking you'd never show up — you have absolutely horrible people watching your gates, did you know? I told them that I was your new court mage and they said they hadn't heard of such a thing! Can you imagine that? So preposterous — surely an occasion of such import would've gotten around your entire Wayfort by now! Well, I wasn't about to take such hazing lying down; if you let people get away with being cheeky they'll just be emboldened to take advantage of you more. Nevertheless, I'm sure my —" All right, at this point you're pretty sure that Meira is, as they say, taking the piss; she certainly didn't behave like this when you first met her in the forest all that time ago. And if this is a deliberate act... well, you'll be able to deal with her once you get her settled in. Now, what's with all this stuff, and why did she show up at the south gate? You were under the impression she'd be coming directly from [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja's |her mother's ]. "Oh! This is all the stuff I'll be needing to do all the court mage things I'll be doing when working for you!" Meira gives the sled and the items bound atop it a firm smack. "Stuff like my bed, a couple of tools, some reagents to start, that sort of thing! I also went down to Hawkethorne with Senja to get a few things we didn't have spares of in the house, so there's that — [evergreen.dealtWith |she really needs to get out of the house these days, and I felt obliged to give her an excuse to do it |she really likes heading down to town, and was really having fun thinking she was showing me around. I didn't have the heart to tell her that I already knew my way around ]." You eye Meira's floating sled, the thing wobbling a little as it strains under its load, then sigh and motion for her to follow you into the Wayfort. Even in all of this, her clothes make her really stand out amidst the other denizens, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. As she pointed out the last time, part of her job will be dealing with people, and being memorable has to be in her favor. Right? Right? She's had a look around when you brought her here on a date — does she have anyplace in mind for where she'll be staying? "We-ll... technically you decide that, since you're my boss. But if you're asking me, I do have an idea in mind. I don't really want to bunk down with the help — not only do I need some personal space to get my things set out, but I don't think they'd appreciate having me do all my magic stuff right next to their beds." Sounds reasonable. Where would she prefer to put down her roots, then? "We-ll... there's that old watchtower off by the side of the Wayfort. [wayfort.hasAileh |I get that there's someone living upstairs, but the ground floor is pretty empty, the walls are plenty thick |No one's using it at the moment ], and from what I remember it looks to have been occupied by someone bookish in the past. [var0 |You also set up that summoning circle you bought from us in the place, so that more or less seals the deal. |There's a nice spot where I can set up a summoning circle for the both of us — you can use it when I'm not busy, as a bonus. How's that for a starter? ] Such a nice spot would be wasted on anyone else, I tell you; I don't want you to regret any part of this decision, so you should help me help you help us all, yes?" The argument does make sense in spite of its bratty delivery. It's not as if the ground floor of the watchtower is in use anyway, and [wayfort.hasAileh |Aileh presumably won't be too bothered by what goes on under her |having someone in residence will at least keep the dust and spiders out ]. All right, then. Sounds like a plan.
rows.translation: 在你还未走到南门之前，梅拉的声音就已经传到了你的耳边——从院子的另一头，你就能听到她在怒斥某个可怜的人。你的理智告诉你，她其实是在说一些有意义的话，但她的愤怒之情太过强烈，以至于那些词语都被混合在了一起，形成了一连串语无伦次的咆哮声。 你得承认，这种说法确实很有说服力——因为满足她的要求，很可能是让她闭嘴离开的最简单办法。幸运的是，你一出现在现场，她的注意力就立刻转移到了你身上，于是那个被她欺负的可怜人就赶紧逃到了安全的地方。 哦，嘿， [pc.name]我还在想你根本不会出现呢——你知道吗，看守你大门的人简直糟糕透了！我告诉他们我是你的新宫廷法师，但他们却说从来没听说过这种职位！你能想象吗？太荒谬了——这么重要的事情，现在整个荒废驿堡地区应该都已经传开了吧！哼，我可不会任由这种欺负行为继续下去；如果你们允许人们肆无忌惮地顶嘴、耍无赖，他们只会更加胆大妄为，继续欺负你们。不过，我确信我的——” 好吧，在这种情况下，你相当漂亮我敢肯定，梅拉是在开玩笑吧；当初你在森林里第一次见到她的时候，她绝对不会表现得这样的。如果这是她故意这么做的……嗯，等她安顿下来后，你肯定能应付得了她。现在，这些东西都是怎么回事？她为什么会出现在南门那里？你原本以为她会直接从[evergreen.dealtWith |森娅的 |她母亲的 ]哦！这些就是我在为你工作时所需要的所有东西了，用来履行那些宫廷法师的职责的！”梅拉用力拍了一下雪橇以及上面绑着的那些物品。“比如我的床、几件工具、还有一些初始实验所需的炼金材料，就是这类东西！我还和森娅一起去了鹰棘镇，去买了些家里没有的备用物品，所以这些也都包括在内了—— [evergreen.dealtWith |这些天她真的需要出门走走，我觉得我有责任给她一个出门的理由。 |她真的很喜欢去城里逛，还兴致勃勃地想着要给我当向导。我实在不忍心告诉她，其实我早就熟悉那条路了。 ]你注视着梅拉那架漂浮的雪橇，它承载着沉重的负荷，微微摇晃着。你叹了口气，示意她跟随你进入荒废驿堡。在这一切环境中，她的穿着确实让她在其他生物中显得格外醒目，但这也未必是件坏事。正如她上次所说，她的工作中有一部分就是与人打交道，因此给人留下深刻印象对她来说肯定是有利的，对吧？ 对吧？ 当你带她来这里约会时，她应该已经环顾了一下四周了吧——她有没有考虑过自己会住在哪里呢？ 我们……严格来说，这个决定应该由你来做，因为你是我的上司。但如果你问我的话，我确实有个想法。我其实并不想和那些助手们住在一起——不仅因为我需要一些个人空间来安排我的事情，而且我觉得他们也不会乐意看到我在他们的床边做那些魔法相关的事情。听起来挺合理的。那么，她更愿意在哪个地方安家呢？ “我们……嗯，就在荒废驿堡旁边那座旧瞭望塔附近吧。 [wayfort.hasAileh |我知道楼上有人住，但一楼几乎空无一人，墙壁也相当厚实。 |目前没有人在使用它。 ]据我回忆，那里过去似乎住着一位喜欢读书的人。 [var0 |你也在那个地方布置了从我们这里购买的召唤阵，这样一来，整个交易基本上就完成了。 |有个很不错的地方，我可以在那里为我们俩建立一个召唤圈——等我不忙的时候，你也可以使用它，当作一个额外的福利吧。这样作为开始，你觉得怎么样？ ]我告诉你，这么好的机会如果给了别人，简直太浪费了。我绝对不希望你为这个决定而后悔，所以你应该帮我，帮我帮助大家，好吗？确实尽管表达方式有些任性，但这种设计其实还是合理的。反正瞭望塔的一楼本来也没被使用，所以[wayfort.hasAileh |艾莉大概不会太在意她脚下发生的事情吧。 |让某人住在那里，至少可以防止灰尘和蜘蛛进入。 ]好吧，那就这么定了。听起来是个不错的计划。
