女孩子总得做女孩子该做的事。我收拾好东西，立刻动身离开了。途中顺道去了鹰棘镇，想弄清楚事情的来龙去脉，确认你并没有死……现在，我是来要求你履行你的承诺的。就是这么简单。很简单。虽然你没有答应让她坐在大厅的正中央，就在你的王座下方，一边品尝你的葡萄酒，一边对别人发号施令，表现得好像这个地方是她的一样，但在邀请她来到你家的时候，你其实很清楚她的性格。你本应该告诫她不要随意滥用自己的权力，但奥利维亚本质上就是一个表里不一的人。我想，这大概就是她的性格使然吧。
rows.raw: " [wayfort.hasDaliza |Just as you're about to enter the grand hall, you're stopped at the doorway by a plainly very, very cross Daliza. Arms folded and lips set into a straight line, your bailiff gives you a curt nod as she sees you approach. "[pc.mf |Sir |Ma'am ]." Much more curt than her usual %"Baron[pc.mf | |ness ]". What's gotten into her? "Just... go in and see for yourself. I know you enjoy adopting strays, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], but surely a line has to be drawn somewhere!" ] As you step into the grand hall proper, a sinking familiar sight meets your eyes: that of Olivia lounging about in a high chair, the stem of a wine glass gripped between her furry fingers. [wayfort.hasMaids |By her side, one of your maids dutifully fills her glass from an open bottle; Olivia swirls, sniffs, and sips in the approved manner before giving the maid a contended nod. "Thank you, dearie. Leave the bottle, won't you?" As the maid departs, Olivia turns the full force of her gaze upon you, her smile widening into a grin. "Now where were you, [pc.name]? I've been waiting for the better part of an hour at this point. I didn't know you were such a fan of all things Yvennese to go as far as to dress up your maidservants in such style." To be perfectly honest, you weren't specifically aiming for it, but that's how things turned out. Are their uniforms authentic enough for her, then? "A little too authentic, to be honest; a pastiche of what they really are like back home. So long as they know how to pour wine, I don't really care." |[var0 |It really is like how it was in the old mine, right down to a couple of the corrupted lupines fawning over her hand and foot, filling her glass while she reclines and looks appropriately regal. "Thank you, boys. Leave the bottle, won't you? I need a little privacy here." As the lupines depart, Olivia turns the full force of her gaze upon you, slowly shaking her head in mock disappointment. "Now where were you, [pc.name]? I've been waiting for the better part of an hour at this point." [corlup.imprisoned |Wait, how did she get some of the corrupted lupines out of the dungeon? They're supposed to be behind bars! "Oh, I didn't take all of them. Just the few I remembered being useful from back in the — that disgusting place. They're just as eager to serve now as they were, so long as I throw a crumb of feigned affection now and again." That's not the point! How did she get them out of your dungeon? "Oh, don't worry; they're not in any risk of running a jailbreak any time soon. I just convinced the right people to let me have a couple, especially after a demonstration of how hopeless they were around me." |She's taken a couple of the lupines for herself, then. "Just the few I remembered being useful from back in the — that disgusting place. They're just as eager to serve now as they were, so long as I throw a crumb of feigned affection now and again." So long as she doesn't distract them from their usual duties. What they do off the clock isn't your business, so long as they keep out of trouble. Olivia rolls her eyes. "Oh, please. It's not as if they're actually doing anything useful 'guarding' the place — you and I know they're just here because you're too soft-hearted to send them to their deaths. Them being an effective garrison? Curing them? I think they're much more suited to waiting on me, don't you think?" ] |By her side, Rumie dutifully fills her glass from an open bottle; Olivia swirls, sniffs, and sips in the approved manner before giving the maid a contended nod. "That'll do. What a useful girl you are!" The words hit Rumie like a bolt from the heavens — the poor dear buzzes with delight as her cheeks color. You've known Rumie long enough to be aware that a simple compliment shouldn't get the beetender this wound up, and yet Olivia's words, by all appearances, are quite mundane. Hey, now. Rumie can't wait on her all day — she has a bar to run, too. Keeping her smile frozen, Olivia turns the full force of her gaze upon you, then gives Rumie a side-nod. "Yes, yes, of course. Run along now, dearie; [pc.names] finally deigned to show up, so I don't need you any longer. And leave the bottle, if you please!" As Rumie buzzes off, Olivia sips the wine and gives you a nod. "That one reminds me of the Baranians back home — the sheepfolk. Natural servants, the lot of them: eager to please, thirsty for praise, and docile to a fault. I can see why you keep her around. "Now where were you, [pc.name]? I've been waiting for the better part of an hour at this point." ] ] Maybe you should be the one asking the questions. Between last leaving her chambers in the mine and her showing up now, you haven't seen hide or hair of Olivia. For all you knew... "It would be convenient for you if I just disappeared after your victory, wouldn't it?" Olivia wrinkles her nose and sniffs. "That'd absolve you of your promise after having gotten the goods. Too bad it's not happening." [pc.isDK |She's right. Even if it might have not come to mind at the time, it would have been convenient. |Seriously, now. Does she think you'd stoop so low? ] "By all accounts, you didn't bother looking for me while running your victory lap, what with being busy freeing all the captives and getting a whole bunch of forelock-tugging. That, and cozying up with that doggy squeeze of yours." Can she stop trying to put you on the defensive here and actually answer your question? Where was she in between then and now? "[silly |I pretended I was a bar of soap and slipped past you |I fucked off ]." Olivia takes a sip from her wine glass and lets the moment sink in. "[silly |I made like a tree and left. Bounced. Hightailed it. ]The sounds coming up from down below were pretty ugly, and I wasn't about to stick around — if you lost to Asgeir, I'd need a head start on getting away from that meathead and his flunkies. If you won... well, it'd just be getting ahead of the rush and any particularly vengeful ex-captives who remembered my face. "Girl's got to do what a girl's got to do. I gathered my things and made a break for it. Stopped by Hawkethorne to get the rest of the story and figure you weren't dead, and now I'm here to collect on your promise. Simple enough." Simple enough. While you didn't promise her sitting at the head of the hall just under your throne, sipping your wine and bossing people around like she owns the place, you knew what she was like when you invited her into your home. You'd warn her against indiscriminately throwing her weight around, but Olivia's capable of being a two-faced creature through and through. Comes with the territory, one supposes. "

rows.original: [wayfort.stateABC |"Now then," Olivia says with a scowl, "let's discuss the state of my accommodations." That being...? "This place —" she points around at the great hall in all directions — "is a fucking dump. I checked out some of the chambers in the far wings, trying to find at least one that wasn't completely ruined, and nope. Nada. Nothing. It's a fort, all right, but it's a shitty fort. Small wonder that [wayfort.hasDaliza |your little band of elves hasn't already overthrown you for garrisoning them in such horrible conditions. And I thought I was bad with my [silly |simps |adoring fans ] |there are still people willing to pass through here just to use the bridge. The way things are, it might just collapse into the river without warning ]." She's not happy, huh? "Is it that obvious?" Olivia folds her furry hands under her tits and stares [pc.heightRange 65 |up ]at you defiantly. "When you first said you had a wayfort, I was expecting someplace clean, at least. Before you say it, no, you weren't lying, but this is downright deceptive." Well, you remember offering to discuss the matter further beforehand, but she said she'd get to that later and never followed up, instead choosing to disappear after you'd dealt with Asgeir and not showing her face up until now. "Sounded like you were losing, and I thought I'd skip out before he finished dealing with you and came around to me for my treachery." Pft. That still doesn't change the fact that it's still her fault. Look, if the Wayfort offends her refined sensibilities that badly, she's free to take a hike all the way back to Yvennes where she came from. You'll pay for her passage and a bonus on top of that, if that's what it takes; you're not about to have a sourpuss marring your great hall when it's already full enough with dust and cobwebs. A bitter laugh. "Dearest, do you seriously think I could return to Yvennes even if you gave me every hawk in those dry coffers of yours?" [pc.isCunning |You have some idea, but that doesn't mean it's impossible. "It's not impossible, but it's more of a risk than I'm willing to take. |What? Why not? "You really are an idiot, aren't you? ] Before, I'd have said anything to be out of that hole, but now that I'm actually out going home has become a lot less of an option. Think — the mercenaries the local lady hired to patrol the roads have turned into bandits themselves. There're demons wandering the countryside, not to mention the creeps who accompany them. Then I've heard distant rumors that there're holy armies being mustered and converging on this spot. I damn well don't want to meet them coming the other way. "And even if I did make it back to Yvennes, what then? I don't look like how I did when I left —" she gestures to her furred and clawed limbs — "and that means inconvenient questions. Also, what happened to the rest of my colleagues, answering questions about why they aren't with me isn't something I really want to do." Come to think of it, you don't remember seeing any of Olivia's adventuring party on the way out of the mine while you were freeing the captives. Or more probably, you didn't recognize any of them, given she didn't tell you what they looked like. "Doesn't matter. If they're dead, I get grilled. If they're not dead and make it back to Yvennes to tell how I made a deal with Asgeir to not be made a fuck-slave along with the rest of them, I get quite literally grilled. Considering how I look now, they might decide to burn me without bothering with questions." All very good reasons, you have to admit, but you feel there's more she isn't telling you. Olivia sniffs. "Suit yourself. Whatever the case, I'm stuck in this ruin; at least it's better than a dark, musty hole in the ground. Hmph.[silly | My disappointment is immeasurable and my day is ruined. ]" She has at least found somewhere to lie down, right? "Privately. I'm not bunking down with [wayfort.hasDaliza |your elves |the bee ], that's just disgusting. All those smells crammed into one room, it's enough to make a girl retch. I've had enough of that for an entire lifetime with those miserable dogs reeking." Sure, sure. |"Now, if you don't mind," Olivia says, keeping her thin-lipped smile, "let's discuss the state of my accommodations, shall we?" Hopefully you haven't oversold the wayfort. It's gotten some much-needed repairs and isn't an absolute dump any longer, but there're still places which need touching up. "That's an understatement," she replies, dismissing your words with a waggle of her fingers. "Still, it's only to be expected when everything in this part of the world is either rustic or ancient. I saw the local baroness' castle on my way into the Marches, and that was a dump. Ew. Marchers have no sense of pride in themselves — that, or a long melancholy. Either way, ew.[wayfort.hasDaliza | It's okay for that garrison of elves you're keeping around, but certainly you think yourself above mere grunts. ]" Is she actually unhappy with the state of things, or not? If she's trying to be passive-aggressive, the passive is quite lacking. "It's fine. Very much so. But it could be better, as you pointed out yourself. Still, the locals speak well of your reconstruction efforts, so I daresay you aren't going to be resting on your laurels, yes?" Just to be sure, if she's getting buyer's remorse, she's free to leave any time. Part of the agreement was that she could come and go from the wayfort as she pleased — and that means all the way back to Yvennes, if it comes to that. You aren't going to keep her a prisoner, force her to stay against her will regardless of the circumstances. A giggle. "Charming offer. One might even think that you were trying to get rid of me — but no, I do intend to stay here for some time. Why do you think I left the comfort of Yvennes to go rough it with a bunch of mercenaries to begin with?" She didn't explain back in the mine — so yes, why did a pampered princess like her join up with what in her eyes must be a bunch of roughnecks? "Something's going on in this part of the world," Olivia replies, the smile vanishing from her face as her expression turns serious. "A bunch of mangy dogs is the least of it. Events are afoot, and when I passed through Hawkethorne on my way here word is great holy armies are being amassed in Jassira and the old heartlands to march on this very region. "Now, I can't control the entire narrative — I'm well aware that there are others of my ilk who'll be telling different tales. But this is my chance to actually make my mark on history, tell the tale my way, be remembered. Be more than just a do-nothing in a corner of Yvennes. Call it a premonition or just plain luck, but that's the feeling I had months ago... and now it turns out I was right. That, my dear, is worth enduring a little discomfort for." It's much better than a musty hole in the ground and coming this close to being a sex slave. "Quite so. See? You can be quite perceptive when it suits you, Dearest." She has at least found somewhere to lie down, right? "Privately. This place has several empty chambers, and I appropriated one of them for myself; I need some privacy if I'm to reach my muse. I'm not bunking down with [wayfort.hasDaliza |your elves |the bee ], that's just disgusting. All those smells crammed into one room, it's enough to make a girl retch. I've had enough of that for an entire lifetime with those miserable dogs reeking." All right, you can live with that. |"Now, if you don't mind," Olivia says, her smile widening, "let's discuss the state of my accommodations, shall we?" Impressive, isn't it? "For what's supposed to be a military fort? Yes, it's fairly luxurious." She dismisses the notion with a waggle of her fingers. "Credit where credit's due: I'd expected that this part of the world be utterly bereft of high culture and aesthetic sense, but clearly old Belhar had influence even here. That, and the relative proximity to Estelore had an impact on the region, I'm sure." Coming from her? That's high praise. So, you take it she has no issues with her new home, then? Olivia holds up a clawed finger. "Ah, ah. I didn't say anything of the kind — there's always some jot or tittle that can be grouched over if one makes the effort to find it. What I did say is that it's satisfactory. It's clean, it's not an eyesore, and the people coming and going over the bridge are at least decent[wayfort.hasDaliza |. No doubt your garrison of elves keeps out the riff-raff. | by the local standards. At least they've bathed, which is more than what can be said for where I was. ]" From a musty hole in the ground to the lap of luxury: no doubt she considers it a step up in the world befitting her personage, then. All that being said... she's no intention of returning to Yvennes? "Not in the foreseeable future, Dearest. Maybe never." A sigh, and her expression turns serious. "Ever used that head of yours and wondered why someone like me would leave the center of high culture and come to this gods-forsaken corner of the world? No, obviously not. Something's going on in these parts, and a bunch of mangy dogs is the least of it. Events are afoot, and when I passed through Hawkethorne on my way here, I heard word that great holy armies are being amassed in Jassira and the old heartlands to march on this very region. "Now, I can't control the entire narrative — I'm well aware that there are others of my ilk who'll be telling different tales. But this is my chance to actually make my mark on history, tell the tale my way, be remembered. Be more than just a do-nothing in a corner of Yvennes. Call it a premonition or just plain luck, but that's the feeling I had months ago... and now it turns out I was right." That makes... a surprising lot of sense. Well, assuming that Olivia deems her thirst for fame to be worth it. "I won't deny that there're times that I regretted it, Dearest. For example, when it looked like I was going to be made into a fucktoy. But... everything's worked out in the end, so this was obviously the right thing to do. "And even if I did make it back to Yvennes, what then? I don't look like how I did when I left —" she gestures to her furred and clawed limbs — "and that means inconvenient questions. Also, what happened to the rest of my colleagues, answering questions about why they aren't with me isn't something I really want to do. "So no, I think I'll be staying here for a while. If anyone back home actually cares about me, he or she can come up all the way here to start looking." All right, if she's content with how things have turned out, you've no cause to complain, either. That being said, she's found somewhere to lie down, right? "Privately. This place has several empty chambers, and I appropriated one of them for myself; I need some privacy if I'm to reach my muse. I'm not bunking down with [wayfort.hasDaliza |your elves |the bee ], that's just disgusting. All those smells crammed into one room, it's enough to make a girl retch. I've had enough of that for an entire lifetime with those miserable dogs reeking." No more questions from you, then. Looks like Olivia's taken the initiative and gotten herself settled in the Wayfort quite nicely. ]

I'm not bunking down with [wayfort.hasDaliza |your elves |the bee ], that's just disgusting. All those smells crammed into one room, it's enough to make a girl retch. I've had enough of that for an entire lifetime with those miserable dogs reeking." No more questions from you, then. Looks like Olivia's taken the initiative and gotten herself settled in the Wayfort quite nicely. ] "

rows.original: And now, since she's done talking, it's time for you to lay down what you expect of her to earn her keep around the place. "I expected as much. You're not the kind to let me loaf around and drink your wine day in, day out. I suppose you'll want me to put my talents at your service?" What Asgeir intended to have her do, you want her to apply herself to in your service. Main difference is, she might even have pleasant conversation and better drink than what the corrupted lupines could provide. "I note the use of the word 'might'. [wayfort.stateABC |Perhaps 'almost certainly won't would be more accurate, but I'm hardly in a position to quibble. |Hedging your bets, aren't you? |Personally, I'd say 'probably', but I get what it means to underpromise and overdeliver ]. But sure, I can twist things in your favor, embellish a tale here and there." She'll have to do more than that, you're afraid. When she's on the job, you want her to put on that other face of hers. Charm and speak to anyone important coming through. Add a little entertainment when you hold court. Since she's interested in local events, she can tell you if anything of note's happening in the Marches. Olivia rolls her eyes. "You want me to play spymaster? Don't you think that's asking too much of a single girl?" Spymaster? No, she shouldn't be putting on such airs — maybe several years down the line when you're more established. For now, entertainment, conversation, and [pc.isDK |propagandizing |framing local events to paint you in a better light ]. She can handle as much. "Hmph." What's with the face? As you mentioned before, she was willing to sing Asgeir's praises — for a cause that she no doubt didn't believe in the slightest, for a man she despised enough to betray at the slightest notice. If her morals are flexible enough for that, no doubt she has no qualms about tooting the horn of [pc.isBaron |a local baron[pc.mf | |ness ] |a self-made [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ], right? Sure, you're not holding the threat of sexual slavery over her head like Asgeir was, but you'd rather prefer her to be doing this willingly than not. [wayfort.stateABC |Olivia scowls. "I have no qualms about doing my job, love. What I do resent is being asked to do my job without the proper tools. You want me to chat up anyone important who might be coming through? With the way your dump is, people might come to use your bridge, but they sure aren't going to stay any longer than they have to! "You can't ask me to sing your praises with a straight face while you're living in a dump — I can try, but every word that comes out of my mouth is going to ring false. I may have a pretty face, but it's not good enough to make people disbelieve their lying eyes when they look past me and see only cobwebs and rubble. You're not much of a [pc.isBaron |marcher-baron[pc.mf | |ness ] |local war[pc.mf |lord |lady ] ] if you're wallowing in a pigsty, for the gods' sake. It's like putting rouge on a pig." You shake your head. Given the way Olivia's knuckles are whitening about the stem of her wine glass, she's on the verge of tossing it to the ground [silly |and declaring the entire wayfort a miserable pile of secrets |in a fit of petulance ]. But for all her airs, she was willing to do it from a hole in the ground? "I hadn't gotten started yet, idiot. Did you see anyone who wasn't one of those mangy dogs around me when we met? I thought not. Asgeir was saving me up for after he'd forced a meet, moot, or whatever it was called, I don't fucking care; presumably we'd have moved out of that hole by then. I brought up the matter with him, and he just shrugged as if to say that was my problem. Well, it fucking wasn't, and it isn't now, either. If you want me to do my job, please provide me with the tools to get it done — or at least, those I didn't bring with me." And just so that you're not misunderstanding her, those tools would be...? "A pleasant environment would be ideal, but I'll settle for a clean one for now." She waggles a hand at the great hall about her. "Clear out the dust and cobwebs, mend the walls, get some decent furniture that isn't infested with either mold or bedbugs. Some decent lighting would be nice to set the mood, and to clear out the damp in the air. "There need to be some people in the background — other people coming through, maids, riff-raff you've picked up and decided to keep as pets, I don't care. People get uptight and antsy when the room gets too empty. It's like... what do they call it in Macah? Feng shui? Good aesthetics, that's the thing. Pleasant vibes. "And finally, something to drink that doesn't offend everyone's sensibilities. If all you have to offer around here is dregs that're barely above swill, little wonder that that bee of yours is barely covering her expenses. Please, I'm not loosening lips with this. This entire place used to be wine country — I know full well that the old empire went absolutely crazy over ice wine. Find some of that, or anything at all that tastes and smells decent. "So yes. I'll take this entire thing as seriously as you are, which currently is not very much so. I'll do what I can in the meantime, but don't expect wonders even from me when you can't be assed to set your own home in order. Asgeir and his mangy dogs didn't have any choice but to live in a hole in the ground; you damn well do." |"Oh, did I look less than pleased? Excuse me." Olivia smiles, or rather, turns up the corners of her lips. The end result is very deliberate, and just as fake. "There, is that better?" No. A sigh. Slouching in her seat, Olivia swirls the wine in her glass and regards it morosely. "Look... I have no qualms about doing my job; you're right in that I was going to do it for Asgeir. It's just that I'd like to have the best tools for the job at hand, you understand me? What you've here right now... is satisfactory. It'll do, but it's very aggressively mediocre, and while I'll do what I can I don't want mediocrity, and neither do you. Presumably. Convincing people that you're the bee's knees is going to be a lot easier when I'm able to back it up with the sights and sounds. You need to present yourself as a [pc.mf |man |woman ] of culture." And what does that mean, exactly? She isn't exactly in Yvennes any more, if she's noticed. "Funny you should bring up home. We have a saying in Yvennes that roughly translates to Belharan as 'to be complete in the twin arts of the sword and pen'. It's a lot snappier in the original language, I assure you. Asgeir was, is... a musclehead." She wrinkles her nose, dripping distaste. "Even if you hadn't come along, his stupid moot idea would've lasted as long as it took for either Tharsus, me, or anyone else to stab him in the back." Which she just did, and Tharsus was planning to do all along. "Ex-actly. It would never have worked out, and he fell victim to the idiotic might-makes-right philosophy that he claimed legitimacy by. I might've sung his praises a bit if it was that or be a fucktoy, but ultimately the words would've been unconvincing, hollow. You can't inspire genuine loyalty with a strong arm, Dearest — I'd be looking for the earliest opportunity to escape." You're starting to understand what Olivia's getting at — she wants you to spruce up the Wayfort, add a little decor here and there, make it pleasing to the eye. Air the place out a bit, make it a little less cold and foreboding, a little more inviting and filled with comfortable sights and scents. "Now we're on the same page. I'm not expecting you to turn this into a Mallachite boudoir, but it's possible to add a little color here and there without forgetting that this is supposed to be a fort with a military purpose. Embellishment gets harder the more outright lies you have to weave into the tale. Suggesting and leaving the mind to fill in the blanks is much more effective." You've patched up the stonework and cleaned up the place, so that's not a problem. Art, tapestries, some decent alcohol? Anything else she needs to have in order to do her job well? Olivia squints at you over her wine glass. "You're not stupid. You understand these things." [pc.bgMulti noblescion minstrel |You grew up in a noble household, so yes, you're aware of basic aesthetic sense. "I... how..." Olivia takes a deep breath and shakes her head. "No, don't tell me. I'd prefer to believe that you accept mediocrity because you're short on resources, far away and disconnected from your house, as opposed to accepting living under such conditions when you know you're worth more than that. I mean it, don't tell me." That's a pretty big overreaction, but if that's what she wants. |Of course you do. You used to perform for nobs all the time in their own homes; you know something about basic decoration and aesthetics. "Wait. If you..." Olivia's words trail off as she raises a finger and gesticulates hopelessly at the air. "Why the fuck do you need me when you can just do the job yourself, then?" Because she should know that you can't do these things for yourself; it's like trying to enjoy a novel that you've written. It just doesn't ring true, and you can't enjoy it. |You do? Well, you've experienced a lot of things since winding up in the Marches. Olivia shrugs. "One of the things I heard about you in Hawkethorne is that you pick up on things pretty quickly, so sure, I can buy that." It's a little odd that she's taking your words at face value just like that, but sure. ] "Oh, whatever. Your great hall isn't the worst, I'll admit. That being said, you could stand to let a few people in at all times, unless you're holding audiences, court, or something. Give it a bit of life, help people feel at ease and loosen their tongues. This isn't enough, it needs to feel... hmm... lived-in, for lack of a better word." |Olivia arches an eyebrow. "Come again? Do I really look upset? I'm fairly content with how things have turned out, and as it stands I'm a pretty difficult woman to please, just so you know. You should take pride in the fact that you've managed it." [pc.isDK |Okay, so she's not mad, she just has a bad case of resting bitch face. Got it. |All right, so the tales were true. If you keep on making that face, it does get frozen that way. ] "Hmph. If this seat weren't so comfortable and I weren't worried about spilling this wine, I'd..." Olivia thinks a moment, then her expression brightens, gracing you with what by all appearances is a genuine smile. "Know what? Never mind. No point spoiling a good thing with a petty slapfight. I'll admit that I was skeptical about your promise to put me up in this wayfort of yours, but now that I'm here... well, one can always find something to complain about if one's sufficiently motivated, but you've managed to put me off nitpicking. "Look, I have no qualms about doing my job; you're right in that I was going to do it for Asgeir. And here? You've given me all the tools I need for the job before I even asked for them, which is far more than the meathead ever gave me. So thank you for that: make my job easy, and in return you'll get all the embellishment that's within reason. Convincing people that you're the bee's knees is going to be a lot easier when I'm able to back it up with a kernel of truth." Things may not be exactly to her taste, but that's only to be expected. Any suggestions for improvement? "I'd love to be able to get my hands on some of the local elven wine. Apparently it was really big in the heartlands a couple centuries ago, one of those imports that wasn't just notable because it came from far away, but was genuinely good. That's a tiny thing, though. Look, I'm not saying that you should rest on your laurels, Dearest, but you've got a genuinely good thing going on here. For example, it's actually clean when most people in this part of the world think taking a bath every few days to a week is just fine. Look at the hall around you — it's nice and filled with warm colors, compared to the miserable chill outside. "People are drawn to these walls, even if they don't know it, want to sit down and relax a little, become... suggestible. You could stand to let a few more people in at all times, unless you're holding audiences, court, or something. Give it a bit of life, help people feel at ease and loosen their tongues. This isn't enough, it needs to feel... hmm... lived-in, for lack of a better word. Don't open it to the public, but for those living here, it's good to be reminded of just who the baron[pc.mf | |ness ] is on a daily basis, right? "At the same time, there's no doubt that this is a fort with military value[wayfort.hasDaliza |, what with your garrisoned elves goose-stepping all over the place ]. Strength in beauty, like a wild rose." ]
rows.translation: 现在，既然她已经说完了，是时候让你说明一下，你希望她做些什么才能继续在这里生活下去。 “我本来就预料到会这样。你不是那种会任由我整天无所事事、喝你的酒的人。我想你应该是希望我运用自己的能力来为你服务吧？” 阿斯盖尔想要她做的事情，其实就是希望她能为自己效力。不同的是，她带来的可能不仅仅是帮助，还可能有愉快的交谈，以及比那些被腐蚀的狼族所能提供的更好的饮品。 我注意到了‘might’这个词的使用。 [wayfort.stateABC |或许说“几乎可以肯定不会”会更加准确，但我实在没有资格去争论这一点。 |你在分散风险，不是吗？ |就我个人而言，我会说“大概吧”，但我理解那种先低调承诺、最后超额完成的效果是什么。 ]不过当然，我可以把事情往对你有利的方向歪曲，再添油加醋地编些故事。” 不过，恐怕她需要做的不止这些。当她工作的时候，你希望她能展现出另一面——那种迷人的、能够吸引任何重要人物的形象。在开会的时候，不妨加些娱乐元素。既然她对当地的活动很感兴趣，那么她就可以告诉你边境地区有没有什么值得关注的事情发生。 奥利维亚翻了个白眼：“你想让我扮演间谍头目？你难道不觉得这对一个女孩子来说要求太高了吗？间谍大师？”不，她现在还不应该摆出这种架子——也许等几年后，等你的事业更加稳固了，再这样也好。目前来说，娱乐、聊天，就可以了。 [pc.isDK |进行宣传推广 |通过描绘一些当地的事件来让你显得更加优秀。 ]她能承受这么多。” “哼。” 她那副表情是什么意思？正如你之前所说，她愿意为某个她根本不相信的理由，为那个她厌恶到会随时背叛他的男人，去赞美阿斯盖尔。如果她的道德标准真的那么灵活的话，那么她肯定也不会对为这样的人吹嘘鼓掌感到有任何愧疚吧。 [pc.isBaron |当地的贵族[pc.mf | |特性 ] |白手起家的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]对吧？当然，你并没有像阿斯盖尔那样用性奴役的威胁来逼迫她，但你更希望她是出于自愿才这么做，而不是被迫的。 [wayfort.stateABC |奥利维亚皱起了眉头：“我做自己的工作可从没有一丝犹豫，亲爱的。我只是确实你们让我做我的工作，却没有提供必要的工具。你们想让我去搭讪那些可能会经过的重要人物吗？以你们那个破烂的地方来看，人们可能会来使用你们的“桥梁”，但他们肯定不会在那里待太久！ “你们让自己住在这么破烂的地方，却还要求我面带微笑地夸赞你们——这我可做不到。尝试一下吧。但我说的每一句话都会显得虚假可笑。我或许有一张漂亮的脸，但这并不足以让人们在看到我背后的蛛网与废墟时，仍然不相信他们自己的眼睛。你也不是什么了不起的人[pc.isBaron |领主骑士[pc.mf | |特性 ] |局部战争[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]如果你一直待在肮脏的环境里，看在诸神的份上，那简直就像在猪身上涂胭脂一样。” 你摇了摇头。看奥利维亚握着酒杯的手指都快变白了，她随时都可能把酒杯扔到地上。 [silly |并宣称整个韦斯特福特其实只是一堆令人痛苦的秘密罢了。 |一时冲动之下 ]可尽管她摆出一副高人一等的样子，其实她也是愿意从地洞里爬出来去做这件事的吧？” “我还没开始呢，白痴。我们见面的时候，你看到我身边有除了那些脏兮兮的狗之外的其他人吗？我想没有吧。阿斯盖尔本来打算等强行安排了那次会面、讨论会，或者不管那叫什么之后再跟我谈这件事，但我他妈才不在乎呢；反正到那时候，我们应该已经摆脱了那个困境吧。我跟他提起了这个事情，他只是耸了耸肩，好像在说这是我的问题似的。哼，根本不是这样，现在也依然不是。如果你想让我好好完成工作，那就请提供我所需的工具——至少是那些我没有带过来的工具。” 顺便说一下，为了避免你们误解她的意思，这些工具确实是必不可少的。一个舒适的环境当然是理想的，但就算没有也能接受。干净先就这些吧。”她朝周围的大厅挥了挥手，“把灰尘和蜘蛛网清理干净，修补墙壁，再购置一些既没有霉菌也没有臭虫的合格家具。安装一些不错的照明设备，既能营造良好的氛围，也能消除空气中的潮湿气息。 房间里总需要有一些人在场——那些偶尔出现的人，女仆们，还有一些你收留下来当作宠物的人，我都不在乎。当房间里太安静时，人们就会变得紧张不安，就是这个道理。在马卡哈，他们把这种东西叫什么来着？风水良好的审美效果，这才是关键。整体氛围也要让人感到愉悦。” “最后，还需要提供一些不会冒犯任何人感官的饮品。如果这里提供的都只是连糟粕都算不上的东西，那就难怪你们的‘蜜蜂’连基本开销都难以维持了。拜托，我可不是随便说说而已。这个地方原本可是盛产葡萄酒的地区——我非常清楚，那个古老的帝国对冰酒简直痴迷到了极点。想办法弄些冰酒来，或者任何味道和气味都还算不错的酒都行。 所以，是的。我会像你一样认真对待这件事——不过目前你的态度似乎并不怎么认真。在这段时间里，我会尽我所能，但如果你连自己的生活都整理不好，也别指望我能创造什么奇迹。阿斯盖尔和他的那些脏兮兮的狗们别无选择，只能住在地洞里；你也是同样的处境啊。 |哦，我看起来是不是不太高兴？对不起。”奥利维亚笑了笑，或者说，只是微微扬起了嘴角。这个表情显然是刻意做出来的，显得非常做作。“这样，好些了吗？” “并没有。” 她叹了口气。奥利维亚瘫坐在椅子上，轻轻摇晃着杯中的葡萄酒，神情忧郁地望着它。“听着……我对完成自己的工作没有任何怨言；你说得对，我本来确实是打算为阿斯盖尔去做这件事的。只是，我希望自己能拥有完成这项工作所需的最佳工具，你明白我的意思吗？你现在所拥有的……就是令人满意还行吧，但实在平庸得有些过分了。虽然我会尽力去改进，不过……还是觉得效果不太理想。想要平庸之人，你大概也是吧。不过，当我能够用视觉和听觉效果来证明你的实力时，说服别人你确实非常出色就会容易得多。你得把自己塑造成一个[pc.mf |男人 |女性 ]的文化那么，这到底意味着什么呢？如果她注意到了的话，她其实已经不再属于伊文尼斯了。 “有趣，你竟然提到了‘家’。在伊文尼斯，我们有一句谚语，用贝尔哈兰的语言来说，大致意思是‘在剑术与笔术这两门技艺上达到完美境界’。我向你保证，用原语言表达会显得更加简洁有力。阿斯盖尔，过去是，现在依然是……个蠢货。她皱起鼻子，露出不屑的神情：“就算你没有出现，他那个愚蠢的主意也会一直持续下去，直到塔苏斯、我，或者其他人中的任何一个出手背叛他为止。她刚刚就这么做了，而萨鲁斯从一开始就打算这么做。 “正是这样。那样的做法根本行不通，他只是陷入了那种自以为理直气壮的愚蠢哲学之中，才落得了这样的下场。如果真是那样的话，我或许会过分夸赞他，或者干脆成为他的傀儡，但那样的话，我说出的话也必然缺乏说服力，空洞无物。亲爱的，你无法用武力来换取真正的忠诚——我只会寻找机会尽快逃离。你现在开始明白奥利维亚的意图了——她希望你能让荒废驿堡这个地方变得更加美观一些，在这里那里添加一些装饰，让它看起来更赏心悦目。让这个地方空气流通一些，减少那种寒冷和阴森的气氛，让它变得更加温馨，充满舒适的感觉和宜人的气息。 "现在我们意见一致。我并不指望你把这里变成一个华丽的闺房，但适当添加一些装饰元素也是可以的，只要记住这里本来就是一座具有军事用途的堡垒。不过，当你不得不在故事中编造一些明显的谎言时，装饰就会变得越发困难。相比之下，只是给出一些暗示，让读者自己去填补空白，效果会好得多。 你已经修好了石墙，也把这里清理得干干净净，所以那就是没问题。艺术品、挂毯，再准备些不错的酒？还有其他她开展工作所需要的东西吗？ 奥利维亚透过酒杯眯着眼睛看着你：“你并不傻，这些事情你肯定明白的。 [pc.bgMulti noblescion minstrel |你在一个贵族家庭中长大，所以，你当然具备基本的审美观念。 “我……这怎么可能……”奥利维亚深吸一口气，然后摇了摇头。“不，别告诉我。我宁愿相信，你之所以接受这种平庸的东西，只是因为资源匮乏，地处偏远，与你的家族失去了联系，而不是明知自己值得更好的生活，却甘愿接受这样的环境。我是认真的，别跟我说谎。 这样的反应未免有些过激了，但如果那就是她想要的，那也没办法。 |你当然懂。你以前经常在那些人的家里为他们表演，所以你对基本的装饰和审美风格肯定有所了解。 “等等……如果你……”奥利维亚的话突然中断了，她举起手指，绝望地朝空气中比划着。“如果你自己就能完成这项工作，那你究竟为什么还需要我呢？” 因为她你应该明白，这些事情是你自己无法完成的；这就好比试图去欣赏自己写的那本小说一样——根本感觉不到真实感，也就无法从中获得乐趣。 |你这么认为吗？嗯，自从来到这些边境地区以来，你确实经历了很多事情。 奥利维亚耸了耸肩：“在鹰棘镇，我听说你很善于观察周围的事物，所以我觉得你说得有道理。” 她竟然这么直接地相信你的话，有点奇怪吧，不过也没关系。 ] 哦，算了。我得承认，你的大厅确实不算太差。不过，你还是应该让一些人随时都能进入这里，除非你正在举行宴会或者举行什么正式的仪式。这样能让大厅显得更有生机，让人们感到放松，从而更愿意开口说话。现在这样还不够，这个地方需要给人一种……嗯……生活气息十足的感觉，实在找不到更好的词来形容了。 |奥利维亚挑了挑眉毛：“你说什么？我看起来真的不高兴吗？其实我对目前的发展结果相当满意，而且说实话，要取悦我是一件相当困难的事，你最好记住这一点。你能做到这一点，应该感到自豪才对。 [pc.isDK |好吧，其实她并没有生气，只是摆出了一副“生闷气”的表情而已。明白了。 |好吧，原来那些故事都是真的。如果你继续做出那种表情的话确实就这样被冻住了。 ] 哼，要不是这个座位这么舒服，也不担心会把酒洒出来，我就会……”奥利维亚思考了一会儿，然后她的表情突然变得明亮起来，露出一个看起来非常真诚的微笑。“你知道吗？没关系。用一些琐碎的争执来破坏这么美好的事情实在没有必要。我必须承认，当初对你承诺会用这种方式安排我住下时，我其实持怀疑态度，但既然我现在已经到了这里……嗯，只要有心找茬，总能找到一些可抱怨的地方，不过你确实让我没有理由再去挑剔了。 听着，我做这份工作毫无怨言；你说得对，我当初确实是为了阿斯盖尔才去做这份工作的。但现在呢？你们甚至在我还没有提出要求之前，就为我提供了完成工作所需的一切资源，这远远超过了那个笨蛋曾经给过我的东西。所以，真的非常感谢你们：让我的工作变得如此轻松。作为回报，你们会得到所有合理的装饰和点缀。当我的话能够有事实依据作为支撑时，让别人相信你们确实是无可挑剔的，就会容易得多。事情可能并不会像预期的那样发展。正好这正是她所喜欢的，不过这也情有可原。有没有什么改进的建议呢？ “我真的很想尝尝那些当地的精灵葡萄酒。据说在几个世纪前，这种酒在内陆地区非常受欢迎，它不仅因为产自远方而备受瞩目，其品质也确实上乘。不过，这也只是个小细节而已。亲爱的，我并不是说你应该因此而满足于现状，但你目前做的事情确实做得很好。比如说干净在这个地区，大多数人认为每隔几天到一周洗一次澡就已经足够了。看看你周围的这个大厅吧——与外面刺骨的寒冷相比，这里非常舒适，充满了温暖的色调。 人们会被这些墙壁吸引，即使他们自己也没有意识到这一点，他们会想要坐下来休息一会儿，变得……更容易接受外界的影响。除非你正在举办演出、举行会议之类的活动，否则你完全可以随时让更多的人进入这些空间。让它充满生机，让人们感到放松，敢于开口说话。这样还不够，它还需要给人一种……嗯……仿佛真正有人居住在那里的感觉，虽然找不到更合适的词来形容。不要对公众开放，但对于那些生活在这里的人来说，这样的环境能让他们清楚地记住，这位男爵究竟是一个怎样的人。[pc.mf | |特性 ]这是每天都在发生的事情，对吧？ “同时，毫无疑问，这座堡垒具有军事价值。[wayfort.hasDaliza |你的那些驻扎在各地的精灵们不都是整整齐齐地列队行进吗？ ]美丽中蕴含着力量，就像野玫瑰一样。 ]
rows.raw: " And now, since she's done talking, it's time for you to lay down what you expect of her to earn her keep around the place. "I expected as much. You're not the kind to let me loaf around and drink your wine day in, day out. I suppose you'll want me to put my talents at your service?" What Asgeir intended to have her do, you want her to apply herself to in your service. Main difference is, she might even have pleasant conversation and better drink than what the corrupted lupines could provide. "I note the use of the word 'might'. [wayfort.stateABC |Perhaps 'almost certainly won't would be more accurate, but I'm hardly in a position to quibble. |Hedging your bets, aren't you? |Personally, I'd say 'probably', but I get what it means to underpromise and overdeliver ]. But sure, I can twist things in your favor, embellish a tale here and there." She'll have to do more than that, you're afraid. When she's on the job, you want her to put on that other face of hers. Charm and speak to anyone important coming through. Add a little entertainment when you hold court. Since she's interested in local events, she can tell you if anything of note's happening in the Marches. Olivia rolls her eyes. "You want me to play spymaster? Don't you think that's asking too much of a single girl?" Spymaster? No, she shouldn't be putting on such airs — maybe several years down the line when you're more established. For now, entertainment, conversation, and [pc.isDK |propagandizing |framing local events to paint you in a better light ]. She can handle as much. "Hmph." What's with the face? As you mentioned before, she was willing to sing Asgeir's praises — for a cause that she no doubt didn't believe in the slightest, for a man she despised enough to betray at the slightest notice. If her morals are flexible enough for that, no doubt she has no qualms about tooting the horn of [pc.isBaron |a local baron[pc.mf | |ness ] |a self-made [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ], right? Sure, you're not holding the threat of sexual slavery over her head like Asgeir was, but you'd rather prefer her to be doing this willingly than not. [wayfort.stateABC |Olivia scowls. "I have no qualms about doing my job, love. What I do resent is being asked to do my job without the proper tools. You want me to chat up anyone important who might be coming through? With the way your dump is, people might come to use your bridge, but they sure aren't going to stay any longer than they have to! "You can't ask me to sing your praises with a straight face while you're living in a dump — I can try, but every word that comes out of my mouth is going to ring false. I may have a pretty face, but it's not good enough to make people disbelieve their lying eyes when they look past me and see only cobwebs and rubble. You're not much of a [pc.isBaron |marcher-baron[pc.mf | |ness ] |local war[pc.mf |lord |lady ] ] if you're wallowing in a pigsty, for the gods' sake. It's like putting rouge on a pig." You shake your head. Given the way Olivia's knuckles are whitening about the stem of her wine glass, she's on the verge of tossing it to the ground [silly |and declaring the entire wayfort a miserable pile of secrets |in a fit of petulance ]. But for all her airs, she was willing to do it from a hole in the ground? "I hadn't gotten started yet, idiot. Did you see anyone who wasn't one of those mangy dogs around me when we met? I thought not. Asgeir was saving me up for after he'd forced a meet, moot, or whatever it was called, I don't fucking care; presumably we'd have moved out of that hole by then. I brought up the matter with him, and he just shrugged as if to say that was my problem. Well, it fucking wasn't, and it isn't now, either. If you want me to do my job, please provide me with the tools to get it done — or at least, those I didn't bring with me." And just so that you're not misunderstanding her, those tools would be...? "A pleasant environment would be ideal, but I'll settle for a clean one for now." She waggles a hand at the great hall about her. "Clear out the dust and cobwebs, mend the walls, get some decent furniture that isn't infested with either mold or bedbugs. Some decent lighting would be nice to set the mood, and to clear out the damp in the air. "There need to be some people in the background — other people coming through, maids, riff-raff you've picked up and decided to keep as pets, I don't care. People get uptight and antsy when the room gets too empty. It's like... what do they call it in Macah? Feng shui? Good aesthetics, that's the thing. Pleasant vibes. "And finally, something to drink that doesn't offend everyone's sensibilities. If all you have to offer around here is dregs that're barely above swill, little wonder that that bee of yours is barely covering her expenses. Please, I'm not loosening lips with this. This entire place used to be wine country — I know full well that the old empire went absolutely crazy over ice wine. Find some of that, or anything at all that tastes and smells decent. "So yes. I'll take this entire thing as seriously as you are, which currently is not very much so. I'll do what I can in the meantime, but don't expect wonders even from me when you can't be assed to set your own home in order. Asgeir and his mangy dogs didn't have any choice but to live in a hole in the ground; you damn well do." |"Oh, did I look less than pleased? Excuse me." Olivia smiles, or rather, turns up the corners of her lips. The end result is very deliberate, and just as fake. "There, is that better?" No. A sigh. Slouching in her seat, Olivia swirls the wine in her glass and regards it morosely. "Look... I have no qualms about doing my job; you're right in that I was going to do it for Asgeir. It's just that I'd like to have the best tools for the job at hand, you understand me? What you've here right now... is satisfactory. It'll do, but it's very aggressively mediocre, and while I'll do what I can I don't want mediocrity, and neither do you. Presumably. Convincing people that you're the bee's knees is going to be a lot easier when I'm able to back it up with the sights and sounds. You need to present yourself as a [pc.mf |man |woman ] of culture." And what does that mean, exactly? She isn't exactly in Yvennes any more, if she's noticed. "Funny you should bring up home. We have a saying in Yvennes that roughly translates to Belharan as 'to be complete in the twin arts of the sword and pen'. It's a lot snappier in the original language, I assure you. Asgeir was, is... a musclehead." She wrinkles her nose, dripping distaste. "Even if you hadn't come along, his stupid moot idea would've lasted as long as it took for either Tharsus, me, or anyone else to stab him in the back." Which she just did, and Tharsus was planning to do all along. "Ex-actly. It would never have worked out, and he fell victim to the idiotic might-makes-right philosophy that he claimed legitimacy by. I might've sung his praises a bit if it was that or be a fucktoy, but ultimately the words would've been unconvincing, hollow. You can't inspire genuine loyalty with a strong arm, Dearest — I'd be looking for the earliest opportunity to escape." You're starting to understand what Olivia's getting at — she wants you to spruce up the Wayfort, add a little decor here and there, make it pleasing to the eye. Air the place out a bit, make it a little less cold and foreboding, a little more inviting and filled with comfortable sights and scents. "Now we're on the same page. I'm not expecting you to turn this into a Mallachite boudoir, but it's possible to add a little color here and there without forgetting that this is supposed to be a fort with a military purpose. Embellishment gets harder the more outright lies you have to weave into the tale. Suggesting and leaving the mind to fill in the blanks is much more effective." You've patched up the stonework and cleaned up the place, so that's not a problem. Art, tapestries, some decent alcohol? Anything else she needs to have in order to do her job well? Olivia squints at you over her wine glass. "You're not stupid. You understand these things." [pc.bgMulti noblescion minstrel |You grew up in a noble household, so yes, you're aware of basic aesthetic sense. "I... how..." Olivia takes a deep breath and shakes her head. "No, don't tell me. I'd prefer to believe that you accept mediocrity because you're short on resources, far away and disconnected from your house, as opposed to accepting living under such conditions when you know you're worth more than that. I mean it, don't tell me." That's a pretty big overreaction, but if that's what she wants. |Of course you do. You used to perform for nobs all the time in their own homes; you know something about basic decoration and aesthetics. "Wait. If you..." Olivia's words trail off as she raises a finger and gesticulates hopelessly at the air. "Why the fuck do you need me when you can just do the job yourself, then?" Because she should know that you can't do these things for yourself; it's like trying to enjoy a novel that you've written. It just doesn't ring true, and you can't enjoy it. |You do? Well, you've experienced a lot of things since winding up in the Marches. Olivia shrugs. "One of the things I heard about you in Hawkethorne is that you pick up on things pretty quickly, so sure, I can buy that." It's a little odd that she's taking your words at face value just like that, but sure. ] "Oh, whatever. Your great hall isn't the worst, I'll admit. That being said, you could stand to let a few people in at all times, unless you're holding audiences, court, or something. Give it a bit of life, help people feel at ease and loosen their tongues. This isn't enough, it needs to feel... hmm... lived-in, for lack of a better word." |Olivia arches an eyebrow. "Come again? Do I really look upset? I'm fairly content with how things have turned out, and as it stands I'm a pretty difficult woman to please, just so you know. You should take pride in the fact that you've managed it." [pc.isDK |Okay, so she's not mad, she just has a bad case of resting bitch face. Got it. |All right, so the tales were true. If you keep on making that face, it does get frozen that way. ] "Hmph. If this seat weren't so comfortable and I weren't worried about spilling this wine, I'd..." Olivia thinks a moment, then her expression brightens, gracing you with what by all appearances is a genuine smile. "Know what? Never mind. No point spoiling a good thing with a petty slapfight. I'll admit that I was skeptical about your promise to put me up in this wayfort of yours, but now that I'm here... well, one can always find something to complain about if one's sufficiently motivated, but you've managed to put me off nitpicking. "Look, I have no qualms about doing my job; you're right in that I was going to do it for Asgeir. And here? You've given me all the tools I need for the job before I even asked for them, which is far more than the meathead ever gave me. So thank you for that: make my job easy, and in return you'll get all the embellishment that's within reason. Convincing people that you're the bee's knees is going to be a lot easier when I'm able to back it up with a kernel of truth." Things may not be exactly to her taste, but that's only to be expected. Any suggestions for improvement? "I'd love to be able to get my hands on some of the local elven wine. Apparently it was really big in the heartlands a couple centuries ago, one of those imports that wasn't just notable because it came from far away, but was genuinely good. That's a tiny thing, though. Look, I'm not saying that you should rest on your laurels, Dearest, but you've got a genuinely good thing going on here. For example, it's actually clean when most people in this part of the world think taking a bath every few days to a week is just fine. Look at the hall around you — it's nice and filled with warm colors, compared to the miserable chill outside. "People are drawn to these walls, even if they don't know it, want to sit down and relax a little, become... suggestible. You could stand to let a few more people in at all times, unless you're holding audiences, court, or something. Give it a bit of life, help people feel at ease and loosen their tongues. This isn't enough, it needs to feel... hmm... lived-in, for lack of a better word. Don't open it to the public, but for those living here, it's good to be reminded of just who the baron[pc.mf | |ness ] is on a daily basis, right? "At the same time, there's no doubt that this is a fort with military value[wayfort.hasDaliza |, what with your garrisoned elves goose-stepping all over the place ]. Strength in beauty, like a wild rose." ] "

rows.original: All right, you think you've heard all you want to hear from Olivia for now. While you do wish she'd been a little more discreet about her arrival than just showing up and claiming a place at the table, that's your own fault: you knew what kind of creature she was when you first met. "Just so. Well, if you ever want to find me, you know where to look. It's not like my job is one with regular hours." Olivia snaps her fingers, and [var0 |another of the wayfort's numerous maids comes trundling in with a refill. Olivia's demeanor flips seamlessly in the blink of an eye, cooing and fussing over the maid as the wine is poured; she heaps praise upon how absolutely authentic the maid dress is and how much it really is like those back at home. |yet another of the corrupted lupines comes sidling over with a refill. Olivia's demeanor flips seamlessly in the blink of an eye, fussing warmly over the silly dog as the wine is poured; it's amazing how much she can get out of the weak-minded with a little bit of praise or the implication of sexual favors that will never materialize. |Rumie comes trundling back in with a refill. Olivia's demeanor flips seamlessly in the blink of an eye, turning all petulant and bossy; she's never outright cruel to your bee-tender, but acts just stuck-up and indignant enough to push all of Rumie's bulliable buttons even as the wine is poured. ] Frankly, it's a little sickening to watch, even if you know you hired this yappy little dog precisely because of how two-faced she is. Well, you knew what you were getting into: for better or for worse, Olivia's going to be a permanent fixture in your grand hall going forward. No regrets, right? [var1 |"Before you go, Dearest, one last thing. You borrowed my spellsinger back in that hole, and now that everything's over, I'd like to have it back. If you didn't already notice, this bard needs an instrument to do her job, and even if I had another one I was pretty clear that it means a lot to me. Sentimental value — you do understand, right?" Olivia holds out her free hand expectantly, beckoning with her fingers. You look at the spellsinger amongst your things, and sigh. Imagining that Olivia would conveniently forget about her most prized possession in all the confusion was a long shot, but it was a nice hope while it lasted. "Oh ho ho. I can see that you've grown quite attached to it, and I do empathise, my dear. Nevertheless, I must insist. Tell you what, Dearest: if you've taken a shine to the spellsinger, I can get you something just as good as a gift to fill in the hole it's going to leave in your heart. Call it a gesture of goodwill to commemorate our new working relationship. How does that sound?" Decently. All right, she can have it back. You hand over the electrum flute, and watch Olivia coo and fuss over it as if it were a puppy. At last, she stows it away, then turns back to you. "Thank you, Dearest. I genuinely do appreciate you actually taking the trouble to keep it much as when you borrowed it; you didn't know whether you'd ever see me again, yet hung onto it and kept it in decent shape. The group I came up north with would've pawned it off for drinking money at the first opportunity if they thought they could get away with it. "Don't think I won't remember this... or my promise of a gift. The world could use a little more mindfulness here and there." ]
rows.translation: 好吧，你觉得自己现在已经听够了奥利维亚说的话。虽然你确实希望她在到来的时候能更谨慎一些，而不是一出现就直接坐到桌旁，但这也是你自己的错：在第一次见到她的时候，你就知道她是什么样的人。 “就这样吧。嗯，如果你以后想找我的话，你知道该去哪里找。毕竟我的工作并没有固定的工作时间。”奥利维亚打了个响指，说道。 [var0 |韦弗特家的众多女仆中又有一位端着补酒走了进来。奥利维亚的态度瞬间发生了彻底的变化——当酒被倒出来时，她开始对这位女仆百般呵护、温柔对待，还不停地夸赞她多么优秀真实的这条女仆装，真的和家里那些一模一样啊。 |又有一只被“洗脑”了的狼犬摇摇摆摆地走过来，带着补充的酒水。奥利维亚的态度瞬间发生了彻底的变化——当酒被倒出来时，她开始温柔地照料这只傻乎乎的狗。真是不可思议，只要稍微给予一些表扬，或者暗示一些永远不会实现的性暗示，她就能让这些意志薄弱的人做出这样的反应。 |露米摇摇晃晃地拿着补货回来。奥利维亚的态度瞬间发生了翻天覆地的变化，变得任性又专横起来；她虽然从未对你的贴心人表现出刻薄的言行，但她的傲慢与不满已经足以触怒露米，哪怕在酒被倒出来的那一刻也是如此。 ] 说实话，看着这种场面真的有点让人反感，尤其是当你明知自己雇用这个嘴碎又虚伪的小东西，正是看中了她这种两面派的性格。不过，你当初也是清楚自己会遇到什么情况的：不管结果是好是坏，从现在起，奥利维亚都将永远成为你大厅里的一道“风景”。应该没有什么后悔的吧？ [var1 |在你离开之前，亲爱的，还有一件事。你之前在那个地方借走了我的咒歌者，现在一切都结束了，我希望把它还回来。如果你还没注意到的话，这位吟游诗人需要一件乐器来表演，而且即使我还有另一件乐器，我也非常清楚它对我来说意义重大——这是一种情感上的寄托，你应该能理解吧？ 奥利维亚满怀期待地伸出空着的手，用手指向你示意。 你看着自己物品堆中的那件咒歌者，叹了口气。本来就觉得奥利维亚在这么混乱的情况下会不小心忘记自己最珍视的东西，这种希望其实很渺茫，但只要这种希望还存在，就总归是美好的。 哦呵呵，我看你已经对它产生了深厚的感情，我真的很能理解你的感受，亲爱的。不过，我还是坚持要这么做。这样吧，我最亲爱的：如果你真的喜欢上了那件咒歌者，我可以送你一样同样珍贵的礼物，来填补你心中留下的空缺。就当作是我们新建立的合作关系的一种象征吧。你觉得怎么样？ 还行吧。好吧，她可以把那个东西拿回去。你把那支电银笛交给她，然后看着奥利维亚像照顾小狗一样细心地照料它。最后，她把笛子收好，再回到你身边。 “谢谢你，亲爱的。我真心感谢你竟然费心把它保管得和你借走时一样好；你当时甚至不知道是否还能再见到我，但还是把它留了下来，并且保持在了良好的状态。如果是我那些一起北上的人，他们一有机会就会把它当掉换酒喝，因为他们觉得这样就能蒙混过关。 别以为我会忘记这件事……还有我承诺送的礼物。这个世界上，确实需要更多的人们能够多一些善意与关怀。 ]

If anything, your bee-tender is rather disappointed that your court bard's imperious hysteria has vanished now that the puppy's out of her belly — it's as if all the evil bitchiness has left her body along with the child, leaving poor Rumie thoroughly unsatisfied with this state of affairs. "Rumie, more wine, if you would please." "Yes, Mistress Leroux." You can just hear the sigh in Rumie's voice as she refills Olivia's glass, especially at the %"please". At length, the both of them notice you, and Olivia waves you over. "Oh, fancy seeing you here, Dearest." This is your home. "Yes, but you're away so often. Not that it's unexpected given everything that's been happening in this benighted corner of the world as of late, but... you know." Yes, you know. Sighing, you look between Olivia and Rumie, then dismiss the latter with a wave of your hand. Nodding, your bee-tender bows, then makes to withdraw. "I'll give the both of you some space, then." Olivia watches Rumie retreat, then shrugs. "Oh, don't look at me like that, Dearest. I know what she's here for, but I just can't work myself up to being absolutely wretched to her like she's so desperately hoping for. I just don't have it in me any more, I'm afraid." You can tell. It's going to take a little while to get used to Olivia as she is... for now, anyway. Who knows what might happen the next time around, if a little piece of the old her might come back? "Oh, there won't be a next time around so easily, let me tell you that. But we're getting sidetracked. Was there something you wanted of me, Dearest?" ] |As you approach Olivia, you find her busy entertaining several well-dressed people at the table; she's got out several small shots of wine and a plate of cheese and crackers, yapping away animatedly and giving the impression of a small but very noisy dog. Well, she's not so small any more, and it shows in both her demeanor and her guests' reactions — a mature lady despite her petite stature — she's more serious these days, her imperiousness having exchanged flighty hysteria for unreasonable gravitas. Noticing you draw close, Olivia's guests part like water around a rock, falling away to the other tables and giving the both of you your space. "Hello, Dearest." Hope you're not interrupting anything. She seemed to be enjoying herself, especially now that she can drink again. "Oh no, it was just wrapping up anyway. Because let me tell you, while it's just right for how this part of the world it, it's not exactly great for when it comes to entertaining guests... "...Or for pups to grow up in, for that matter." You don't know about that. This is the kind of place where dark, brooding, humorless lords are born and raised. Olivia rolls her eyes and sighs, folding her arms under her huge, milky tits. "Please don't say that even in jest, Dearest. I'd rather not even entertain the idea that I might've birthed another Asgeir. Being a mirthless wretch is no way to go through life." All right, all right. You get her point. |Now that I'm a lot lighter on my feet, I'm back at the job — and how so. Considering the differences between then and now, it's quite obvious people in this part of the world prefer their women more... thickset, shall we say?" Now that she mentions it, the difference is quite stark: Olivia used to be a lot more slender and lopsided from her corruption, but at least she's more balanced both above and below. Nature tries to re-assert itself despite what was done to her, it seems. "I'd make a dry joke about me being more charismatic after having put on several pounds of puppy fat, but it wouldn't be a joke at this point." Olivia sighs. "Hey, at least people agree I look better this way as opposed to being a bimbo, and that already gave me a pretty good draw." Is she getting back into her old business of leading people around by the nose, then? |I think that lot was warmly surprised to find a bit of comfort in these miserable wilds. If this weren't a military installation first and foremost, I'd suggest letting out accommodation in any spare rooms you have." Hey, that doesn't stop people passing through from filling up the courtyard at night. It can get quite ridiculous at times. "When even your courtyard is more inviting than some of the so-called accommodation the Marches has to offer." Olivia sips her wine and smiles. "I think this is a nice place for our son to grow up. A small splash of color on the river, with eternal grey dreariness just outside one's door. Kind of like Yvennes, and Claremont in particular." That's... an interesting way to put it. "A small bastion of sanity... and the eternal threat of misery at one's gates lest one be tempted to grow soft, that's what I mean. The best of both worlds, much like where I grew up myself. Our son won't turn into a brooding humorless brute like Asgeir was — he'll be able to tell a joke. I swear by the gods, I'll make sure of it myself the moment he can speak, or else." As it happens, you've come just in time to catch the tail end of her show — as the crowd moves to disperse, Olivia readies to chat up a couple of likely prospects, then notices you and you're instantly the focus of her attention. "Oh, Dearest. Fancy you showing up now." Why, that was quite the tune she was playing just now. It was almost cheerful, you daresay — something that the old Olivia would never have managed. "...You know, Dearest, I can't argue with that. I've tried to work myself up to deal with certain annoyances around the wayfort of late, and —" she snaps her fingers — "the spite just won't come." Oh, and she's self-aware too. The old Olivia would never have known she'd changed to begin with. "Now, Dearest. Don't push it." Heh. But in the end... it's turned out for the better as a whole, right? People like her more now, and that's a good thing given the job you've set her to. Putting on a show face all the time has to be tiring — the closer her stage persona is to her real self, the less strain it places on her. "I still have to decide on that, thank you very much." Olivia sighs. "I'm well aware of the effect I have on others — in some respects, it's more intense than before. But at the same time, it feels... it feels like a piece of me has broken off and left my body with our son. I can't get angry at the drop of a hat any more, and... well, I do understand it's for the best that I be patient when I have a pup to mind, but at the same time it sobering to realize what's happened to me and not know exactly why." There, there. Olivia's face tightens as if trying to pout, but true to her word, she can't get mad this easily. After several seconds of trying, the little yappy dog sighs and smiles weakly. "See what I mean, Dearest? Anyway, we've dithered enough. Was there something you needed of me?" ] ]

"Don't worry about it too much, just get them if you know any prospective candidates who're eager enough. I can school them in proper maidly etiquette, if it somes to that. Well, that's a bit of a stretch — it's mostly Rumie hanging around the little [pc.isDK |bitch |yappy dog ] and looking hopeful while Olivia goes about her business. Sighing, you look between Olivia and Rumie, then dismiss the latter with a wave of your hand. Nodding, your bee-tender bows, then makes to withdraw. "I'll give the both of you some space, then." Olivia watches Rumie retreat, then shrugs. "Oh, don't look at me like that, Dearest. I know what she's here for, but I just can't work myself up to being absolutely wretched to her like she's so desperately hoping for. I just don't have it in me any more, I'm afraid." You can tell. Noticing you draw close, Olivia's guests part like water around a rock, falling away to the other tables and giving the both of you your space. "Hello, Dearest." Now that she mentions it, the difference is quite stark: Olivia used to be a lot more slender and lopsided from her corruption, but at least she's more balanced both above and below. Nature tries to re-assert itself despite what was done to her, it seems. "I'd make a dry joke about me being more charismatic after having put on several pounds of puppy fat, but it wouldn't be a joke at this point." Olivia sighs. "Hey, at least people agree I look better this way as opposed to being a bimbo, and that already gave me a pretty good draw." Is she getting back into her old business of leading people around by the nose, then? |I think that lot was warmly surprised to find a bit of comfort in these miserable wilds. If this weren't a military installation first and foremost, I'd suggest letting out accommodation in any spare rooms you have." Hey, that doesn't stop people passing through from filling up the courtyard at night. It can get quite ridiculous at times. "When even your courtyard is more inviting than some of the so-called accommodation the Marches has to offer." Olivia sips her wine and smiles. "I think this is a nice place for our son to grow up. "A small bastion of sanity... and the eternal threat of misery at one's gates lest one be tempted to grow soft, that's what I mean. The best of both worlds, much like where I grew up myself. Our son won't turn into a brooding humorless brute like Asgeir was — he'll be able to tell a joke. I swear by the gods, I'll make sure of it myself the moment he can speak, or else." It's good to see Olivia in a jovial mood once more, she was a real sourpuss at points while she was with child. ] "I wish. Anyway, was there something that you wanted, Dearest?" |playing a little ditty on her flute for an audience. She's really getting into the swing of the music, although judging by the stares she's receiving from some of the audience, there's more to her charisma than just the performance; more than the music's swinging, that's for sure. As it happens, you've come just in time to catch the tail end of her show — as the crowd moves to disperse, Olivia readies to chat up a couple of likely prospects, then notices you and you're instantly the focus of her attention. "Oh, Dearest. Fancy you showing up now." Why, that was quite the tune she was playing just now. It was almost cheerful, you daresay — something that the old Olivia would never have managed. "...You know, Dearest, I can't argue with that. I've tried to work myself up to deal with certain annoyances around the wayfort of late, and —" she snaps her fingers — "the spite just won't come." But in the end... it's turned out for the better as a whole, right? People like her more now, and that's a good thing given the job you've set her to. Olivia sighs. "I'm well aware of the effect I have on others — in some respects, it's more intense than before. "See what I mean, Dearest? Anyway, we've dithered enough. Was there something you needed of me?" ] ] "

rows.original: Olivia gives you a sweet smile. "Of course, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. [olivia.isPregnant |[rand |I need to stretch my legs anyway — as fat and heavy as you've made me again, sitting down all day isn't good for my circulation." And Olivia looks rather fetching with a fat, heavy waddle. A sigh. "You know, once I'd have written that off as you teasing me, or at most your opinion being skewed because it's your pup in my belly. But after being the subject of certain attentions... I can believe that." |Honestly, I'm glad you asked — I'm so full that I wasn't sure I'd make it to the next feeding without excusing myself anyway, ha." With Olivia as she is now, you honestly can't tell any difference. "Being pregnant and milky will do that to you." Olivia raises an eyebrow. "I suppose you find it quite gratifying to know you've done this to me?" |My thoughts have been wandering this last hour — maybe seeing our son with you will set things straight." She doesn't have to look so guilty about it, her body's going through a lot right now. "And whose fault might that be, hmm? Trick question — mine, of course." ] Oh, enough fooling around. You reach down, grab Olivia by under her arms, and pull her out of her seat. All the added weight from her transition into motherhood is palpable, but she makes up for that by leaning herself against you and curling her tail about your legs. |[rand |I'm starting to tire of this tedious bunch, anyway — can't think of a better excuse to escape them than see our son." Disillusioned quickly? "Or maybe I just prefer spending time with our son at this point." |You're showing more of an interest in our son than my parents ever bothered with me or any of my siblings." That's a little sobering, but it does explain Olivia's attitude towards motherhood. "Ironic that a bastard should receive more affection than his actual heiress of a mother ever did, but just because you've had misfortune doesn't mean you have any right to inflict it upon others." |If anyone's to give me leave from my duties, it'd be you, wouldn't it?" Well, when she puts it that way... A laugh. "Just a small reminder not to be overfamiliar — we are in public, after all, and I am in your employ despite having borne you pups. Or maybe I'm just teasing you." ] With that, Olivia waves off the last of her so-called adoring fans and rises — you have to take her hand to steady her against her recently expanded maternal proportions, something which you receive several envious glances for. ] "All right, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Let's be off."
rows.translation: 奥利维亚向你露出了甜美的微笑：“当然，我亲爱的。[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]。 [olivia.isPregnant |[rand |不管怎样，我都需要活动活动腿脚了——毕竟你又把我弄得这么胖这么重，整天坐着对血液循环可没好处。” 而奥利维亚那胖乎乎、摇摇摆摆的步态，倒也显得挺有韵味的。 唉……“你知道吗，要是在以前，我肯定会把这当成你在逗我，或者至多觉得你的看法有失偏颇，因为在我肚子里的是你的孩子。但在受到了一些特别的关注之后……我倒是相信了。” |说实话，我很高兴你问了——我吃得太饱了，本来就不确定自己能撑到下次喂奶，不找借口离席的话恐怕都熬不到，哈哈。” 以奥利维亚现在的状态来看，真的根本看不出有什么不同。 “怀孕又泌乳就会这样。”奥利维亚挑了挑眉，“我猜，知道是你把我弄成这样的，你挺得意吧？” |这一小时里我的心思一直飘忽不定——也许和你一起去看看我们的儿子，能让我理清头绪。” 她没必要表现得那么内疚，她的身体现在正经历着许多变化。 “那这该怪谁呢，嗯？这是个陷阱问题——当然怪我自己。” ] 哦，别再胡闹了。你伸手抓住奥利维亚的胳膊，把她从座位上拉起来。她因为成为了母亲而体重增加，这一点显而易见，但她会靠在你身上，把尾巴缠在你的腿上，以此来弥补这一点。 |[rand |“反正我也开始厌烦这群无聊的家伙了——想不出比去看我们儿子更好的脱身借口。 这么快就失望了？ “又或者，我只是更愿意在这时候陪陪我们的儿子。” |“你对咱们儿子的关心，比我父母当年对我和我任何一个兄弟姐妹都要多。 这确实让人有些深思，但这也解释了奥利维亚对母性的那种态度。 “讽刺的是，一个私生子得到的关爱，竟比他那位正经女继承人的母亲得到的还多；但你自己遭遇过不幸，并不代表你有权把不幸加诸他人。” |“要是有人能准我放下职责，那也只能是你了，对吧？ 好吧，她这么一说…… 她笑了笑。“只是小小提醒你一下，别太没大没小——毕竟我们是在公共场合，而且尽管我为你生了孩子，我是受你雇用的。又或者，我只是在逗你。” ] 说完，奥利维亚挥手打发走最后一批所谓的崇拜者，站起身来——你不得不握住她的手，扶住她那近来因母性而愈发丰满的身形，为此你还招来了好几道嫉妒的目光。 ] “好吧，亲爱的[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]。 我们出发吧。”
rows.raw: " Olivia gives you a sweet smile. "Of course, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. [olivia.isPregnant |[rand |I need to stretch my legs anyway — as fat and heavy as you've made me again, sitting down all day isn't good for my circulation." And Olivia looks rather fetching with a fat, heavy waddle. A sigh. "You know, once I'd have written that off as you teasing me, or at most your opinion being skewed because it's your pup in my belly. But after being the subject of certain attentions... I can believe that." |Honestly, I'm glad you asked — I'm so full that I wasn't sure I'd make it to the next feeding without excusing myself anyway, ha." With Olivia as she is now, you honestly can't tell any difference. "Being pregnant and milky will do that to you." Olivia raises an eyebrow. "I suppose you find it quite gratifying to know you've done this to me?" |My thoughts have been wandering this last hour — maybe seeing our son with you will set things straight." She doesn't have to look so guilty about it, her body's going through a lot right now. "And whose fault might that be, hmm? Trick question — mine, of course." ] Oh, enough fooling around. You reach down, grab Olivia by under her arms, and pull her out of her seat. All the added weight from her transition into motherhood is palpable, but she makes up for that by leaning herself against you and curling her tail about your legs. |[rand |I'm starting to tire of this tedious bunch, anyway — can't think of a better excuse to escape them than see our son." Disillusioned quickly? "Or maybe I just prefer spending time with our son at this point." |You're showing more of an interest in our son than my parents ever bothered with me or any of my siblings." That's a little sobering, but it does explain Olivia's attitude towards motherhood. "Ironic that a bastard should receive more affection than his actual heiress of a mother ever did, but just because you've had misfortune doesn't mean you have any right to inflict it upon others." |If anyone's to give me leave from my duties, it'd be you, wouldn't it?" Well, when she puts it that way... A laugh. "Just a small reminder not to be overfamiliar — we are in public, after all, and I am in your employ despite having borne you pups. Or maybe I'm just teasing you." ] With that, Olivia waves off the last of her so-called adoring fans and rises — you have to take her hand to steady her against her recently expanded maternal proportions, something which you receive several envious glances for. ] "All right, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Let's be off." "

"It's not every day that [drifa.isCollared |[pc.Master] |[pc.name] ] shows up in person, so I understand." |Drifa beams. "Thanks for coming, [drifa.isCollared |[pc.Master] |[pc.name] ]. I've been hearing how awful things are getting out there, so both Olivia and I are glad you're able to come home and check in on your son." ] Olivia says nothing, but grins and picks up the bundle of black fur from where he's curled up on Drifa's rug, fussing over your son for a bit before handing him over to you. ] Oof. The little bastard's heavy for his size, and that's something considering he's huge for his age — you can see how Olivia absolutely expanded while he was in her belly. As your arms strain with the sudden weight, your son quietly regards you with a gaze that can only be described as calmly sullen, staring up at you with big eyes while you pet his thick fur. [pc.isDK |Aww. So young, and he's already mastered the art of villainous brooding without even needing to be taught. There's a bright future ahead for your son, that's for sure |Huh. Your son's the exact opposite of his mother, perfectly content to brood quietly as opposed to Olivia's constant need for chatter and attention. ]. It's undeniable that he's been tainted like his mother, but it doesn't seem to be in the same way as any of the corrupted lupines you've known. Maybe it'll manifest itself more obviously when he gets older, but for now being a quiet child is hardly cause for panic. Olivia's eye catches yours, and you can tell she's thinking similar thoughts. You draw her close, your son between the both of you, and tell her not to worry about Louis' future. "I-I wasn't worrying!" Olivia huffs. "I was just getting sentimental about seeing you together, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]." As she will. And you've to thank Drifa too, for minding [drifa.hasKids |your pups |the pup ] while you and Olivia are busy. Drifa [drifa.isCorrupt |crooks a smile. "You know I always have your happiness at heart, [drifa.isCollared |[pc.Master] |Darling ]. You'd be upset if anything happened to [drifa.hasKids |the children |your lovely little bastard ], so I'm just doing right by you." |blushes. "I-it's nothing, really. It's just like looking after my little sister all over again, [drifa.hasKids |just with a lot more feeling because they're your own." Even Louis? "Well, he, Siegfried and Giselle are half-siblings, so there isn't any difference in that regard, is there?" You wouldn't expect Drifa to see things any other way. |so I don't really mind. Louis is pretty well-behaved, except when he wants to exert himself, and even then it's just a matter of giving him plenty of things to climb safely." rows.original: [drifa.hasKids |[rand |After several moments of petting Louis and getting quiet stares from your son in return, you set him back down with his half-siblings and sit back to observe. Immediately, his demeanor changes, forgetting all about the adults and going straight for Siegfried and Giselle. A mess of puppy yips and barks rises from the trio as they butt heads against each other — it doesn't seem to be mean, violent or anything in that vein, but the pups are clearly having a tussle at each others' tails. Drifa chuckles. "Interesting, isn't it? Elise and I were too far apart to get up to this kind of fun, but all three of them change when you put them together. The twins are much more of a handful when their half-brother isn't around to play-fight with them." "And I prefer noisy mischief to quiet mischief," Olivia adds with a sigh. "Louis terrified me the first time I realized he could climb before even walking. Little bastard, just sleeping atop the bookshelf without so much as a by-your-leave." It doesn't seem fair, though. Louis is much bigger than his half-siblings. "Size isn't everything, [drifa.isCollared |[pc.Master] |Darling ]." Olivia snickers. "That's what she said." "Oh, please. But seriously: look at how Siegfried and Giselle are hounding him. And they're not even working together, going at each other as much as Louis. Sometimes, being big just means making yourself more of a target." You watch the pups tussle for several moments more — where there was peace and quiet, the trio of half-siblings now have an inexhaustible supply of energy to spend on each other. They don't just play-fight all day, right? "They do have their quieter moments, [drifa.isCollared |[pc.Master] |Darling ]. But it's much easier for me when I can just leave them to their own devices and get more done. If I need a bit of quiet, I just separate the trio for a bit." |After several more moments of putting up with your fluffing, Louis starts squirming in your grasp, wanting to be put down. As he wishes, then — no sooner have you set him back on the rug that that big dark puppy bounds after his half-siblings, suddenly filled with a lot more energy. Well, like his mother, he certainly isn't shy about making clear who and what he cares for. Olivia chuckles dryly and lays a comforting hand on your arm. "It hurts, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but that's how children are, the center of their own worlds. Don't fret — it isn't because of any lack on your part. I'm here for him all the time, and yet sometimes he's just not interested. "Besides, it's better that he has others his age to get up to mischief with. Neither Drifa nor I had the privilege." Drifa nods. "Elise and I were too far apart for that." You turn your attention back to the trio of pups playing on the rug — no one seems to have the upper hand in the game they're playing, but then again it is a game of two against one. "Don't be fooled, [drifa.isCollared |[pc.Master] |Darling ]. They're at each others' throats up until they want something from their mothers, then the half-siblings are as thick as thieves." By all appearances, the trio of pups bring out in each other traits that likely would've lain latent for a good long while. They do have a lot more energy when they're together. As to whether that'll be a good or bad influence on the whole, that remains to be seen. "Oh, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Don't you go fretting on my behalf, now. It wasn't easy for me to see off those gnawing worries, so just enjoy the moment, won't you? You're looking at the future rulers of the scattered lupine tribes having a bit of rough-and-tumble as pups — treasure this memory, because twenty years from now you'll be thinking back on this and laughing." ] |[rand |After several moments of petting, Louis grows restless in your arms, the big black pup pawing at the air towards [pc.mf |his mother. Olivia |Olivia. The little dog ] sighs, smiles, and makes to receive your son from you, undoing her little red dress and letting her titanic tits fall out as the cloth rolls off her shoulders. "Sorry about that, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Nothing but his dear old mother will sate him." Drifa [drifa.isCorrupt |rolls her eyes |smiles weakly ] and gestures at the empty bottles on a nearby table. "It's true. rows.original:
You spend the next hour or two fussing over [drifa.hasKids|the trio of pups|Louis, who endures the attention with quiet dignity], but eventually it's time for you to go. Olivia takes you by the hand as you leave Drifa's quarters, and together you set a leisurely pace back to her chambers.
    
    "You don't mind if I take another hour or two off, Dearest[olivia.isCollared
        | [pc.Master]
    ]? I need to get back in the proper mindset for entertaining your guests after getting all baby-brained. Not that treating most of them like infants wouldn't work just as well, but... you know. Someone might get all huffy."
    
    Ha. As amusing as that might be, she's welcome to take the rest of the day off if she wants. Some small recompense for producing and raising such a fine son for you.
    
    Olivia blushes, but draws herself together as regally as she can. "It's nice to finally have someone appreciate your efforts. Don't mind if I do, then. And Dearest[olivia.isCollared
        | [pc.Master]
    ]... I, too, appreciate you showing more interest in your son than my own [pc.mf
        |father
        |mother
    ] ever did for me.
    
    "Thank you for that, and I'm sure Louis feels the same way too, little bastard that he is. Ironic, isn't it, that a bastard should get more care and attention than his heiress mother ever did?"
