rows.original: Olivia Bellamon Leroux is a petite half-lupine at four feet eleven inches — either they make them much shorter down in Yvennes compared to the local breed in the Marches, or she's an outlier in that regard. What she lacks in height, though, her body has compensated for by growing out — [olivia.pregStage 1 6 |an effect that's doubly so now that she's conceived. Perhaps because it's been repressed for so long, Olivia's figure is responding intensely to being with child, steadily creeping towards proper shortstack proportions with each passing day. Even though her tits and hips are swelling out and firming up in response to pregnancy hormones, her middle has been absolutely expanding with pup, making her look much better proportioned than the perverse hourglass shape she used to fit. On one hand, this feels like more of Tharsus' handiwork; on the other, surely not all of Olivia's woes can be blamed on the old warlock. "Oh, it's absolutely him," Olivia mumbles, both hands resting on her swollen bump. "He's petty and vindictive enough to have done all of this. I bet he was banking on some hypervirile meathead knocking me up through my preventatives, too." She does look a lot better like this, even if she has to find a new schtick, at least until the pup's out of her. Has she considered taking a peek at classical lumian iconography for fertility idol aesthetics. Olivia rolls her eyes. "Mmmh. Don't push your luck just because it's your pup in my belly. I suppose it does have its merits — I'm no less popular, at least on the surface, but the constant flow of thinly veiled propositions has dried to a trickle." |after having pushed a pup out of her belly, Olivia looks better-proportioned than what she used to when she first arrived at the wayfort. Sure, her tits and hips have been permanently widened by pregnancy, but her waist has thickened considerably as well. At the very least, she looks more like a normal shortstack and less like a waspish bimbo. "Imagine that," Olivia says with a small, uncertain smile. "Demented warlock's plans ruined by motherhood. Not sure if it'll make a good tale for anyone but you and me, but I'm inspired to try nevertheless." She does look a lot less prone to being snapped in two by the wind. Hope it hasn't affected her routine any? "We-ll... people have expectations, you know?" Olivia raises a finger to her lips. "And these expectations are shaped by appearances. I still can pull off the princess schtick, but of late there've been increasing calls for tiny dommy mommies, so I have to play to my audience and put on a show face." Which is perfectly fine. She can be a petty little tyrant to anyone who wants it from her — it just makes it all the more special when she understands she's your pet. "It really is that way, isn't it? Even if you didn't mean to, Dearest, you did end up changing my body, perhaps even more than Tharsus did... and frankly, I like this a lot more in both journey and destination." |her pronounced hourglass shape is right on the border of double-take territory, given how her waist is compared to both above and below. The bard looks more like someone in one of those stylized Belharan woodcuts than an actual person, although it admittedly isn't enough to spook anyone looking too closely. "Tharsus' handiwork. Sure, I wasn't flat before, but I was a lot more slender and better proportioned," Olivia grumps. "Blowing up my tits and hips is what the old creep thought was the pinnacle of feminine beauty." Or he knew full well what he was doing and just wanted to torment her, given what he was getting up to in private. Olivia rolls her eyes. "I guess. That doesn't make it better." The blatant hourglass shape seems to have worked, both with the lupines and now people coming and going to and from the wayfort. "It... it has its merits. I just wish it didn't... you know what? rows.original: "That would be appreciated, Dearest. While I can spin a yarn out of thin air, that'd be counterproductive to actually getting people to have a favorable disposition towards you. Why don't you sit down and have a drink with me, tell me something of what you've been doing out there?" You pull up a chair by the high table and let Olivia serve you a little wine — the audience she's gathered prior to your arrival hasn't budged any, and you guess they're your audience now. "That's right, Dearest." She gives you a sweet smile. "I imagine everyone's more than eager to hear the tales right from the source, aren't they? I may do the retelling, but there's nothing quite like hearing it from someone who was actually there. [pc.bgMulti noblescion minstrel courtesan |Now pull together that noble presence of yours and regale these fine people with your adventures beyond these walls, if you would. |You may be out adventuring more these days, but you haven't lost your touch at showmanship, have you? |Come now, certainly you haven't forgotten how to be charming, no? Or has roughing it in the wilderness sanded off all your refinement? |Don't worry about getting tongue-tied — I know this wasn't your job, but telling an interesting tale is something everyone should be able to do. ]" Well, when Olivia puts it like that, you can hardly say no, can you? Settling in, you give your court bard a quick run-down of what you've been up to since you last set foot in the wayfort: the tale gets long in the telling, but it's also one of the few times when Olivia just shuts up. She doesn't interject much, and when she does she never attempts to change the subject to anything about herself, instead choosing to affirm bits of your tale here and there. You note that she doesn't write anything down — is her memory that good? Those in her line of work do tend to rely on a lot of oral traditions, after all. But eventually, you're done — and just as your wine glass has begun to run dry, too. Olivia gives you a nod as you finish recounting your adventures, then leans back in her seat with a smile. "Is that all, Dearest?" That's all. "I can work with that, I suppose. You dear audience —" she waggles a hand at the gathered people — "seems to like it just fine. Of course, I can work with anything, the best don't let things like that get in the way of greatness... but it's nice to not have to put lipstick on a pig. Look forward to it when you next come back, okay?" Right, right. "Perfect. Is there anything else I can do for you?"
rows.translation: “那就太感谢了，亲爱的。我虽然能凭空编出一套说辞，但那样反而不利于让别人对你产生好感。不如坐下来陪我喝一杯，跟我讲讲你这些日子在外面都做了些什么？” 你拉过一把椅子，在高桌旁坐下，让奥利维亚给你倒了些葡萄酒——在你到来之前她召集的那些听众一个都没走，你猜他们现在都是你的听众了。 “没错，亲爱的。”她向你露出甜美的微笑，“我想大家都迫不及待想从当事人那里亲耳听到这些故事，对吧？复述的人可以是我，但没有什么比听亲历者亲口讲述更动人的了。[pc.bgMulti noblescion minstrel courtesan |那就拿出你那副高贵的气场，给这些好心人讲讲你在城墙之外的冒险吧，如果你愿意的话。 |这些日子你或许更多地在外冒险，但表演的本事应该还没丢吧？ |来吧，你总不至于忘了怎么讨人喜欢吧？还是在荒野里吃苦把你那点优雅都磨光了？ |别担心会说得结结巴巴——我知道这本来不是你的活儿，但讲一个有趣的故事，人人都该做得到。 ]” 嗯，奥利维亚这么一说，你几乎没法拒绝，对吧？你安顿下来，向你的宫廷吟游诗人简要讲了讲自从你上次踏进驿堡以来都做了些什么：这个故事讲起来很长，但这也是少有的几次奥利维亚彻底闭嘴的时候。她很少插嘴，即便插嘴也从不试图把话题引到自己身上，而是时不时对你的讲述表示赞同。你注意到她什么都没写下来——她的记性真有那么好吗？毕竟干她这一行的人，往往很依赖口述传统。 但最终，你讲完了——正好你的酒杯也快见底了。你讲完自己的冒险经历后，奥利维亚朝你点了点头，然后微笑着靠回椅背。 “就这些，亲爱的？” 就这些。 “我想这些素材可以用。你们这些亲爱的观众——”她朝聚集的人群摆了摆手——“似乎还挺喜欢的。当然，什么素材我都能处理；真正的顶尖高手不会让这种小事妨碍自己的伟大……但不用给猪涂口红，总归是件好事。等你下次回来的时候就好好期待吧，好吗？” 好，好。 “太好了。还有什么需要我帮忙的吗？”

rows.translation: [corlup.imprisoned |奥利维亚皱着眉头看你。“我本没有资格质疑你的决定，毕竟正是你的仁慈让我坐在这里，而不是躺在坟墓里……但你不会打算把那些狗一辈子锁着吧，亲爱的？” 如果她担心的是它们有没有受虐待，那大可放心。那些狼族会定期被放到院子里活动，吃得也不差，不至于在牢房里衰弱下去。这是你至少能做的，直到它们不再对自己和他人构成威胁。 “那你为这些目标做了什么？” 德莉法在找治疗方法。是认真的，不像塔尔苏斯那样只会空口许诺。进展一直很慢——她正从不同角度入手解决这个问题，而说实话，你最近没怎么去关心她的进展。她是那种一旦有突破就会主动来找你的人。 奥利维亚翻了个白眼。“那当然了，亲爱的。” 她怎么这么感兴趣？ “无非是些实际问题。囚犯得喂、得给水、得看管、得圈起来。这些都要耗费物资、时间和精力。伊文尼斯佣兵之所以打得那么凶，部分原因就是我们知道自己不会被赎，所以每一场战斗都是死战。 “我明白最终能研制出解药、或许还能用在除这群癞皮狗之外的人身上，确实很有吸引力……但谁也说不准那要花多久，所以我才问你，万一那种传说中的治疗剂始终没能问世，你对它们有没有实际打算。[silly |就算你能在游戏剩下的时间里一直关着他们，关 |L ]他们锁一辈子也根本不划算。干脆处死反而更仁慈。” 这……你叹了口气。你隐隐怀疑，奥利维亚的怨恨正在影响她的判断。 “我不是叫你处决或驱逐他们，你这白痴。但你得有个计划，而不是永远把他们扔进地牢然后指望奇迹。这种安排撑不了多久，还在消耗本可以用在正事上的资源。你可以来问我有什么办法，但我保证，我的办法你听了都会觉得难以下咽。” “你可以释放阿斯盖尔；他那套扭曲的荣誉准则会让他不会故技重施。其余那些？可就未必了。” |“你为什么问起他，亲爱的？你是不是后悔把他流放了？你是不是怕自己犯了错——放过阿斯盖尔，却无意中害了他和他的族群接下来盯上的人？” 当时，把他和他的族群送去走冰原似乎是最好的办法。至少，那是阿斯盖尔更愿意接受的命运，毕竟这是狼族传统的刑罚。 “那是一句没骨气的判决，亲爱的。奥利维亚嗤了一声。名义上不是处决，实际上却是，由一群懦弱到不敢自己挥斧的人想出来的——他们非得让荒野替他们动手。但我怀疑阿斯盖尔本人不会就这么躺下认命。他的手下或许会。但他不会。他会毫无理由地继续走下去，因为他就是这样的人。” “也许哪天你还会见到他。也许不会。不管怎样，这已经比他应得的多太多了；我还记得他向我摊开他的计划，以及我该怎么让其他人也能接受那些计划。人们总是用冠冕堂皇的说辞包装自己那些令人作呕的行径，他也一样。” ]
rows.raw: " [corlup.imprisoned |Olivia frowns at you. "Far from it being my place to question your decisions, since it's your kindness that has me sitting here instead of in a grave... but you don't intend to keep the dogs locked up for the rest of their lives, do you, Dearest?" They're not mistreated, if she's worried about that. The lupines are let out in the yard regularly for exercise and fed decently so they don't waste away in their cells. It's the least you can do, until they're no longer a danger to themselves and to others. "And what are you doing to those ends?" Drifa's looking for a cure. In earnest, as opposed to Tharsus' empty promises. Progress has been slow — she's trying different angles of approach to the problem, and admittedly you haven't checked in with her that recently. She's the kind who'll come up to you should she have a breakthrough. Olivia rolls her eyes. "But of course, Dearest." Why's she so interested, anyway? "Simple matters of practicality. Prisoners have to be fed, watered, minded, corralled. All of these cost goods, time, and effort. Part of the reason why Yvennese mercenaries fight so furiously is that we know no one is going to bother ransoming us, so every fight is one to the death. "While I can see the appeal of eventually being able to develop a cure and perhaps apply that to those other than this mangy pack of dogs...there's no telling how long that might take, which is why I'm asking if you have an actual plan as to what to do with them should this fabled remedy for their condition cease to materialize. [silly |Even if you can keep them imprisoned for the rest of the game, l |L ]ocking them up for the rest of their lives simply isn't efficient. A swift death would be more merciful." It's... you sigh. You have just the slightest suspicion that Olivia's spite is coloring her opinion. "I'm not telling you to execute or banish them, you idiot. But you need to have a plan that's more than throwing them in the dungeon forever and hoping for a miracle. This arrangement can't last long, and it's draining resources that could be spent on constructive purposes. And while you could ask me for solutions, I assure you that you'd find all of mine quite unpalatable. "You could release Asgeir; his twisted code of honor would prevent him from trying the same thing all over again. The rest of them? Much less so." |"Why do you ask about him, Dearest? Are you regretting your decision to exile him? Do you fear that you made a mistake and in sparing Asgeir, you've inadvertently harmed whoever he and his pack impose themselves upon next?" Sending him and his pack to walk the ice seemed to be the best thing to do at the time. It was, at least, a fate Asgeir would be more willing to accept, being a traditional lupine punishment. "It's a gutless sentence, Dearest." Olivia sniffs. "An execution in all but name, created by a people too cowardly to wield the axe themselves, that they must have the wilds do the killing for them. But I doubt Asgeir himself will just allow himself to lie down and give up. His underlings, maybe. But not him. He'll just go on without any reason, because that's what he is. "Maybe you'll see him again someday. Maybe not. It's more than what he deserved, anyway; I still remember when he was laying out his plans to me, and how I was to make them palatable for everyone else. People wrap up their disgusting actions in noble-sounding words all the time, and he was no exception." ] "

rows.original:
Olivia frowns at you. "Far from it being my place to question your decisions, since it's your kindness that has me sitting here instead of in a grave... but are you sure it's wise to make them part of your garrison?"
    
    [pc.isDK
        |As the saying goes, keep your friends close and your enemies closer. Asgeir and the corrupted lupines don't have access to any truly sensitive sections of the wayfort, so they'll be just fine where you can keep an eye on them
        |Whether it's wise or not is immaterial. You're the only one who has the capability of taking care of the corrupted lupines, and given your involvement in the whole situation the responsibility falls on your shoulders
    ]. And at the end of the day, what these dogs need right now is useful work. Keeps them busy, gives their lives a purpose instead of acting out from sheer boredom.
    
    "So, busywork." Olivia sniffs and wrinkles her nose. "Not that they can tell the difference."
    
    It'll do until Drifa can figure out a cure for them.
    
    "Please, Dearest. Assuming it can be done to begin with, your little priestess working on her own isn't going to be producing results in any reasonable period of time.[silly
        | Certainly not before the game ends, at any rate.
    ] Expending this kind of constant effort keeping that ragtag bunch in line must be draining for whichever poor soul you've set to the task."
    
    That would be Asgeir himself; no reason to change the leader of the pack when it's what these dogs are used to. Why, what's with the look? Does she suspect that Asgeir's word may not be good? Just because she and Tharsus were more than happy to stab him in the back doesn't mean everyone's that way.
rows.translation:
奥利维亚皱起眉头看着你。“我本没有资格质疑你的决定，毕竟是你的善意让我坐在这里，而不是躺在坟墓里……但你确定把他们编入你的驻军是明智之举吗？”
    
    [pc.isDK
        |俗话说，要亲近你的朋友，更要亲近你的敌人。阿斯盖尔和腐化狼族接触不到驿堡里任何真正敏感的区域，所以只要你能盯着他们，他们就不会有事
        |明智与否并不重要。你是唯一有能力照料腐化狼族的人，而鉴于你参与了整件事，这份责任就落在你肩上
    ]。 归根结底，这些狗现在需要的是一份有用的活计。让他们忙起来，给他们的生活一个目标，而不是因为纯粹的百无聊赖而闹事。
    
    “所以，是些打发时间的差事。”奥利维亚嗤了一声，皱了皱鼻子。“反正他们也分不出区别。”
    
    在德莉法能为他们找到解药之前，这样也行。
    
    “拜托了，亲爱的。就算这事一开始真能做到，你那位单打独斗的小女祭司也不可能在什么合理的时间内出成果。[silly
        | 至少在游戏结束前肯定不行。
    ]为了管住那群乌合之众而持续付出这种精力，无论你派了哪个可怜虫去干这活，肯定都累得够呛。”
    
    那个人就是阿斯盖尔本人；既然这些狗已经习惯了，就没理由换掉狼群的首领。怎么，你这表情是什么意思？难道她怀疑阿斯盖尔的话靠不住？她和塔尔苏斯当初可是巴不得在他背后捅刀子，但这不代表所有人都那样。

rows.original: "No, Dearest. It's just..." Olivia pauses, drumming her claws on the table. "Hmm. To make things clear, I'm sure that Asgeir's loyalty is absolute now that you've established dominance —" she spits the words — "over him. Tell me, Dearest, what do you know of the ancient customs of these parts? "No, don't answer, that was a rhetorical question. Point being, when en route to this miserable corner of the world, I did my reading. The very first inhabitants of the Frost Marches were the local lupines, and then the pale elves came down from the glaciers and settled the lands, displacing the tribes of dogs. Then after that came the Belharans up from the south and did much the same, leaving the dogs utterly dispossessed and without a single scrap of land overlooked by the two powers." What's she getting at? "The point I'm working my way to, Dearest, is that this entire 'friendship-by-victory' nonsense is just [silly |one big cope |an acceptance of the yoke ] by the local lupines. Tharsus called Asgeir's code of honor a laughable imitation of the old lycan rites, but even the original rites he refers to are nothing but the rationalizations of a downtrodden, broken people as to why they owe their masters loyalty. It certainly isn't something that's inherent to lupines in general — you won't find this line of thinking in Yvennes in the slightest. "Now, as to how this all relates to Asgeir... I believe that his loyalty to you is absolute, and that he'll serve you doggedly to the utmost of his ability, which is more than what can be said of his underlings. And should it happen one day that you're dethroned by someone for whatever reason... that undying faithfulness of his will transfer to your successor in its totality. Just as, I note, how his people's loyalties seamlessly passed from their own leaders, then to the rulership of the elves, and finally to the empire. It is how the quiet, useful servant survives; one master is little different from another." That's an extremely cynical perspective to take. "Dearest... you can put lipstick on a pig, but that doesn't make it any less of a pig. You can dress it up and call it honor and hierarchy, but all I see is dust and tears. Asgeir's beliefs aren't even dead, they were stillborn to begin with."
rows.translation: “不是，亲爱的。只是……”奥利维亚停下来，用利爪敲击桌面。“嗯。说清楚一点，既然你已经对阿斯盖尔确立支配地位——”她咬牙吐出这几个字，“我相信他如今绝对忠诚。告诉我，亲爱的，你对本地的古老习俗了解多少？ “不，别回答，那只是个反问。重点是，我在前往这个悲惨的世界角落途中读过相关资料。霜冻边境最早的居民是本地狼族；后来苍白精灵从冰川南下，在这里定居，将犬族部落逐出土地。再后来，贝尔哈兰人从南方到来，做了几乎同样的事；犬族被彻底剥夺了家园，在两方势力管辖之外连一小片土地都没有。” 她想表达什么？ “亲爱的，我绕来绕去想说的是，整套‘胜者为友’的鬼话只是本地狼族的[silly |大型自我安慰 |认命戴上枷锁 ]。塔尔苏斯说，阿斯盖尔的荣誉准则是对古老狼人仪式的可笑模仿；可即便他所说的原始仪式，也不过是一个受尽压迫、支离破碎的民族用来解释自己为何效忠主人的托词。这当然不是狼族天生共有的思维——你绝不会在伊薇恩人身上看到这种想法。 “至于这和阿斯盖尔有什么关系……我相信他会绝对忠于你，竭尽全力、像狗一样为你服务；他的手下可远远做不到这一点。假如有一天，你因为某种原因被别人推翻……他不朽的忠诚会完完整整地转移给你的继任者。正如他的人民曾经毫无阻碍地把忠诚从自己的领袖转向精灵统治者，最后再转向帝国。这就是沉默而有用的仆人如何存活；换一个主人也没有多少区别。” 这种看法未免愤世嫉俗到了极点。 “亲爱的……给猪涂上口红，它依然还是猪。你可以粉饰这一切，称之为荣誉与等级制度，可我只看见尘土与泪水。阿斯盖尔的信念甚至谈不上死去，因为它们从一开始就是死胎。”

rows.original: "Oh." Olivia rolls her eyes. "An insufferable scold, that one. No sense of humor and completely uptight, blunt enough to get the point across, but mindful enough to not be outright insubordinate. Dry and bitter, like several of the wines I've had the misfortune to sample in the past. "Which is great to have in a bailiff. You're a lucky [pc.mf |man |woman ] to have her around, Dearest. A miserable lump of salt who can't be swayed by force, words or bribery — you can go to bed knowing that your walls and vaults are safe, or if they aren't you'll be awakened extremely quickly and rudely." That's a surprising summary given all that she said in the first half. "Is it, Dearest?" A shrug. "If I dismissed everyone whom I found personally repugnant, I wouldn't have had very many [silly |simps |adoring fans ] at my beck and call, nor would I be sitting here talking to you. After all, my personal opinions are just that, and people have their uses regardless of what I think of them." That's... well. She certainly doesn't — didn't — act like it. "Point being, Dearest, don't expect me to like your bailiff, at least personally. She's good and possessed of the traits that make for a good bailiff, but just because I admit that vinegar has a purpose doesn't mean I want to chug it from the bottle. Daliza is good at her job and you should keep her around, but excuse me if I'd rather put as much distance between that humorless snowflake and myself as I can."
rows.translation: 哦。”奥利维亚翻了个白眼，“那个家伙真是个让人难以忍受的责骂者。毫无幽默感，整个人都绷得紧紧的，说话直截了当却也懂得分寸，不会太过顶撞别人。他的言辞干巴巴的，就像我过去尝过的一些难喝的葡萄酒一样。 “不过，对于一个执达员来说，这样的性格倒也是挺好的。你真幸运啊。 [pc.mf |男人 |女性 ]有她在身边，真是太好了，亲爱的。她就像一块坚硬的盐块，无论是强迫、言语还是贿赂都无法打动她——你可以安心睡觉，因为知道自己的墙壁和金库都是安全的；就算出了什么问题，你也会很快被惊醒，而且方式会相当粗暴。” 考虑到她前面说了那么多话，这个总结确实有些出乎意料。 “是吗，亲爱的？”他耸了耸肩，“如果我把所有让我觉得厌恶的人都赶走，那我身边就几乎不会剩下任何人了。 [silly |傻瓜们 |狂热的粉丝们 ]随时听我的差遣，否则我也不会坐在这里和你聊天。毕竟，我的个人看法只不过是个人看法而已，无论我对这些人有什么看法，他们都有自己的用处。” “嗯……她确实没有表现出这样的态度。” “总之，亲爱的，别指望我会喜欢至少就我个人而言，她并不适合担任这个职位。她确实很优秀，也具备担任执行官所需的各种素质，但仅仅因为我认为醋确实有其用途，并不意味着我就想直接从瓶子里喝下去。达莉莎工作能力很强，你们应该继续留用她，不过恕我直言，我宁愿与这个毫无幽默感的人保持尽可能大的距离。

rows.original: So, does she think Tharsus is out there? Hiding and plotting? "Of course, Dearest. What else is an old creep like him going to do? Realize the error of his ways in the wake of his defeat and settle down to a quiet life somewhere? Burn away his remaining years as a hedge-wizard and live off dispensing weak potions and casting cantrips? Please." You didn't get the impression that he was about to give up either, given the things he was cooking up in his corner of the mines. Then again, you've known him for all of a single conversation, so you were hoping that Olivia might have more insight on the man and what moves he might make next. Olivia sighs and rubs her temples. "[var0 |I'd tell you to go and ask Asgeir yourself, since he was the one who brought in Tharsus and made him a 'captain'. But the big lunk has absolutely zero insight into and empathy for other people, otherwise he'd have realized he was taking a rat into his midst from the get-go. Seriously! How much of an idiot do you have to be to not see right through someone like Tharsus and his endless promises of finding a cure?" If she would stay focused on the subject instead of turning this into venting her personal gripes about Asgeir... |As much as I'd like to forget the man ever existed, it's not something that's happening when I'm faced with his handiwork in the mirror every day. So let me just think back for a bit..." Anything in particular she recalls? "The old creep was always bellyaching about not having some reagent or the other for his work — one day it'd be this tincture, a root the next. The boys were more than willing to help him given they believed he was trying to cure them, but... you know. They're not exactly smart. "Any large stockpiles of alchemical supplies in the region?" You can think of a few likely prospects, although none of which would be easily raidable by a lone wolf, aggrieved as he might be. Any other ideas? ] "Yes, yes. Hmm..." She taps her chin. "I remember Tharsus being interested in securing a number of Asgeir's men for himself. Since that particular plan fell through, I suppose he could have gone to find some more warm bodies. I don't know if he needed those particular meatheads, or if any unfortunate bodies will do for whatever he's got planned. The entire marches are dotted with secluded lupine villages, the way they've lived for generations trying to avoid the eyes of first the elves, and then the empire. rows.original: "Lovely lady. Honestly, couldn't live without her — she knows where to get clothes with class, drink that I don't have to filter the dregs out of, and much, much more. Most merchants in this part of the world aren't worth spit, but she knows how to get the good stuff, and I reward her with my patronage." So most of the stuff she has right now is from Farrah? "Quite so, Dearest. All the furniture I ordered, for one — you didn't think I'd put up with what's lying around the wayfort if I could help it, did you? Lady drives a hard bargain, but I'm also not one for haggling for its own sake. Plus, I get little useless gifts from all kinds on a regular basis; she's more than happy to let me trade them in for things I do need. I don't need twenty boxes of preserved sweetmeats, but I would like to have some nice curtains to keep the cold out. Since we're both more or less permanent fixtures in the wayfort, it's easy to have a good working relationship." You've never really thought about where Farrah sources her stock from, but that makes sense. She's always willing to buy your cast-offs, after all. "She may not — and rightfully shouldn't — partake of any of her goods, but she does know every detail about anything she keeps in stock. I was quite surprised and much delighted to find a taste of home the first time I entered her little self-made emporium. Euphoric indeed. If only all merchants were like her instead of the miserable half-hearted chumps who pay your bridge tolls, your wayfort would be much better supplied. "But that's how it is, Dearest — most people simply muddle through life without much conscious direction. Farrah? She knows what she wants and has a plan to get it, and all the better if I'm around to make use of her ambitions to feather my own nest."
rows.translation: “她是位可爱的女士。说实话，没有她我可活不下去——她知道去哪里弄到有品位的衣服、不必让我滤去残渣的酒，还有许许多多其他东西。这个世界角落的大部分商人一钱不值，可她懂得如何弄到好货，所以我也用自己的生意回报她。” 所以，她现在拥有的大部分东西都来自法拉？ “正是如此，亲爱的。比如我订购的所有家具——你不会以为，只要有选择，我还会容忍驿堡里随处可见的那些东西吧？那位女士讨价还价毫不手软，但我也不是为了还价本身而讨价的人。此外，我经常收到各种各样没用的小礼物；她很乐意让我拿去换真正确实需要的东西。我不需要二十箱果脯，但的确想要几幅漂亮窗帘挡住寒气。既然我们两个或多或少都是驿堡里的固定住户，建立良好的合作关系很容易。” 你从未认真想过法拉从哪里进货，不过这很合理。毕竟，她总是愿意买下你淘汰不用的东西。 “她也许不会——而且理所当然不该——亲自使用任何商品，但她的确对库存中的每样东西都了如指掌。第一次走进她亲手打造的极乐商店，品尝到家乡风味时，我相当惊讶，更是无比欣喜。的确令人极乐。要是所有商人都像她，而不是那些勉强缴纳过桥费的可悲蠢货，你的驿堡便会得到充足得多的补给。 “可事实就是如此，亲爱的——大部分人毫无明确方向，只是浑浑噩噩地活着。法拉？她知道自己想要什么，也有计划将其弄到手；要是我能在身边利用她的野心为自己筑巢，那就更好了。”

rows.original: "Such a delightful little dear, submissive and eager to please to the point where she gets off on it. Reminds me of the baranians we have at home — she's their kin in spirit, if not flesh. My main concern is that she's simply taken on too many responsibilities at once just to experience the euphoria that comes with being put-upon... while that feeling may be intensely pleasurable for the poor dear, it's also not healthy for her if she overindulges. I've had to command her to rest more than once now, regardless of how eager she might be [pc.bg noblescion |to have someone she can serve hang around reliably |to actually be able to serve someone with a bona fide air of nobility about her ]." Yeah. Every time you come up to the bar, day or night, Rumie's there running the place. She presumably must sleep sometime given that you've seen the bee-tender's mussed bedsheets, but she's never done it while you're around. "She does sleep from time to time, I can assure you of that, Dearest. It's just never when you're around — I suppose that she does feel the obligation to look busy when the [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the wayfort is around. That, or she's hoping for something from you. "Don't you worry about Rumie — I'll ensure that she takes care of herself while you're away. It would be a shame to lose such a devoted servant over simple overindulgence, wouldn't it?"
rows.translation: “多么讨人喜欢的小家伙，顺从又热衷于取悦他人，甚至会因此兴奋。她让我想起家乡那些巴拉尼亚人——即使血脉不同，精神上也是同类。我主要担心的是，她只是为了体验受人差遣时的快感，一口气承担了太多责任……那种感觉对可怜的姑娘或许极其愉悦，但若沉溺过度，也会伤害她的身体。无论她多么渴望[pc.bg noblescion |身边总有一位可以稳定侍奉的人 |真正侍奉一位货真价实、气质高贵的人 ]，我现在都不止一次命令她去休息了。” 确实。无论白天还是夜晚，你每次走到吧台旁，露米都在那里打理生意。既然你见过蜂女酒保凌乱的床铺，她想必总要睡觉，只是在你身边时从未睡过。 “她的确偶尔会睡觉，我可以向你保证，亲爱的。只不过你在时从来不会——我想，驿堡的[pc.mf |领主 |女主人 ]在场时，她觉得自己有义务表现得很忙。又或者，她正期待从你这里得到些什么。 “别担心露米——你不在时，我会确保她照顾好自己。仅仅因为过度沉溺，就失去如此忠诚的仆人，未免太可惜了，不是吗？”

rows.original: You've been wondering. No sooner had Olivia arrived at the wayfort that she gathered a retinue of your maids who're all falling over themselves to wait on her hand and foot — and all without letting you know. How did she gather them up so quickly? A giggle. "Well, Dearest. To be perfectly honest, it was they who gathered me up — your lovely girls instinctively recognized my air of nobility and were seized with desire to serve me, that's all. Don't worry, I only took a handful for myself; you still have all you need to maintain the grounds." They sensed her air of nobility and gathered her up. A likely story worthy of a bard like her, you're sure. "Why, Dearest, you sound just a little unconvinced that either side could pull off such a thing. Nevertheless, reality doesn't hinge upon you finding it credulous. Ever since the time of old Belhar, the image of Yvennese domestic help has captured the imaginations of people across the imperium and that hasn't changed one jot or tittle since its fall. How else would you have found someone to make these passable replicas of our maid uniforms, otherwise? "The girls want to learn to be proper maids oh-so-desperately, Dearest. No sooner had they discovered I was a Yvennese lady that they absolutely imposed themselves upon me, begging to be taught the etiquette and decorum to be true maids." And Olivia knew as much to teach them that in the first place? One would imagine that imparting such manners would be left to whoever was in charge of the household, not a lady herself. "Yes and no." Olivia thinks for a moment, drumming her claws on the table. "Dearest... back home, we have expectations of the hired help, and they of us. My parents were always kind to the household staff, and wouldn't stand for any abuse just because we paid them — they were part of the estate, after all. We knew their limits, and they ours; the kind of relationship that was associated with more civilized times. "It's from those unspoken agreements that stories sprang to capture the imaginations of the rest of old Belhar and reach even this miserable corner of the world. You don't imagine your girls put on these frilly encumbering dresses for nothing, do you?" That, and being Olivia's handmaidens means a lot of standing around and looking pretty as opposed to doing actual work. When the worst one has to deal with is fetching and carrying instead of miserable back-breaking scrubbing... "Oh, don't you worry about that in the slightest, Dearest. The girls work hard to keep everything, from my chambers to my clothes, as clean as they can be; they're not shirking their duties in the slightest. No, if I teach them well, perhaps in time to come they'll get to oversee their sisters as seniors. It's so adorable, not just seeing a household hierarchy come into existence, but also having a hand in shaping its foundations. Makes me feel like a girl again."
rows.translation: 你一直在琢磨这件事。奥利维亚刚到驿堡，就召集了一群你的女仆，个个争先恐后地服侍她——而这一切都没让你知道。她怎么能这么快就把她们聚拢起来的？ 一声轻笑。“这个嘛，亲爱的。老实说，是她们把我聚拢起来的——你那些可爱的姑娘们凭本能认出了我的高贵气质，被想要服侍我的渴望攫住了，仅此而已。别担心，我只给自己挑了一小撮；你维持这片宅邸所需的人手一个都不少。” 她们察觉到她的高贵气质，就把她聚拢起来了。这种说法倒是很配像她这样的吟游诗人，你确信如此。 “哎呀，亲爱的，你听起来有点不太相信这件事两边有哪一边办得到。可现实并不取决于你是否觉得它可信。自旧贝尔哈的时代以来，伊文尼斯家仆的形象就抓住了整个帝国人们的想象，而自从帝国倾覆以后，这一点连一丝一毫都没有改变。不然你又是怎么找到人来仿制这些还算过得去的女仆制服的？” “那些姑娘们急不可耐地想要学会做合格的女仆，亲爱的。她们一发现我是一位伊文尼斯女士，就绝对是硬缠上我，求我教她们礼仪和规矩，好成为真正的女仆。” 而奥利维亚当初居然懂得这些，能教她们？一般人会以为，传授这类礼数该由管家的人来做，而不是由一位女士亲自出马。 “也对，也不对。”奥利维亚想了一会儿，用爪子敲着桌子。“亲爱的……在我老家，我们对雇来的仆人有我们的期待，他们对我们也有他们的期待。我父母一向对家里的仆人很好，绝不会因为付了工钱就容忍任何苛待——毕竟他们也是这产业的一部分。我们了解他们的限度，他们也了解我们的；那是与更文明的时代相称的一种关系。” 正是从那些心照不宣的约定里，故事才生长出来，抓住了旧贝尔哈其余地方的想象，甚至传到了世界这个凄凉的角落。你总不会以为你的姑娘们穿上这些满是褶边、碍手碍脚的裙子是白穿的吧？ 除此之外，做奥利维亚的侍女还意味着大把时间都花在站在一旁、打扮得漂漂亮亮上，而不是真的干活。最糟的差事也不过是跑腿搬东西，而不是那种累死人的刷洗擦扫…… “哦，你一点都不用担心这个，亲爱的。姑娘们很卖力，从我的房间到我的衣服，她们都尽量保持得一尘不染；她们丝毫没有偷懒。不，如果我教得好，也许将来她们还能作为资深侍女去管束自己的姐妹。这真是太可爱了，不只是看着一套宅邸的等级制度成形，还能亲手塑造它的根基。让我觉得自己又变回了一个小姑娘。”
rows.raw: " You've been wondering. No sooner had Olivia arrived at the wayfort that she gathered a retinue of your maids who're all falling over themselves to wait on her hand and foot — and all without letting you know. How did she gather them up so quickly? A giggle. "Well, Dearest. To be perfectly honest, it was they who gathered me up — your lovely girls instinctively recognized my air of nobility and were seized with desire to serve me, that's all. Don't worry, I only took a handful for myself; you still have all you need to maintain the grounds." They sensed her air of nobility and gathered her up. A likely story worthy of a bard like her, you're sure. "Why, Dearest, you sound just a little unconvinced that either side could pull off such a thing. Nevertheless, reality doesn't hinge upon you finding it credulous. Ever since the time of old Belhar, the image of Yvennese domestic help has captured the imaginations of people across the imperium and that hasn't changed one jot or tittle since its fall. How else would you have found someone to make these passable replicas of our maid uniforms, otherwise? "The girls want to learn to be proper maids oh-so-desperately, Dearest. No sooner had they discovered I was a Yvennese lady that they absolutely imposed themselves upon me, begging to be taught the etiquette and decorum to be true maids." And Olivia knew as much to teach them that in the first place? One would imagine that imparting such manners would be left to whoever was in charge of the household, not a lady herself. "Yes and no." Olivia thinks for a moment, drumming her claws on the table. "Dearest... back home, we have expectations of the hired help, and they of us. My parents were always kind to the household staff, and wouldn't stand for any abuse just because we paid them — they were part of the estate, after all. We knew their limits, and they ours; the kind of relationship that was associated with more civilized times. "It's from those unspoken agreements that stories sprang to capture the imaginations of the rest of old Belhar and reach even this miserable corner of the world. You don't imagine your girls put on these frilly encumbering dresses for nothing, do you?" That, and being Olivia's handmaidens means a lot of standing around and looking pretty as opposed to doing actual work. When the worst one has to deal with is fetching and carrying instead of miserable back-breaking scrubbing... "Oh, don't you worry about that in the slightest, Dearest. The girls work hard to keep everything, from my chambers to my clothes, as clean as they can be; they're not shirking their duties in the slightest. No, if I teach them well, perhaps in time to come they'll get to oversee their sisters as seniors. It's so adorable, not just seeing a household hierarchy come into existence, but also having a hand in shaping its foundations. Makes me feel like a girl again." "

But let's be frank about it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]... the princess is better suited as a monster, isn't she?" Olivia's hardly the worst amongst the motley crew you've gathered under your roof, that's true. And as for what she looks like... if the fairy tale she's referencing the one you're think she is, then there's a lesson in there about not judging people by their appearances. She's a lot more pleasant and mindful of others these days, regardless of what she looks like now. "Tch, you know how to flatter a girl. But back to the point, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ] — sure, if there was any chance I wasn't disowned or considered dead already, that's gone with Louis' birth. And that's fine, my place for the foreseeable future is here at your side. Maybe some news of this vaguely familiar beastly wolf-woman will filter back to Clairemont, or maybe the do-gooder gothmanders will see fit to inform my house just what's happened to me and their precious spellsinger." Speaking of that... might there be a chance someone might come up to try and at least reclaim that? "The spellsinger? I doubt it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Not that I'll write it off completely, but I think I might have been the only Leroux in two generations to touch that thing in the vault, what with all the dust it'd gathered. The only actual loss to my folks would be of prestige if it ever got known I'd stolen it before heading up north, but that's between the gothmanders and my folks to sort out." Well, it's not like you're about to give up Olivia or the spellsinger even if her family did come knocking. [olivia.isCollared |She's now your property, and you're not in the habit of letting others just lay claim to your things. Olivia gives you a smile that's equal parts nasty and rueful. "Oh, don't I know it, Dearest [pc.Master]. |[pc.bg noblescion |You're probably just a little biased, but you're all in favor of noble brats striking out on their own. Likely not to begin with, but I'm sure together, we could give them some incentive to agree with us. |She's under your protection now. If you can stare down gothmanders for her sake, a couple of aristocrats with pretensions as to the old empire shouldn't be any trouble. Olivia gives you a nasty grin. "I don't think my folks have ever been told no directly to their faces. Now I'm almost hoping that they'll show up just to be shut down. ] ] "One way or the other, though... despite everything that's happened, I'm glad to be here, including having given you a pup and all. Whatever happens back in idyllic, warm Clairemont by the sea... that's their own business. If Louis keeps his temperament as a pup for the next two decades or so... maybe his dear old mother will ask if he's interested in claiming his birthright. We'll see what happens then." |[pc.bg noblescion |Olivia rolls her eyes. "Please, Dearest. Your situation and mine are nothing alike." Both she and you are noble scions who left home due to circumstances to make their own way in the world. Isn't that good enough? "That's like saying that we're alike because we have eyes and noses — technically true, but also extremely meaningless. I may not have been the Leroux heir, but at least I was the spare. You didn't even rise to that honor. "Not that I'm saying that my situation was superior to yours — I sure did envy my spoiled little brother in several ways, given that being the spare's spare means one possesses a lot more autonomy that one would otherwise. But we're nothing alike." |Olivia sighs and looks askance. "Waiting for me? Hardly. I suppose my departure and purloining of the family's spellsinger would cause some embarrassment, but I was the spare, after all. I can't imagine my spoiled little brother being very happy at the situation, given that he's in all likelihood had to give up his carefree life for some small responsibility." She sounds like she left home under difficult circumstances, to put it lightly. "There were several personal differences in opinion, that's all. And before you start thinking of runaway princesses, they had nothing to do with me being the spare, or the role that was intended for me and that I'd understood to be my fate from the outset. In fact, I quite liked it; how things have ended up isn't what I'd have wanted, but it's the hand I've been dealt." ] Then she was permitted to leave home? "I wasn't permitted, Dearest." Oh, brother. rows.original:
So, about the rest of her folks...
    
    "What's there to say? The Leroux estate and its fiefdom's down by the south-eastern coast. Small port city, mostly for ships to take on necessities than any actual trade. Mild all year round, great soil for pears and pear wine. One of my ancestors distinguished himself during the Godswar and eventually came home with a spellsinger from up north, carved out a little fiefdom. Lovely, idyllic, happy fat people, lovely river barges as the waters get shallow near the coast, none of the violent nonsense that goes on in the heartlands.
    
    "I had everything I ever wanted, Dearest. But the gods can be cruel, and they play games with our lives. So here I am, probably unrecgonizable by my own kin at this point, narrowly having avoided becoming rape bait for a pack of beasts."
    
    She's being very evasive about the details of her family.
    
    "Yes, I am. And maybe someday the issue will be forced... but for now, there's no point in discussing them overmuch, and it makes me depressed. So please, bear with me if I dance around the issue in response to you pressing me."
rows.translation:
那么，关于她其他的家人……
    
    “有什么好说的呢？勒鲁家的宅邸和封地在东南沿海。那里有座小港口城市，主要是让船只补给必需品，谈不上什么正经贸易。那里全年气候温和，土壤非常适合种梨和酿梨酒。我的一位祖先在神战中建功立业，后来从北方带回了一位咒歌者，开辟了一小块领地。那地方可爱、宁静，人们心宽体胖、安居乐业；近海处水浅，河上还有漂亮的驳船；完全没有腹地那些暴力纷争的破事。
    
    “我曾拥有我想要的一切，亲爱的。但神明有时很残忍，他们会拿我们的性命当游戏。所以现在我成了这副模样，恐怕连自己的亲族都认不出来了，还险些沦为一群野兽的泄欲对象。”
    
    她对家里的事避而不谈，非常回避细节。
    
    “是的，我确实在回避。也许有一天这事会被逼到台面上……但现在，过多谈论他们毫无意义，只会让我心情低落。所以如果我面对你的追问总是绕圈子，请多包涵。”

rows.original: Olivia's eyes mist over a little as her gaze grows distant. "Oh, Dearest... it's just a little place off the east coast of the Belharan mainland. A beautiful land blessed with rolling hills and fertile valleys, and the coast keeps the weather mild all year round. The worst we have to worry about are tribespeople from Valgar causing trouble... there's no serious work for mercenaries, which is why we export so many inland, haha. "By good fortune, we were largely untouched by the worst of the Godswar... the grassy downs of the heartlands plains, without the caravan-swallowing chasms that just yawn as they please. A place where people have moved past scrabbling in the dirt and can turn their minds to culture." Such an idyllic and rich land must be well-defended to survive amidst no end of hungry gazes in that part of the world and beyond. "As I said, Dearest, one of our biggest exports are mercenaries. Fight them over there before they get to our borders... and if they do get to our shores, every family is obliged to own and maintain a weapon or three to fight off the vultures. There's the paladin order, of course, but they have their own agenda which doesn't always dovetail neatly with what the secular rulers want. Power grinds against power even if the two ostensibly work together; small scuffles between church and state are only to be expected at times. "But I saw little of that growing up, even if it was expected that at least one Leroux of each generation would spend some time in a mercenary company. It was a distant future to a girl enjoying the cool summers and warm winters eating lemon and honey cakes." ... "I'd be lying if I said I didn't want to go home someday, but that day isn't today. You don't know what you're going to miss until it's gone, and perhaps for good." She turns over her hands and looks down into her furry palms. "So..." Fine wines and cheeses, freshly baked bread? "The landward breeze coming in over a long, gentle shore, with home just visible in the distance and no one else around for an eternity." Olivia sighs. "Little pups playing in the shade of the trees, unaware of the cruel and uncaring world that lies beyond the mountains. Yvennes is worth preserving, and was fortunate to be unscathed."
rows.translation: 奥利维亚的目光渐渐变得遥远，眼中也蒙上了一层雾气。“哦，亲爱的……那只是贝尔哈兰大陆东海岸的一个小地方而已。那是一片风景优美的土地，有连绵的丘陵和肥沃的山谷，而海岸线也让那里的天气一年到头都很温和。最让我们担心的是瓦尔加族的部落成员会惹麻烦……对于雇佣兵来说，根本没有什么真正的战斗任务可做，这就是为什么我们要把这么多雇佣兵派往内陆地区，哈哈。 “幸运的是，我们在这场神战之中基本上没有受到太大的影响。…那些长满青草的平原地带，没有那些会吞噬商队的深谷，那些深谷可以随心所欲地张开它们的口。在这里，人们不再需要在泥土中挣扎求生，而是可以将精力投入到文化的发展之中。 这样一片理想而富饶的土地，要想在世界上那个地区以及更广阔的区域里生存下来，就必须有严密的防御措施来保护它。 正如我所说，亲爱的，我们最重要的出口产品之一就是雇佣兵。在他们来到我们的边境之前，就在那里把他们消灭掉……这样就不会有麻烦了。确实当这些威胁来到我们的海岸时，每个家庭都不得不拥有一两件武器，用来抵御那些掠夺者。当然，还有圣骑士团，但他们有自己的目的，而这些目的并不总是与世俗统治者的意愿相符。力量与力量之间总是会产生冲突，即使表面上看它们是在合作；教会与国家之间偶尔发生一些小摩擦也是意料之中的事。 “但在我成长的过程中，我几乎没见过这类事情发生，尽管人们预计每一代人中至少会有一名勒鲁家族的人在佣兵组织里待上一段时间。对那个喜欢在凉爽的夏天和温暖的冬天里品尝柠檬蜂蜜蛋糕的女孩来说，那是一个遥远的未来。 …… 如果我说自己不希望有一天能回家，那肯定是谎言。但那天还不是今天。直到某样东西真正消失，你才会意识到自己将会失去什么——而也许，那种失去是永久性的。她双手交叠，低头凝视着自己那布满绒毛的手掌，然后说道：“那么……” 美酒与奶酪，还有新鲜出炉的面包吗？ “海风从漫长而平缓的海岸吹来，远处的家乡清晰可见，而周围却空无一人，仿佛时间在这一刻静止了。奥利维亚叹了口气：“那些小狗在树荫下玩耍，却不知道山外有一个如此残酷、冷漠的世界。伊薇恩是个值得被保护的存在，她很幸运，没有受到任何伤害。

rows.original: [olivia.anyKids |"Oh, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. It's ironic, isn't it? If I'm to be honest with myself, it's only gotten worse —" Yes, about that. If it's any consolation, Olivia doesn't look any different than she did when she arrived at the wayfort. There's that matter of her MILFing out in all directions, but as the name suggests that's just an effect of having had pups. "That's very nice of you to say, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but I can feel it. Even if it's not as plain at what happened with all of those brutes like Asgeir or Refnir, I know it's happening inside me, and having had your pups has only hastened the process. That's what Drifa says, at any rate. "Look, don't give me that face. If I've finally gotten over fretting about it, I don't want you doing so in my place, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. [drifa.isCorrupt |Besides, racing Drifa to the bottom is so much more fun now that there haven't been any serious negatives on either Louis or me |Drifa isn't the kind to ever give up hope, so I'm sure she's still all about finding a cure. But I've long since put any notions of being cured behind me — I've to work with what's there, not what I would like ]. "It's a sensation, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ] — I don't know how to put it otherwise. A feeling in the pit of my stomach, under my skin... [olivia.isCollared |I suppose the way I've been acting hasn't helped any, but I don't fear it the way I did any more |now that I know to look for it, I can feel it acting up every time I take brown leaf, making it clear the drug won't be effective forever, and that day will come sooner than I think ]." ...You take it she still wants you to kill Tharsus if you ever meet the warlock again? "Yes, but now it's more of him being an annoying menace to others than anything else. Things may have turned out well for me, but I'm more than aware of how lucky I am, the close calls I've had, and the people who were here to help me. Whoever his next victims are, I have my doubts about whether they'll be as fortunate as I've been. "And to be sure, just because I've turned around his machinations to my benefit doesn't mean he ought to get away with what he intended for me. I may have accepted my corruption after realizing it's not a threat to me any longer, but that doesn't absolve that old perv any less — quite the opposite, if anything." [pc.swornGod nareva |It's your job to deal with those like Tharsus. Olivia scoffs. "As much as I'm glad to you for being lenient with me, Tharsus is a completely different case and utterly unrepentant to boot. Please don't make the same mistake of trying to take him in if your paths ever cross." At this point, his crimes likely warrant something more severe than being made dreamless. |You get the feeling that he'll be forcing the issue should you ever meet again. Olivia nods slowly. "As much as I'm glad to you for being lenient with me, Tharsus is a completely different case and utterly unrepentant to boot. I know I'm not who I was compared to when I set foot under this roof, let alone when I was dragged into that miserable hole or when I left home. [drifa.isCorrupt |Drifa and I are |I'm ] becoming something else, moreso with recent events, but... I don't fear the change for what it might do to me or our son any longer. So much of my fretting has been just me making up imaginary problems for myself, I'm sort of embarrassed. Maybe it'd have been more of a problem had I fought it more strongly, but using this power for what it can do for me hasn't been so bad, either." |Olivia is silent for a minute or two, her expression carefully neutral and unreadable. Then, slowly, she shakes her head and sighs. "Dearest. Have you ever wondered why one of my conditions for stepping aside while you went at Asgeir was to kill Tharsus?" If you remember correctly, none of the words she used at the time were %"kill" or any synonym thereof. If she'd wanted you to kill Tharsus rather than just give him a good beating, well, it's the first time you're hearing of it and way too late for that. "Way too late, I agree. After meeting him for yourself, no doubt you understand why I expected any fight with him would've been to the death or worse. But as I may or may not have mentioned at the time, he was the reason I was stuck in that hole." The jailor, Gertrude... you're beginning to see where this is going. Olivia nods slowly. "He told Asgeir that it would affirm my loyalty to the cause, and the sweeter I was as eye candy, the better at my intended task I would be. The first... well, I'm here, and the second..." With how many [silly |simps |adoring fans ] she had amongst the corrupted lupines? Not wholly incorrect. "Don't get me wrong, Dearest — it's not all bad, or at least that's what I tell myself when I'm alone. But it's also possible to do the right thing for the wrong reasons, or to make the best out of a bad situation. "Look at me. Tharsus turned my body into that of a furry bimbo's — if it weren't for my face, I don't think anyone back in Yvennes would be able to recognize me at this point." She thins her lips. "The creep just wanted to see what he could get away with; I'm sure he'd have given me the brains of a bimbo as well if Asgeir weren't breathing down his neck the entire time he was working on me. I can't ever go home, not without a lot of inconvenient questions being asked that I really would prefer not to answer. "But you know what worries me the most? That what he did to me doesn't just stop on the outside. I won't go into the details and I'm fine for now, but it keeps me awake at night. Whatever Tharsus did to me, alchemy isn't fixing it: trust me, that blind elf tried, and none of her usual potions had any effect on me. Whatever he did, it's more deeply rooted than that, and it makes my skin crawl." ... "So no. I didn't always look like this, Dearest. And just so we're clear: if you see Tharsus again, kill him if you can. Hack off his head and burn the body, because you just know that you need to be sure with someone like him." Next time — if there's a next time — he won't be getting away. "Good." A sigh. "I guess there's a silver lining in all of this: whatever Tharsus did to me, it's quite territorial and doesn't like sharing. I did mention the alchemy stuff earlier, but... well, there've been a few other things I've tried in my spare time, and none of them worked. If there's any means of getting me back to how I used to be, it's not going to be by means of forcing the issue, it seems." rows.original: Olivia wrinkles her nose. "That thing's still there? I would've imagined some god-botherer or the other would've come by and emptied it out posthaste." [var0 |Well, Drifa's trying to find a cure for the corrupted lupines. As irksome as it may be, devising a remedy should be easier if the source of the affliction can be studied in addition to its victims. "That's the same bullshit Tharsus fed Asgeir." Lies need a kernel of truth to be plausible, she should know as much. An antidote is much easier to concoct if you have the viper that bit you in the first place. A sigh. "Just be careful that your dear little doggy doesn't accidentally slip and fall in while studying it, that's all. It would be a terrible shame if she went for a dive in the goop and ended up a permanently horny bimbo slut, too turned on to piece two thoughts together." [drifa.isCorrupt |Oh, is that the worst that can happen? In that case, you don't need to worry, because Drifa is already a constantly horny goth bimbo slut. There's nothing more the goop pool can do to her, so she'll be just fine, and yes, she does retain her capability for higher thought |After seeing what happened to the various people who've been exposed to it, you have complete confidence in Drifa's desire to avoid the same fate ]. Besides, it's not like Drifa's the butter-fingered sort. Unless there's someone who might be motivated to push her in? "I have no idea what you're insinuating, Dearest. It's not as if I care to leave my seat most days. Never want to go back to that place again." Even to get rid of a rival? |It's more the question of how to dispose of it safely, which means you ought to learn all you can about it first to avoid some kind of unfortunate accident. "Details like that shouldn't bother people like old man Sanders. Mark my words: once a crusader, always a crusader at heart. Sure, he's not the type to charge in blazing with holy might, but neither is he the kind to pass a fault like that." Or maybe you're just aware that the pool isn't going to do anything on its own and you can spend all the time you need to learning about it so you can get rid of it safely. That, and Tharsus and his work are still out there somewhere. "Oh, so you haven't even told the old man about it?" Drifa's handling the matter. You trust her to do as she sees fit. When she decides that nothing more can be learned and it's time to get rid of it, you'll see about roping in some help for the act. "That little slip? Pft. She's liable to accidentally fall in and emerge [drifa.isCorrupt |even more of a bimbo than she is already |an airheaded bimbo ]. Actually, scratch that; becoming a bimbo would be an improvement on what she is right now." Misery loves company, doesn't it? Is Olivia worried that Drifa might be competing with her for your affections? ] "Her? A rival? You wound me, Dearest; we aren't even in the same league, so don't you deign to drag me down to her level. If you have a romantic drama rattling around in that skull of yours, put it down on paper and leave the both of us out of it." Anyways, enough byplay. What does she know about the [silly |goop |eldritch ] pool? "It was there before I arrived, I know as much. Can't say for sure if Tharsus made it himself, or if he simply found it and harnessed its powers, but I think it's the latter because the old creep didn't seem wholly in control of what it did to people. He could point it in a general direction, but didn't have that much control over the details. Wouldn't have need of experiments if he were its creator, right? "Or maybe he did create it and it went out of his control, or it became more than what he expected and he was trying to rein in his wayward creation. I dunno. [var0 |Since Asgeir's still hanging around, why don't you ask him about it? |Too bad you sent Asgeir and his lot to walk the ice. Bet he could answer a whole lot of questions I can't, heh. ]" And her experience with the [silly |goop |eldritch ] pool? Olivia winces. "I don't want to talk about it." There're many things in life that one may find unsavory but have to do nonetheless. A sigh. "I really can't tell you much. Tharsus had me tied up and drugged for the whole thing, because, in his own words: 'she's a feisty one'. It was hot, and it felt like my body was burning up... it wasn't just what was in the pool, too, because he dumped a whole lot of foul-smelling stuff into it before he had Asgeir hold me down under the surface. "From how I saw the brutes behaving around it from time to time, I don't think it's a big problem on its own. Makes you horny for a bit, but that passes. It's more a catalyst for other things that might happen or be added to it, makes things act in unpredictable ways. I may look and feel fine now, but there's always the lurking dread in the back of my mind that I might just wake up one morning with an extra arm or leg or something." That's unlikely, given that Asgeir needed her presentable in order to do her job. "Weren't you listening? Whether he made or found it, Tharsus didn't have perfect control over what the pool did. What if he made a mistake? What if he was just a spiteful old creep? What if —" All right, you get her drift. You're not going to be getting much you don't already know about the pool out of Olivia, it seems. "There is one thing, I suppose. Now that I look like this, my body refuses to change by any means that might be considered artificial. I spent a small fortune on that blind elf trying to put myself right, and nothing worked. The alchemy wasn't wrong or anything, it just didn't take; I guess the goop must have done it. "I'm not a magician or anything, I'm afraid, and I just told you all I know. Take it or leave it, Dearest." Olivia's ears droop, and she [olivia.isPregnant |rolls her eyes |drains her wine glass in a single large gulp ]. "It's all so tiring."

生活中有很多事情，虽然让人不情愿去做，但却不得不面对。 她叹了口气：“我真的没什么可以告诉你的。在整个过程中，萨瑟斯把我绑起来，还给我下了药，因为用他自己的话来说：‘她是个脾气暴躁的人’。当时天气很热，我感觉自己的身体都在燃烧……而且不仅仅是游泳池里的水，因为在阿斯盖尔把我按在水下之前，他还往里面倒了很多散发着恶臭的东西。 从那些野兽偶尔围绕它活动的样子来看，我觉得这个问题本身并不严重。虽然会让人产生一些奇怪的念头，但很快就会过去。更重要的是，它可能会引发其他一些事情的发生，或者促使某些新的元素被添加进来，从而使事情的发展变得难以预测。现在我看起来和感觉都挺正常的，但心里总隐隐担心，也许有一天早上醒来，我会发现自己多出了一条胳膊或一条腿之类的。 这不太可能，因为阿斯盖尔需要她具备良好的形象，才能胜任这份工作。 “你没在听吗？无论那是他制造的，还是他找来的，塔苏斯其实并不能完全控制那个装置的功能。要是他出了错怎么办？要是他只是一个心怀恶意的老变态怎么办？要是…… 好吧，你应该明白她的意思了。看来，从奥利维亚那里，你很难得到关于那个泳池的什么新信息了。 “不过有一件事吧。现在我变成了这个样子，我的身体就是拒绝接受任何可能被认为是人工手段的改造。我花了大笔钱请那个盲人精灵来帮我恢复原状，但什么方法都不管用。炼金术本身并没有问题，只是根本不起作用；我想，可能是那些黏稠的物质起了反作用吧。 我并不是什么魔术师，也不是什么特别的人，我只是把我知道的一切都告诉你们了。你们爱信就信，不信就算了，亲爱的。”奥利维亚垂下了耳朵，说道。 [olivia.isPregnant |翻了个白眼 |将酒杯里的酒一饮而尽 ]这一切真的太让人疲惫了。
rows.raw: " Olivia wrinkles her nose. "That thing's still there? I would've imagined some god-botherer or the other would've come by and emptied it out posthaste." [var0 |Well, Drifa's trying to find a cure for the corrupted lupines. As irksome as it may be, devising a remedy should be easier if the source of the affliction can be studied in addition to its victims. "That's the same bullshit Tharsus fed Asgeir." Lies need a kernel of truth to be plausible, she should know as much. An antidote is much easier to concoct if you have the viper that bit you in the first place. A sigh. "Just be careful that your dear little doggy doesn't accidentally slip and fall in while studying it, that's all. It would be a terrible shame if she went for a dive in the goop and ended up a permanently horny bimbo slut, too turned on to piece two thoughts together." [drifa.isCorrupt |Oh, is that the worst that can happen? In that case, you don't need to worry, because Drifa is already a constantly horny goth bimbo slut. There's nothing more the goop pool can do to her, so she'll be just fine, and yes, she does retain her capability for higher thought |After seeing what happened to the various people who've been exposed to it, you have complete confidence in Drifa's desire to avoid the same fate ]. Besides, it's not like Drifa's the butter-fingered sort. Unless there's someone who might be motivated to push her in? "I have no idea what you're insinuating, Dearest. It's not as if I care to leave my seat most days. Never want to go back to that place again." Even to get rid of a rival? |It's more the question of how to dispose of it safely, which means you ought to learn all you can about it first to avoid some kind of unfortunate accident. "Details like that shouldn't bother people like old man Sanders. Mark my words: once a crusader, always a crusader at heart. Sure, he's not the type to charge in blazing with holy might, but neither is he the kind to pass a fault like that." Or maybe you're just aware that the pool isn't going to do anything on its own and you can spend all the time you need to learning about it so you can get rid of it safely. That, and Tharsus and his work are still out there somewhere. "Oh, so you haven't even told the old man about it?" Drifa's handling the matter. You trust her to do as she sees fit. When she decides that nothing more can be learned and it's time to get rid of it, you'll see about roping in some help for the act. "That little slip? Pft. She's liable to accidentally fall in and emerge [drifa.isCorrupt |even more of a bimbo than she is already |an airheaded bimbo ]. Actually, scratch that; becoming a bimbo would be an improvement on what she is right now." Misery loves company, doesn't it? Is Olivia worried that Drifa might be competing with her for your affections? ] "Her? A rival? You wound me, Dearest; we aren't even in the same league, so don't you deign to drag me down to her level. If you have a romantic drama rattling around in that skull of yours, put it down on paper and leave the both of us out of it." Anyways, enough byplay. What does she know about the [silly |goop |eldritch ] pool? "It was there before I arrived, I know as much. Can't say for sure if Tharsus made it himself, or if he simply found it and harnessed its powers, but I think it's the latter because the old creep didn't seem wholly in control of what it did to people. He could point it in a general direction, but didn't have that much control over the details. Wouldn't have need of experiments if he were its creator, right? "Or maybe he did create it and it went out of his control, or it became more than what he expected and he was trying to rein in his wayward creation. I dunno. [var0 |Since Asgeir's still hanging around, why don't you ask him about it? |Too bad you sent Asgeir and his lot to walk the ice. Bet he could answer a whole lot of questions I can't, heh. ]" And her experience with the [silly |goop |eldritch ] pool? Olivia winces. "I don't want to talk about it." There're many things in life that one may find unsavory but have to do nonetheless. A sigh. "I really can't tell you much. Tharsus had me tied up and drugged for the whole thing, because, in his own words: 'she's a feisty one'. It was hot, and it felt like my body was burning up... it wasn't just what was in the pool, too, because he dumped a whole lot of foul-smelling stuff into it before he had Asgeir hold me down under the surface. "From how I saw the brutes behaving around it from time to time, I don't think it's a big problem on its own. Makes you horny for a bit, but that passes. It's more a catalyst for other things that might happen or be added to it, makes things act in unpredictable ways. I may look and feel fine now, but there's always the lurking dread in the back of my mind that I might just wake up one morning with an extra arm or leg or something." That's unlikely, given that Asgeir needed her presentable in order to do her job. "Weren't you listening? Whether he made or found it, Tharsus didn't have perfect control over what the pool did. What if he made a mistake? What if he was just a spiteful old creep? What if —" All right, you get her drift. You're not going to be getting much you don't already know about the pool out of Olivia, it seems. "There is one thing, I suppose. Now that I look like this, my body refuses to change by any means that might be considered artificial. I spent a small fortune on that blind elf trying to put myself right, and nothing worked. The alchemy wasn't wrong or anything, it just didn't take; I guess the goop must have done it. "I'm not a magician or anything, I'm afraid, and I just told you all I know. Take it or leave it, Dearest." Olivia's ears droop, and she [olivia.isPregnant |rolls her eyes |drains her wine glass in a single large gulp ]. "It's all so tiring." "

rows.original: "Oh, plenty of times. I am, after all, an heiress — I was raised to expect it sometime. A duty to be dispensed with for all the nice things that I received thanks to my station. I've never held any illusions about marriage the same way someone with fewer responsibilities and expectations like Drifa would be free to have, but I've never really feared it, either." [pc.bg noblescion |That's about what your experience amounts to as well, being the spare's spare. If you'd stayed at home, that would've been one of your possible fates — more than possible, in fact. Certainly not something on the level of a heiress like Olivia, but... well, the alternative would've been that you'd be sent to some institution or the other you family had good ties with. Going out and making a name for yourself was the right choice, even if it hasn't always been smooth sailing since. "P |Free to have... well, that's technically true, but practically speaking most common folk are limited to finding love within a day's walk of home. Sounds like whether one's high or low-born, it's rare that people actually get to make a meaningful choice about matters of the heart. "You're right. We're all bound," Olivia muses. "Just in different ways. But I was talking about illusions... there's a reason why some of my ilk enjoy playing peasant for a bit, safe in the knowledge they can quit at the slightest genuine adversity. "Now, p ]eople like you, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]? You have genuine choice in both to meet people you like, and the ability to woo them. You've been blessed with a gift one in a million have, so don't waste it." Back to the point, though... Olivia raises an eyebrow. "Why? Thinking of doing it for me? Wait, no, don't answer that. But if you are, I'm glad you at least brought it up before actually making any attempt — there's a lot to consider, some of it which goes beyond you and me." [pc.bg noblescion |You'd be tying your house to hers, if nothing else. "There is that. You're qualified by all the old imperial customs... but how much sway do they still have in this miserable corner of the world? That being said, that isn't my main concern." It's not. |Why? Does the fact that you're not of noble birth make any difference? "Now why would your mind immediately go to that, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]?" Because... well, it's the usual objection that's raised in these situations. "Please. The whole of the law is what the strong agree on, and doubly so in this miserable corner of the continent. But before you raise any objections, that isn't my point anyway." What is, then? ] A sigh. "Look at me, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. I'm damaged goods. It's a toss-up that my kin would recognize me at this point, and even if they did they wouldn't be welcoming the oversexed creature I've become with open arms. Having fun is one thing, but as far as serious commitments are concerned... I'm still working towards coming to terms with everything that's happened. I'm not the woman I used to be coming out of that hole in the ground, and I don't know if I deserve a marriage." [olivia.isPregnant |You point at the round bump that adorns Olivia's middle. And that isn't a serious commitment? "Did you hear what I just said, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]? It wasn't about whether I can handle commitments, it's about whether I deserve them. And I absolutely deserve [olivia.isCollared |pumping brat after brat out of my belly to make a pack for you[drifa.hasKids | with Drifa ] |this for daring to tempt the gods to do their worst ]. "But when it comes to tying the knot? You could do much better, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Given what I've been through and what I am now, I'm not sure I deserve that." It doesn't fully make sense that Olivia's accepted one thing but not the other, but then again this is a matter of the heart and not the head. On the other hand, there is a glimmer of what she's on about: having pups is a different kind of commitment than being wedded, a far more one-sided one, and being surrounded by sycophants means being a lot less leery of genuine affection. "I... I'm getting better." Olivia smiles weakly. "Certainly someday, and perhaps even soon; our son does help put this whole corruption thing in perspective. But not today[silly |, not within the scope of the game. Maybe in an ending? ]" |[olivia.anyKids |You gesture at the somewhat more MILFy and less bimbo-tastic figure that Olivia's toting around these days. Being a mother [olivia.isCollared |and open to the idea of doing it all over again ]isn't a commitment? "That's not what I said, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. I deserve that, not just for tempting the gods, but also for letting myself get too close to you — not that I regret it. But having you — I mean, that supposed someone — reach out to me like that, well. It coming from me, I've grown accustomed to, but having someone else give it to me..." It still doesn't full make sense, but you're starting to understand where Olivia's coming from — it's a matter of emotions, not reason. That, and receiving genuine affection is a thing that's still new to Olivia; she can't have received much of it back in Yvennes, and being stuck in a hole with a gaggle of sycophants must've only made it worse. Olivia catches your eye, nods, and graces you with a thin smile. "I've considered it before, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], and been beset by disquieting thoughts every time. I know it sounds odd to already have pups with someone and not be ready to accept a marriage with [pc.himHer], but they're not the same kind of commitment. "I'm getting better[olivia.isCollared |; being your pet is most genuine affection I've received for the gods know how long ]. Certainly someday, perhaps even soon, I'll be able to entertain the idea; our son does help put this whole corruption thing in perspective. But not today[silly |, not within the scope of the game. Maybe in an ending? |. ]" |[olivia.isCollared |No wedding for the likes of her, huh? You crook a finger, and Olivia obediently lifts her chin to allow you to slip it under her jewelled collar and pull her close. But she's okay with being a pet? "There are those who would say there's not much difference between the two, which I find silly," Olivia replies with a grin, her gaze boring into yours. "But then, it's not what you're thinking, Dearest [pc.Master]." Pray tell, what is she thinking, then? "It's not about what would be expected of me if I were to be wed, it's what would be given from my [pc.mf |husband |wife ]. What I get from being a so-called pet is far more stable — no, sincere. I haven't been under your roof for very long compared to the rest of my life, and even so... look, it's just a nice kind of affection suited for someone who hasn't had much of the genuine deal." No doubt many people have professed to like her over the years, but failed to follow through? "You could say that, I suppose. I still have to get over certain troublesome notions, like whether I'd deserve it or not despite being damaged goods. And don't you tell me I'm not, because I clearly am. "It's strange, isn't it? Most people would consider being a pet degrading, and I certainly would have, but it's all about changing your perspective in the end. Someday, perhaps even soon, I'd consider a wedding... but not [silly |within the scope of the game |now ]." |Damaged goods, huh? That's a depressing way to describe her current condition. "And an accurate one. Someone to be used up and thrown away — which you haven't done. Which then begs the question: why not?" Yes, why not? Nothing you've heard so far has convinced you that Olivia's beyond saving. She wouldn't be here, if that's the way you thought of her. A sigh. "And I have you to thank for that. To be sure, it's not something that I'm used to." You remember her surprise when the gothmanders came calling and you were willing to vouch for her. "No one I've ever known would have done that for me." A thin smile. "Not even if I'd been, uh, yielding from the start. Odd for someone who comes from my station to say, isn't it?" [pc.bg noblescion |No, not really. If you hadn't been the spare's spare and thus largely beneath notice, the world might have been considerably less kind to you. It's not too much of a stretch from your own past to see where Olivia's coming from. |Perhaps. For someone to have always only known the lap of luxury, yet be poor in ways others not so privileged would have enjoyed... you can see where she's coming from, even though it does rankle coming from someone who was born with the proverbial silver spoon in her mouth. ] Olivia shakes her head. "Well, whatever you think, Dearest, having you do all that for me... it's something I still have to get used to. I'm no stranger to responsibilities, but the other half of the equation is still scary." "I know it sounds odd to have gotten to this point with you vouching for me with the Narevans and still be hesitant about this kind of thing, but... it's just different, okay?" You're starting to understand where Olivia's coming from. She can't have received much genuine affection in Yvennes, and being stuck in a hole with a gaggle of sycophants must've only made it worse. To her, marriage was always framed as an arrangement of convenience at best; she's still not used to this kind of freedom. Right?. "I'm coming around to it, especially seeing how Drifa acts around you. But as soon as it might be, I'm still not there yet[silly |, not within the scope of the game. Maybe in an ending? |. ]" ] ] ]
