rows.original: [rand |"Louis? Little bastard's always trying to get out and around, whether it's me or Drifa minding him. He's already crawling and climbing, and absolutely refuses to be contained. I don't know where he got this penchant from — it's a far cry from long walks through the orchards or down the beach that was about all the exercise I got as a girl." It's a good thing that this wayfort is right above a river and wedged in the middle of the forest. A pup like Louis will eventually want rivers to swim in, trees to climb, caves to explore and boulders to test his strength against. Although there's something about what Olivia said... "Yes, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]?" Did she have to call her son a bastard? You know that's what he technically is, but it... it sounds unkind to title him that way for something which isn't his fault. Olivia snaps her fingers, her ears perking up. "Oh, I've been here so long that I forget that I'm in this benighted part of the world. You see, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], %'bastard' has a rather romantic connotation where I come from. As a bard, I'm familiar with quite a few tales, but there's one that has recently found a place in my heart since our son was born." You can guess, but... "It's that of the bastard who has set his eye on what ought to be his," Olivia purrs, pausing to sip from [olivia.isPregnant |a mug of honeyed water |her wineglass ]. "Clad in a suit of fine black armor and a helm that conceals his face, he journeys to the land of his relatives. Of course, they give a bastard no time of day, so he puts them all to the fire and sword, deposes a bunch of self-righteous twits who have never done anything more strenuous than eat honey cakes, and sets things in order before returning to his holdings in colder, harsher place." And behind the bastard will be his dear old mother whom everyone thought dead decades ago? A smile. "I'm not saying that it's a portent of the future; sometimes tales are just tales. But those that stick with us often have the ring of truth to them. The tale of the hard-edged bastard is one that's quite popular in the Clairemont area, mostly because of how many times it played out during the imperium, with half a dozen different actors all playing the role of the bastard. House Leroux escaped being set as the stage for one of those performances... maybe that just means it's overdue for just that. "We'll find out in two decades or so, I'm sure. But even though he's barely out of the womb, it's clear our son is the kind who likes to do things, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. And should he choose to descend upon his ancestral holdings and savage the flock of proverbial sheep... may the gods help all who stand in his way, because I won't. "So don't worry about it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. When I call our son a bastard, it's a loving term of endearment and hope for his future. And should he choose to never bother with the warm, fat heartlands to the south, there's no shortage of things to do in these miserable borderlands, as you can attest." |"Our son is such a hungry little bastard, I love him for it. Always more than happy to oblige me when I wrap things up for the day and am full to bursting." Hey, at least that bust of hers is being put to good use. Olivia rolls her eyes, but keeps her smile. "I know you say that in jest, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but you're not that far off the mark. I wasn't flat to begin with, and even so I'm begrudgingly glad for what's been done to me in that regard. Of course, I did most of the work myself while I was pregnant with your child, but still! It's what it is." You shake your head, remembering just how large and heavy Olivia had become while carrying Louis in her belly. You'd be worried if a pup that size didn't have an appetite to match. "It's kind of troubling, to be honest. He won't take any milk but mine — oh, he'll drink anything else, just gulp it all down like the bottomless pit he is, but keeps on acting as if he hasn't been fed afterwards. I have to squeeze out a whole bunch every morning and bottle it for Drifa while she minds him for me, it's —" — Something she happily does as an excuse to get herself off first thing out of bed. "Well. I'm not denying it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. It helps wake me up, if nothing else. [var0 |He'll take enough of Drifa's milk to stop complaining for a bit, but nothing but that of his dear mother will do." There's a distinct note of smugness in Olivia's voice as she prattles on. |Is it troublesome? Sometimes. But Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], surely you agree that it's but a trifle in the greater picture." A wistful note creeps into Olivia's voice. ] "I didn't think minding a bastard would be this satisfying, but here we are." |"When I think about our son, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], I'm glad that I came up to this miserable corner of the world. By the gods, even enduring that time in a damp hole might just have been worth it." That's a rather sharp about-face from the woman she used to be, but then again having a pup is a pretty big thing in one's life. That being said, what exactly changed her perspective? "I..." Olivia rubs her cheeks and looks a little bashful. "Well, if I'd been back on the estate, Louis wouldn't have been treated like a pup, but as an asset. I... I would've been a lot more of a bitch too, and wouldn't have minded leaving him to a nursemaid all day while I ran the estate. I mean, now I have to have Drifa mind him from time to time while I see to your guests, but that doesn't mean I don't feel bad about it, or that I don't take him with me as much as I can." You nod slowly and motion for Olivia to go on.[pc.bg noblescion | You've been through this before, too — heir or spare, no one likes being reduced to just a role. ] "I've mentioned before that I'd been raised to expect certain things in my life, and Louis would've been seen as just another duty to be dispensed with. That's how the old me would've seen it, I'm sure. But here, living under your roof, having gone through what I did and not having an entire retinue nipping at my heels all day... it's just Drifa[wayfort.hasMaids |, the maids, ] and Rumie, and I'm glad things have shaken out this way. Like this, our son makes me feel wanted, instead of him just being another duty to be dispensed with." When Olivia puts it like that, if that's how she really feels about the situation... you can see where she's coming from. Having her entire mercenary band taken by the corrupted lupines, being dunked in the [silly |goop |eldritch ] pool, changing on the outside and probably a lot more on the inside, and the fate which awaited her if you hadn't intervened... it might all just have been worth it. Olivia sighs. "It was all worth it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ] — both for him and for me. All this acting out... in the end, all I wanted was attention and to be genuinely liked, something which our son isn't shy about giving. And as I've just pointed out, I don't doubt our son is having a better upbringing here than he would've in his ancestral estate. "I just feel like something's finally clicked in that long-held sense of yearning, and I don't have to be as much of a bitch any more, amazing as that might sound. It feels good how glad he is to see me when I pick him up from Drifa, or while feeding him — a pup isn't always popular with those I have to entertain, but I bring him along as much as I can when his presence helps set the proper mood." She is right. This does sound like a better outcome for everyone involved. Olivia looks down at her hands and flexes her fingers. "I don't regret becoming what I am now, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. If that's the price I have to pay, then it's just something I'll have to accept. I get that our son will gradually grow apart from me when he gets older, as ought to be... but I'm [olivia.isCollared |expecting you to have put several more pups into me by then, mmmh |not going to worry so much about the future that I neglect to spend what time I do have with our son now ]." |"Drifa's teaching me to properly mind children," Olivia sighs. "She says that [drifa.isCorrupt |[drifa.hasKids |if we're going to share the credit for being the progenitors of this pack, I ought to put in a bigger share of the work |if I'm going to be the one to have your pups, the least I can do is to raise your offspring right ] |children are precious and they deserve the best of everything we can give ]. And honestly, I don't disagree with her; it's just that it's a lot to take in at once." And neither do you. No matter how she slices it, it isn't right or responsible to foist her pups on a nursemaid when she ought to be the one in charge, especially with her job here at the wayfort keeping her within a stone's throw of your son. "D-don't look at me like that!" Olivia huffs. "I'm no stranger to being responsible for someone else, but there's a whole world's difference between minding a pet and minding a pup. Taking care of your own infant pups was something that only the peasants did, so it's not like I ever had the chance to practise until our son was born." A pet, huh? You'd never have figured Olivia having any kind of pet. "You may not believe it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but I used to be something of a cat and bird person. Of course, even a kitten needs a lot less care than our son does. Point being, I'm aware of what being responsible for someone else entails, but our son is in a class all by himself. "Anyway. There's just so much more to be done, and while our son quietly puts up with a lot from his bumbling mother I'm not sure I can forgive myself for my mistakes." If she needs more time to mind Louis during the day, you're more than happy to ease her from some of her duties. A shake of her head. "It isn't that I don't have time to mind our son, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. It's about knowing how to do so properly. Drifa aside, I'm also checking in with the village's nursery matron — what was her name again? I forget — Louis may be the resilient kind of pup, but that isn't an excuse for me to make mistakes in raising him. I'll... get better at it, I'm sure. It's not as if I have a choice." |So, you hate to bring this up... but Olivia hasn't noticed any overt signs of corruption in your son, has she? "There isn't a single day where it doesn't come to mind. I don't worry about it, but as his mother I have to keep an eye on how he's growing." Olivia sighs. "When it comes down to it, everything about our son has been scarcely normal — from how he was conceived, to his time inside of me, to how much of a little monster he is. It's clear that the things that happened to me, no thanks to Tharsus, have also tainted him. I'm not going to delude myself on that point. "However... is that necessarily a bad thing? He's robust and clearly overdeveloped for a pup his age, but he's hardly a brute; I don't get the same ugly feeling of wretchedness from him that I did from Asgeir or gods forbid, Refnir. I set him down for a while and he's stalking some vermin or the other, yet knows to not do that to people; he's started to teeth at an abnormally young age, yet has never once bitten me while nursing. Maybe it's just me being his mother, but when I look into our son's eyes I don't get the same sense of dumb brutishness that I saw in every single one of the corrupted lupines. Our son's clearly been affected, but... there's hope. Quite a lot of it, in fact." You know how these things go. A little savagery, directed correctly, has its purposes. Well, a whole lot of savagery and violence as well, but she gets the point you're making. "It's undeniably part of him, but doesn't have to rule him the same way it did those dumb brutes, or even Tharsus calculating madness." Olivia sighs and slouches in her seat. "Just like me, actually. Maybe I'm just trying to wish into existence my hopes for our son, and all of this is just a delusion of mine." There, there. She's not the only one keeping an eye on Louis — you'll be sure to do the same. "It's appreciated. I... I do confess that I have high hopes for his future, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. The hand that rocks the cradle rules the world; it's not manipulation if it's something he wants to do anyway and I have his interests in mind, yes?" All right, she doesn't need to put on a show for you. Yes, yes, Olivia's very scheming and devious. Maybe as the years pass, you'll see how much of that passed to your son. |"I... in a way, I'm glad that all this happened to be; this way, I can actually raise our son with my own hands." That's an interesting way to put it. She wouldn't have been expected to do it herself back home? [pc.bg noblescion |Olivia raises an eyebrow. "Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], I know you're the spare's spare, but you're still titled. Do they do things differently from where you come from?" Perhaps not that much depending on the details of your privileged upbringing, but Olivia makes it sound as if the fate that awaited any heirs she might produce was tantamount to abandonment. That's certainly not what your early years were like. |Olivia turns her gaze from yours. "The surprise in your voice hurts more than you may ever know, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but... oh, there's no denying it. Yes." ...Oh. It sounds like a lonely existence. ] Olivia sighs. "It's expected, you see? A mark of privilege, or at least in that idyllic little corner of the world I come from. Child-rearing is peasant work — people of my station have more important things to tend to, can't be expected to waste precious daylight on a task even animals can accomplish. My parents weren't obliged to so much as speak to me before I could hold a half-intelligent conversation, and as soon as I was out of the womb I was shuffled between any number of wet nurses, minders, tutors... I suppose it's a small mercy that I wasn't fostered out in the old imperial tradition, in which case I might have never actually seen my family until I was a grown woman. "For much of my life, I considered this normal and didn't give it much thought: it was the way of the world and if the peasants did things differently, it was because they had to suffer what they must. If I'd chosen to actually mind my own pups... since my house was obviously too well-off to be disparaged for being penniless, unkind rumors of me playing peasant would've been the least of it." You see. [pc.bg scholar |You'd come across some of the old imperial traditions in the course of your scholarly work and the reasons were there for say, the fostering system, but the fears of bloodlines consolidating against imperial authority no longer exist with it being dead more than two centuries now. People just keep on clinging blindly to the customs of old Belhar because they were what the movers and shakers of that time did. "I... I get what you mean." Olivia carefully and deliberately measures her breath. "When I was younger, I had many so-called friends mimic what I was doing without actually knowing why." For an analogy, it's close enough. |It sounds like a harsh existence. ] "It feels strange, to go against everything I've been taught was the hallmark of high class. We can't all have jobs that keep us indoors with our kin; you should know that full well, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. And we'll do our best to not hold it against you in the years to come, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Necessity is what it is." ]

"Oh, I've been here so long that I forget that I'm in this benighted part of the world. You see, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], %'bastard' has a rather romantic connotation where I come from. As a bard, I'm familiar with quite a few tales, but there's one that has recently found a place in my heart since our son was born." You can guess, but... "It's that of the bastard who has set his eye on what ought to be his," Olivia purrs, pausing to sip from [olivia.isPregnant |a mug of honeyed water |her wineglass ]. "Clad in a suit of fine black armor and a helm that conceals his face, he journeys to the land of his relatives. Of course, they give a bastard no time of day, so he puts them all to the fire and sword, deposes a bunch of self-righteous twits who have never done anything more strenuous than eat honey cakes, and sets things in order before returning to his holdings in colder, harsher place." And behind the bastard will be his dear old mother whom everyone thought dead decades ago? A smile. "I'm not saying that it's a portent of the future; sometimes tales are just tales. But those that stick with us often have the ring of truth to them. The tale of the hard-edged bastard is one that's quite popular in the Clairemont area, mostly because of how many times it played out during the imperium, with half a dozen different actors all playing the role of the bastard. House Leroux escaped being set as the stage for one of those performances... maybe that just means it's overdue for just that. "We'll find out in two decades or so, I'm sure. But even though he's barely out of the womb, it's clear our son is the kind who likes to do things, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. And should he choose to descend upon his ancestral holdings and savage the flock of proverbial sheep... may the gods help all who stand in his way, because I won't. "So don't worry about it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. When I call our son a bastard, it's a loving term of endearment and hope for his future. And should he choose to never bother with the warm, fat heartlands to the south, there's no shortage of things to do in these miserable borderlands, as you can attest." |"Our son is such a hungry little bastard, I love him for it. Always more than happy to oblige me when I wrap things up for the day and am full to bursting." Hey, at least that bust of hers is being put to good use. Olivia rolls her eyes, but keeps her smile. "I know you say that in jest, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but you're not that far off the mark. I wasn't flat to begin with, and even so I'm begrudgingly glad for what's been done to me in that regard. Of course, I did most of the work myself while I was pregnant with your child, but still! It's what it is." You shake your head, remembering just how large and heavy Olivia had become while carrying Louis in her belly. You'd be worried if a pup that size didn't have an appetite to match. "It's kind of troubling, to be honest. He won't take any milk but mine — oh, he'll drink anything else, just gulp it all down like the bottomless pit he is, but keeps on acting as if he hasn't been fed afterwards. I have to squeeze out a whole bunch every morning and bottle it for Drifa while she minds him for me, it's —" — Something she happily does as an excuse to get herself off first thing out of bed. "Well. I'm not denying it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. It helps wake me up, if nothing else. [var0 |He'll take enough of Drifa's milk to stop complaining for a bit, but nothing but that of his dear mother will do." There's a distinct note of smugness in Olivia's voice as she prattles on. |Is it troublesome? Sometimes. But Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], surely you agree that it's but a trifle in the greater picture." A wistful note creeps into Olivia's voice. ] "I didn't think minding a bastard would be this satisfying, but here we are." |"When I think about our son, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], I'm glad that I came up to this miserable corner of the world. By the gods, even enduring that time in a damp hole might just have been worth it." That's a rather sharp about-face from the woman she used to be, but then again having a pup is a pretty big thing in one's life. That being said, what exactly changed her perspective? "I..." Olivia rubs her cheeks and looks a little bashful. "Well, if I'd been back on the estate, Louis wouldn't have been treated like a pup, but as an asset. I... I would've been a lot more of a bitch too, and wouldn't have minded leaving him to a nursemaid all day while I ran the estate. I mean, now I have to have Drifa mind him from time to time while I see to your guests, but that doesn't mean I don't feel bad about it, or that I don't take him with me as much as I can." You nod slowly and motion for Olivia to go on.[pc.bg noblescion | You've been through this before, too — heir or spare, no one likes being reduced to just a role. ] "I've mentioned before that I'd been raised to expect certain things in my life, and Louis would've been seen as just another duty to be dispensed with. That's how the old me would've seen it, I'm sure. But here, living under your roof, having gone through what I did and not having an entire retinue nipping at my heels all day... it's just Drifa[wayfort.hasMaids |, the maids, ] and Rumie, and I'm glad things have shaken out this way. Like this, our son makes me feel wanted, instead of him just being another duty to be dispensed with." When Olivia puts it like that, if that's how she really feels about the situation... you can see where she's coming from. Having her entire mercenary band taken by the corrupted lupines, being dunked in the [silly |goop |eldritch ] pool, changing on the outside and probably a lot more on the inside, and the fate which awaited her if you hadn't intervened... it might all just have been worth it. Olivia sighs. "It was all worth it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ] — both for him and for me. All this acting out... in the end, all I wanted was attention and to be genuinely liked, something which our son isn't shy about giving. And as I've just pointed out, I don't doubt our son is having a better upbringing here than he would've in his ancestral estate. "I just feel like something's finally clicked in that long-held sense of yearning, and I don't have to be as much of a bitch any more, amazing as that might sound. It feels good how glad he is to see me when I pick him up from Drifa, or while feeding him — a pup isn't always popular with those I have to entertain, but I bring him along as much as I can when his presence helps set the proper mood." She is right. This does sound like a better outcome for everyone involved. Olivia looks down at her hands and flexes her fingers. "I don't regret becoming what I am now, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. If that's the price I have to pay, then it's just something I'll have to accept. I get that our son will gradually grow apart from me when he gets older, as ought to be... but I'm [olivia.isCollared |expecting you to have put several more pups into me by then, mmmh |not going to worry so much about the future that I neglect to spend what time I do have with our son now ]." |"Drifa's teaching me to properly mind children," Olivia sighs. "She says that [drifa.isCorrupt |[drifa.hasKids |if we're going to share the credit for being the progenitors of this pack, I ought to put in a bigger share of the work |if I'm going to be the one to have your pups, the least I can do is to raise your offspring right ] |children are precious and they deserve the best of everything we can give ]. And honestly, I don't disagree with her; it's just that it's a lot to take in at once." And neither do you. No matter how she slices it, it isn't right or responsible to foist her pups on a nursemaid when she ought to be the one in charge, especially with her job here at the wayfort keeping her within a stone's throw of your son. "D-don't look at me like that!" Olivia huffs. "I'm no stranger to being responsible for someone else, but there's a whole world's difference between minding a pet and minding a pup. Taking care of your own infant pups was something that only the peasants did, so it's not like I ever had the chance to practise until our son was born." A pet, huh? You'd never have figured Olivia having any kind of pet. "You may not believe it, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but I used to be something of a cat and bird person. Of course, even a kitten needs a lot less care than our son does. Point being, I'm aware of what being responsible for someone else entails, but our son is in a class all by himself. "Anyway. There's just so much more to be done, and while our son quietly puts up with a lot from his bumbling mother I'm not sure I can forgive myself for my mistakes." If she needs more time to mind Louis during the day, you're more than happy to ease her from some of her duties. A shake of her head. "It isn't that I don't have time to mind our son, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. It's about knowing how to do so properly. Drifa aside, I'm also checking in with the village's nursery matron — what was her name again? I forget — Louis may be the resilient kind of pup, but that isn't an excuse for me to make mistakes in raising him. I'll... get better at it, I'm sure. It's not as if I have a choice." |So, you hate to bring this up... but Olivia hasn't noticed any overt signs of corruption in your son, has she? "There isn't a single day where it doesn't come to mind. I don't worry about it, but as his mother I have to keep an eye on how he's growing." Olivia sighs. "When it comes down to it, everything about our son has been scarcely normal — from how he was conceived, to his time inside of me, to how much of a little monster he is. It's clear that the things that happened to me, no thanks to Tharsus, have also tainted him. I'm not going to delude myself on that point. "However... is that necessarily a bad thing? He's robust and clearly overdeveloped for a pup his age, but he's hardly a brute; I don't get the same ugly feeling of wretchedness from him that I did from Asgeir or gods forbid, Refnir. I set him down for a while and he's stalking some vermin or the other, yet knows to not do that to people; he's started to teeth at an abnormally young age, yet has never once bitten me while nursing. Maybe it's just me being his mother, but when I look into our son's eyes I don't get the same sense of dumb brutishness that I saw in every single one of the corrupted lupines. Our son's clearly been affected, but... there's hope. Quite a lot of it, in fact." You know how these things go. A little savagery, directed correctly, has its purposes. Well, a whole lot of savagery and violence as well, but she gets the point you're making. "It's undeniably part of him, but doesn't have to rule him the same way it did those dumb brutes, or even Tharsus calculating madness." Olivia sighs and slouches in her seat. "Just like me, actually. Maybe I'm just trying to wish into existence my hopes for our son, and all of this is just a delusion of mine." There, there. She's not the only one keeping an eye on Louis — you'll be sure to do the same. "It's appreciated. I... I do confess that I have high hopes for his future, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. The hand that rocks the cradle rules the world; it's not manipulation if it's something he wants to do anyway and I have his interests in mind, yes?" All right, she doesn't need to put on a show for you. Yes, yes, Olivia's very scheming and devious. Maybe as the years pass, you'll see how much of that passed to your son. |"I... in a way, I'm glad that all this happened to be; this way, I can actually raise our son with my own hands." That's an interesting way to put it. She wouldn't have been expected to do it herself back home? [pc.bg noblescion |Olivia raises an eyebrow. "Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], I know you're the spare's spare, but you're still titled. Do they do things differently from where you come from?" Perhaps not that much depending on the details of your privileged upbringing, but Olivia makes it sound as if the fate that awaited any heirs she might produce was tantamount to abandonment. That's certainly not what your early years were like. |Olivia turns her gaze from yours. "The surprise in your voice hurts more than you may ever know, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ], but... oh, there's no denying it. Yes." ...Oh. It sounds like a lonely existence. ] Olivia sighs. "It's expected, you see? A mark of privilege, or at least in that idyllic little corner of the world I come from. Child-rearing is peasant work — people of my station have more important things to tend to, can't be expected to waste precious daylight on a task even animals can accomplish. My parents weren't obliged to so much as speak to me before I could hold a half-intelligent conversation, and as soon as I was out of the womb I was shuffled between any number of wet nurses, minders, tutors... I suppose it's a small mercy that I wasn't fostered out in the old imperial tradition, in which case I might have never actually seen my family until I was a grown woman. "For much of my life, I considered this normal and didn't give it much thought: it was the way of the world and if the peasants did things differently, it was because they had to suffer what they must. If I'd chosen to actually mind my own pups... since my house was obviously too well-off to be disparaged for being penniless, unkind rumors of me playing peasant would've been the least of it." You see. [pc.bg scholar |You'd come across some of the old imperial traditions in the course of your scholarly work and the reasons were there for say, the fostering system, but the fears of bloodlines consolidating against imperial authority no longer exist with it being dead more than two centuries now. People just keep on clinging blindly to the customs of old Belhar because they were what the movers and shakers of that time did. "I... I get what you mean." Olivia carefully and deliberately measures her breath. "When I was younger, I had many so-called friends mimic what I was doing without actually knowing why." For an analogy, it's close enough. |It sounds like a harsh existence. ] "It feels strange, to go against everything I've been taught was the hallmark of high class. Maybe it took taking me down a peg or two to see it for myself." Olivia's smile trembles at the corners. "It always hurts when I have to leave Louis with Drifa. I know that it isn't really the same thing I went through and that I can't appeal to all audiences with a pup in tow, especially those who would be turned off by the thought of — well, you know. But our son is getting so much more than I ever did, and I hope that he won't have to suffer the same loneliness that I did, looking back on it." You can see how she views using Drifa as a nursemaid while she entertains your guests as akin to her own youth, but... does she want you to change her duties? "No, no. We can't all have jobs that keep us indoors with our kin; you should know that full well, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. I'll just do my best, and hope our son doesn't hold it against me in the years to come. And we'll do our best to not hold it against you in the years to come, Dearest[olivia.isCollared | [pc.Master] ]. Necessity is what it is." ] "

rows.original: [olivia.correctionRange 0 5 10 15 |"Oh, what's this? Some of what this part of the world has to offer?" Olivia takes your gift from you and sniffs. "Well, it's fine, I guess. After growing up on what comes out of the Yvennese hills, anyone would be spoiled for taste; few things in all the world can match the fine wines of my homeland. Olivia waves off your concern. "Oh, of course not. rows.translation: [olivia.correctionRange 0 5 10 15 |哦，这是什么？这是这个地方能提供的东西之一吗？”奥利维亚接过你送的礼物，闻了闻。“嗯，还算不错吧。我也该因为在这里付出的努力得到一些认可了，这是理所应当的。 她听起来并不是很感兴趣。 “嗯，我把自己的标准定得这么高，确实有点不公平。在习惯了伊文尼斯山区出产的那些美酒之后，任何东西都难以满足我的口味了；世界上几乎没有什么东西能与我家乡的优质葡萄酒相媲美。 rows.raw: " [olivia.correctionRange 0 5 10 15 |"Oh, what's this? Some of what this part of the world has to offer?" Olivia takes your gift from you and sniffs. "Well, it's fine, I guess. About time I got some recognition for my efforts around here, as ought to be." She doesn't sound too impressed. "Well, it's not quite fair for me to set my standards so high. After growing up on what comes out of the Yvennese hills, anyone would be spoiled for taste; few things in all the world can match the fine wines of my homeland. "Still... my job does mean I need to be open to experience and note down things as they are, so I'll accept the gift and taste it later. That, and it's the thought that counts, isn't that right? Those mangy dogs did their best to get me the good stuff while I was still stuck in that hole... it wasn't much, but it was their effort which I was really after." So, the same applies here? Olivia waves off your concern. "Oh, of course not. This is much better than the swill they could get their hands on stealing it off... wherever they were stealing it from[pc.isBaron |; you are the local baron[pc.mf | |ness ], after all, and I'd expect more from you than a bunch of hounds in a hole ]." But the booze isn't the point, it's that they were giving her the best that they had. "Exactly. Watching them grovel, simper and abase themselves just for the privilege of receiving a smile... that eagerness was stomach-turning, yet addictive.[pc.isBaron | You rule over this wayfort and its immediate environs, you should understand. Sitting on that throne of yours..." [pc.isDK |Maybe you do, just a little. But she shouldn't be getting any airs about the nature of this gift. "Oh, of course. It's a small mercy you're not the one demanding I give you my best, eh? |No, you don't. It's your role here to mind those under your care, not exploit them to feed your ego. That's why you're giving her a gift, not some kind of labyrinthine power play that's only in her head. "Tsk. Patting yourself on the back for being magnanimous is the same thing, only by another route. But I shan't quibble, for it'll do neither of us any good. ] ]" ... "Well, that's that; like I said, I'll take it and give it a taste later, maybe let you know my thoughts. Is there anything else?" |Olivia accepts your gift, and her expression softens. "Why, Dearest. You really shouldn't have." Is the drink not up to her standards? A sigh. "You already know the answer to that. It's... acceptable. That, and it's not really about the gift in and of itself — I have my means. Save for stuff like pale elf mirrorwine that no one can get anyway, I could have my run of just about every shade of alcohol that money can buy in the entire Marches. "Point is, it's important because you're the one giving it to me, and it took you at least some effort to get. If it were just about the booze, you could simply call up Rumie to serve us a round." Well, you should be glad that she thinks so highly of you, that a gift should mean so much to her. "Mhm." Olivia pushes your gift to the side and slouches in her seat. "It's about the things money can't buy. Pleasant conversation, for one, which is why I went uphill against my nature to learn how to do it, and do it well. You could pay me to make idle talk with you, but then it's not genuine, is it? There's no magic there if it's not genuine. "So... yes. Thanks for the gift and everything, I do appreciate it. But it's more the giving that matters than the gift itself, so don't worry about getting something that's up to my tastes... well, unless it's something that you moved the earth and sky to get. Then by all means, bestow upon me my rightful dues, ho ho. Now, is there anything else you'd like of me?" |Olivia's ears perk up at the notion of getting a gift from you, then catches herself and does her best to calm herself and not get too overexcited — a futile endeavor. "More? You shouldn't have. As much as I'd love to get smashed every day, Dearest, even I know that's not the way one such as me should live life. You do know that I don't have any choice but to pass on most of the gifts I receive to [wayfort.hasMaids |the maids, don't you? They need a little fun every now and then |Rumie, don't you? Help her keep a little something extra in stock ]." Passing on her received gifts, huh? It's not like her to admit as much. "Well, I'm certainly not able to drink it all. You aren't the only admirer I have, Dearest — it's a hazard of the job you set me to, unfortunately, and it's not as if my tastes are hard to discern." Olivia raises her wine glass to you with a sheepish smile. "Besides, you know full well at this point that it's not the actual drink that counts." [pc.isDK |No, it's more a measure of what you went through to get it, and how much it hurt to part with the gift. "Cynical, aren't we? There are other priorities, let's just leave it at that." |Because she can buy just about anything that tickles her fancy in the Marches, and what she wants isn't purchasable with hawks. "Oh ho ho. Despite the demeanor, I'm not as wealthy as one might imagine, Dearest. Certainly I wouldn't go hungry even in this corner of the world, but that's about it. Still... the sentiment isn't wrong. The wine and spirits are nice, but it's an aside; that's what all those admirers fail to grasp." ] Mostly, it's that your gift comes from you. And once it passes from your hands to hers, it ceases to retain that meaning and becomes just more booze in the heap she already has. Others might not agree with the sentiment, but that's why she doesn't see a problem with passing along the gifts she receives from others. A smile. "You get it. You really do — I really didn't expect others to agree, but even understanding is hard to come by. Thank you so much — it's more precious than the drop of drink that you just gave me. Or maybe all of this is just a poor girl rationalizing having to give away all the stuff she keeps on receiving. "Oh well. I can't help if I'm popular, ho ho. Keeps you on your toes and pushes you to do ever better, Dearest. Now in return, is there anything I can do for you?" |Olivia's eyes brighten as she receives your gift, tail starting to wag before she catches herself and leans back in her seat. "A treat? For me? And what about enjoying it with you? "That would be ideal, but it's not about the drink, isn't it?" Olivia winks. "This... oh ho ho. I have means of getting the very same thing, through one means or another. But you? You're a much more scarce commodity, Dearest, and this has actual meaning because you took some of your time to get it for me. "So... thanks." The little yappy dog's shivering with delight; she's forgotten herself, her tail a blur behind her. "Even if I'm likely to pass it on to [wayfort.hasMaids |the maids |Rumie ] later on, it's appreciated. Unless you're going to follow up on that offer and have a lovely [dayNight |afternoon |evening ] with me and a drink between us?" You'll have to consider that. "Oh, how cruel of you to get me worked up and deny me, Dearest. Well, it's just how things are, hm? rows.original: "Oh, Dearest. [olivia.correctionRange 0 5 15 |Elven mirrorwine? I do have to admit that you're more useful than I first thought — finally, I'm being paid what I'm worth, and it's all mine.[wayfort.hasDaliza | Sucking up to the boreal elves does have its benefits, hm? ]" |You really shouldn't have. Elven Mirrorwine? Even the elves themselves don't make it any more, I hear; it's nice to be appreciated, that's for sure.[wayfort.hasDaliza | Well, if you're going to be a vassal to the boreal elves, then you might as well take them for everything they're worth, huh? ]" |Thank you, thank you, thank you! I can't stress this enough. Tell me, what did you go through to get this for me? I'm sure it'll be a good tale for the telling!" ] You hand over the fine glass bottle and Olivia fusses over it, running a claw over the ancient glass while her gaze burns into the dusty label. Can she actually read boreal elf writing? "Read? No, but I can recognize it. They've got ruins all over the woods, and it's not hard to pick up on their alphabet; it's quite distinctive." She sighs. "This stuff was all the rage in the imperial heartlands centuries ago, and not just because it was exotic and came from far away. Enough to spark a little interest in the boreal elves as a culture and people, at any rate. "It's almost too good to drink. My heart aches; it feels like a crime to put it to my lips. But..." Olivia turns the bottle over in her hands. As tough as the ancient cork may be, it's no match for her clawed fingers and comes off in one easy motion that she's been practising ever since her days of being stuck in a hole in the ground. No corkscrew necessary — one of the small benefits of who she is now. Instead of pouring it out into her glass or asking for a new one, she instead sets down her wine glass and raises the bottle itself to her nose, giving it a few tentative sniffs. "Ah..." Then, Olivia tips her head back in the most unladylike fashion and starts chugging ice wine straight from the bottle. Ancient elven wine, vinted and bottled by their druids, aged over more than a century, every drop precious in all senses of the word — and she's guzzling it as fast as those dainty lips of hers will allow. To her credit, she doesn't spill a single drop of the ancient vintage during the process, all of it washing over her tongue as it pours down her throat. Her eyes close in simple bliss and her tail's wagging furiously, but eventually, Olivia has no choice but to pull away. "Oh." A sigh. "Gods, that's good. [olivia.correctionRange 5 |Thank you so much, [pc.name] |Finally, I feel like I'm being given my dues, and not a moment too soon ]." You look down at the bottle in Olivia's hands — despite all her theatrics, she's only emptied anywhere between a quarter to a third of its contents. On one hand, that means she's a lightweight, even for someone as petite as her; on the other, it also means that she can guzzle herself silly all the more... She has to finish it soon, doesn't she? Now that the bottle's been opened, it's only a matter of time before the wine goes off? Olivia grins and lightly slaps her now-reddened cheeks. Surely just that much can't have had so strong an effect on her, right? There has to be something else at play here, right? "You know, Dearest, you're absolutely right. I guess I do have to empty the bottle soon. Just... not all of it at once. "Heh. Ice wine indeed — it chills itself, that's for sure." Did she have to chug it straight from the bottle like that? It's most uncharacteristic of her — you'd have expected a slower appreciation involving all five senses. "Pish-posh." Olivia waves off your words even as she stumbles over her own. "That's... for lesser things. When you get something as good as this, you... you want to make it give you as hard a kick as possible, cram as much of it into as small a space as you can. And that... finally, in so long, one last flicker of nobility in this wretched world, found within a mouthful of ancient wine. Bet it's the only reason why it hasn't soured into vinegar long ago."
rows.translation: 哦，亲爱的。 [olivia.correctionRange 0 5 15 |精灵镜酒？我确实不得不承认，你比我最初想象的要有用得多——终于，我得到了应得的报酬，而且这一切都归我所有了。[wayfort.hasDaliza | 讨好那些北方精灵确实有一些好处，嗯？ ]" |你真的不应该这么做的。精灵镜酒？据我所知，就连精灵们自己也不再酿造这种酒了；能够得到别人的赏识，当然是一件好事。[wayfort.hasDaliza | 嗯，如果你决定成为北方精灵的附庸，那么最好充分了解他们的实力和特点，对吧？ ]" |谢谢，谢谢。谢谢。就是你！这一点我再怎么强调也不为过。告诉我，你究竟经历了什么才弄到这个东西给我？我相信，这个故事一定非常精彩！ ] 你将那个精美的玻璃瓶递给她，奥利维亚仔细地端详着它，用手指轻轻触摸那古老的玻璃，同时她的目光紧紧地盯着那布满灰尘的标签。 她真的能看懂极北精灵的语言吗？ “看懂？不，但我能认出那些文字来。他们的森林里到处都是废墟，他们的字母系统也很容易被辨认出来，确实非常独特。”她叹了口气，“几百年前，这些东西在帝国的中心地区曾经风靡一时，而不仅仅是因为它们很奇特，来自遥远的异国他乡。至少，这足以让人对极北精灵这个民族及其文化产生一些兴趣。 这酒简直美得让人不忍下口。我的心都在疼了，觉得把这种美酒送到嘴边简直是一种罪过……但是……” 奥利维亚将瓶子在手中转动着。尽管那个古老的软木塞非常结实，但在她那布满老茧的手指面前，它根本不是对手——只需一个简单的动作，软木塞就被取了下来。而这个动作，她从自己被困在地下洞穴里的那些日子起，就一直在练习。不再需要用螺旋开瓶器了——这也是她现在这个身份带来的小便利之一。她没有把酒倒入杯中，也没有去要一个新的酒瓶，而是将酒杯放在一旁，直接把酒瓶举到鼻子前，轻轻闻了几下。 啊……” 然后，奥利维亚以一种极其不淑女的方式仰起头，直接从瓶子里大口喝起冰酒来。这种古老的精灵葡萄酒是由他们的德鲁伊们酿造并装瓶的，经过一个多世纪的陈酿，每一滴都堪称珍贵至极——而她却以自己那娇嫩的嘴唇所能承受的最快速度将它们喝下去。值得称赞的是，在整个过程中，她没有让那一滴古老的葡萄酒溢出来——所有的酒都直接流进了她的喉咙。她闭上眼睛，脸上洋溢着幸福的表情，尾巴也兴奋地摇个不停。不过最终，奥利维亚还是不得不离开。 哦。”一声叹息。“天啊，太好了。 [olivia.correctionRange 5 |非常感谢您， [pc.name] |终于，我觉得自己得到了应得的回报，而且这个时刻来得正是时候。 ]你低头看了看奥利维亚手中的瓶子——尽管她表现得那么夸张，但实际上她只喝掉了瓶子里四分之一到三分之一的酒。一方面，这说明她的酒量其实很小，即使对于她这样身材娇小的人来说也是如此；另一方面，这也意味着她可以更加肆无忌惮地喝酒了。她必须尽快完成这件事，对吧？既然瓶子已经打开了，酒变质只是时间问题而已。 奥利维亚笑了笑，轻轻拍了一下自己现在已经变红的脸颊。应该不会因为这么一点事情就产生这么大的影响吧？这里肯定还有其他原因在起作用，对吧？“你知道的，亲爱的，你完全说得对。我想我确实得尽快把瓶子里的酒喝完。只是……不能一下子全喝光。 “呵呵，冰酒果然不一样——它本身就能带来清凉感，这一点确实没错。” 她非得直接从瓶子里大口喝下去吗？这完全不符合她的风格啊——按常理来说，她应该会用五种感官来慢慢品味这种酒才对。 胡说八道。”奥利维亚一边说着，一边自己也说错了话，但她根本不在乎。“那种话……是用来形容一些不值钱的东西的。但当你得到了像这样好的东西时，你就会想要让它带给你最大的满足感，想要把它的所有优点都压缩到最小的空间里。而那就是……在经历了如此漫长的岁月之后，这个糟糕的世界里终于再次出现了一丝高尚的气息，它存在于那一口古老的葡萄酒之中。可以肯定，这才是为什么这种酒至今还没有变成醋的原因吧。
rows.raw: " "Oh, Dearest. [olivia.correctionRange 0 5 15 |Elven mirrorwine? I do have to admit that you're more useful than I first thought — finally, I'm being paid what I'm worth, and it's all mine.[wayfort.hasDaliza | Sucking up to the boreal elves does have its benefits, hm? ]" |You really shouldn't have. Elven Mirrorwine? Even the elves themselves don't make it any more, I hear; it's nice to be appreciated, that's for sure.[wayfort.hasDaliza | Well, if you're going to be a vassal to the boreal elves, then you might as well take them for everything they're worth, huh? ]" |Thank you, thank you, thank you! I can't stress this enough. Tell me, what did you go through to get this for me? I'm sure it'll be a good tale for the telling!" ] You hand over the fine glass bottle and Olivia fusses over it, running a claw over the ancient glass while her gaze burns into the dusty label. Can she actually read boreal elf writing? "Read? No, but I can recognize it. They've got ruins all over the woods, and it's not hard to pick up on their alphabet; it's quite distinctive." She sighs. "This stuff was all the rage in the imperial heartlands centuries ago, and not just because it was exotic and came from far away. Enough to spark a little interest in the boreal elves as a culture and people, at any rate. "It's almost too good to drink. My heart aches; it feels like a crime to put it to my lips. But..." Olivia turns the bottle over in her hands. As tough as the ancient cork may be, it's no match for her clawed fingers and comes off in one easy motion that she's been practising ever since her days of being stuck in a hole in the ground. No corkscrew necessary — one of the small benefits of who she is now. Instead of pouring it out into her glass or asking for a new one, she instead sets down her wine glass and raises the bottle itself to her nose, giving it a few tentative sniffs. "Ah..." Then, Olivia tips her head back in the most unladylike fashion and starts chugging ice wine straight from the bottle. Ancient elven wine, vinted and bottled by their druids, aged over more than a century, every drop precious in all senses of the word — and she's guzzling it as fast as those dainty lips of hers will allow. To her credit, she doesn't spill a single drop of the ancient vintage during the process, all of it washing over her tongue as it pours down her throat. Her eyes close in simple bliss and her tail's wagging furiously, but eventually, Olivia has no choice but to pull away. "Oh." A sigh. "Gods, that's good. [olivia.correctionRange 5 |Thank you so much, [pc.name] |Finally, I feel like I'm being given my dues, and not a moment too soon ]." You look down at the bottle in Olivia's hands — despite all her theatrics, she's only emptied anywhere between a quarter to a third of its contents. On one hand, that means she's a lightweight, even for someone as petite as her; on the other, it also means that she can guzzle herself silly all the more... She has to finish it soon, doesn't she? Now that the bottle's been opened, it's only a matter of time before the wine goes off? Olivia grins and lightly slaps her now-reddened cheeks. Surely just that much can't have had so strong an effect on her, right? There has to be something else at play here, right? "You know, Dearest, you're absolutely right. I guess I do have to empty the bottle soon. Just... not all of it at once. "Heh. Ice wine indeed — it chills itself, that's for sure." Did she have to chug it straight from the bottle like that? It's most uncharacteristic of her — you'd have expected a slower appreciation involving all five senses. "Pish-posh." Olivia waves off your words even as she stumbles over her own. "That's... for lesser things. When you get something as good as this, you... you want to make it give you as hard a kick as possible, cram as much of it into as small a space as you can. And that... finally, in so long, one last flicker of nobility in this wretched world, found within a mouthful of ancient wine. Bet it's the only reason why it hasn't soured into vinegar long ago." "

rows.original:
Without waiting for your response, Olivia raises the bottle to her lips again and takes several heavy swallows, draining as much of the elven wine into herself as she can. Her entire petite body sways with — is it effort? Pleasure? Concentration? Her throat, her bosom, her fingers, her tail — there's no part of her that isn't dedicated to the cold, calculated act of drinking herself silly. Then...
        
        "A final flicker of nobility in this wretched world," Olivia mumbles. She doesn't resist as you loosen her fingers from about the bottle's neck and push the cork back in. Whatever this is, it isn't all from the ice wine, but watching the yappy little dog's half-lidded eyes and turned-down ears, it's clear that she's not going to be good for very much for the next several hours. "All of them winking out, one by one."
        
        Does she want ink and parchment, to capture this moment of inspiration from her helper before it passes her by?
        
        Olivia shakes her head and sighs, suddenly extremely melancholy as she slumps into her seat — an actual slump, as opposed to the carefully cultivated slouch of impudent bluebloods. She needs to be brought back to her quarters... but on the other hand, your great hall is pretty safe, and perhaps letting others see her like this would humble her a little.
        
        Whatever's in boer'alvar mirrorwine, it's touched the bard — and likely her muse — in a way that only she can sense. If it helps her sing your praises down the line, then it's a gift well given, for what it's worth...
rows.translation:
不等你回应，奥利维亚又把酒瓶举到唇边，狠狠灌了好几口，尽可能把那些精灵酒都吞进肚里。她整个娇小的身体都在摇晃——是在使劲吗？是快感？还是专注？她的喉咙、她的胸脯、她的手指、她的尾巴——她身上没有哪一处不是在投入这场冷酷而精于算计的自我灌醉。然后……
        
        “这糟糕世界里最后一丝高贵的光，”奥利维亚咕哝道。你把她抠在瓶颈上的手指掰开、把软木塞重新塞回去时，她并没有反抗。不管这是怎么回事，都不全是冰酒的功劳；但看着这只爱叫的小狗那半阖的眼睛和耷拉的耳朵，显然接下来几个小时里她是干不了什么正事了。“它们一个接一个地熄灭。”
        
        她想要墨水和羊皮纸吗？趁这份由她的帮手激起的灵感还没溜走，把它记下来？
        
        奥利维亚摇摇头，叹了口气，突然极其忧郁地瘫进椅子里——是真的瘫倒，而不是那些无礼的蓝血贵族刻意养出来的懒散坐姿。她该被送回自己的房间去……但另一方面，你的大厅相当安全，而且也许让别人看到她这副样子，能让她稍微收敛一点。
        
        不管布尔阿尔瓦镜酒里有什么，它都触动了这位吟游诗人——很可能还有她的缪斯——以只有她自己才能感知的方式。如果这能让她日后歌颂你的功绩，那这份礼物就送得值，不管怎样……

rows.original: You hand over the bottle, and Olivia raises an eyebrow, trying to read the label and giving up. "Huh, it's not written in Belharan. One of the local lupine tongues, I assume. Local product, then? Wait, no, that's a stupid question — of course it has to be. Nothing ever comes up here except trouble, and this isn't trouble, haha." You see no reason to correct Olivia as she jabs the claw on her index finger into the cork, using it much like anyone else would a corkscrew and popping open the bottle. [var0 |One of the wayfort's many maids shuffles in from the side |One of her many lupine [silly |simps |fans ] sidles in from the crowd |While she's at it, Rumie stops by in her efforts to tend to the crowd in the great hall ] and offers Olivia a clean wine glass, which she accepts and replaces with her old one before shooing off the interloper. "Run along now, [pc.name] and I are busy." Turning back to you, Olivia graces you with a small smile. "Let's see what this is all about, shall we? Surprise me with what you have, Dearest. I love this kind of puzzle." To be honest, you're the one who was hoping to be surprised by her reaction, but it's all well and good if she gets some fun out of all of this. Olivia pours a small measure of Kasyrra's wine into the glass, eyeing its clear red color and looking contemplative. She swirls. She sniffs. She sips, letting the flavor coat her tongue; finally, she drains the entire glass in a gulp, looking thoughtful. The both of you sit in silence for a minute or so; you wonder just what Kasyrra's vintage might do to her as Olivia is trying to get her thoughts on what she's just tasted in a straight line. ...Nothing. "What was that, Dearest?" How does it taste? How does she feel? "Feel... well, it's not something I'd drink on a cold night to keep me warm, that's for sure. And as for the taste, it's okay, I suppose." Okay? "Not good. Not bad. It's... aggressively mediocre. How should I put it, Dearest? This... whatever alcohol this is, doesn't leave much of a lasting impression at all; it doesn't actually taste of nothing, but for all intents and purposes it may as well be completely blank. I could pair it with any meal, and it wouldn't change one bit or make one iota of difference. "I repeat myself, it's not bad. Making dregs and swill is easy, anyone can foul up. This... how should I put it? This is nothing, and it tries to be so. For the unsuspecting, it's a blank canvas upon which someone could paint his or her expectations upon, and it'd turn into that. But me? Nothing escapes my notice when it comes to appreciation, Dearest." As far as you can tell, the red cow wine has had absolutely no effect on Olivia. Maybe not the transformative aspect of it, but not even a little libido... maybe it's because she's already been corrupted that there's no space for more, or there's nowhere for Kasyrra's tricks to find purchase on her after being subject to Tharsus' handiwork? "You're looking pretty thoughtful, Dearest. Something on your mind?" Sort of. You just didn't expect Olivia to deliver a verdict so different from what you expected. "Oh ho ho. Don't worry about it — like I said, this... alcohol is an empty canvas on which you're supposed to paint what you expect. Or maybe a mirror in which you see yourself. Thing is, it loses all its magic once you realize it's only a reflection and you see the blank slate beneath. Aggressively mediocre, like I said. "To make an analogy, something that's used to pick up on the flavor of what it's served with often has little taste of its own. That's what's happening here, Dearest." Oh. "You sound disappointed. Don't be. Like I said, it's very easy to simply make something taste bad, but this isn't it. I'd say a lot of care went into making it extremely tasteless, and whoever came up with this could've put that effort towards making it a pleasant experience. Still, I wouldn't spend good money on this, even if it's a curiosity; hope you didn't, Dearest. "Now, is there anything else?
rows.translation: 你把瓶子递过去，奥利维亚挑了挑眉毛，试图看清标签上的文字，但最终放弃了。 “哈，上面不是用贝尔哈兰语写的。应该是当地的某种语言吧？那么这是本地生产的产品吗？等等，不，这个问题太愚蠢了——当然是本地生产的啊。这里来的东西从来都不会带来好事，不过这个瓶子应该不会惹麻烦吧，哈哈。” 你觉得没有必要纠正奥利维亚，只见她用食指上的“爪子”戳住瓶塞，就像别人使用开瓶器一样，轻松地把瓶子打开了。 [var0 |韦弗特的众多女仆之一从旁边走了过来。 |她众多的狼族[silly |追随者 |崇拜者 ]之一从人群中凑了过来 |顺道一提，露米也过来帮忙招呼大厅里的人群了。 ]然后递给奥利维亚一个干净的酒杯，她接过来后，还是用自己原来的杯子把那个干净的杯子换掉了，接着就把那个不速之客赶走了。 “快走吧， [pc.name]我有点忙。”奥利维亚转过身来，对你露出了一个微笑。“让我们来看看这到底是怎么回事吧？亲爱的，用你准备的东西来给我一个惊喜吧，我就喜欢这种谜题。” 说实话，其实你才是希望被她的反应所惊喜的人，不过如果她能从这一切中得到乐趣，那也挺好的。奥利维亚往杯子里倒了一小杯卡希拉葡萄酒，凝视着那清澈的红色液体，若有所思地望着。 她轻轻旋转着酒杯，闻了闻酒香，然后小口啜饮，让酒香在舌头上弥漫开来；最后，她一饮而尽，神情若有所思。你们俩沉默地坐了一会儿，你不禁在想：卡希拉这款陈年佳酿究竟会给她带来什么影响？而奥利维亚也在努力整理自己对刚才品尝到的酒味的感受。 那是什么呀，亲爱的？” 这种东西尝起来怎么样？她喝后有什么感觉？ “感觉嘛……嗯，肯定不是那种在寒冷的夜晚喝来保暖的东西。至于味道，还算可以吧。” 还算可以？ 不算好，也不算坏。可以说……它就是平平无奇。该怎么形容呢，亲爱的？这种酒根本留不下任何深刻的印象；它的味道其实也不算完全难喝，但事实上，它就跟没有味道一样。无论搭配什么食物，都不会产生任何不一样的效果。 我再说一遍，这不是糟糕制造渣滓和污物很容易，任何人都有可能把事情搞砸。而这个……该怎么说呢？其实这根本不算什么，但却试图被当作什么重要的东西。对于那些毫无戒心的人来说，这就像是一块白纸，别人可以在上面描绘自己的期望，然后它就真的变成了那个人所想象的样子。但是我呢？在欣赏美的事物方面，没有什么能逃过我的注意，亲爱的。” 从你的观察来看，那种红牛葡萄酒对奥利维亚完全没有产生任何影响。也许它并没有带来什么改变，甚至连她的性欲都没有丝毫影响……也许是因为她已经被腐蚀得无法再接受任何影响了，又或者，在经历了塔尔苏斯的操控之后，卡希拉的那些诡计已经无法在她身上产生任何作用了？ “你看起来思考得很深入呢，亲爱的。你在想些什么吗？” “算是吧。你只是没料到奥利维亚会给出一个与你预期完全不同的结论。” “哦呵呵，别担心——就像我说的，这个…… 酒精它就像一块空白的画布，你需要在这上面描绘出自己所期望的东西；又或者像一面镜子，让你能够看到自己的模样。然而，一旦你意识到它只不过是某种反射，而下面其实是一块空白的空间，它的“魔力”就会瞬间消失殆尽。正如我所说，这种东西充其量只能算是一种平庸至极的东西。 “打个比方，那种用来辨别所搭配食物味道的调料，本身往往几乎没有味道。现在的情况就是如此，亲爱的。” 哦。 你听起来很失望啊。别这样。就像我说的，让某样东西变得好喝其实非常简单。糟糕但这并不是我想要的。我觉得，制作这个产品的人一定是花了很大的心思去让它变得毫无趣味可言；其实，把同样的精力用在让体验变得愉快上，效果肯定会好很多。不过，即便这只是个新奇的东西，我也不会花大价钱去购买它……希望你也没有这么做，亲爱的。 “那么，还有其他事情吗？

Olivia pours a small measure of Kasyrra's wine into the glass, eyeing its clear red color and looking contemplative. She swirls. She sniffs. She sips, letting the flavor coat her tongue; finally, she drains the entire glass in a gulp, looking thoughtful. The both of you sit in silence for a minute or so; you wonder just what Kasyrra's vintage might do to her as Olivia is trying to get her thoughts on what she's just tasted in a straight line. ...Nothing. "What was that, Dearest?" How does it taste? How does she feel? "Feel... well, it's not something I'd drink on a cold night to keep me warm, that's for sure. And as for the taste, it's okay, I suppose." Okay? "Not good. Not bad. It's... aggressively mediocre. How should I put it, Dearest? This... whatever alcohol this is, doesn't leave much of a lasting impression at all; it doesn't actually taste of nothing, but for all intents and purposes it may as well be completely blank. I could pair it with any meal, and it wouldn't change one bit or make one iota of difference. "I repeat myself, it's not bad. Making dregs and swill is easy, anyone can foul up. This... how should I put it? This is nothing, and it tries to be so. For the unsuspecting, it's a blank canvas upon which someone could paint his or her expectations upon, and it'd turn into that. But me? Nothing escapes my notice when it comes to appreciation, Dearest." As far as you can tell, the red cow wine has had absolutely no effect on Olivia. Maybe not the transformative aspect of it, but not even a little libido... maybe it's because she's already been corrupted that there's no space for more, or there's nowhere for Kasyrra's tricks to find purchase on her after being subject to Tharsus' handiwork? "You're looking pretty thoughtful, Dearest. Something on your mind?" Sort of. You just didn't expect Olivia to deliver a verdict so different from what you expected. "Oh ho ho. Don't worry about it — like I said, this... alcohol is an empty canvas on which you're supposed to paint what you expect. Or maybe a mirror in which you see yourself. Thing is, it loses all its magic once you realize it's only a reflection and you see the blank slate beneath. Aggressively mediocre, like I said. "To make an analogy, something that's used to pick up on the flavor of what it's served with often has little taste of its own. That's what's happening here, Dearest." Oh. "You sound disappointed. Don't be. Like I said, it's very easy to simply make something taste bad, but this isn't it. I'd say a lot of care went into making it extremely tasteless, and whoever came up with this could've put that effort towards making it a pleasant experience. Still, I wouldn't spend good money on this, even if it's a curiosity; hope you didn't, Dearest. "Now, is there anything else? "

rows.original: Olivia raises an eyebrow when you pass over the sealed gourd. "Now what's this, Dearest?" To make it brief? Grain liquor you had imported. Stuff from the Belharan Heartland is one thing, but this is from another continent altogether. Everything foreign's got to be better when it's taken the trouble to come all the way to this benighted corner of the world, right? "Oh, puh-lease. Just because I'm amazing doesn't mean that everything else that comes from far away is. Still, I can see how easy it might be to make that mistake. Now then... grain liquor, huh?" You nod. "Not my usual fare, but far from it being me to turn it down. Let's see what this is all about, then." Olivia extends a claw and nicks open the gourd tip, then pauses; her instincts catch her unaware, clearly unsure what to do with the foreign alcohol. Happily, [var0 |one of the wayfort's many maids shuffles in from the side |one of her many lupine [silly |simps |fans ] sidles in from the crowd |Rumie stops by in her efforts to tend to the crowd in the great hall ] and offers Olivia a clean wine glass, which she accepts and replaces with her old one before shooing off the interloper. "Very nice and I appreciate it, but [pc.name] and I are having a moment here, if you don't mind." Turning back to you, Olivia's about to smile, but it's arrested by the scent rising from the now-open gourd. Just the slightest hint of distaste mars her features as she wrinkles her nose and thins her lips, fixing her gaze on yours. "Whew. Now that's strong." As you understand it, the liquor's meant to be taken in small shots. Perhaps smaller for the likes of Olivia. "Mmmh. Allow me to correct you, Dearest — I may be petite, but I'm most certainly not a lightweight. Are we clear on that?" With that, Olivia pours out a measure of cloudy liquor into the glass, the heady, warming smell of strong liquor filling the air between the both of you, laced with just a tinge of bitterness. Certainly nothing you'd find down at Rumie's or Garth's; and Olivia herself appears intrigued at the novelty, tail wagging slowly as she swirls the grain liquor from side to side in the glass. "I take it I'm breaking all kinds of etiquette for where this came from, but when all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail. Bottoms up!" Poor Olivia. Clearly stung by your earlier remark, the small yappy dog drains her glass in one gulp, then stares defiantly at you. She's clearly challenging you to do something about her, but that isn't necessary. Olivia's the architect of her own demise, and that becomes evident a minute or two; her cheeks and collarbone are already coloring lightly as she moves to pour another measure of lustful liquor into her glass. There is a reason why the kitsune call it lustful liquor, after all... "See? That wasn't so bad. You can't have a healthy appreciation for the finer things in life if just a bit turns you into a hot mess. Remember that, Dearest. It never does to underestimate me." Your bad. As you eye Olivia, though, she's not so much drunk as she's getting warm — after all, every word in that last sentence was perfectly enunciated without the least bit of slurring. Still extremely smug with herself, the small yappy dog pours herself another shot. And another. And another. Certainly has something to prove, doesn't she? "Of course I've got something to prove. You ostensibly rule this wayfort, after all. Anyone getting tongues wagging that I of all people can't hold my drink would be bad enough, but if it were to involve you as well? Oh, no no no. Can't have that. Can't have that at all." You knew that lustful liquor worked quickly, but not this quickly — maybe it's a side effect of what Tharsus did to her, maybe it's just her ego finally being given free rein to speak its mind. Whatever the case, you're still pretty sure that Olivia isn't actually drunk, the bitter tinge on her breath notwithstanding; she stands up from her seat, tail wagging, and leans over the table to get her face as close to yours as she can. "Oh, that stuff was strong," she purrs. "But I'm stronger. Imagine if I'd gotten drunk in front of my [silly |simps |adoring fans ] while still back in that hole; I don't doubt they'd have taken it as a go-ahead to violate me in every possible fashion, ha. So don't go thinking for a moment that I'm easy to —" She's not drunk, but something else in the liquor is affecting her, all right. By now, Olivia's blush has spread all the way into her shoulders and heavy tits, and she's breathing so hard that they're jiggling inside of her crimson bodice. "Proved it to you. Don't you ever go saying that I'm a lightweight — true or not, I'd never live down that kind of talk." Her tail wags so quickly, it's a blur as she cozies up to you. "Actually, I may just keep the rest of this stuff around, if you don't mind. Nights can get pretty cold around these parts, and the icy river doesn't help." [olivia.fucked |It's clear at this point that with Olivia firmly in your personal space and rubbing up against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun], she wants something from you. What that happens to be is pretty obvious from the warmth exuding from her petite body: Olivia may not be drunk on alcohol, but she's definitely drunk on something else. Are you going to respond to her advances, or not? ]
rows.translation: 当你走过那个密封的葫芦时，奥利维亚挑了挑眉毛：“这又是什么呀，亲爱的？” 长话短说吧？这是你进口的谷物酒。贝拉兰心脏地带的特产是一回事，但这种酒却来自完全不同的大陆。凡是从遥远的异国他乡来到这个偏僻角落的东西，肯定都会更好吧？ “哦，拜托了。仅仅因为我很棒，并不意味着所有从远方带来的东西也都同样优秀。不过，我确实能理解为什么会犯那种错误。那么……谷物酒，是吧？” 你点了点头。 “这不是我平时常喝的酒，但既然有人提供，我当然不会拒绝。那就让我们看看这酒到底怎么样吧。 奥利维亚伸出爪子，轻轻划开了葫芦的顶端，然后停住了；她的本能反应让她一时不知所措，显然不知道该如何处理这种陌生的酒精。不过，幸运的是[var0 |韦弗特家的众多女仆之一从旁边走了过来。 |她众多的伴侣之一[silly |傻瓜们 |粉丝们 ]从人群中悄悄走过来 |露米前来帮忙，致力于安抚大厅里的人群。 ]她递给奥利维亚一个干净的酒杯，奥利维亚接过来后，还是用自己原来的杯子替换了它，然后把那个不速之客赶了出去。 “非常感谢，我真的很感激，但是[pc.name]其实我有话想跟你说，如果你不介意的话……”奥利维亚转过身来，正准备微笑，但这时从那个已经打开的葫芦里散发出来的气味让她停住了动作。一丝轻微的厌恶之情浮现在她的脸上，她皱起了鼻子，嘴唇也紧绷了起来，然后将目光紧紧地盯着你。呼，这酒真烈啊。” 正如你所知道的，这种酒应该小口小口地喝。对于像奥利维亚这样的女性来说，或许应该喝得更少一些。 “嗯，让我纠正你一下，亲爱的——虽然我身材娇小，但我可绝对不是不是这是一种酒精度较低的酒。我们明白这个意思了吗？” 说完，奥利维亚往玻璃杯里倒了一杯浑浊的酒。浓郁而温暖的酒香弥漫在你们两人之间的空气中，其中还带着一丝苦味。在露米's或加斯's，你肯定找不到这样的东西；而奥利维亚本人似乎也对这种新奇的事物感到好奇，她一边在玻璃杯中轻轻摇晃着这种谷物酒，一边慢慢地摇着尾巴。 “我想，这种酒的来历肯定违背了很多礼仪规范，但当你只有一把锤子时，任何东西看起来都像钉子。干杯！” 可怜的奥利维亚……显然被你之前的话伤到了，那只小狗一口喝光了杯中的酒，然后挑衅地盯着你。它显然在挑战你，让你对它采取行动，但其实并没有这个必要。奥利维亚其实是自己命运的破坏者，这一点在一两分钟内就显而易见了。当她再次往自己的杯子里倒入那些令人陶醉的酒液时，她的脸颊和锁骨已经微微泛起了红晕。是看到了吧？其实也没那么糟糕。如果一点点这样的东西就能让你变得如此失控，那你就无法真正欣赏生活中那些美好的事物了。记住这一点，亲爱的。永远不要低估我。” 不过，这确实是你自己的错。当你看着奥利维亚的时候，你会发现她其实并不是喝醉了，只是有点微醺而已——毕竟，她最后那句话里的每一个字都发音得非常清晰，丝毫没有含糊不清的地方。那只自鸣得意的小狗又给自己倒了一杯酒，然后又倒了一杯……再倒一杯另一个她肯定有什么要证明的，对吧？ “我当然有东西要证明。毕竟，这个地方实际上是你在掌管。如果有人开始议论说，偏偏是我这种人连酒都喝不醉，那已经够糟糕的了；但如果连你也被牵扯进来……哦，不行，绝对不行。” 你早就知道这种酒会很快起作用，但没想到这个很快——也许这是塔尔苏斯对她所做之事产生的副作用，也许只是她的自尊心终于得到了释放，得以随心所欲地表达自己。无论原因是什么，你仍然很确定，奥利维亚并不是这样。其实虽然嘴里还带着一丝酒味，但她还是从座位上站了起来，摇着尾巴，然后俯身把脸凑得离你越近越好。 “哦，那酒确实很烈，”她轻声说道，“但我可更坚强。想象一下，要是我在别人面前喝醉了该多尴尬[silly |傻瓜们 |忠实的粉丝们 ]虽然我还被困在那个洞里，但我毫不怀疑，他们会把这当作一个机会，用各种可能的方式来侵犯我，哈哈。所以，千万别以为我是个容易对付的人——” 她并没有喝醉，但酒里含有的某种成分确实对她产生了影响。此时，奥利维亚的脸色已经红到了肩膀和丰满的胸部，她的呼吸变得如此急促，以至于那些胸部在她的深红色胸衣里不停地晃动。 “我已经向你证明过了，不是吗？曾经他们总说我是个弱者——不管这是不是事实，我永远都无法忍受这种说法。”它的尾巴快速地摇动着，身体紧紧地贴向你。“其实，如果你不介意的话，我可能会把剩下的这些东西都留着。在这附近，夜晚会变得非常寒冷，而那条冰冷的河流更是让情况更加糟糕。 [olivia.fucked |现在很明显，奥利维亚已经彻底进入了你的私人空间，而且还在不断地与你亲密接触[pc.skinFurScalesNoun]她想要从你这里得到些什么。到底是什么呢？那个从她那娇小的身体散发出的热情来看，这一点再明显不过了：奥利维亚或许并没有喝醉，但她肯定是被其他什么东西“迷住了”。你打算回应她的示好吗，还是不打算呢？ ]

"I can't indiscriminately lead people on by the nose, give them the wrong idea and false hope. It's already bad enough given all the people I have to charm every day — can you imagine if I went around thanking them for even the smallest things which I'm entitled to? Eugh, no. "All of life's a stage, and we're to play our parts. My part doesn't involve making people think they have a chance, thank you very much." You roll your eyes. Look, even granting if everything she just said was true — and you're not giving her that, just to be sure — [pc.bg noblescion |you're every bit as blue-blooded as Olivia is. If you can thank her, she can thank you — if nothing else, you're pretty sure you're a cut above the average [silly |simp |adoring fan ] she has to rub shoulders with. A sniff, although Olivia can't hide the grin. "No less annoying, though." No less annoying, but certainly more entertaining. |you think you've proved yourself enough by beating the stuffing right out of Tharsus and Asgeir, something that she certainly wasn't capable of. Not that you necessarily care about such things, but if there were anyone worth granting you a title these days you'd think you'd damn well earned it. That, and you're giving her a job and a roof over her head. A sniff, although Olivia can't hide the grin. "Now, Dearest, you were the one who suggested I come here." And she was the one who was asking for a place to stay! This is ridiculous — an argument just to avoid having to thank someone for a gift? Maybe you should've just bent her over your knee from the outset and spanked her for being the petulant [pc.isDK |bitch |pup ] she is right from the outset! ] Olivia mulls over that for a moment. "Actually, Dearest? You're right. This is rather more fun than the usual fare — bowing and scraping gets old after a little while, and I do feel a lot livelier for having butted heads with you. So while I won't thank you for your gift, I will thank you for being quite refreshing and providing a change of pace. "Is that good enough for you, or are we going to quibble some more? I'm perfectly fine with either." Ugh... well, you've wrung a concession out of Olivia, even if it isn't a big one. Guess that'll have to do for now — it's not as if you didn't know what you were getting into when you brought this small yappy dog home. Even so, you don't have any more stomach for Olivia and her attitude for just a little while more... "

rows.original:
Know what? She's right. People prefer her as a haughty, incorrigible creature, and if that's the mask she has to put on in order to get the job done then you won't get in her way. Hope she has plenty of [silly
        |simps
        |sycophants
    ] for the rest of the day — may the wayfort's reputation grow by leaps and bounds.
    
    "Glad to hear you see things my way, Dearest. [wayfort.stateABC
        |Although to be honest, you'd be better served making this place less of a dusty ruin, but what do I know?
        |This place is a bit sparse, but grim and barren seems to be the favored aesthetic in these parts.
        |It's a pretty good location, by local standards.
    ] Most importantly, though? Your wayfort's got me in it."
    
    It hasn't escaped your notice how Olivia's pivoted the topic away from her ingratitude to herself, but it's not as if you didn't know what you were getting into when you brought this small yappy dog home. 
    
    Underneath that smugness, though? You're pretty sure Olivia looks bored, and isn't trying to hide it. Maybe she was itching for a fight — being surrounded by yes-men all day isn't easy, as you should know. Maybe she's disappointed you didn't put up more resistance — even so, you don't have any more stomach for Olivia and her attitude for just a little while more...
rows.translation:
你知道吗？她说得对。人们更喜欢她那个高傲、无可救药的形象，如果她必须戴上这样的面具才能完成工作，那么你就不要去妨碍她。希望她能顺利达成目标。 [silly
        |傻瓜们
        |马屁精
    ]在今天剩下的时间里，但愿荒废驿堡的声誉能够迅速提升。
    
    “很高兴听到你同意我的看法，亲爱的。 [wayfort.stateABC
        |说实话，把这里变成一个不那么破败的地方会更好，但我又懂什么呢？
        |这个地方显得有些荒凉，但在这种地方，阴郁而荒芜似乎才是人们偏爱的审美风格。
        |按照当地的标准来看，这个位置相当不错。
    ]不过，最重要的是……你的方式让我也卷入了其中。
    
    你肯定已经注意到，奥利维亚是如何把话题从她对自己的忘恩负义上转移开来的，但当你把这只爱叫个不停的小狗带回家时，你其实早就知道自己会陷入这样的局面。 
    
    然而，在那种傲慢的外表之下呢？你很清楚，奥利维亚看起来其实很无聊，而且根本不在试图掩饰这一点。也许她其实很想找人吵架——整天被那些唯唯诺诺的人围绕在身边，这种日子肯定不好过，你应该很明白这一点。也许她对你没有表现出更多的反抗感到失望……但无论如何，现在你实在再也无法忍受奥利维亚以及她的那种态度了……

rows.original: Actually, whether it's because you don't have anything suitable on hand, or because you have your own reasons, you change your mind about gifting Olivia. Not that she notices — she's been talking all this while, absorbed in the sound of her own voice while the entire notion played out in your head from start to end. "And that's how it went," she says. "Is something up, Dearest? You looked a little distracted throughout all that." No, it's fine. "Just as well, because that's the end of that story. Did you want anything else from me?"
rows.translation: 其实，不管你是因为手头没有合适的礼物，还是另有原因，你都改变了给奥利维亚送礼物的主意。不过她并没有察觉——她一直在滔滔不绝，沉醉在自己说话的声音里，而整个念头在你脑中从头到尾演了一遍。 “事情就是这样的，”她说。“怎么了，亲爱的？刚才那段时间你看起来有点心不在焉。” 不，没什么。 “那也好，因为那个故事就到此为止了。你还想让我做点别的什么吗？”

rows.original: As you step into your chambers, a large parcel on the bed draws your attention: wrapped in paper and tied with a ribbon, the brightly-colored package is clearly intended to draw your attention. After ensuring it's not a trap or anything else untoward, you approach and and pick up the wrapped gift; it's heavy for its size, and there's a small roll of parchment tied into the ribbon. The handwriting is small and neat, complete with an aggressive elegance that reminds you of someone you know. Hello, Dearest: You're often out of the Wayfort and I don't know when you're slated to return, so this is the best way to ensure that you receive this gift. A bit colder than handing it over in person, but you'll excuse me if I don't feel like holding onto it for weeks while constantly being on the lookout for you to show your face. I promised you something for returning my spellsinger, and here it is. Took me a while to have it made, but it got done in a lot less time than I was expecting; things get done really quickly around these parts, don't they?[wayfort.stateABC | | I heard that refurbishing this place from the miserable ruin it used to be took about ten days from start to end; that's pretty amazing. I'll have to include it somewhere in one of the songs. | I heard that it took less than a month to completely redo the wayfort from the miserable ruin it used to be into someplace livable. Credit where it's due; that's pretty amazing. I'll have to include it somewhere in one of the songs. ] Truth be told, Dearest, a gift shouldn't be necessary. It speaks of the times we live in that we can't expect borrowed items to be returned in the condition they were lent in, if at all, but since there is someone who can actually exhibit basic courtesy it behooves me to try and at least foster this kind of behavior. If you can inspire a few benighted people to more civic-minded actions, that's a small win for me. Imagine if you'd simply given it to someone else, or pawned it off, or... actually, don't imagine that. Anyway, as I was saying, a little something from me to you. Now we're even. Love, Olivia. Fair enough. You undo the ribbon and pick apart the wrapping paper to find a glass flute of Tychrisian make packed in soft wool. That would explain how dense it is — while it doesn't look exactly fragile, it's still not the kind of thing that you'd whack someone over the head with. Raising the mouthpiece to your lips, you give it an experimental blow, and discover to your delight that it is, indeed, quite functional despite the material of its make. You obtain the Tychrisian Flute. Well, that's that. Now, why were you here to begin with, anyway?
rows.translation: 当你走进自己的房间时，床上一大个包裹吸引了你的注意：用纸包着，还用丝带系好，这个色彩鲜艳的礼物显然就是为了吸引你的注意而准备的。在确认它并不是什么陷阱或别的危险物品之后，你走过去拿起了这个包装好的礼物。相对于它的大小来说，它显得相当重，而在丝带里还绑着一小卷羊皮纸。上面的字迹小巧而工整，带着一种独特的优雅气质，让你立刻想起了某个你认识的人。 亲爱的， 你最近经常不在荒废驿堡，我也不清楚你什么时候会回来，所以这样送礼物才是最稳妥的方式。虽然这种方式比当面交给你要稍微麻烦一些，但如果你知道我一直在等待你的出现，却不得不把礼物留着好几周的话，你应该会理解我的吧。 我答应过你，会为你找回我的咒歌者，现在它终于到手了。虽然制作这个东西花了我一些时间，但实际上完成得比我预想的要快得多——在这附近，事情确实会进展得非常迅速，不是吗？[wayfort.stateABC | | 我听说，把这个地方从曾经的一片废墟中重新修复出来，整个过程总共花了大约十天的时间；真是太了不起了。我一定要在某首歌里提到这件事。 | 我听说，他们只用不到一个月的时间，就把那个曾经破败不堪的地方彻底改造成了一个可以居住的地方。确实值得称赞，这真是太了不起了。我一定要在某首歌里提到这件事。 ] 说实话，亲爱的，送礼物其实并不是必须的。这恰恰反映了我们生活的时代：我们根本不能指望借来的东西能完好无损地被归还，甚至根本不可能期待它们会被归还。不过，既然已经这样了是一个真正懂得基本礼貌的人，我自然应该尽力培养这种行为。如果你能激励一些缺乏这种意识的人采取更加有公民意识的行为，那对我来说就是一个小小的胜利。想象一下，如果你把这些品质给了别人，或者把它们当作礼物送人了，又或者……其实，也别去想象这些了。 总之，就像我刚才说的，这是我送给你的一点小礼物。现在我们算是扯平了。 爱你的， 奥利维亚。 有道理。你解开丝带，拆开包装纸，发现里面包裹着一只用柔软的羊毛包裹着的提克里斯制造玻璃笛子。这就解释了为什么它这么重——虽然看起来并不脆弱，但显然也不适合用来敲打别人。你把吹口放在嘴唇上，试着吹了一下，结果发现，尽管材质特殊，但这支笛子确实是可以使用的。 你获得了提克里斯之笛。 好吧，事情就是这样。那么，你最初为什么会来到这里呢？
