rows.original:
You give her a lightning fast slap across the cheek. "Enough with this self-dustructive doom and gloom."
    
    Calise blinks. For a second you think she's going to go for her axe, until she just tightens her lips and looks towards the forest. "Yeah. Sorry. I just... I miss her, [pc.name]. I miss my old life. I hate what I am now, and there's nothing I can fucking do about it. Pardon me for being bitter."
    
    "You've got to deal with it. We can't change what you are," you say. "At least, I don't know how. Maybe we can find a way, I don't know, but for now, pull it together."
    
    "I... yeah. I'll try. Fuck, I'm pathetic. I-"
    
    You raise your hand again, and Calise flinches. "Fucking hell, I get it. The next slap's going on my ass, if you want to distract me from this shit."
    
    You grab a handful of Calise's muscular backside and give it a squeeze. "You've got armor over it." 
    
    "Then take it off me, idiot."
rows.translation:
你飞快地甩了她一记耳光。“别再说这种自毁式的悲观丧气话了。”
    
    卡莉丝眨了眨眼。有那么一瞬间，你以为她要去抓斧头，但她只是抿紧嘴唇，望向森林。“是啊。对不起。我只是……我想她，[pc.name]。我想念我过去的生活。我恨现在的自己，可我他妈什么都做不了。请原谅我满腹怨气。”
    
    “你必须面对它。我们没法改变你的本质，”你说。“至少我不知道该怎么改。也许我们能找到办法，我不知道，但至少现在，你先振作起来。”
    
    “我……好吧。我会试试的。操，我真可悲。我——”
    
    你又举起手，卡莉丝缩了一下。“该死的，我懂了。下一个耳光就打在我屁股上吧，如果你想让我从这些破事里分分心的话。”
    
    你一把抓住卡莉丝结实的屁股，捏了捏。“你那儿隔着护甲呢。” 
    
    “那就把它给我脱了，白痴。”

rows.original: "So you haven't heard?" Calise says, looking you up and down. "[pc.bg acolyte |Thought a priest at least woulda. ]Shit, this is how that bitch of a queen managed to impersonate me, isn't it? Nobody up here knew a thing about me. Some Champion!" Calise manages to laugh, leaning back against the wall. "It didn't seem like much at the time. [flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|My Ethlyn|My... a dryad I was with back then] woke up with cold sweats one night, screaming about blood and fire gouging out the heart of the forest we lived in. I'd never seen her so terrified. So I gathered up my axe and bow and went hunting, prowled the forest for the better part of a week, but found nothing. [flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|My Ethlyn|The damned deer] got more desperate with each passing night, practically tearing her hair out with the nightmares." You watch Calise's features darken. "Before I'd even been born, her seed had been carried clear to the other side of the shadow forest by a lover. A Valgar druid. Finally those prophetic dreams cleared up, and [flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|my Ethlyn|she] realized what Velun had been trying to tell her: that her seed-tree had been burned. Gods! I never saw a woman cry so much. I had to leave; I couldn't handle watching her break down. So I went hunting again. This time I knew it wasn't a beast I was looking for. Just a pack of monsters on two legs." "I found them a few days later. Valgarmen, faithless fucks who'd turned from the druids' path to worshipping Lumia, but they'd convinced themselves that meant they needed to burn away every last vestige of the old ways. Of the Old Wyld." Calise's hands tighten around her axe. "They were celebrating when I came upon them. Dancing around the burned husk of the seed-tree. Half of them were naked, fucking in the ashes. Those heartless fucking savages!" The sheer furor in her voice causes you to take a step back. "I fell on them like the gods' own vengeance. Not just Velun's, but Lumia's too, for perverting her teachings to justify their atrocity. I couldn't have stopped myself if I wanted to: all I could think about was [flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|my Ethlyn|that tree's mother] crying her eyes dry after days of torment, for a seed she'd never seen planted. I ripped those bastards to shreds." A cruel, bloodthirsty smile spreads across Calise's features. "And for that, when the screaming stopped, a proud stallion appeared from the ashes, and he spoke to me... told me I'd avenged his daughter. That I was a force of nature, as unstoppable as a landslide. Hah, how wrong he was!" Calise spits into the river. "That's when he made his offer. He picked up their leader's axe, still stained with Wyldsap, and told me to take it as a reminder of what I'd done there. That monsters come in all forms, and that it was my duty to scour them from his domain. Fuck, even then I think I resented him for it. Giving me a weapon with... with her seed-tree's blood on it. I'm glad to be rid of it... and the title. Champion's ass." She sounds like she's trying to convince herself of that more than you...
rows.translation: “你还没听说吗？”卡莉丝上下打量着你说道。“[pc.bg acolyte |本以为至少会有牧师听说过吧。 ]该死，原来那个贱人女王就是用这种办法冒充我的，对吧？这上头根本没人了解过我。还冠军呢！” 卡莉丝勉强笑了笑，靠在墙上说道：“当时看来也没什么大不了的。 [flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|我的艾丝琳|我……那时候和我在一起的那个树精]有天晚上惊醒过来，浑身冷汗，尖叫着说什么血与火正在掏空我们栖身森林的心脏。我从没见过她那么恐惧。于是我拿起斧头和弓去打猎，在森林里搜寻了大半个星期，却一无所获。 [flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|我的艾丝琳|那只该死的鹿]一夜比一夜更绝望，那些噩梦几乎要把她的头发扯光。” 你看到卡莉丝的表情阴沉下来。“甚至在我出生之前，她的种子就被一位情人带到了阴影森林的另一边——一位瓦尔加尔德鲁伊。终于，那些预言的梦境平息了，[flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|我的艾丝琳|她]也明白了维伦一直想告诉她的事：她的母树被烧毁了。天哪！我从没见过哪个女人哭成那样。我不得不离开，我实在受不了看着她崩溃。于是我又去打猎了。这一次我知道我要找的不是野兽，只是一群两条腿的怪物。” “几天后我找到了他们。瓦尔加门——那些背弃德鲁伊之道、转而崇拜卢米娅的没信仰的混蛋，可他们却说服自己，那意味着必须烧尽旧有习俗的最后一丝痕迹，烧尽古老荒野的一切。”卡莉丝的手在斧柄上收紧。“我撞见他们的时候，他们正在庆祝。围着种子树烧焦的残骸跳舞。有一半人赤身裸体，在灰烬里交合。那些没心没肺的野蛮人！” 她声音里的狂怒让你不由得后退了一步。 “我像众神本身的复仇一般扑向他们。不只是维伦的复仇，也是卢米娅的——因为他们歪曲她的教诲来为自己的暴行正名。就算我想停手也停不下来：我满脑子只有[flags.REAL_CAL_TLK_SELF|我的艾丝琳|那棵树的母亲]在数日折磨之后哭干了眼泪，为一颗她从未见其种下的种子。我把那些混蛋撕成了碎片。”卡莉丝脸上浮现出残忍嗜血的笑容。“也正因如此，当尖叫声停下来时，一匹骄傲的种马从灰烬中现身，对我开口……告诉我我为他的女儿报了仇。说我是一股自然之力，如山崩般不可阻挡。哈，他错得多离谱！” 卡莉丝朝河里吐了口唾沫。“他就是在那个时候提出那个条件的。他捡起他们首领的斧头，上面还沾着荒野树液，让我把它带走，当作我在那里所做之事的提醒。他说怪物有各种形态，而我的职责就是把它们从他的领地上清除干净。操，即便在那时，我想我也为此怨恨他。给我一件沾着……沾着她母树之血的武器。我很高兴能摆脱它……还有那个头衔。冠军个屁。” 听起来她更像是在说服自己，而不是在说服你……

            |"If you have any advice, I'm happy to take it."
            |"Oooh... mmn, you're definitely right. But like, who could help us?"
        ]
        
        Her painted lips quirk up — just for the slimmest moment — into a smile, before she busies her hands with adjusting her hair. "You want my advice? That's actually a little novel... hmm." The bailiff glances off northwards into the middle-distance. "Avoid asking for the Winter City's aid, then. As much as I'm sure they'd be willing to help, we've been given independence to operate here; if we go crying to them like this for a matter literally as basic as, 'help us take out the trash and knock a few thrashed walls in' they're all going to look down on us."
        
        Instead she turns her gaze south, pondering a few moments more. "Hawkethorne is to the south; they'll have a bunch of lumberjacks and all sorts of meatheads wandering around. It would be good to encourage some trade between us, and good to give my soldiers the chance to do their own jobs."
        
        Garth could probably arrange that for you with little-to-no difficulty if you gave him a few hundred electrum.

rows.original:
When you reach the courtyard it's hard to restrain at least a small cringe; with the oversized boulder removed from it, the empty space is like a missing tooth. "It will take a lot more time and money to get the courtyard serviceable for much more than just drills, but the stone went to good use patching up ruined walls, the odd roof, and a few arches." Daliza explains, kicking over a dirt pile. "The hope is that it doesn't just turn into a mud-pit."
        
        ...You could probably think of a few ways to enjoy a mud-pit in the middle of the courtyard, to be fair.
rows.translation:
当你走进那个庭院时，很难不感到一阵尴尬——原本那里有一块巨大的巨石，现在这块石头被移走了，留下的空地就像缺了一颗牙一样。要让这个庭院重新恢复使用功能，所需要的时间和金钱远远超过了仅仅进行钻孔修复的工作。不过，那些石头被用来修补那些被毁坏的墙壁、一些破损的屋顶，以及几处拱门结构，也算是物尽其用了。达莉莎一边踢着一堆泥土一边解释道：‘我们希望它不会变成一个泥坑。’”
        
        ……公平地说，你大概也能想出一些办法来享受院子中央那个泥坑吧。

            "I hope you don't think this improper of me, but do you actually plan to put this in place one day?"
            
            "The stockades?" A fair question, but a little hard to imagine when you're staring at a bunch of worthless planks in an otherwise-empty courtyard. "Maybe."
            
            The bailiff sighs and rubs the back of her head, "I'm not inclined towards public humiliation, although I suppose it shows a gentler hand for lesser crimes. So long as passers-by aren't throwing rotten fruit like we're some kind of savages."

            ]

            ]

rows.original: "And this is your throne room, I wish I could say there was much of interest, but as you can see..." Daliza trails off and points at her own sitting spot, into which a dagger has been stabbed in order to pin any messages that came through in her absence. "A lot of it is requests for future improvements... I hear talk that a few of my soldiers expect you to just whip a few thousand electrum out of nowhere and solve all their minor gripes." "Anything else?" You ask, looking back across the hall. "The kitchen is workable, most of us have taken places in the living quarters, and my soldiers and I have occupied a few other portions of the fort for ease of access..." The bailiff sighs and thinks, foot tapping on the floor with a soft 'click-tinkle' of metal buckles. "Ah. Kindly do not forget to look in on the tower, if only to dispel any concerns that there are monsters flying around it?"

rows.original:
Daliza salutes you, smiling and adjusting her cloak. "About time you arrived, I'd half expected to keep walking out here and waiting forever. No doubt you have much to occupy your time... so shall we?" 

    She waves you forward with authority, watching as a number of the soldiers scatter and return to their duties.
    
    "Nothing much here; this is just the road, although it has had all of the broken bits of rock and masonry removed from it. Good thing too, after one of my soldiers turned an ankle in the dark."
rows.translation:
达莉莎微笑着向你致意，同时整理着自己的斗篷。“你总算来了，我差点就要一直在这里等着了。想必你也有很多事情要处理吧……那我们开始吧？”

    她带着不容置疑的权威示意你向前走，同时看着那些士兵们散开，各自回到自己的岗位上。
    
    这里没什么特别的，只不过是一条道路而已，只不过路上的那些碎石和砖块都已经被清理掉了。这也真是太好了，否则我的一个士兵在暗影中就会扭伤脚踝了。

rows.original:
[wayfort.hasAlraune
            |Daliza sighs once your walk takes you up to an initial garden, even as her hand unconsciously finds a passing effigy and pats it. "These girls have proven to be... excitable, to tell the truth. They stayed away mostly while the laborers were within the Wayfort, but the moment they left it has been baskets of flowers and various attempts to bed my soldiers. Would you be willing to speak with them at that... Matron's garden?"
            
            "Have they been too much trouble to manage?"
            
            At the very least the bailiff gives the matter more than a moment's thought, rubbing her chin and humming. "Not too much, no. I will admit they helped a lot with the road. There was a lot of de-weeding to do and applying the stone edging would likely have kept the laborers occupied for an extra few days. They performed these duties for free."
            
            That's good to know, at least.
            
            The herald waves at you without a pause in her song, tapping away on her little drums and blowing you a kiss.
            |Daliza walks through the grounds of the garden quietly, scratching one of her ears slowly before turning to face you. "Were druids living here once?"
            
            "What makes you say that?"
            
            The bailiff clicks her tongue, gesturing to the fertile grass. "The loamy soil, the scent of sex. It's like an Old Wyld fuck-circle out here."
            
            You shake your head and briefly explain the presence of the Alraune.
            
            "You slew them outright? A shame, if they could perhaps have been... educated away from their previous course of action. But I suppose you did what appeared right in the moment. Needless to say, the grounds here are still quite fertile."
        ]

            “她们是不是太难管了？”
            
            执法官至少认真思考了片刻，揉着下巴低声沉吟。“倒没有太难管。我承认，她们修路时帮了不少忙。当时需要清除许多杂草；若没有她们，铺设石质路缘大概还要多占用工人几天。她们做这些事没有收钱。”
            
            至少知道这一点很好。

There's a moment of pride out of the bailiff as you cross the southern bridge, and she casts a hand out. "Although it was the laborers you brought in that masoned the new rock, it is actually my soldiers and I who put this bridge back together again. rows.original:
You saunter up to the strange idol standing in the ancient fort's courtyard. This must be what Evergreen was referring to... the same place where you first met Etheryn. You remember seeing the blue gem embedded in the chest of the statue when you first passed by, but never thought anything of it... until now. 

        Alright, let's give this a try. You take the leather thong from around your neck and hold up the queer blue stone Kasyrra gave you, aiming it straight for the statue's own brooch. And in that moment, there's a buzz in the air, a crackling of power through the air between your charm and the nameless lord formed of stone. The sensation lasts a mere second, and then the gem in the statue takes on a faint, pulsing glow — like it's awoken from some ageless slumber. Slowly, you lower your charm, and watch as the statue's radiance fades away once more.
rows.translation:
你漫步走向古老驿堡庭院里的奇异神像。这一定就是常青女士提到的东西……也是你最初遇见伊瑟琳的地方。你记得第一次经过时曾见过嵌在雕像胸口的蓝色宝石，却从未把它放在心上……直到现在。 

        好吧，试试看。你从颈间取下皮绳，举起卡希拉送你的奇异蓝色石头，将它正对雕像自身的胸针。就在这一刻，空气嗡鸣起来，力量噼啪作响，在你的护符与石刻的无名领主之间流过。这种感觉仅仅持续一秒，雕像上的宝石便泛起微弱而有节律的光芒——仿佛从亘古长眠中醒来。你缓缓放下护符，注视着雕像的光辉再次消退。

rows.original:
You pause a moment, halfway across the old stone bridge. The overpowerful aroma of oversexed flowers is finally starting to fade, washed away by the scent of cold, clear water running under the bridge. 

        A deep breath to collect your thoughts after... everything... doesn't seem unwarranted. You lean onto the stone and set your weapon aside for a moment. [flags.ALRAUNE_KILLED|Gods, you really killed that creature. Corrupted as she was, that was still a life taken. The heaviness of the act weighs on your heart like an anchor. But she won't hurt anyone again, and her daughters have been scattered to the winds. An undeniable victory. ]So this is the corruption Kasyrra is spreading: twisting the life of Savarra into her corrupted playthings, unleashing them on the unsuspecting world. Poor Hawkethorne had no idea what was coming. If you hadn't come along, it's possible the Alraune's progeny would have overrun the town.
        
        [party.has Cait|"You okay, [pc.name]?" Cait asks, hefting herself up onto the railing beside you. One of her hands brushes your shoulder. "You look a million miles away."
        
        "I'm fine," you tell her, [cait.fucked|giving her thigh a little squeeze|squeezing her hand]. "It's just a lot to take in."
        
        She smiles sympathetically. "Take all the time you need. And if you ever need to talk..."]
        
        You take one last breath to clear your head and push off, turning towards the other side of the river. The old fortress on the far bank is crumbling from centuries of neglect. The way Garth told it, nobody from the village has been north of the river since the Godswar, and it's clear that the old wayfort's been abandoned just as long. The roof is falling in on itself, the gates are smashed in... its last owners likely died two, maybe three, hundred years ago. It looks almost mournful in its decay, a sad reminder of Savarra's glory days long faded.
        
        [flags.ALRAUNE_KILLED|A fortress like that, out here in the middle of nowhere and now with plenty of cleansed land to sustain its populace... it could be a bastion again, a place for folk like you that don't have a real home in the civilized parts of the Marches. The term 'warden' comes to mind. The old empire used the term for warrior-lords that protected the roadways from banditry... and for jailers, keeping folk that can't be trusted in civilization from running amok.
        |A fortress like that, out here in the middle of nowhere and connected to your new submissive plant-woman's garden... it could be a bastion for people like her. A place people tainted by Kasyrra and left broken, unable to cope with civilization, could go to find solace. If somebody like you were just around to keep it up, and keep them all under control. The term 'warden' comes to mind. The old empire used the term for warrior-lords that protected the roadways from banditry... and for jailers, keeping folk that can't be trusted in civilization from running amok.]
        
        But that's a thought for another time. For when you've caught up with Kasyrra. She's so close you can practically smell her!
        
        [party.has cait|"Come on," you tell Cait, taking her hand. "Let's go!"
        
        "Right behind you!" she grins, letting you pull her down off the edge.]
rows.translation:
你在那座古老的石桥上停下了脚步。那些浓烈得令人窒息的花香终于开始消退，被桥下流淌的冰冷清水的味道所取代。

        深吸一口气，整理一下思绪……经历了这一切之后，似乎一切都有了合理的解释。你靠在石桥上，把武器暂时放在了一旁。 [flags.ALRAUNE_KILLED|天啊，你们真的消灭了那个生物。尽管它已经堕落了，但那仍然是一条生命的终结。这种行为的沉重感像锚一样压在你的心上。不过，它再也不会伤害任何人了，它的后代们也四散而去。这确实是一次不可否认的胜利。 ]这就是卡希拉正在蔓延的腐化势力：她将萨瓦拉的生命扭曲成自己那些被腐化的玩物，然后将它们释放到这个毫无防备的世界中。可怜的鹰棘镇根本不知道即将发生什么。如果你没有出现，阿尔劳奈的后代或许早就占领了这个小镇。
        
        [party.has Cait|你没事吧？ [pc.name]怎么了？”凯特问道，她走到你身旁，靠在栏杆上。她的手轻轻触碰了你的肩膀。“你看起来心事重重的。”
        
        “我没事，”你告诉她。 [cait.fucked|轻轻捏了捏她的大腿|握住她的手]这些信息实在有点让人难以消化。”
        
        她同情地笑了笑：“你可以慢慢来，慢慢理解。如果你什么时候需要倾诉……]
        
        你深吸一口气，让头脑清醒些，然后开始划桨，朝着河对岸的方向前进。对岸那座古老的堡垒因为数百年的无人照料而逐渐倾塌。据加斯所说，自从那场神战之后，村里就再也没有人去过河的北岸，显然，那座古老的堡垒也早已被废弃了。屋顶已经开始坍塌，大门也被撞得粉碎……它的最后主人很可能在两三百年前就已经去世了。这种荒废与破败的场景看起来几乎带有一种哀伤的气息，它无声地提醒着我们，萨瓦拉曾经拥有的辉煌岁月早已一去不复返了。
        
        [flags.ALRAUNE_KILLED|像这样的堡垒，坐落在偏远之地，而现在又拥有充足的肥沃土地来养活居民……它完全可以再次成为一道屏障，成为那些在边境文明地区没有固定居所的人们们的庇护所。“守卫”这个词浮现在我的脑海中——古代帝国就用这个词来指那些负责保护道路免受盗贼侵扰的武士领主，同时也用来指那些看守那些在文明社会中无法被信任的人、防止他们为非作歹的狱卒。
        |像这样的堡垒，坐落在荒凉之地，却又与你们那些新建立的、充满顺从与和谐的植物女性花园相连……它完全可以成为像她这样的人的庇护所。对于那些被卡希拉的影响所扭曲、心灵受到伤害、无法适应文明社会的人们来说，这里正是他们寻找慰藉的地方。如果有像你这样的人在场，维持秩序并控制住所有人，那么“守卫”这个称呼就再合适不过了。古代帝国就用这个词来指那些负责保护道路免受盗贼侵扰的武士领主……同时也用来指那些看守那些在文明社会中无法被信任的人、防止他们为非作歹的狱卒。]
        
        不过，这个话题可以留到以后再讨论。等你们追上卡希拉的时候再聊吧——她已经离你们这么近了，你们几乎都能闻到她的气味了！
        
        [party.has cait|来吧，”你牵着凯特的手说，“我们走吧！”
        
        “我紧跟在你后面！”她笑着，让你把她从边缘拉下来。]
rows.raw:
"
        You pause a moment, halfway across the old stone bridge. The overpowerful aroma of oversexed flowers is finally starting to fade, washed away by the scent of cold, clear water running under the bridge. 

        A deep breath to collect your thoughts after... everything... doesn't seem unwarranted. You lean onto the stone and set your weapon aside for a moment. [flags.ALRAUNE_KILLED|Gods, you really killed that creature. Corrupted as she was, that was still a life taken. The heaviness of the act weighs on your heart like an anchor. But she won't hurt anyone again, and her daughters have been scattered to the winds. An undeniable victory. ]So this is the corruption Kasyrra is spreading: twisting the life of Savarra into her corrupted playthings, unleashing them on the unsuspecting world. Poor Hawkethorne had no idea what was coming. If you hadn't come along, it's possible the Alraune's progeny would have overrun the town.
        
        [party.has Cait|"You okay, [pc.name]?" Cait asks, hefting herself up onto the railing beside you. One of her hands brushes your shoulder. "You look a million miles away."
        
        "I'm fine," you tell her, [cait.fucked|giving her thigh a little squeeze|squeezing her hand]. "It's just a lot to take in."
        
        She smiles sympathetically. "Take all the time you need. And if you ever need to talk..."]
        
        You take one last breath to clear your head and push off, turning towards the other side of the river. The old fortress on the far bank is crumbling from centuries of neglect. The way Garth told it, nobody from the village has been north of the river since the Godswar, and it's clear that the old wayfort's been abandoned just as long. The roof is falling in on itself, the gates are smashed in... its last owners likely died two, maybe three, hundred years ago. It looks almost mournful in its decay, a sad reminder of Savarra's glory days long faded.
        
        [flags.ALRAUNE_KILLED|A fortress like that, out here in the middle of nowhere and now with plenty of cleansed land to sustain its populace... it could be a bastion again, a place for folk like you that don't have a real home in the civilized parts of the Marches. The term 'warden' comes to mind. The old empire used the term for warrior-lords that protected the roadways from banditry... and for jailers, keeping folk that can't be trusted in civilization from running amok.
        |A fortress like that, out here in the middle of nowhere and connected to your new submissive plant-woman's garden... it could be a bastion for people like her. A place people tainted by Kasyrra and left broken, unable to cope with civilization, could go to find solace. If somebody like you were just around to keep it up, and keep them all under control. The term 'warden' comes to mind. The old empire used the term for warrior-lords that protected the roadways from banditry... and for jailers, keeping folk that can't be trusted in civilization from running amok.]
        
        But that's a thought for another time. For when you've caught up with Kasyrra. She's so close you can practically smell her!
        
        [party.has cait|"Come on," you tell Cait, taking her hand. "Let's go!"
        
        "Right behind you!" she grins, letting you pull her down off the edge.]
        "

rows.original: Your walk along the courtyard is interrupted by an audible snarl, and the sound of someone being slammed into the ground. "Guh!" Daliza inhales sharply, rolling out of the way when a heavy, blunted training axe crashes into the dirt she'd just been occupying. She manages to roll deftly to her feet still, although she looks to be muscling away a winding. "You're quick! Stop being flat-footed Dally!" Jael'yn grins wickedly, hefting a massive blunted sword with unsettling ease. Aileh laughs, tail whipping out and forcing Daliza to jump so that she can try and swing her straight out of the air. At least this time the bailiff is quick enough to flatten her training spear against her body, riding the impact with nothing but a bruise to show for it. The only downside is it sends her careening into Jael'yn's curvaceous, muscular form... and for once she doesn't seem to be trying to crush Daliza in some kind of surprise grope. The huge demonic elf lowers her stance and scoops, throwing the lithe redhead over her shoulder and leaving her sprawled in the mud once more. "You're always so smug watching us go at it, Jael'yn. How about you show me what you've got?" Aileh hefts her axe, slamming her tail into the ground and kicking up a muddy puddle. It must have rained the previous night, as the muck is already up to her knees, splashed along her chest, and utterly coating Daliza herself. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |Elthara waves you over with a smile, having been set up with a comfortable chair to observe. "I'm almost envious, they're having a great time, aren't they?" She strokes a hand over her [elthara.pregStage 1 |pregnant tummy |toned abdomen ], eyes glittering as she takes in the sight of three muscular, mud-soaked women. ]All three of them have dressed down to nothing more than underwear — with an additional wrapping for Jael, thanks to her massive prick — and they're sucking down huge breaths and glistening with sweat. Daliza climbs to her feet, wincing and tucking back her hair. She frowns at the sight of her training spear splintered through, and stretches until something clicks. "She makes a point, lady Jael'yn..." The bailiff glances around in the mud before finding and pulling out a weighted, blunted bronze-edged wooden katana. "There you are." The massive demon licks her lips, glancing between the two and flexing slowly, showing off a frankly incredible amount of muscle despite her jiggling curves. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |Elthara gasps beside you, wiggling in her chair. [wayfort.hasMaids |A couple of maids buzz over with a chair for you to sit in too, before they return to pampering the [elthara.pregStage 1 |pregnant |charming ] elf. |One of Daliza's guards wanders over with a chair for you too, smiling politely. ] |[wayfort.hasMaids |A couple of maids buzz over with a chair for you to sit in, apparently more than happy to watch the show too. |One of Daliza's guards wanders over with a chair for you too, smiling politely. ] ] "I hate to break it to you, girls, but [pc.name] was the only one to take me in a fight before I became this, now I'm even stronger!" The draconic ex-general snorts, waving Dal over. "Oi, skinny, how about we dump your teacher on her fat rear?" Daliza flounders for a moment, at least until Jael'yn turns to face her. The demon licks her lips and lifts two fingers to them, dropping her tongue between a suggestive, lurid V. "Come on Daldal, I bet you can take me down a peg if you work together! I'll do aaaanything you want if you win." Despite the mud covering her body, Daliza's blush is just about visible. She puts her guard up and rotates around Jael'yn until she's shoulder-to-shoulder with Aileh — who makes sure to flap her wings for good measure. "Alright, blue, let's get you laid!" They may just be a bunch of women in mud-coated underwear holding training gear, but they make an impressive lineup. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |Elthara gives you a muted 'mnf', gently crossing a leg over and leaning back. "This should be fun." ] Jael'yn is first to make her move however; she leads in with a heavy stomp and a sweep with her greatsword, forcing the two of them back before swapping to one hand and launching a fist that makes your teeth ache just to remember. "Ah crud—" Aileh only just manages to get her shoulder in the way to avoid getting her throat flattened, but Daliza is quick to snap out at a slice for the demon's wrist. Unfortunately for her, Jael's tail already found the bailiff's foot, and it tugs the taller elf over with a quick snap that has her dumped in the mud once more. "Those flat, flat feet! Dance Dally, dance for momma— ooph!" Her taunting is interrupted by the need to block Aileh's axe. There's enough impact to force Jael'yn away, which gives Daliza time to haul herself to her feet again. "That hurt you ffuuu— dger." Daliza, and even Jael'yn pause, guard only halfway up. "A what?" Aileh huffs and tucks her hair back again, shaking off some of the mud clinging to her body and retracting her wings again. "Shut up." Jael recovers first, diving into the duo with obvious glee, throwing herself to the task of battering Aileh back with raw force, and keeping Daliza too off-balance to get a real swing in. Heat radiates from the red dragon-woman, sweat droplets steaming, entirely at odds with the respective chills of the elven women— although they still look plenty shiny despite the mud. They do grow tired though, even Jael'yn seems to be reaching her limit despite looking previously indomitable. It's Aileh that gives up first, yawning and stretching and dumping her axe into the dirt. "I'm out! Done! You win, big girl." Daliza looks between Aileh, and Jael'yn, and then down at her training weapon; it's already a bent and battered wreck, and though you can't make out the details from where you're sat there are probably cracks spider-webbing the entire thing. "I admit defeat, thank you, lady Jael'yn." The demon does a little bounce on the spot that forces her training bra to finally give up the ghost, snapping away and letting her huge tits free. "Aaah. A shame you couldn't take me, I wanted to find out what you had in mind." Daliza mumbles something that you can't make out, but Jael'yn laughs loudly. "I'm sure I will, Dally." Aileh snorts and wings off to the tower, no doubt rushing to get cleaned up. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |"Can you read lips? That was adorable." "What was?" "She said 'maybe you'll find out anyway' — fun development, no?" ]
rows.translation: 你正沿着庭院行走，突然听到一声低沉的咆哮，紧接着有人被猛地摔在地上的声音。“啊！”达莉莎猛地吸了一口凉气，赶紧侧身躲开——这时，一把重型的、钝头的训练斧重重地砸在了她刚才站立的地方。她敏捷地翻滚着站了起来，不过看样子还是被这一击撞得有些踉跄。 你动作真快！别再这么笨手笨足部了，达莉！”杰尔林坏笑着，轻松地举起了那把巨大的钝剑。 艾莉哈哈大笑，她的尾巴猛地一甩，迫使达莉莎跳了起来，这样她就能在半空中直接挥剑了。至少这一次，执达官动作足够迅速，将她的训练用长矛按在她的身体上，因此她只受了一处淤伤。唯一的缺点就是，这一撞击让她猛地撞上了贾琳那曲线优美、肌肉结实的身体。这一次，她似乎并没有试图用那种突然的举动来压制达莉莎。这个高大的恶魔精灵降低了身形，一把将那身材娇小的红发女子甩到自己的肩上，让她再次重重地摔在泥地里。 你总是那么得意洋洋地看着我们忙碌，贾尔琳。那你何不也展示一下你的本事呢？”艾莉举起她的斧头，用尾巴猛地敲打地面，溅起一片泥水。显然前夜下过雨，泥水已经没到她的膝盖，溅到了她的胸前，而达莉莎整个人也被泥水弄得浑身都是。 [wayfort.eltharaPresent |艾尔萨拉微笑着向你招手，为你准备了一把舒适的椅子，让你可以坐下来观看。“我都有点羡慕了，他们玩得这么开心，不是吗？”她轻轻抚过自己的手[elthara.pregStage 1 |怀孕的腹部 |紧实的腹部 ]她的眼睛闪闪发亮，当她看到那三个肌肉结实、浑身沾满泥浆的女性时。 ]他们三个人都只穿了内衣，而由于贾埃尔那巨大的……部位，她还需要再裹上一层东西。他们大口地喘着气，身上都冒出了汗珠。 达莉莎站了起来，微微皱着眉头，把头发掖到身后。看到自己的训练用长矛被劈成碎片，她皱起了眉头，然后活动身体，直到某个部位发出“咔嗒”的声响。“她确实很认真啊，杰琳女士……”执事在泥泞中四处寻找，最终找到了一把装有重物、刀刃被磨钝的青铜边木质武士刀，并将其拔了出来。就是你。” 那只巨大的恶魔舔了舔嘴唇，目光在两人之间来回扫视，同时缓缓地活动着自己的肌肉——尽管她的身材充满了曲线美，但她的肌肉力量确实令人难以置信。 [wayfort.eltharaPresent |艾尔萨拉在你身旁倒抽着气，坐在椅子上不停地扭动身体。 [wayfort.hasMaids |几名女仆拿来一把椅子，让你也可以坐下休息，然后她们便继续去照顾其他人了。 [elthara.pregStage 1 |怀孕的 |迷人 ]精灵。 |达莉莎的一名护卫也微笑着走过来，为您拿了一把椅子。 ] |[wayfort.hasMaids |几名女仆赶紧拿了一把椅子过来让你坐，显然她们也很乐意观看这场表演。 |达莉莎的一名护卫也微笑着走过来，为您拿来一把椅子。 ] ]姑娘们，我很不想让你们失望，但是[pc.name]是唯一一个在打架时愿意保护我的人。在……之前我变成了现在这个样子，现在我甚至更强大了！” 那位曾经是龙族将军的人哼了一声，然后将达尔招到身边：“喂，瘦子，我们是不是该让你的老师尝尝她自己那肥屁股的滋味？” 达尔扎愣住了，至少在杰尔琳转过身来面对她之前，她还是处于这种状态。恶魔舔了舔嘴唇，然后用两根手指触碰自己的嘴唇，将舌头伸成一种充满诱惑意味的形状。“来吧，达尔达尔，我相信如果我们合作的话，你一定能让我知道什么叫失败！如果你赢了，我愿意做任何你想要的事情。 尽管身上沾满了泥浆，达莉莎的脸色依然清晰可见。她警惕地转过身，与杰尔琳并肩而立，此时艾莱也特意扇动翅膀，以示自己的存在。“好了，蓝色生物，我们该带你走了放置好的她们或许只是一群穿着沾满泥浆的内衣、手持训练装备的女性，但整体看起来确实相当引人注目。 [wayfort.eltharaPresent |艾尔塔拉为你提供了这种低调、不显眼的设计风格。mnf她轻轻地把一条腿搭在另一条腿上，然后向后靠去，说道：“这应该会很有趣吧。 ] 然而，贾艾琳率先采取了行动；她首先用重型的脚步声震慑对手，接着用巨剑横扫，将两人逼退，随后改用单手攻击，挥出的拳头让人光是回想起来就会感到牙酸。啊呀——”艾莉勉强用肩膀挡住了去路，才避免被恶魔咬住喉咙，但达莉莎却迅速出手，咬住了恶魔的手腕。 不幸的是，贾埃尔的尾巴早已缠住了执事的足部，它猛地一拉，就把这个高个子的精灵拽到了泥地里，让她又一次陷进了泥潭中。那些扁平的足部啊！跳支舞吧，为妈妈跳支舞吧——哎哟！”她的嘲弄话音刚落，就不得不立刻挡开艾莱赫挥来的斧头。那股冲击力足以将杰琳撞开，这也让达莉莎有时间重新站起身来。 那个受伤你这家伙……” 达莉莎，甚至贾埃尔琳也都停下了动作，只将护盾举到一半的高度。“什么？” 艾莉赫气呼呼地把头发重新塞回耳后，甩掉身上粘着的泥巴，然后又把翅膀收了回去。闭嘴。” 贾埃尔最先恢复过来，她兴奋地冲向那两人，使出全力去反击艾莱，同时也让达利扎无法稳住身体，无法有效地进行反击。那红发龙女身上散发着炽热的气息，汗水不断蒸发，这与两位精灵女子身上散发出的寒冷气息形成了鲜明的对比——尽管她们身上沾满了泥浆，但依然显得光彩照人。 他们确实也会感到疲惫，就连看起来坚不可摧的杰琳似乎也快要达到极限了。最先放弃的是艾莱，她打了个哈欠，伸了个懒腰，然后把斧头扔到了地上。“我不行了！真的不行了！你赢了，大姑娘。达莉莎的目光在艾莱和杰尔林之间来回移动，然后落在她那把训练用武器上；那把武器早已变形、破损不堪，虽然从你现在的位置看不清细节，但想必整把武器上布满了裂纹。我认输吧，谢谢你，杰琳女士。 那个恶魔在原地跳了几下，结果她的训练胸罩终于不堪重负，断裂开来，让她那巨大的胸部彻底暴露了出来。“啊……真可惜你没能抓住我，我本来还想看看你到底有什么打算呢。” 达莉莎低声说了些什么，但大家都听不清楚，而杰琳却放声大笑起来：“我相信我以后一定会知道的，达莉。 艾莱赫哼了一声，然后飞向了塔楼，肯定是去清洗自己了。 [wayfort.eltharaPresent |你会读唇语吗？刚才那样子真是太可爱了。” “什么样子？” “她说‘也许你迟早会弄清楚的’——这个发展真是有趣，不是吗？ ]

At least this time the bailiff is quick enough to flatten her training spear against her body, riding the impact with nothing but a bruise to show for it. The only downside is it sends her careening into Jael'yn's curvaceous, muscular form... and for once she doesn't seem to be trying to crush Daliza in some kind of surprise grope. The huge demonic elf lowers her stance and scoops, throwing the lithe redhead over her shoulder and leaving her sprawled in the mud once more. "You're always so smug watching us go at it, Jael'yn. How about you show me what you've got?" Aileh hefts her axe, slamming her tail into the ground and kicking up a muddy puddle. It must have rained the previous night, as the muck is already up to her knees, splashed along her chest, and utterly coating Daliza herself. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |Elthara waves you over with a smile, having been set up with a comfortable chair to observe. "I'm almost envious, they're having a great time, aren't they?" She strokes a hand over her [elthara.pregStage 1 |pregnant tummy |toned abdomen ], eyes glittering as she takes in the sight of three muscular, mud-soaked women. ]All three of them have dressed down to nothing more than underwear — with an additional wrapping for Jael, thanks to her massive prick — and they're sucking down huge breaths and glistening with sweat. Daliza climbs to her feet, wincing and tucking back her hair. She frowns at the sight of her training spear splintered through, and stretches until something clicks. "She makes a point, lady Jael'yn..." The bailiff glances around in the mud before finding and pulling out a weighted, blunted bronze-edged wooden katana. "There you are." The massive demon licks her lips, glancing between the two and flexing slowly, showing off a frankly incredible amount of muscle despite her jiggling curves. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |Elthara gasps beside you, wiggling in her chair. [wayfort.hasMaids |A couple of maids buzz over with a chair for you to sit in too, before they return to pampering the [elthara.pregStage 1 |pregnant |charming ] elf. |One of Daliza's guards wanders over with a chair for you too, smiling politely. ] |[wayfort.hasMaids |A couple of maids buzz over with a chair for you to sit in, apparently more than happy to watch the show too. |One of Daliza's guards wanders over with a chair for you too, smiling politely. ] ] "I hate to break it to you, girls, but [pc.name] was the only one to take me in a fight before I became this, now I'm even stronger!" The draconic ex-general snorts, waving Dal over. "Oi, skinny, how about we dump your teacher on her fat rear?" Daliza flounders for a moment, at least until Jael'yn turns to face her. The demon licks her lips and lifts two fingers to them, dropping her tongue between a suggestive, lurid V. "Come on Daldal, I bet you can take me down a peg if you work together! I'll do aaaanything you want if you win." Despite the mud covering her body, Daliza's blush is just about visible. She puts her guard up and rotates around Jael'yn until she's shoulder-to-shoulder with Aileh — who makes sure to flap her wings for good measure. "Alright, blue, let's get you laid!" They may just be a bunch of women in mud-coated underwear holding training gear, but they make an impressive lineup. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |Elthara gives you a muted 'mnf', gently crossing a leg over and leaning back. "This should be fun." ] Jael'yn is first to make her move however; she leads in with a heavy stomp and a sweep with her greatsword, forcing the two of them back before swapping to one hand and launching a fist that makes your teeth ache just to remember. "Ah crud—" Aileh only just manages to get her shoulder in the way to avoid getting her throat flattened, but Daliza is quick to snap out at a slice for the demon's wrist. Dance Dally, dance for momma— ooph!" Her taunting is interrupted by the need to block Aileh's axe. Jael recovers first, diving into the duo with obvious glee, throwing herself to the task of battering Aileh back with raw force, and keeping Daliza too off-balance to get a real swing in. Heat radiates from the red dragon-woman, sweat droplets steaming, entirely at odds with the respective chills of the elven women— although they still look plenty shiny despite the mud. They do grow tired though, even Jael'yn seems to be reaching her limit despite looking previously indomitable. It's Aileh that gives up first, yawning and stretching and dumping her axe into the dirt. "I'm out! Done! You win, big girl." "I admit defeat, thank you, lady Jael'yn." The demon does a little bounce on the spot that forces her training bra to finally give up the ghost, snapping away and letting her huge tits free. "Aaah. A shame you couldn't take me, I wanted to find out what you had in mind." Daliza mumbles something that you can't make out, but Jael'yn laughs loudly. "I'm sure I will, Dally." Aileh snorts and wings off to the tower, no doubt rushing to get cleaned up. [wayfort.eltharaPresent |"Can you read lips? That was adorable." "What was?" "She said 'maybe you'll find out anyway' — fun development, no?" ]"

"M-[pc.master] [pc.name]!" Rumie shouts the moment you enter the room. She's nervous, diligently cleaning a mug that looks like it has already been cleaned more than a dozen times this last hour. 
    
    "What's wrong?" you say as you approach the bee and gently get that mug from her hands.
    
    "A weird couple came a short while ago. They said they knew you, so I let them stay around. Now they've taken over the back room next to the pantry and are saying that it's their VIP casino room."
    
    [caera.isDisguised
        |"A muscular girl and a petite one?"
        |"Are they demons?"
    ]
    
    "Yes! [jaelyn.isBartender
        |[caera.isDisguised
            |
            |A red one, and the other one was blue. 
        ]I'm... I'm sorry I let them in, [pc.master] [pc.name]."
        
        [pc.isBimbo
            |"Aww, come here sweetie," you say as you lean forward and hug her.
            |"Why're you sorry? You did good. They must be Sandre and Caera."
        ]
        
        "S-so you aren't mad?" Rumie says, way more calm.
        
        "Why would I be?"
        
        "But Jael'yn said that..." The bee girl turns around to see the demon maid leaning on the bar, trying to hold her laughter.
        
        "Oh, you look so cute when you're in distress," Jael'yn says, teasing the bee. 
        
        "No bully bee!" Rumie says.
        
        "Yes bully bee," Jael'yn answers as she walks to the kitchen with a grin still on her face.
        |Oh gods, so you know them. What a relief; I thought they had taken advantage of me!" 
        
        "They wouldn't dare," you tell her, playing it down with a hand gesture. "Unless you let them, of course."
    ]

rows.original:
You take a small, narrow door that was supposed to lead to a storage room, but what you find inside has nothing to do with brooms nor shelves. You find tulle-like stripes of cloth hanging from the ceiling like curtains and lights with different shades of red coming from the walls, clearly a product of Caera's magic. 
    
    The translucent drapes hide what's beyond. The fabric is soft to the touch and you make your way through them until you see the demon couple sitting around a table with a bunch of Daliza's men. Sandre is armwrestling a bulky guy covered in armor, while Caera sits back and enjoys the show from behind her book with a grin on her unmoving face. With one last grunt, Sandre takes the guy's hand to the table and rises as victor.
    
    "Yes! Take that!" Sandre says, standing up with a wide smile. "Time to pay up, weakling. Maybe tomorrow you'll get a bit luckier."
    
    The guy curses under his breath and throws a bag of electrum on the table.
    
    "That's not all, right?" Caera says, leaning over the table to take the bag. "It was double or nothing."
    
    "Okay, here you go," the guy says as he takes some more coins. "Happy now, bitch?"
    
    "That's better," Caera says. "And I'll take it as a compliment. Now would you mind leaving us alone, guys? It seems like we have an important guest."
    
    "Hey there, Champ," Sandre says, falling into her chair again while the soldiers leave with their pockets a little bit lighter than they were when they walked in. "It's a pleasure seeing you around here. I gotta say this castle of yours is awesome."
    
    "I knew you were gonna love it," Caera says as she also sits back. "But now to what really matters. What can we do for you, [pc.name]?
rows.translation:
你推开一扇本该通往储藏室的小窄门，但里面的东西跟扫帚和架子毫无关系。你看到天花板上垂着薄纱般的条纹布料，像窗帘一样；墙上透出深浅不一的红光，显然是凯拉的魔法造物。 
    
    半透明的帷幔遮住了后面的景象。那布料摸起来很柔软，你穿过它们，直到看见那对恶魔夫妇和达莉莎的一群手下围坐在桌边。桑德蕾正在和一个身披护甲的壮汉掰手腕，而凯拉则靠坐着，躲在自己的书后面，带着一脸笑意从那张纹丝不动的脸上欣赏这场好戏。随着最后一声闷哼，桑德蕾把那名男子的手按到桌上，以胜利者的姿态站起身。
    
    “好耶！接招吧！”桑德蕾说着站起来，笑容满面。“该付账了，弱鸡。也许明天你会走运一点。”
    
    那家伙低声骂了一句，把一袋琥珀金扔在桌上。
    
    “这还不是全部吧？”凯拉说着，俯身越过桌子去拿那个钱袋。“说好的是翻倍或者一分不给。”
    
    “好吧，给你，”那家伙说着又掏出几枚硬币。“现在满意了吗，婊子？”
    
    “这样就好多了，”凯拉说。“我就当这是赞美了。现在，你们介意让我们单独待会儿吗，各位？看来我们有位重要的客人。”
    
    “嘿，冠军，”桑德蕾说着重新跌坐回椅子里，而那些士兵正离开，口袋比进来时轻了一点。“很高兴在这儿见到你。我得说，你这座城堡真棒。”
    
    “我就知道你会喜欢它的，”凯拉说着也靠坐回去。“不过现在说正事。我们能为你做点什么，[pc.name]？

rows.original:
You accept Sandre's proposition and take the stool right next to her. She then hits the bar twice with her knuckles and in a matter of seconds there are two jugs of liquor in front of you, courtesy of your favorite bee girl, Rumie.
    
    "It's nice to have some company when drinking," Sandre laughs. "It gives you an excuse to keep drinking some more."
    
    "What do we drink to?" 
    
    "To starting over," she says as she makes her jug clash with yours.
    
    You watch as she drinks it all in one gulp, and then she asks Rumie for yet another one. If she keeps this up it won't be long until you run out of every kind of alcohol in your pantry. 
    
    "You girls seem pretty keen on starting over," you tell her. "Was it so bad when you were a human?"
    
    "Not really. I just didn't like it. It's Caera who hates the person she was."
    
    "How come?"
    
    "She just... I don't know. Everyone has a story, and some people have it harder than others, but what really matters is how we deal with it. Many would consider hers not especially hard, but she didn't know how to face it, and that marked her whole life."
    
    She stops for a second to stare at the bottom of her glass before resuming her talk.
    
    "Caera... Her mother was a Mallachite. She worked at the temple and planned for Caera to do the same: finding the best way to suck a cock, getting pounded night after night and claiming you do it for a higher power... That would've been her life, but her father managed to take her out of that place when she was still young, and they ran away to Belhar, where he was originally from. As you can guess, the mother didn't go with them. Caera says that for that woman her father was only a customer, and that she didn't even see her as a daughter, but probably as another product to offer to Mallach and nothing more. Caera hated her for that. She hated her and her memory with all her guts, for why would that woman smile at her? Why would she brush her hair and tell her tales if she would later abandon her to the temple?"
    
    [party.has cait
        |Cait sighs, resting her hands in her chin. "Poor girl, reminds me of Calla. She'd get that way sometimes, but it didn't stick with her. Some kids never really understand Mallach's way, that all he wants for us is to be true to ourselves and our passions — and that we clergy have the privilege of helping others. Sometimes it never sinks in. I'm glad she had the chance to leave, but clearly it didn't help..."
        
        "You can say all that to me, Mallachite, but please, don't bring it up in front of her. I can't stand seeing her when she tries to hold back her tears," Sandre says. "Anyway, a
        |"A
    ]ll she wanted was to forget, but every time she looked in the mirror she could see how similar she was to the mother she remembered, and that frightened her. Even if it doesn't make any logical sense, she says she was afraid of people judging her and comparing her to that woman. I think she was scared of herself, because deep down she was the one making the comparison. She was so desperate to act like the mother who abandoned her never existed that she couldn't stop thinking about her. So, that fear of what people could think or say led to her isolation. She would spend her days alone, doing the only thing that allowed her to escape those fears: read. And that's all she did until I found her."
    
    You've finished your drink without noticing, but Rumie is already handing you another one while leaning against the bar to hear Sandre's story.
    
    "You become quite talkative when you drink," you say.
    
    "I guess I do," she laughs.
    
    "And what's your story, Sandre?" you ask her. 
    
    "Mine's way simpler. Just a common thug, raised in the back alleys of the damned Holy City of Belhar where I had to fight every other orphan for a piece of bread. I grew up seeing how Belharan soldiers always had enough to fill their stomach and a roof over their head; they had everything they wanted, and when they didn't have it, the sword allowed them to just go and take it. I wanted that for myself, but it wasn't easy. It doesn't matter how small Belhar has become, it doesn't matter that it's now little more than a rotten city, those elitist bastards wouldn't let just anyone enter their ranks. I knew how to fight —with my fist that is— but I didn't have any weapon knowledge and what's worse: not even a surname. There was nothing a criminal like me could offer to the proud Belharan soldiers. But then I saw a lonely girl reading under a tree, and I thought to myself that maybe if I knew how to read and write I'd stand a chance to be a knight."
    
    "So you do know how to read and write?"
    
    "Why do you sound surprised?" she asks, stopping midway from taking the new jug to her lips. "I was top of my class."
    
    "You also were the only one in the class," Caera's voice says. You turn your head to see the girl, who has just arrived and is taking a seat at the other side of Sandre. She then throws her arms at the red demon to hug her from behind and resumes her talk. "I take it you've already told everything to everyone. You become quite talkative when you drink, honey."
    
    "She does."
    
    "So yeah, after that we only grew closer as we grew up, and we found out that we both hated it in Belhar," she says now looking at you. "It wasn't hard for Sandre to convince me to join her and become knights. It gave us an excuse to leave the city with enough money and supplies. But leaving for good seemed impossible; deserting the army is not an easy task. In a sense we got lucky that we were captured. We wouldn't have had the opportunity to start over if it wasn't for that."
    
    "No, we got lucky because we got to meet each other," Sandre says, moving drowsily to hug her girl.
    
    Caera smiles, takes the jug from Sandre's hands and gives it to Rumie. 
    
    "Okay, I think you've drunk enough, big girl," the blue demon says. "Hey [pc.name], I'm gonna take her to bed. Good night, I'll see you around."
    
    And with those words she helps a sleepy Sandre stand up, and they start walking while Rumie cleans the collection of jugs that the red demon has left behind.

你接受了桑德的邀请，坐到了她旁边的位置。随后，她用指关节敲了两次吧台，不一会儿，你面前就出现了两壶酒——这些都是你最喜欢的蜜蜂女孩露米送来的。
    
    “喝酒时有个人陪在身边确实不错，”桑德笑着说，“这样你就有借口继续喝下去了。
    
    我们喝什么来庆祝呢？”
    
    “为了重新开始，”她边说边将自己的酒壶与你的酒壶轻轻碰了一下。
    
    你看着她一饮而尽，然后她又向露米要了另一杯。如果她继续这样下去，不久你的储藏室里各种酒类就会全部用光了。 
    
    你们这些女孩似乎都很想重新开始，”你对她说，“当你们还是人类的时候，生活真的有那么糟糕吗？”
    
    “也不算吧。我只是不喜欢那种生活而已。真正讨厌自己过去身份的人是凯拉。”
    
    “为什么呢？”
    
    “她只是……我也说不清楚。每个人都有自己的故事，有些人的经历确实更艰难，但真正重要的是我们如何面对这些经历。对很多人来说，她的经历或许并不算特别艰难，但她不知道该如何面对它，而这影响了她的一生。
    
    她停顿了一下，盯着杯底看了一会儿，然后继续说道：
    
    “凯拉……她的母亲是一名马拉克信徒教徒。她在神庙工作，也希望凯拉能走同样的道路：找到最能让男人愉悦的方式，夜复一夜地接受他们的宠爱，同时声称自己是在为某种更高的力量做这些事。那本该是她的命运，但在她还很年轻的时候，她的父亲设法将她从那个地方带了出来，他们一起逃到了贝尔哈尔——他的故乡。可你也能猜到，她的母亲并没有和他们一起离开。凯拉说，对那个女人来说，她的父亲只不过是一个顾客而已；她甚至并不把凯拉当作自己的女儿来看待，而可能只是将她视为另一种可以献给马拉克的商品罢了。凯拉因此而恨她。她从内心深处恨这个女人，也恨与这个女人有关的所有回忆——为什么那个女人会对她微笑？为什么会在给她梳头发、给她讲故事之后，却将她抛弃在神庙里？
    
    [party.has cait
        |凯特叹了口气，双手托着下巴说道：“可怜的女孩，这让我想起了卡拉。她有时候也会这样，但这种情绪并不会持续太久。有些孩子永远都无法真正理解马拉赫的初衷——他只是希望我们能够做自己，追随自己的热情；而我们这些神职人员，更有责任去帮助他人。有时候，这些事情就是让人难以接受。我很高兴她有机会离开，但显然，这并没有起到什么帮助作用……”
        
        “你可以把这些话都告诉我，马拉克信徒，但请不要在她面前提起这些。每当我看到她努力忍住泪水的时候，我真的无法忍受。”桑德蕾说道。不管怎样，一个……
        |A
    ]她所渴望的只是忘记一切，但每当她照镜子时，都会看到自己与记忆中的那位母亲有多么相似，而这让她感到恐惧。尽管这种感觉在逻辑上并不成立，但她还是害怕别人会评判她，会把她和那个女人相提并论。我认为她其实是害怕自己，因为在她内心深处，正是她在不断地进行这种比较。她如此迫切地想要装作那个抛弃她的母亲从未存在过，以至于她无法停止思考关于那个母亲的事情。因此，这种对别人可能会怎么想、会说什么的恐惧，最终导致了她的孤立。她整天独自一人，做着唯一能让她摆脱那些恐惧的事情：读书。在我找到她之前，她一直只是这样度日而已。
    
    你不知不觉就已经喝完了饮料，而露米却已经靠在吧台上，一边听桑德蕾讲故事，一边递给你另一杯酒。
    
    “喝酒之后，你就会变得特别爱说话呢，”你说。
    
    “大概是吧，”她笑着说。
    
    “那么，桑德蕾，你的故事是什么呢？”你问她。 
    
    我的经历要简单得多。我只是一个普通的混混，在那个该死的贝尔哈尔圣城的阴暗小巷里长大，为了得到一块面包，我不得不和其他孤儿们争斗。我亲眼看到，贝尔哈尔的士兵们总是有足够的食物填饱肚子，有房子遮风挡雨；他们拥有想要的一切，而当他们得不到这些东西时，剑就成为了他们获取一切的工具。我也很想要那样，但这一切并不容易。无论贝尔哈尔变得多么渺小，无论它现在只不过是一座破败的城市，那些自命不凡的混蛋们也不会让随便什么人加入他们的行列。我知道如何打架——也就是用拳头打架——但我对任何武器都一无所知，更糟糕的是：我甚至连一个姓氏都没有。像我这样的罪犯，根本无法为那些骄傲的贝尔哈兰士兵提供任何帮助。但是，后来我看到一个女孩独自在一棵树下读书，于是我想，如果我会读写的话，或许就有机会成为一名骑士。"
    
    所以你确实会读写啊？”
    
    “你为什么听起来这么惊讶？”她问道，将新水壶拿到嘴边的动作突然停住了。“我在班上可是成绩最好的。”
    
    “而且你也是班上唯一会读写的人。”凯拉的声音说道。你转过头，看到了那个刚刚到达的女孩，她正坐在桑德蕾的另一边。然后她伸出双臂，从背后抱住了那个红色恶魔，继续她的谈话：“我想你应该已经把一切都告诉大家了吧。亲爱的，你一喝酒就会变得特别爱说话呢。
    
    她确实这么做了。”
    
    “所以，随着我们渐渐长大，我们的关系反而变得更加亲密。后来我们发现，我们俩都讨厌贝尔哈尔。”她现在看着你说，“对桑德蕾来说，说服我加入她，一起成为骑士并不是什么难事。这给了我们一个借口，让我们能够带着足够的钱和物资离开这座城市。但彻底离开那里似乎是不可能的——退出军队绝非易事。从某种意义上说，我们运气很好，因为被俘了。如果没有那件事，我们就不会有重新开始的机会。
    
    不，我们只是运气好，才能相遇吧，”桑德蕾昏昏欲睡地说着，然后抱住了她的女朋友。
    
    凯拉微笑着，从桑德蕾手中接过水壶，递给了露米。
    
    “好了，我觉得你已经喝够了吧，大姑娘，”那个蓝色恶魔说道。“嘿[pc.name]，我得送她去睡觉了。晚安，回头见。”
    
    说完，她扶着昏昏欲睡的桑德蕾站了起来，两人开始往家里走，而露米则开始清理那个红色恶魔留下的那些罐子。

'
    You accept Sandre's proposition and take the stool right next to her. She then hits the bar twice with her knuckles and in a matter of seconds there are two jugs of liquor in front of you, courtesy of your favorite bee girl, Rumie.
    
    "It's nice to have some company when drinking," Sandre laughs. "It gives you an excuse to keep drinking some more."
    
    "What do we drink to?" 
    
    "To starting over," she says as she makes her jug clash with yours.
    
    You watch as she drinks it all in one gulp, and then she asks Rumie for yet another one. If she keeps this up it won't be long until you run out of every kind of alcohol in your pantry. 
    
    "You girls seem pretty keen on starting over," you tell her. "Was it so bad when you were a human?"
    
    "Not really. I just didn't like it. It's Caera who hates the person she was."
    
    "How come?"
    
    "She just... I don't know. Everyone has a story, and some people have it harder than others, but what really matters is how we deal with it. Many would consider hers not especially hard, but she didn't know how to face it, and that marked her whole life."
    
    She stops for a second to stare at the bottom of her glass before resuming her talk.
    
    "Caera... Her mother was a Mallachite. She worked at the temple and planned for Caera to do the same: finding the best way to suck a cock, getting pounded night after night and claiming you do it for a higher power... That would've been her life, but her father managed to take her out of that place when she was still young, and they ran away to Belhar, where he was originally from. As you can guess, the mother didn't go with them. Caera says that for that woman her father was only a customer, and that she didn't even see her as a daughter, but probably as another product to offer to Mallach and nothing more. Caera hated her for that. She hated her and her memory with all her guts, for why would that woman smile at her? Why would she brush her hair and tell her tales if she would later abandon her to the temple?"
    
    [party.has cait
        |Cait sighs, resting her hands in her chin. "Poor girl, reminds me of Calla. She'd get that way sometimes, but it didn't stick with her. Some kids never really understand Mallach's way, that all he wants for us is to be true to ourselves and our passions — and that we clergy have the privilege of helping others. Sometimes it never sinks in. I'm glad she had the chance to leave, but clearly it didn't help..."
        
        "You can say all that to me, Mallachite, but please, don't bring it up in front of her. I can't stand seeing her when she tries to hold back her tears," Sandre says. "Anyway, a
        |"A
    ]ll she wanted was to forget, but every time she looked in the mirror she could see how similar she was to the mother she remembered, and that frightened her. Even if it doesn't make any logical sense, she says she was afraid of people judging her and comparing her to that woman. I think she was scared of herself, because deep down she was the one making the comparison. She was so desperate to act like the mother who abandoned her never existed that she couldn't stop thinking about her. So, that fear of what people could think or say led to her isolation. She would spend her days alone, doing the only thing that allowed her to escape those fears: read. And that's all she did until I found her."
    
    You've finished your drink without noticing, but Rumie is already handing you another one while leaning against the bar to hear Sandre's story.
    
    "You become quite talkative when you drink," you say.
    
    "I guess I do," she laughs.
    
    "And what's your story, Sandre?" you ask her. 
    
    "Mine's way simpler. Just a common thug, raised in the back alleys of the damned Holy City of Belhar where I had to fight every other orphan for a piece of bread. I grew up seeing how Belharan soldiers always had enough to fill their stomach and a roof over their head; they had everything they wanted, and when they didn't have it, the sword allowed them to just go and take it. I wanted that for myself, but it wasn't easy. It doesn't matter how small Belhar has become, it doesn't matter that it's now little more than a rotten city, those elitist bastards wouldn't let just anyone enter their ranks. I knew how to fight —with my fist that is— but I didn't have any weapon knowledge and what's worse: not even a surname. There was nothing a criminal like me could offer to the proud Belharan soldiers. But then I saw a lonely girl reading under a tree, and I thought to myself that maybe if I knew how to read and write I'd stand a chance to be a knight."
    
    "So you do know how to read and write?"
    
    "Why do you sound surprised?" she asks, stopping midway from taking the new jug to her lips. "I was top of my class."
    
    "You also were the only one in the class," Caera's voice says. You turn your head to see the girl, who has just arrived and is taking a seat at the other side of Sandre. She then throws her arms at the red demon to hug her from behind and resumes her talk. "I take it you've already told everything to everyone. You become quite talkative when you drink, honey."
    
    "She does."
    
    "So yeah, after that we only grew closer as we grew up, and we found out that we both hated it in Belhar," she says now looking at you. "It wasn't hard for Sandre to convince me to join her and become knights. It gave us an excuse to leave the city with enough money and supplies. But leaving for good seemed impossible; deserting the army is not an easy task. In a sense we got lucky that we were captured. We wouldn't have had the opportunity to start over if it wasn't for that."
    
    "No, we got lucky because we got to meet each other," Sandre says, moving drowsily to hug her girl.
    
    Caera smiles, takes the jug from Sandre's hands and gives it to Rumie. 
    
    "Okay, I think you've drunk enough, big girl," the blue demon says. "Hey [pc.name], I'm gonna take her to bed. Good night, I'll see you around."
    
    And with those words she helps a sleepy Sandre stand up, and they start walking while Rumie cleans the collection of jugs that the red demon has left behind.

You're just about to leave when you hear someone opening the door and walking towards you.
    
    "Well, well, if it ain't [pc.mf
        |Mr
        |Ms
    ] [pc.name]" says a woman's voice, one that you are quick to recognize as Lyla's. She approaches you and gently bumps her fist into your shoulder. "The [pc.mf
        |lord
        |lady
    ] of the castle, in the flesh."
    
    "Lyla? I didn't picture you as the gambling type."
    
    "Nah, I just saw a bunch of elves crying about losing money to some couple. The names they spoke sounded familiar so I came to see if..."
    
    Lyla stops mid sentence when she lays her eyes on the two girls behind the curtains. She starts walking slowly, with care, clearing the translucent drapes out of her way until she reaches the center of the room, where the couple awaits, both showing a stupefied expression if you've ever seen one. 
    
    "What in the actual fuck?" Lyla says. "It really is you." 
    
    "You gotta be kidding," Sandre says. "Sargeant?"
    
    "For all the glory of Belhar, you girls made it," Lyla says, then she lets a relieved smile shine. "I thought I'd never see one of you alive again but... here you are. I can't believe it."
    
    The knight takes a seat at the table, moving slowly, afraid that the smallest movement would break the spell and she'd wake up alone in her tent. 
    
    "I... I'm really glad you're here though," she says, then her eyes light up with hope. "What about the rest of the squad? Did you manage to get any information about them before escaping?"
    
    "We have no idea," Sandre says with a shrug. "They could have been in the room next door or taken somewhere else. "
    
    "Also, we didn't escape," Caera completes. "We deserted."
    
    "Then...?" Lyla asks with a confused frown. Then she notices Caera's black tail wrapped around her leg as if it were part of her boot. 
    
    "Yeah," Caera says. "We took their deal."
    
    "You what?" Lyla says.
    
    "We became demons. We agreed to serve some big, blue demon and then deserted as soon as they sent us away to help with some smuggling operation on the Undermountain. We got complete freedom and the chance to start anew, leaving everything behind at the cost of what? Our souls? Seems like a bargain to me," Caera says. "Or it would be if we could actually leave everything behind."
    
    A smuggling operation around there? That rings a bell.
    
    "What the fuck is wrong with you?" Lyla says standing up, more indignant than angry. "Was it that easy to convince you to give your humanity up?"
    
    "Easy?" Caera says with a huff and her expressionless mask breaks for a moment, letting you see her lip trembling with either rage or distress. "I gave up my soul as soon as I could. I'm tired of acting like corruption is bad. Corruption is liberation. Those harpies that go around assaulting people, those kobolds that do the same, or those mercenaries that do even worse... you know what the difference is between us and them? That they try to make up excuses for what they do. They try to convince themselves that they do it for the survival of their nest, for their goddess or even for the greater good. Us? We accept that the real reason we do anything is because we want to. We are tired of pretending. Tired of having to mask our desires and having to worry about what everyone else would think. I don't give a shit anymore. I am who I am. Who I want to be. And I don't regret it." 
    
    "I take it that you don't give a damn about what happens to the rest of the squad."
    
    "Not in the least," Caera says with her arms crossed over her chest. "Why would I? When has anyone cared about me?"
    
    "Then who you really want to be is just a fucking selfish coward."
rows.translation:
就在你准备离开的时候，听到有人打开了门，正朝你的方向走来。

“哎呀，没想到会是你[pc.mf
        |先生
        |女士
    ] [pc.name]是一个女人的声音，你立刻就能认出那是莉拉的声音。她走到你跟前，轻轻用拳头碰了碰你的肩膀，说道：‘该[pc.mf
        |领主
        |女士
    ]城堡里的那个人，真人版的。”

“莉拉？我本来没觉得你会喜欢赌博这种东西。”

“嗯，我只是看到一群精灵因为输钱而哭哭啼啼的。他们说的那些名字听起来很耳熟，所以我就过来看看是不是真的认识他们。当莉拉看到窗帘后面那两个女孩时，她的话突然停住了。她小心翼翼地慢慢走过去，拨开那些半透明的窗帘，终于走到了房间的中央——那对情侣正站在那里，他们的表情简直可以用“惊呆了”来形容。 
    
    这他妈到底是怎么回事？”莱拉说道，“真的是你啊。”

“你一定在开玩笑吧，”桑德蕾说，“中士？”

“看在贝尔哈尔的份上，你们几个终于成功了，”莱拉说道，随后露出如释重负的笑容，“我本来以为再也见不到你们中的任何一个活着了，但……你们居然在这里。我简直不敢相信。
    
    骑士缓缓地坐在桌旁，生怕自己的任何动作都会打破这个魔法，让她独自在帐篷中醒来。

“我……真的很高兴你来了，”她说，然后她的眼中燃起了希望，“那队里的其他成员呢？你在逃跑之前有没有得到关于他们的任何消息？
    
    我们完全不知道，”桑德蕾耸了耸肩说道，“他们可能就在隔壁的房间里，也可能去了别的地方。”

“而且，我们并不是逃走的，”凯拉补充道，“我们是自己主动离开的。”

“那么……？”莉拉困惑地皱起了眉头。这时，她注意到凯拉的黑尾巴缠绕在她的腿上，仿佛那是她靴子的一部分。 
    
    是啊，”凯拉说，“我们接受了他们的提议。”

“你什么？”莱拉惊讶地问道。

“我们变成了恶魔。我们同意为某个巨大的蓝色恶魔效力，但当他们派我们去山腹深域协助一场走私行动后，我们立刻逃走了。我们因此获得了完全的自由，也得到了重新开始的机会。不过，我们为此付出了什么代价呢？我们的灵魂吗？在我看来，这简直是一笔划算的交易。”凯拉说道，“当然，前提是我们真的能够抛下一切。
    
    那边有走私活动？听起来挺耳熟的……”

“你到底怎么回事？”莉拉站起身来，语气中更多的是愤慨而非愤怒，“居然这么容易就让你放弃了作为人类的身份？”

“容易？凯拉气呼呼地说道，她那毫无表情的面具在这一刻被打破了，你可以看到她的嘴唇因为愤怒或痛苦而颤抖着。‘我尽快放弃了自己的灵魂。我厌倦了装作腐败是坏事的样子。腐败其实就是解放。那些到处袭击他人的女妖，那些干着同样事情的狗头人，还有那些行为更加恶劣的雇佣兵……你知道我们和他们之间的区别是什么吗？那就是他们会试图为自己所做的行为找借口。他们试图说服自己，认为自己这么做是为了保护自己的家园、为了他们的神明，甚至是为了更大的利益。而我们呢？我们清楚地知道，做任何事情的真正原因，仅仅是因为我们想要这么做。我们已经厌倦了伪装。我受够了不得不隐藏自己的欲望，也不想再担心别人会怎么想。我再也不在乎了。我就是我，我想成为的那个人，而且我对此毫不后悔。 
    
    我看你根本不在乎小队其他人的命运吧。”

“一点也不在乎，”凯拉双臂交叉在胸前说道，“我为什么要关心呢？有谁曾经真正关心过我吗？”

“那么，你真正想成为的，不过是个自私至极的懦夫罢了。

"So, about the smuggling operation going on around the Undermountain..." you start saying.
    
    "What about it?" Caera says. 
    
    "What can you tell me?"
    
    "Close to nothing," Caera says. "It's not like they disclose the logistics behind their operations to anyone who happens to be around." 
    
    "Okay, let's hear what you know. Tell me your story there."
    
    "It's not a long story, but sure, why not?" Sandre says with a shrug. "After our souls were already gone, some angry looking demon comes to us, giving us orders as if we were in the fucking Belharan army. We know better than to defy people like that, so we play along and follow her to some boat where she's gathered a bunch of other demons and some imps."
    
    "Do you know anything about the boat?"
    
    "We know that it was a boat. And that it floated," Caera says. "[pc.name], you really overestimate how much information they trust their subordinates with."
    
    "So, we start sailing..."
    
    "And no, before you ask, we don't know from where we departed either," Caera says. 
    
    "Honey, I'm trying to tell a story here," Sandre says, and Caera only rolls her eyes as a response. "Anyway, we started sailing. The view from the deck was amazing, but the angry looking knight kept ordering us around, and we spent most of the time taking care of whatever they were shipping. Before we know it, there's no more sky above our heads and we are entering the Undermountain. You see? We became demons because we wanted freedom. And having that prick with the armor nearby was the complete opposite of freedom. So what do we do? We desert. Just like that. We leave them all behind and run for our lives, we go deep enough inside those caves that they wouldn't bother to look for us. It's not hard when you have the shadows on your side and half of the crew are too busy getting their rocks off to even care."
    
    [pc.isBimbo
        |"That sounds fun! But I'm not sure if that's helpful information..." 
        |"So, it's true that you have no information,"
    ] you say. 
    
    "I told you. We've got no information at all," Caera answers.

rows.original: The fort's solitary tower seems like the perfect place to inscribe Evergreen's ancient magics. You don't know if the fort's former owner housed a court magician here, but even if not, it's a fitting place for a ritual circle. You take out the tome and pouch of components, flipping through the weathered old pages to try and puzzle out what to do. You'd really have expected such a tome to be full of complex formula and arcane symbology, [pc.bg arcanist |like a proper spellbook, ] but what Evergreen's given you reads much more like a recipe book complete with a few simple, common-language diagrams you can follow. It calls for powdered chalk and silver, a few esoteric herbs that it helpfully illustrates, and five small electrum balls to form the points of a pentagram. Everything you need is in the bag the witch gave you, right down to the dried milkweed. It takes about an hour to carve out the channel for the circle in the tower's ground floor, and a bit longer than that to fill the knife-wrought channels with the herbal admixture, and to affix the five electrum bearings to the points. It almost feels underwhelming when you're done: there's no great magical fanfare or eruption of power, just... a quiet hum as the last silvery ball snaps into place. It settles a moment later, leaving you with silence. The summoning circle is finished! You can interact with certain summonable creatures through a magic ritual performed at the circle.

rows.original: You step to the edge of the summoning circle and flip your spellbook, couched under an arm, to the rite of binding used to command the spirit of Viv's loyal wolf-hound. No sooner have you spoken the incantation than the veil parts in a shimmer of misty magics, and the great muscular body of the spectral hound appears before you, ears up and alert for danger. But this time, there's none to be had. The wolf-spirit glances around, assuring itself of safety, before turning its full attention to you with a great big wag of its tail and a bark that resonates through the air as if from miles and miles away. But it's close enough to melt your heart all the same. You give the ghost-dog a great big smile and get down on your knees, throwing your arms open invitingly; a split second later and the pup's nuzzled right up into your embrace, panting and wagging and slathering your cheeks in faintly-cold kisses. "Who's a good boy? Who is it?" you [pc.mf |chuckle |giggle ], patting the wolf-hound's head. "Is it you?" "Woof!" "That's right! You're a good boy!" The pup wiggles ecstatically from head to rump, eventually so overtaken by its own exuberance that it flops onto its back and presents its stomach for petting. You do so with gusto, running your fingers through cold, soft ghost-fur until the wolf's delighted wiggling finally settles into utter contentment. It makes a little snort of a whine in the back of its throat and rests its head against your [pc.leg], totally secure in your affectionate pets. You carry on for a few minutes longer, enjoying the slice of normality found in just sitting around and petting a pup — even a big, ghostly one — until the ghostly beast is fast asleep in your lap. Only then do you dismiss the spell, letting the goodest boy in the Marches fade away back to the aetheric mists from whence he came. What a good dog...

rows.original: You prepare the summoning circle, then mouth the incantations necessary to bring Thalia to you. No sooner have you finished that a burst of static fills the air and Thalia winks into existence within the inscribed boundaries, picking herself up from... well, whatever it was that she was doing before you called for her. "So, you called for me again." So you did. She looks a little more presentable than the last time, which speaks well of her. Thalia smiles. "Well, I had more warning this time, and if I was going to leave [pc.swornGod nareva |our |the ] goddess' Dream I might as well gussy up, hmm? Especially considering who it is who's summoning me?" [pc.swornGod nareva |More warning, huh? Nareva, then? "Time doesn't flow the same way in the Dream that it does here. But yes, she did say 'Thalia dear, you'll be up shortly. [pc.names] looking for you'." You sigh. Maybe it's just your imagination, but is Nareva setting you up for her own amusement? "Who cares if she is?" Thalia moves to clap you, then remembers her claws and settles for a friendly nudge with an elbow. "Strictly speaking, I'm dead, and only out here on a technicality — nothing serious is ever going to come out of this, just a bit of fun |Well, if she isn't making you feel special. "You are special, [pc.name]; you'd have to be to go through what you did and come out in one piece ]. So just relax, and we can spend a little time together." A little time together, huh? Well, you might as well cut to the chase — you know what she wants, and she knows why you summoned her. "And truth be told, I wouldn't have it any other way." Thalia bites her lip, then breaks out into a toothy grin. "I thought you'd never get around to asking!" Well, now you have, and by the looks of it she's more than willing. If she wouldn't mind taking a tour of your private bedchambers? Hopefully you'll have done it up better than its previous owner. "Not a high bar to clear, sad to say. Anyone would've had more aesthetic sense than the commander I knew." The gothmander reaches out a hand, and you take as much of the scales and claws into yours as you can. She's surprisingly gentle despite all appearances, and allows you to lead her through the Wayfort into your bedchambers. She's still wearing that heavy getup, eh? You can see the resemblance to Tychris fashion of today, but really, it's more than two centuries dated at this point! "Does it matter? It'll be off soon enough." Oh, it will. Or at least, it will be — Thalia smirks and turns up her hands at the sight of you struggling with the elaborate, heavy knots that fasten her clothes. Would it have made any difference to a half-broken ghost caught in a warped reality? "Yes!" Oh. Well then, ] "By the grace of the goddess, yes." She heaves a sigh and dusts off her rather dated clothing. "Once I'd been restored, I asked my goddess for a chance to properly thank my savior, and... well, she granted it to a degree quite beyond my expectations. So long as you summon me, I have her leave to be free of her Dream for a little while to keep you company — I can't leave the Wayfort, of course, but otherwise have few restrictions on these little sojourns." That's very gracious of her. You can't imagine that Tira is happy with this situation. "Nareva isn't just magnanimous, she's reasonable. She said that since I held the faith for an eternity, it'd be remiss of her to grant anything less... that, and I ought to see how far the Wayfort's come since my time. A just reward for a devout servant. Whatever the goddess paid for my exception, she did it more than willingly." Just as the first Astrida gave themselves to her more than willingly. A faint smile. "You understand." Well, that's all and over with. Now, what's she going to do while back in the world, if for a little bit? She doesn't mind if you ask a few questions, does she? "Oh no, ask away. It's the least I can do after all that you've done for me.""

rows.original: So, how's she feeling? It was a little alarming when you couldn't hear her from her urn after you returned to the present-day Wayfort — you thought you'd lost her until Nina confirmed that she was still there, just inaudible. Thalia makes a show of going over the monstrous draconic claws that pass for her hands. "The goddess has restored me to the best of her ability once I was in her care. However, there're some things that even a divine can't replace once lost. A material form after a fashion is easy enough to replicate, but my self less so; I feel that there're gaps in my memory where something big should be, especially in the days leading up to the Wayfort's demise." Those likely went into the void serpent that inhabited the shadowlith. A nod. "The goddess agrees. Dark matter, as she calls it, doesn't have any intelligence — it simply has power, something like ley-crystals. That intelligence that animated said power had to have come from somewhere, and given the form it took I doubt that it came from the commander or the garrison. Everything considered, I think I'm better off without those parts of me that went into the serpent, so all's well that ends well." Indeed. That being said... the claws, Nareva couldn't fix those for her now? [pc.swornGod nareva |You daresay that she's gotten a lot better at this, given how deftly she reshaped your body into her image. ] "Oh, I wouldn't dream of it, and not just because I'd have to relearn to do everything again. At this point, it's a badge of honor amongst the first generation — none of the others whom I've met in her Dream have chosen to do away with their particular maluses, either. It's part of who I am now, [pc.name].[pc.swornGod Nareva | While I'm glad that you don't need to suffer what the first Astrida went through, what we have is a reminder of our sacrifice to the goddess. ] To take that away would be sacrilegious — not just to her, but to what we lived through." You see. Well, if she feels that way, you won't bring it up again. "I'm not mad, so don't worry about it. Is there anything you'd like to make clear?"
rows.translation: 那么，她感觉怎么样？你回到如今的驿堡后，再也听不见骨灰瓮里的声音，这多少令人惊慌——你以为自己失去了她，直到妮娜确认她仍在那里，只是无法被听见。 塔莉娅煞有介事地检查着代替双手的骇人龙爪。“女神将我纳入照料后，已经尽其所能恢复了我。然而有些东西一旦失去，即使神祇也无法替换。某种意义上的物质形态不难复现，我的自我却没那么容易；我感觉记忆中存在空缺，本该有某些重要事物，尤其是驿堡覆灭前的那些日子。” 那些部分大概进了栖息于影石内的虚空巨蛇。 她点点头。“女神也这么认为。按照她的称呼，暗物质不具备任何智慧——它只有力量，类似地脉水晶。驱使那份力量的智慧必定来自某处；鉴于它所呈现的形态，我认为那智慧并非源于指挥官或驻军。综合考虑，我最好还是不要那些进入巨蛇的自身部分；结局圆满便万事如意。” 的确。话虽如此……那些爪子，娜瑞瓦现在无法替她修复吗？[pc.swornGod nareva |你敢说她在这方面已经长进许多，毕竟她极其娴熟地将你的身体重塑成自己的形象。 ] “哦，我做梦也不会那么想，不只是因为自己将不得不再次学习怎样做所有事。如今，这在第一代中是一枚荣誉徽章——我在她梦中遇见的其他人同样没有选择摆脱自己特有的缺陷。这已经成为如今的我，[pc.name]。[pc.swornGod Nareva | 我很高兴你不必承受第一代阿斯特里达经历的一切，但我们身上的痕迹提醒着我们为女神作出的牺牲。 ] 将其抹去将是一种亵渎——不仅亵渎她，也亵渎我们亲身经历的一切。” 你明白了。既然她这样认为，你不会再提。 “我没有生气，所以别担心。还有什么想弄清的吗？”

You see. Well, if she feels that way, you won't bring it up again. "I'm not mad, so don't worry about it. Is there anything you'd like to make clear?""

rows.original: How's she holding up since the last time you spoke?
rows.translation: 自从你上次和她联系后，她的情况怎么样？
rows.raw: "How's she holding up since the last time you spoke?"

rows.original: A nod. "Given what I'd suffered through, the goddess offered me rest and oblivion, but since I know what awaits me beyond the Ways I'm in no hurry to embrace it just yet. Maybe in the far future I'll grow weary and ask for release, but until then I serve in death as I did in life. "Besides, I'm not alone. I shouldn't be surprised, but many of the first Astrida chose to serve the goddess after death — we are especially beloved, after all. To see so many familiar faces after so long, and more that I feel I should remember but can't..." It'll be fine. She'll have plenty of time to repair what memories she can, and to make new ones to replace those which were lost. After what she's suffered through, Thalia deserves a new lease on — well, not life, but existence, certainly. You can't imagine that Nareva's Dream lacks for anything that she might want. "No, it doesn't. If anything, it's made to evoke memories of the Tychris I remember." Can she tell you something of how she's serving Nareva? [pc.swornGod astrida |Thalia raises an eyebrow and wrings her claws. "The goddess' personal champion isn't familiar with her Dream?" Nareva keeps you busy enough that attending garden parties or making courtesy calls isn't in your schedule, even in your sleep. You may have visited once or twice, but it was never to stop and smell the roses. Besides, this isn't asking about the Dream... it's asking about her. "O-oh." Thalia colors a bit and looks sheepish at that. "Well, a good number of us, myself included, help our goddess catalogue the Well of Memory. After all, it's the greatest collection of experiences — a living library — and if she's to find anything she desires in any reasonable time, our help is needed to keep everything sorted and indexed, amongst other things. "It's also gratifying to work with something that you helped create — maybe the novelty will wear off someday, but I really like looking into the well's swirling depths and knowing that my soul's in there somewhere. As is yours, [pc.name], and every other Astrida's." [pc.bg scholar acolyte arcanist |An afterlife of being an glorified librarian... actually doesn't sound that bad, given what you used to do before all this happened. One supposes that after a lifetime's worth of danger and excitement of being a mage-hunter, an idyllic retirement reminiscent of the academia you left might be welcome |Huh. An eternity of being a glorified librarian... well, it's not quite your style. You don't mind serving Nareva after death — it is part and parcel of what you signed up for, after all — but with no background in academia hopefully she'll find some other use for you that's more inclined to your skills. While others might see a bookish retirement as a welcome thing after a lifetime's worth of danger and excitement of being a mage-hunter, it's not your style Thalia smiles. "I'm not sure if wandering spirits of champions are allowed in the world under Tira's law. We haven't known each other that long, but with how you handled yourself back in the Wayfort's past I do agree that your talents would be wasted doing the work I do. " Exactly ]. "Either way, it's a peaceable existence, [pc.name]. The company of my peers and goddess, meaningful work in her service, and wanting for little at all. Plenty of small talk, too — for example, it's said that our goddess is hosting Philander and Phyria in her Dream as well, but we've never actually seen them around. If anyone were to be beloved of the goddess, it would be those two. "Anyway, I think that's all there is to be said — is there something else you'd like to ask?" |Thalia thinks a moment, then gives you a rueful smile. "I'm afraid I can't go into the details, but suffice to say that I'm being kept busy. It's pretty satisfying and meaningful work that I'm suited for, so I have no complaints." Sounds like something you'd like to enjoy after you pass yourself. "Quite so. Is there anything else I can clear up for you?" ]
rows.translation: 点了点头。“鉴于我所经历的一切，女神赐予我安宁与遗忘，但既然我知道前方等待我的是什么，我暂时并不急于接受它。也许在遥远的未来，我会感到疲惫，从而请求解脱，但在那之前，我会在死亡中继续履行我在生前的职责。 而且，我并不是一个人。其实我并不应该感到惊讶，因为很多最初选择追随阿斯特里达的人，在死后都选择了侍奉这位女神——毕竟，我们才是她特别宠爱的存在。时隔这么久，看到这么多熟悉的面孔，其中还有一些我应该记得，但却想不起来的人……没关系的。她会有足够的时间去修复那些还能恢复的记忆，也会创造新的记忆来替代那些失去的。经历了这一切之后，塔莉娅确实值得重新开始生活——虽然不是重新开始整个生命，但至少是重新开始她的存在。你绝对想象不到，娜瑞瓦的梦境里没有任何她可能会想要的东西。 “不，并没有。相反，这个梦境正是为了唤起我对曾经拥有的提克里斯的记忆而创造的。” 她能告诉你一些关于她是如何为娜瑞瓦服务的吗？ [pc.swornGod astrida |塔莉娅挑了挑眉毛，然后拧了拧她的爪子：“这位女神的私人护卫竟然不熟悉她的‘梦境’？” 娜瑞瓦让你忙得不可开交，以至于连参加花园派对或进行礼节性拜访都根本没时间，哪怕是在梦里也不可能去做这些事。你可能去过一两次，但从来都不是为了欣赏那些美丽的花朵……再说，现在问的也不是关于‘梦境’的事情……而是关于别的她哦……”塔莉娅有些脸红，显得有些尴尬。“其实，包括我在内，有很多人都在帮助我们的女神整理‘记忆之井’中的资料。毕竟，那可是最珍贵的经验宝库——一座活生生的图书馆。如果她想要在合理的时间内找到自己需要的东西，我们就必须帮忙整理这些资料，确保它们都能被妥善分类和索引。 能够参与自己曾经帮忙创造的东西，也是一件令人欣慰的事情。也许这种新鲜感有一天会消失，但我真的很喜欢凝视那口井中旋转的深水，知道自己的灵魂就在那里的某个地方——你的灵魂也是如此。 [pc.name]，以及所有其他的阿斯特里达们。 [pc.bg scholar acolyte arcanist |如果成为一名“高级图书管理员”作为自己的来世……考虑到你在此之前所从事的工作，其实这个想法听起来也并不坏。可以想象，经过一生作为法师猎人的危险与刺激之后，能够过上一种类似于你曾经就读过的学术环境的宁静退休生活，想必会让人感到非常惬意。 |哈，一辈子都当个高级图书管理员……嗯，这确实不符合你的性格。你并不介意死后继续为娜雷瓦服务——毕竟这也是你当初选择这条道路时所同意的——但既然你没有学术背景，希望她能找到其他更能发挥你能力的工作方式。虽然对于那些一生都在经历危险与刺激、从事法师猎人的工作的人来说，过上书生般的退休生活或许是一件令人欣慰的事情，但这并不是你的风格。 塔莉娅微笑着说道：“我不确定根据蒂拉的法律，那些英雄的游荡灵魂是否被允许存在于这个世界上。我们相识的时间虽然不长，但从你之前在荒废驿堡公司的表现来看，我确实认为你的才能去做我现在这份工作实在是浪费了。” 正是如此。 ]无论如何，这都是一种平静的生活方式。 [pc.name]我和我的同伴们一起为这位女神服务，做着有意义的工作，而且几乎不求任何回报。当然，也少不了闲聊——比如，据说我们的女神还在她的梦境中招待着菲兰德和菲莉亚，但我们其实从未见过他们出现在那里。如果真有人能得到女神的青睐，那肯定就是这两个人了。 “总之，我想说的就是这些——还有其他你想问的吗？ |塔莉娅思考了一会儿，然后露出一个遗憾的笑容：“恐怕我不能详细说明，但可以告诉你，我现在很忙。这份工作很适合我，也让我感到很有成就感，所以我没有任何怨言。” 听起来像是你完成自己的使命之后也会想要去做的事情吧。 “确实如此。还有其他什么我可以帮你解答的吗？ ]
